en: Title: *Amoghapāśakalparāja* Published: In installments in the *Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taishō University*, by the Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai (Esoteric Scripture Research Group) Source: A unique manuscript (*codex unicus*) from China
Péter Tongori, *Amoghapāśakalparāja* – Part I,

Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara! Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling on Mount Potalaka, in the abode of Avalokiteśvara, which was adorned with many *sāla*, *tamāla*, *campaka*, *aśoka*, and *atimuktaka* trees, as well as various other trees, together with a community of monks consisting of eight thousand and ninety-nine [thousand] monks.

2. Surrounded and honored by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas and hundreds of thousands of sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa host, he was teaching the Dharma with reference to the gods Īśvara, Maheśvara, and Brahmā. Then, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, and placed his right knee upon the ground.

Having established himself facing the Blessed One, he bowed with palms joined toward where the Blessed One was, and with a smiling face, addressed the Blessed One as follows: "The Heart-mantra named Amogharāja, which I previously received from the presence of the Tathāgata Lokendrarāja in the world-system Vilokitā during the ninety-first aeon—by means of which [mantra], having placed the sons of the gods, Īśvara and Maheśvara, at its head..."

4. I have inspired thousands of sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa host toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and I have attained one million samādhis, foremost among which is the Array of Non-delusive Knowledge. Furthermore, Blessed One, in whichever place on earth this heart-mantra should circulate, it should be known, Blessed One, that in that place on earth there is Īśvara—

5. Twelve thousand sons of the gods, headed by Īśvara and Brahmā, will stand there for the sake of protection, defense, and guardianship. That spot of earth where this *Amoghasampada-hṛdaya* shall circulate will become a place honored as a *caitya*, O Blessed One. Those beings, O Blessed One, who here [recite] the *Amoghapāśa*... will have planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas.

6. Blessed One, whoever—be they a perpetrator of offenses, one who practices evil dharmas, a reviler of the noble ones, a rejecter of the true Dharma, one destined for the Avīci hell, or one rejected by all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas—should feel remorse and undertake restraint for the future, then, Blessed One, by the mere recitation of a single fast-day vow (*upavāsa*), even in this very life...

In this life, those karmas are purified, brought to exhaustion, or cast out. Whether it be by a fever occurring every day, every second day, every third day, or every fourth day; or by a fever occurring every seventh day less one; or by pain in the eyes, pain in the ears, pain in the nose, pain in the teeth or lips, pain in the tongue or palate, pain in the heart, pain in the abdomen, or pain in the sides or the waist—[these are all purified].

Or not by pain in the limbs or minor members, or by throat-seizure, dysentery, or diarrhea; or by [pain in] the hands or feet, or by illness of the nose or head; or by ringworm, vitiligo, leprosy, eczema, psoriasis, erysipelas, fistula-in-ano, boils, epilepsy, spells, or other malevolent rites (*kṛtyā*); or by execution, imprisonment, beating, threatening, false accusations, or defamation—in short, O Blessed One, whether by bodily affliction, mental anguish, or by the sight of bad dreams, that karma—

2. It comes to exhaustion; it reaches its end even before [the end of] impure beings who are resolved through faith, O Blessed One, if the four assemblies and the four castes—even those with deceit and guile—should hear this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* of mine, and should take it up, preserve it, recite it, write it, cause it to be written, and master it; or at the very least, having remained within the ear-cavity of those belonging to the animal realm, [it enters] the ear...

3. When they shall offer these vajra-words, they should contemplate them as being without diminution, without form, without conceptualization, without origination, without movement, without action, without stain, free from even-mindedness, and devoid of the five aggregates. By this yoga, the recollection of the Buddha (buddhānusmṛti) should be cultivated; then, from those ten directions, one will behold thousands of Buddhas at their head.

4. They will suffer; they will confess their transgressions, and so forth. Or, having written it in a book, they will keep it in their home. Whether out of fear of their masters, or out of compliance with others, or for the sake of high status, they will hear [this]. O Blessed One, it should be known by the wise that through the power of the noble Avalokiteśvara, that sound will fall into the hollows of their ears. Just as, O Blessed One, if—

5. It is just like this, O Blessed One: suppose a person were to revile, abuse, grind upon a stone, and smear himself with sandalwood, camphor, or musk. Yet that sandalwood, camphor, or musk does not think: "I have been reviled or abused by this man; I shall depart because of his odor. On the contrary, it remains simply fragrant. In the same way, Blessed One, this—

6. O Blessed One, for any wicked being who, having treated [this] *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* with contempt or spoken [of it] deceitfully—even if they should worship it with guile and hypocrisy—that very act will become a cause of merit for them. Wherever they are reborn, they shall never be separated from the equipment of ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, and merit; they shall indeed make their ethical discipline fragrant. And, O Blessed One, whichever son of good family or daughter of good family...

7. Whether it be a monk, a nun, a layman, a laywoman, or any other sentient being, whoever observes the fast on the eighth day of the bright fortnight dedicated to the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, reciting the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* twenty-one times without speaking to anyone—twenty-one benefits are to be expected for that person by the Blessed One in this very life. What are these twenty-one? Namely, [the cessation of] diseases...

1. No diseases will arise in his body; and the diseases that have already arisen will quickly subside through the power of his karma. His limbs will be supple and pleasing to behold; he will be dear to many people; and his sense faculties will be well-guarded. Furthermore, he will obtain [his goals]: whatever wealth arises for him, thieves shall not carry it off, fire shall not burn it, and water shall not sweep it away. Nor is a king able to seize it by force. And his undertakings will flourish.

They shall come to pass. There will be no fear of destruction, nor fear of drought. There will be no fear of wind or rain. Having recited the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* seven times over ashes and water, one should perform the binding of the cardinal and intermediate directions, as well as the regions below and above. All calamities will be pacified; and the snatchers of vitality (*ojohāra*) will not be able to steal away one's vitality. One will become dear and pleasing to all sentient beings, and there will be no fear of enemies for such a person. [When] it arises—

3. Furthermore, his fear of enemies will quickly be pacified; he shall have no fear of non-human beings (*amanuṣya*), no fear of *kākhorda* spells, and no fear of *ḍākinīs*. Nor shall he experience intense primary or secondary afflictions (*kleśa-upakleśa*). He shall not meet his end through fire or weapons. Deities (*devatā*) shall stand constantly and continuously to provide him with protection, defense, and guardianship. And wherever he is reborn, he shall never be separated [from them].

4. There will be these twenty benefits for him from loving-kindness (*maitrī*), compassion (*karuṇā*), sympathetic joy (*muditā*), and equanimity (*upekṣā*), which he may expect. Furthermore, he shall obtain eight other qualities. What are the eight? At the time of death, the noble Avalokiteśvara will appear before him in the form of a monk; he will pass away in peace; his vision will not be confused; and he will not throw out his hands.

5. He will not die while stepping with his feet, nor while voiding excrement or urine, nor while mounted on a bed; he will possess well-established mindfulness. He will not die with his face turned downward. At the time of death, he will possess inexhaustible eloquence. He will be reborn in whichever Buddha-field he has made his vow for. And he will never be separated from spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), who will attend upon him three times a day and three times a night.

6. [The following] should be avoided: liquor, meat, onions, leeks, garlic, and food prepared from a mixture [of these], as well as leftovers; for one who seeks excellence, these must be shunned. Furthermore, having understood the strength and weakness of sentient beings, this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* Dharma-discourse should be proclaimed to them. One must not practice the "teacher’s fist" (withhold teachings), because Bodhisattvas are free from stain, devoid of stinginess and envy, and act for the benefit of sentient beings. They shall attain the awakening of a Buddha.

7. It is reckoned among the qualities of Bodhisattvas. Enlightenment is said to be wisdom (*prajñā*), and "beings" (*sattva*) refers to skillful means (*upāya*). These two dharmas are not attained by beings unless the Blessed One grants me permission for me to proclaim that *hṛdaya* before the Tathāgata for the sake, benefit, and happiness of the fourfold assembly, and for other evildoers as well. Then the Blessed One [addressed] the noble Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva...

He said this: "Speak, O Pure Being, if you consider now to be the time; it will perform the duty of a father for those who belong to the Bodhisattva vehicle in the future time, in the final age, as approved by the Tathāgata. Then, the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, with unblinking eyes, spoke thus to the Blessed One: "Listen to me, Blessed One, regarding the maṇḍala of liberation honored by all Bodhisattvas."

2. For the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the sake of the great mass of people. Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas established throughout the three times. Homage to the entire Saṅgha of Pratyekabuddhas and Noble Śrāvakas of the past, future, and present. Homage to those who have gone rightly and those who have practiced rightly. Homage to Śāradvatīputra. Homage to those headed by Maitreya.

Homage to all Bodhisattvas, to the great assemblies of Bodhisattvas! Homage to the noble Amitābha, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha! Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One! It is thus: Oṃ cara cara ciri ciri curu curu Mahākāruṇika! Ciri ciri miri!

4. *Miri curu curu*, O Great Compassionate One! *Siri siri ciri ciri*, *siri siri ciri ciri*, O Great Lotus-Handed One! *Kala kala kili kili kulu kulu*, O Great Pure Being! *Budhya budhya dhāva dhāva kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi*, O Supreme Pure Being! *Kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru*, O Attainer of Great Power! *Cala cala saṃcala saṃcala vica-* [move, move, move completely, move completely, move apart—]

5. *Vicala*: *eṭuṭu eṭuṭu*, *bhara bhara*, *bhiri bhiri*, *bhuru bhuru*, *ehy ehi*, O bearer of the great compassionate Great Lord of Beasts (*mahākāruṇika-mahāpaśupati-veśadhara*)! *dhara dhara*, *sara sara*, *cara cara*, *hara haraḥ*! *hāhā hāhā*, *hihi hihi*, *hūhū hūhū*, O wearer of the form of Brahmā of the syllable *oṃ* (*oṃkāra-brahma-veśadhara*)! *dhara dhara*, *dhiri dhiri*, *dhuru dhuru*, *bhara bhara*, *sara sara*, *para para*, *cara cara*, [O you who possess] hundreds of thousands of rays of light (*raśmi-śata-sahasra*)...

To the one whose body is adorned with rays: blaze, blaze! burn, burn! O Blessed One, whose feet are worshipped by the hosts of gods, sages, and the deities of the Moon, Sun, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Brahmā, and Indra! Suru suru! Curu curu! Muru muru! Puru puru! You who assume many various guises as the leaders of the sages and gods, such as Sanatkumāra, Rudra, Vāsava, Viṣṇu, and Dhanada! Dhara dhara! Dhiri dhiri! Dhuru dhuru! Thara thara! Ghara ghara! Yara yara! Lara lara!

Hara hara! Mara mara! Para para! Vara vara! O Bestower of Boons, Samantāvalokita; O Great Lord, Lokeshvara who gazes upon the world! Muhu muhu! Muru muru! Muyā muyā! Muñca muñca! O Blessed One, Noble Avalokiteśvara, protect, protect me and all sentient beings from all fears, all calamities, all misfortunes, all planetary influences, and from killing, binding, beating, and threatening!

1. Deliverer from fatigue, thieves, fire, water, poison, and weapons; *kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu cara cara*, illuminator of the faculties, powers, factors of enlightenment, and the four noble truths; *tapa tapa dama dama sama sama*, dispeller of the blinding darkness of great ignorance; fulfiller of the six perfections; *mili mili ṭaṭa ṭaṭa ṭhaṭha ṭhaṭha ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭuṭu ṭuṭu*, one who has donned a girdle made of eneya-deer skin.

2. Come, come! O destroyer of the hosts of spirits of Īśvara and Maheśvara! Act, act! Move, move! Do, do! Strike, strike! Kaṭa kaṭa! Maṭa maṭa! You who dwell in the pure realm! O Greatly Compassionate One! Wearer of the white sacrificial thread and the jewel-garland crown; wearer of the jewel-garland crown placed upon the head of the Omniscient One! Unshakable through meditation, concentration, and liberation, with hands joined in the great and wondrous lotus gesture! [O you who possess] the continuum of many beings...

3. O Ripener! O Greatly Compassionate One! Purifier of all karmic obscurations! Liberator from all diseases! F fulfiller of all hopes! Consoler of all sentient beings! Homage be to you, svāhā! The rites for one who has achieved success through recitation are as follows: by reciting this three times a day, one purifies the five deeds of immediate retribution and effects the complete purification of all karmic obscurations. [With] agarwood incense...

4. For all fevers, one should perform a boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) with ashes, water, mustard seeds, stakes of *khadira* wood, and so forth. For all diseases, one should give a cord after having consecrated it (*parijapya*) with ghee, oil, or water. It cuts through *kākhorda* spells when used with a blade. For protection, one should use a protective cord. For abdominal pain, salt-water; for destroying poison, earth or water. For eye disease, a white cord should be tied to the ear. [For] tooth...

5. For a stake [used against] a *śūla* (disease), one should take a tooth-stick (*dantakāṣṭha*) of *karavīra*, recite the mantra twenty-one times over a five-colored thread (*pañcaraṅgikasūtra*), tie it to four stakes of *khadira* wood, and bury them in the four directions; thus, a great boundary (*mahāsīmābandha*) is established. For all protections, [one may use] a thread, water, or ashes. For all planetary seizures (*graha*), a five-colored thread is used. For all fevers, a white thread is used. For all insects, spiders, and *lohali* [creatures], [the same applies].

6. In cases of throat-obstructions, [one should use] honey combined with *pippalī*. For eye diseases, one should use scented water, *palāśa* water, or honey-water. For earache, [one should use] oil. In all instances of strife, quarrel, conflict, dispute, or slander, one should recite [the mantra] over water and rinse the mouth. To protect strength, territory, kingdom, and realm, full jars should be established; by one who is pure, dressed in clean garments, having performed a great worship, it should be recited—the Great [Sādhana].

7. With that water, one should sprinkle [the area]; thus protection for all sentient beings is established. All calamities and misfortunes are pacified. For those who have been raised up, anointing with sandalwood paste should be performed after reciting the Heart Mantra twenty-one times; this destroys all acts of immediate retribution (*ānantarya*) through constant recitation. Protection of the home is achieved by the *padma* fire-offering (*homa*), the sustenance of all sentient beings by the *candana* fire-offering, and [protection against] all spirits and seizing demons (*bhūtagraha*)—4a.

1. Protection: *Jayā*, *Vijayā*, *Nākuli*, *Gandhānākuli*, *Vāruṇī*, *Abhayapāṇi*, *Indrapāṇi*, *Gandhapriyaṅgu*, *Tagara*, *Cakrā*, *Mahācakrā*, *Viṣṇukrāntā*, *Somarājī*, *Sunandā*—having recited [the mantra] one hundred and eight times over these, they should be made into a talisman (*maṇi*) and worn, bound upon the head or the arm. For children, it should be tied around the neck; for women, bathing with them is supreme. This brings about good fortune and pacifies misfortune (*alakṣmī*). When bound with this talisman, all protection is secured.

2. This [mantra] becomes [effective]: poison and fire do not approach; no harm caused by poison arises; even if it has arisen, it will not produce suffering; [afflictions] will quickly be pacified. Planets will be pacified; there is the suppression of wind, clouds, and lightning, or the warding off [of calamities] by means of water, the *vāraṇī* creeper, or all [other] means. When the Heart-mantra of the Noble Avalokiteśvara has been accomplished, it performs these rites. Now, if one wishes to accomplish [this], the procedure is as follows: having painted an image of the Buddha on a cloth with non-sticky pigments, [one should paint] the Noble...

3. Avalokiteśvara, wearing a crown of matted hair, clad in the skin of an eneya antelope and the attire of Paśupati, and adorned with all ornaments, should be painted by an artist who observes the poṣadha vows. Then, the practitioner, having prepared a maṇḍala of cow dung before that image and strewn it with white flowers, should place eight full vessels there, as well as eight offerings and sixty-four other offerings.

Free from offerings of meat and blood, one should recite the vidyā eight thousand times while burning agarwood incense. Having fasted for one day and night, or for three nights, eating the "three white foods," bathing at the three times of day, and wearing clean garments, Āryāvalokiteśvara himself will come. He fulfills all [desires]. Having consecrated red arsenic or collyrium with the mantra, [one should apply it] to the eyes.

5. Having performed this, he then becomes invisible; he travels through the sky and shall attain the samādhi called Amoghajñānavyūha (the Array of Unfailing Wisdom). Whatever he desires, he accomplishes it; therefore, it is the means of attainment. Thus spoke the Blessed One, and the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, those sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm, Brahmā Sahāmpati, Īśvara, and Maheśvara were uplifted in mind as the Blessed One spoke.

6. They rejoiced in it. The *Amoghapāśa* is completed. Then, indeed, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, and placed his right knee upon the ground. With a body radiant with rays of light like the sun blazing with a thousand flames, he bowed with palms joined toward the Blessed One and spoke.

7. Having assumed a face that was white, gentle, and smiling with a full orb of a moon, and having brought to mind the power of great loving-kindness and compassion for the sake of the welfare and compassion of the four castes of the world, for the purpose of obtaining the supreme gift of the excellent attainment of the reality (*tattva*) of the Vidyādharas and all accomplishments, he addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, I possess this Great [Amoghapāśa] King, the Unfailing..."

1. Herein, I shall proclaim before the Blessed One this secret chapter on the heart of the mudrās, mantras, and hearts of the supreme great maṇḍala for the accomplishment of reality—the essence of the essence arisen from the great reality of this noble lotus maṇḍala, the supreme maṇḍala of liberation, and the secret of the means for accomplishing the samaya. And here, in the midst of this great assembly of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, and in the presence of the maṇḍala of the accomplished vidyā-deities...

2. In the presence of Īśvara, Maheśvara, Brahmā, the gods, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, the hosts of ṛṣis, the moon, the sun, the clusters of stars and constellations, the siddhas, the vidyādharas, and the goddesses, I proclaim before them the attainment of the supramundane practice which is the heart-essence of reality; the attainment of the practice through recitation and the attainment through meditation in the presence of the Blessed One, surrounded by a retinue of great vidyādhara hosts—I proclaim this supreme secret essence of reality.

"I shall speak it. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, extending his golden-colored arms—which were adorned with the primary and secondary marks of a hundred thousand merits and resembled the trunks of fragrant nāga elephants wreathed in garlands of blazing rays—placed them upon the crown of the head of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara and stroked him, saying: "Speak, O Great—"

"O compassionate one, supreme pure being! Empowered by the Tathāgatas and now empowered by me as well, speak the most secret samaya! Thus empowered and approved by all the Tathāgatas in the ten directions—as many as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Ganges sands—[the speech] was approved and empowered. Then, indeed, the noble Avalokiteśvara—

5. Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, having gazed toward the ten directions, spoke these mantras in the presence of the Blessed One—his own heart-mantra, the secret of reality: [2] *Oṃ padmahasta mahāmoghapāśa sādhaya samayahṛdayaṃ cara cara hūṃ*. This is the heart-mantra of the essential nature of Amoghapāśa. As soon as this secret heart-mantra was spoken by the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara at Potalaka—

6. The king of mountains, together with its peaks, forests, and groves—Sumeru, Cakravāḍa, and Mahācakravāḍa—shook in six ways. All the abodes of the gods trembled; the palaces of the nāgas quaked. The dwellings of the yakṣas and rākṣasas were agitated; the great oceans became turbulent with waves; the waters were stirred up on all sides. The forms of the Buddhas stationed in the ten directions uttered this word of approval: "Excellent, excellent!"

7. "O Son of the Conqueror, this well-spoken [mantra] is the unfailing secret heart, perfected through recitation, unsurpassed. Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, to Avalokiteśvara: "Excellent, excellent, Avalokiteśvara! This is the unfailing secret practice of reality perfected through recitation. Avalokiteśvara replied: "So it is, Blessed One. This secret heart of the dhāraṇī, Blessed One, by the mere act of being uttered once, [acts] individually and separately throughout the ten directions."

1. Extending his arm across hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *gaṅgānadīvālukā* [sands of the Ganges] worlds, the Tathāgata takes hold of one’s head and grants reassurance, saying: "Upon the mere utterance [of this name], you shall behold all the Tathāgatas; you shall be liberated from the diseases of hundreds of thousands of eons; the hells shall perish and dissolve; all evils, all illnesses, and likewise diseases shall be destroyed; sins, wicked beings, adversaries, and enemies shall perish—of this there is no doubt."

2. Noble Avalokiteśvara will always be visible and grant boons with equanimity. Regarding this vidyā, the practitioner of the vidyā (vidyādhara) must be pure; having bathed well, they should wear clean garments. With a mind focused on loving-kindness and compassion, they should be intent upon mercy for all beings. One should worship Noble Avalokiteśvara on a cloth painting (duṣyapaṭa) with flowers, incense, perfumes, and garlands.

3. One should offer ointment and lamps on either the eighth or the fifteenth day, and perform the ritual procedure for recitation and accomplishment (*jāpasādhana*). First, the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* [should be recited]. One hundred and eight recitations should be performed while seated cross-legged before the cloth painting (*paṭa*). Without speaking, one should recite the *Krodharāja* one hundred and eight times; one should be consecrated with water and mustard seeds, and the mudrā should be bound twenty-one times.

The recitations should be performed [the prescribed] number of times, and the mantra-consecration (mantrābhiṣeka) should be performed; the mudrā-consecration (mudrābhiṣeka) should also be performed. Then, the Heart-mantra of Amogha-guhyasamaya should be recited one thousand and eight times. By means of that recitation-mantra as it is uttered, the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa together with the Wrathful King becomes multiplied a hundred-thousandfold through the performance of the recitation rite. When the procedure for the recitation is complete, [one should prepare] a cloth-painting (duṣyapaṭa).

5. Fire blazes and an earthquake occurs; various rays of light issue forth from the body of Avalokiteśvara. The noose held in the hand of the Amoghapāśa-holder blazes. The Vidyādhara rejoices; his head blazes, signs of accomplishment appear, and the sound of "Excellent! issues forth. This is the sign of accomplishment; the mudrā of the Amoghapāśahṛdayakalpa has been perfected. Then, all [attainments]—

6. All rites will be accomplished the very moment they are uttered. Hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, will grant their presence upon being seen; they will place their gold-colored hands upon the crown of one’s head. Established as the very nature of the noble Avalokiteśvara, one will abide with a body that is the secret heart, perfectly clear, stainless, and pure. He—

7. He will bestow the supreme jewel; he will grant all accomplishments (*siddhi*). He will bestow the accomplishment of the mudrās and the ritual manual (*kalpa*) of the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*. He protects [the practitioner] as if he were his own biological son, until he attains the awakening of a Buddha. Then, [he leads him] to the world-realm of Sukhāvatī, which is entirely filled with a complete maṇḍala, adorned with a perfect Buddha-field, and surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas, [under] the noble and supreme Victor Amitābha.

By one who desires to see [the Lord] seated upon a lion-throne adorned with a gabled pavilion, his body illuminated by hundreds of thousands of millions of rays of light as he teaches the Dharma, that Vidyādhara must become pure; with a mind purified by a faultless intention, with a heart of loving-kindness during the fortnight of miracles, with a resolute disposition of compassion, and with reverence and serene faith toward the Guru, he should [worship] the noble Avalokiteśvara’s great cloth-painting (paṭa) according to how it is available.

2. One should worship with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, cloths, and banners. From the eighth day until the thirteenth, one should subsist on the three white foods (*triśuklabhukta*). Day by day, before the painting, one should perform the recitation (*jāpa*) of the Noble Amoghapāśa Secret Heart mantra twenty times, remaining silent. Twenty-one times the Heart and Sub-Heart mantras of Krodharāja, and one hundred and eight times [the main mantra], should be performed while standing before that very painting.

3. One should offer water for the feet (*arghapādya*) three times each day. One should awaken [the deity] with aloeswood (*agaru*), sandalwood (*candana*), frankincense (*turuṣka*), and *guggulu*, together with the essence of flowers, mango juice, and musk (*sakastūrikā*). One should recite the invocation mantra eight thousand times. There is a supreme king of incenses called *Trailokyāmoghavimalā*; by the mere act of burning it, throughout the ten directions, the entire great trichiliocosm world-system—[all] the Buddhas...

4. Great clouds and masses of incense smoke radiate from the *ddha*-fields; by the mere scent of which, all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, receive the great incense-king’s offering of incense. All diseases will vanish, all bad dreams will be pacified, and even those who have gone into the animal realm, upon smelling the fragrance of the incense, shall all—[become...]—ā-...

5. Karmic obstructions leading to rebirth as milk-rice (pāyasa) go to complete exhaustion. All strife, quarrels, famines, conflicts, disputes, riots, tumults, bad dreams, calamities, afflictions, misfortunes, and distresses—through all these, all diseases shall be pacified. All winds, thunderbolts, cold, heat, and clouds shall be pacified. They perish by all evils. All spells, incantations, yogic applications, and poisons—[shall be neutralized].

6. By the rays of this *gara* [incense], all planetary influences (*graha*), all forms of epilepsy (*apasmāra*), and all fevers shall perish; ill-spoken words, transgressions, and evil glances shall depart and be destroyed by the fragrance of the incense. They shall withdraw, never again having power, until the very end at the seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). This king of incenses should be used constantly. Then, on the fourteenth day, having fasted for a day and night, one should recite the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* one hundred and eight times...

7. One hundred recitations of the King of Wrath (*Krodharāja*) should be performed—specifically one hundred and eight—and a threefold white offering (*triśuklabali*) should be presented as it is available. While reciting the Heart and Sub-Heart mantras one thousand and eight times, a lamp should be offered with scented oil. One should sleep before that very cloth-painting until the time of dawn, when one will see in a dream a golden casket [containing] the world-system of Sukhāvatī, together with its celestial palaces and jewel-trees.

He sees the mountain with its jewels, together with its lotus ponds, its residences, its gabled halls, and its celestial palaces, as well as the miraculous display of supernatural powers. He sees the Tathāgata Amitāyus seated within a gabled hall, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas and an assembly of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas. And he encourages that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, and that vidyādhara, saying "Excellent! (sādhukāra).

2. And he will say: "Excellent, excellent, O noble son! You have performed many heroic deeds as a *vidyādhara*. You have planted many roots of merit. You have fulfilled many obligations; you have accomplished what was to be done. You have mastered the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, the *Vimokṣamaṇḍala*, and the *Mahāmudrā-mantra-paṭala-hṛdaya*. You have attained the state of a *vidyādhara-buddha*. This is your final [birth]."

"O Ṛbhus, be born in a birthless state; be reborn in a Buddha-field! Pass from Buddha-field to Buddha-field until you reach the seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa)! Placing his right hand upon the crown of my head, he grants all worldly accomplishments and brings the supramundane path to fruition. "This is the supreme accomplishment," he said, and the awakened one rejoiced himself.

4. He sees him; he becomes free from all obscurations and completely purified. The Noble Avalokiteśvara stands before him in the form of a brahmin and grants him the boon of all his desires. That cloth painting blazes forth, rays of light issue from it, and he obtains many hundreds of thousands of other virtues. He attains worldly prosperity and [the favor of] all people.

The kinsmen, ministers, brahmins, and householders will remain under one's control. One becomes worthy of great honor. From the ascetics and brahmins, one obtains great and unfailing success (*amoghasiddhi*). Three times each day, the mudrā should be performed. Then, on the fourteenth day, first a meal accompanied by ritual fees (*dakṣiṇā*) should be given to the ascetics and brahmins; thereafter, one may eat oneself according to what is available.

6. Furthermore, since you desire the vision of the Buddha, the vision of the Bodhisattvas, and the vision of the deities, this King of Incense should be offered to the Blessed Buddha after reciting the invocation mantra over the incense twenty-one times. By the mere offering of the incense, he will grant a vision. He will declare everything—whether auspicious or inauspicious, decline or prosperity—and will speak until the end of one's life, [and regarding] going...

7. Or they announce his departure. Now I shall explain the ritual of the mantra, as well as the means of accomplishment (*sādhana*) and the rites for specific purposes according to the rules: [3] *Oṃ padmadhara amoghajayade curu curu svāhā*. This is the subsidiary heart-mantra (*upahṛdayamantra*) of the Amogharājahṛdaya. [4] *Oṃ padmapāśadhara amoghavarada saṃcodaya hūṃ*. This is the incitement mantra (*saṃcodanamantra*) [addressed to] all Tathāgatas, Bodhisattvas, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas.

1. Having performed the invocation everywhere by scattering [the substances] in the ten directions twenty-one times recited over human and non-human beings and the like, mixed with water and white mustard seeds and fumigated with incense-king (dhūparāja), they become present. [5] Oṃ trailokyavāhaya amoghapāśa padmavilokita āyāntu bhuvane suru suru suru vimale hūṃ. This is the invocation mantra; it should be scattered in the ten directions with guggulu incense, mixed with water and flowers, having been recited one hundred and eight times.

2. Everywhere, there is the supreme accomplishment of invocation. Oṃ, O Lotus-Armed One, Holder of the Great Noose, I invite you; may those of unfailing power come! Bhuvasva muru muru hūṃ. This is the mantra for invitation. For all Tathāgatas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas, as well as for the gods, nāgas, and others who dwell in all maṇḍalas, this is the vidyā for invitation: by means of water from a ritual vessel (*bhṛṅgāra*), flowers, tooth-sticks, and incense of royal fragrance, recited one hundred and eight times, it serves everywhere.

3. The Universal [Mantra]: Oṃ padmāmogha vajrādhiṣṭhānena kuru kuru svāhā. By means of this, the binding of the mandala on the earth is accomplished. If one strikes the earth with water and white mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited one hundred and eight times, the earth within a circumference of one hundred yojanas becomes empowered as being composed of vajra. Furthermore, all those who are protected by it become firm-minded and invisible to all enemies; they become invisible to all obstacles and calamities.

4. By means of the Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Piśācas, Apasmārakas, Ḍākinīs, and those who assume forms at will (*kāmarūpin*), one becomes invisible everywhere and possesses the firmness of a vajra. [8] *Oṃ amoghapāsa padmottarasiṃhāsana oṭi miri miri hūṃ*. Having recited this seat-mantra (*āsanamantra*) over mustard seeds one thousand and eight times, they should be struck upon the ground; thus the Great Lotus Palace (*mahāpadmavimāna*) becomes empowered as a seat. All—

5. These become supreme offerings consisting of the seven jewels of the Tathāgatas, serving as the empowerment for the lotus lion-throne. The Vidyādhara should sprinkle his own seat with water and mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited twenty-one times. Thereupon, the purification of the lotus throne of the accomplished Vidyādhara will occur. [9] Oṃ mahākaruṇāmoghapāśa dṛḍhavajrādhiṣṭhita bhuru bhuru bhuvanavare svāhā. Samantamaṇḍala—

6. The purification of houses, groves, gardens, monasteries, hermitages, walking paths, caves, and forest retreats should be performed by sprinkling with water scented with sandalwood and mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited one hundred and eight times. This effects the complete purification of all great impurities present in every location. All malevolent Vināyakas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Bhūtas are driven away. This is the mantra for the purification of the site: [10] Oṃ padma, by means of the Amoghapāśa, may there be a boundary everywhere in the ten directions—

7. *Bandhaya turu turu hūṃ*. One should wrap five iron stakes, each measuring eight finger-breadths in length, with a thread of five colors. Having recited the mantra one thousand and eight times, they should be driven into the ground in the four directions, and the fifth should be driven into the center. A boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) extending for seven *yojanas* all around will be established. As long as the stake is not pulled out, that great boundary-binding will remain established. 7a. (P11b5, D.11b5)

1. [11] Oṃ amoghamaṇḍala bandhaya samante padmamahāpadme dhuru dhuru svāhā. Having recited this one hundred and eight times over scented water and mustard seeds, one should sprinkle them all around the mandala. Thus, the binding of the great mandala is performed below and above as well. All obstacles, Vināyakas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, and Piśācas shall be rendered unable to approach. Furthermore, whatever non-malignant beings there may be, or even malignant gods and Nāgas—all shall be rendered subject to the [power of the] mantra.

2. These will become entirely free from all worldly evil deeds, evil mantras, and evil actions of sentient beings. Oṃ amoghapariśuddhe śodhaya samantena dhiri dhiri śuddhasattvamahāpadme hūṃ. Having recited this over water consisting of the five products of a cow one thousand and eight times, [one should sprinkle it] upon the entire ground area, whether in a maṇḍala, a monastery, a forest hermitage, a cave, a thicket, a walking path, a grove, a glade, or a garden.

3. One should consecrate oneself in a dwelling, a shelter, or a house of Rāma. All those who are impure—whether among the pure or the impure—including those covered in mud and excrement, as well as the impure bhūtas, piśācas, pretas, and others, and the outcastes (mātaṅgas), shall be completely excluded. One becomes pure and thoroughly cleansed; one becomes a pure locus. By consecrating oneself, there will be purification from all that was poorly eaten, poorly traversed, ill-placed, ill-beheld, or [worn as] poor dwellings and poor garments.

4. They will become pure and clean; they will become clean even amidst the impure. One who does not practice celibacy becomes a practitioner of celibacy; one who does not observe the fast becomes an observer of the fast. All deities will provide for his protection, defense, and guardianship. Īśvara, Maheśvara, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and the others will always be mindful of him for the sake of protection, defense, and guardianship. All the world—

5. He will become beloved and worthy of honor, and his words will be authoritative. He will be free from all diseases and completely liberated from all evil obstructions, defilements, and the like. One should consecrate him on all sides in the four directions; [thereby] all strife, quarrels, conflicts, disputes, famine, death, calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions are pacified day by day, and he himself—

6. One should sprinkle [the site]; whatever is to be touched shall become successful through the ritual actions of the Mahāvidyā-mudrā-maṇḍala-paṭala. One obtains the unfailing great accomplishment (*amogha-mahāsiddhi*). Wherever one goes, there one becomes greatly honored. Everywhere one’s movement shall be unimpeded. Day by day one sees great dreams of various and most wonderful celestial palaces (*vimāna*). Everywhere one obtains vast boons. All śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas—

Brahmins, kṣatriyas, and householders, along with kings, ministers, and the retinues of the inner apartments, will come under his control. He will become worthy of great veneration; he will be eternally pure, clean, and purified in his conduct. He will always have the desire to behold the noble Avalokiteśvara at all times, and [the deities] will grant him the boons of all his desires. And he will [behold] the Tathāgata, the noble Amitābha, at all times.

1. One sees the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, in a vision in a dream; having passed away, one is reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī. [13] Oṃ padme sara sara tiṣṭha tiṣṭha mahāmoghasamaya svāhā. This is the mantra of the Great Secret Samaya. [14] Oṃ vipulapadmāmogha prasara praviśatu kuru kuru svāhā. This is the mantra for entering. [15] Oṃ amogha anuśaya mahāpadmabandhure hūṃ. This is the mantra for the disciple. [16] Oṃ amoghapadmaśikhe.

2. *Turu turu tiṣṭha vajrabandhe svāhā*. This is the mantra for binding the topknot (*śikhābandhana*). It should be recited twenty-one times. [17] *Oṃ amoghapadmajalotkṣepa bhiri bhiri hūṃ*. This is the mantra for sprinkling water (*jalotkṣepaṇa*). It should be recited twenty-one times. [18] *Oṃ amoghavikaṭa sambhara padmāsane jalavati kuru kuru hūṃ*. This is the mantra for the flask (*kalaśa*). It should be recited one hundred and eight times. [19] *Oṃ padmaprasare amoghavimale bhara bhara svāhā*. This is the mantra for holding the water (*udakadhāraṇa*).

3. By reciting the mantra twenty-one times: *Oṃ amoghapadme supadme pūrṇakare viri viri vimale svāhā*. Having recited this hand-mantra (*karamantra*) one thousand and eight times over the two hands, one should perform all the rites of the maṇḍala mantras, mudrās, rituals, and sādhanas. It should be accomplished in all sādhanas; it is to be performed everywhere in all rites. [21] *Oṃ amogha vimale jihvāgraṃ saṃsodhani padmako-*

4. *Malajihvā saṃśodhaya dhara dhara suvimale svāhā*. This is the mantra for purifying the tongue. Having recited it over scented water one thousand and eight times, one should rinse the mouth; the impurities of the tongue will be completely purified. One’s tongue will become like the delicate petals of a lotus or a water lily. There will be complete purification of the teeth, palate, and throat. [22] *Oṃ amogha gandhavati suru suru prabhuru divyagandhiḥ padmaprabhe svāhā*. With this mantra, the mouth is purified.

5. For the pill (*guḍikā*), one should take sandalwood, *nalada*, *spṛka*, blue lotus (*utpala*), saffron (*kuṅkuma*), and musk (*kāstūrika*) as an enhancer; having made them into a fine powder, one should form a pill the size of a seed of the *akṣa* fruit. Having recited the mantra eight thousand times, one should place it in a copper casket. At the time of recitation, one should apply [the powder] to the mouth and hold the vessel for a short while (*muhūrta*). One’s mouth will constantly emit the fragrance of a blue lotus. Without a doubt, for a distance of one *krośa*, people will be pleased.

All the Tathāgatas and likewise all the Bodhisattvas will be supremely pleased with the noble Avalokiteśvara. The recitation of the Amoghapāśa Vidyā indeed brings about success with ease. This unsurpassed Vidyā always addresses the Vidyādhara; it is free from foul odors, and bile, phlegm, as well as nasal mucus—all these shall quickly perish, and his mouth shall become divine. Whomever he addresses with his voice, that person shall quickly come under his control.

7. Those deities remain under one's control: Indra, the Lord of Śacī, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, the four world-protectors (lokapālas), as well as Soma and Bhāskara—all remain under one's control. By means of this Sudhāraṇā [dhāraṇī] of Sarasvatī, it enters the tip of the tongue; one will become possessed of clear speech and will always have the voice of a kiṃnara. One who recites a thousand verses, free from the defects of impurity, [will attain] what was previously studied. 8a. (P13a8, D.13b3)

1. What was previously studied will not be lost. By the syllable *hūṃ*, all deities come, as do those gods who dwell within the maṇḍala. By the syllable *sphṭa*, evil obstructors, Vināyakas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Pretas, Apasmāras, Bhūtas, and Guhyakas are destroyed; in an instant, they all flee or fall headlong. By holding a medicinal pellet (guḍikā) in his mouth at all times, the wise man quickly attains all accomplishments and shall become long-lived. [It is] smooth, sweet, and soft—

2. By holding this pill (*guḍikā*), one will become eloquent. This is the accomplishment of the pill named *Amoghapadmavimala* (The Stainless Lotus of Unfailing Success). Oṃ malavigate padmavivare sañcara cacare svari hūṃ // Amoghasiddhe śodhaya hūṃ // One should prepare this fine powder from equal parts of *nāgapuṣpa* (Nagakesara), *tvaca* (Cinnamon bark), *uśīra* (Vetiver root), *candana* (Sandalwood), *padmakeśara* (Lotus filament), *lavaṅga* (Cloves), *kākolaka* (Black cardamom), *gandhamāṃsī* (Spikenard), *tagara* (Tabernaemontana), *kuṅkuma* (Saffron), *prapuṇḍarīka* (White lotus), *elā* (Cardamom), and *sāmaka*. This should be made into a subtle [powder].

Having ground [the substance] and mixed it with divine water, one who has bathed well, being pure, clean, and confident, should bathe [the person] while reciting the mantra eight thousand times. One should mix it with warm water; having bathed, even one who has committed most terrible past deeds is liberated. This is proven to remove all diseases and destroy all ailments. One is freed from terrible afflictions, and it dispels the darkness of passion, hatred, and delusion. All impurities are pacified today through this bath.

4. Merely by drinking it, there is no doubt: one blazes with divine splendor, and the heap of merit increases. A mass of radiance blazes eternally, shining forth like the sun. The body becomes divine; the impure body shall become pure. The impure becomes pure; the non-celibate becomes truly celibate, and the non-silent becomes silent. Even one who is not a student of sacred knowledge becomes a student of sacred knowledge, and an old man becomes youthful.

It shall be free from disease; health will be constant, and a divine fragrance will be emitted from the body. Former odors will be dispelled for the distance of an arrow’s length, without a doubt. The body will possess the scent of divine sandalwood, as delicate as the *kumuda* and *padma* lotuses. One will always sleep in comfort and awaken in comfort. It will be unassailable by all the wicked—yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, asuras, and malevolent vināyakas—and no obstacles or enemies shall arise.

6. One should certainly not perform the practice of recitation (*jāpa-sādhana*) as a harsh purification of the body, because it is accomplished through well-performed ritual action. It is successfully achieved in reality; all the Victors and likewise all the Bodhisattvas immediately behold [the practitioner]. All the deities and whoever else dwells within the mandala quickly approach. Amoghasiddhi is eternally present, according to one's desire as it occurs in the mind. Having performed the procedure for the purification of the body at the end, [one proceeds with] the previous mantra—

7. "Perform the ritual action. [24] Oṃ amoghapadmalocane divyadṛṣ� real purity! Suru suru lotus-eyed one! Bhuru bhuru all-observing one! Svāhā! One should prepare this wick from manaḥśilā, rocanā, sea-foam, sahaja, and blue lotus, mixed with honey. While reciting the mantra three thousand times, eight times over, this divine eye-salve is said to be proclaimed by the Tathāgatas; it is praised in the world by Lokeśvara. 8b (P14a5, D.14b2)

1. This praise is proclaimed: one sees all auspicious dreams and does not see diseases or the like; one never sees anything unpleasant, nor ever sees evil sights or wrong views. Fierce hunters, *caṇḍālas*, those who are impure, those who have transgressed against what is impure, those who eat forbidden food, and those with foul shadows—*yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, and *pannagas*—all become invisible by day and night; of this there is no doubt. With divine eyes one sees, and one sees divine dreams for as long as one month.

2. By this, one will possess divine vision; it is a purifier of the eyes. Oṃ budhya budhya vibudhya padmāmoghamukhi vara vara varasu svāhā. Having recited this vidyā over cow bezoar (gorocana) one thousand and eight times, having recited the Amogharāja mantra twenty-one times, having recited the Krodharāja mantra seven times, and having recited the heart-mantra and sub-heart-mantra one hundred and eight times—at the time of recitation, one should also [use] this:

3. Taking a tuft of wool, make a *tilaka* once. Having made the *tilaka*, it remains upon the forehead in the shape of a star. All malevolent beings remain brought under control. Yakṣas, bhūtas, and those who are rākṣasas, as well as obstacles (*vighna*) and impediments (*vināyaka*), all perish; of this there is no doubt. It is not possible for them to withstand it again, whether they be evil beings or even evil spirits; they all go to destruction like moths in a fire. Kings shall be brought under control.

4. Those people, together with their retinues, ministers, and domestic priests, along with the groups of women in the inner apartments—all shall remain under his control. The śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and even the śūdras—all shall go forth as subjects under his power; he will become one worthy of great honor. All the vidyā-deities who dwell within this maṇḍala shall all observe and protect their pledge (samaya), providing protection throughout the ten directions.

5. They will indeed always attain unsurpassed accomplishment. One who applies this *tilaka* while traveling through a caravan in distress will undoubtedly overcome all fears whatsoever: thieves, robbers, and soldiers; even battles and wars; lions, tigers, hyenas, and fierce, terrible elephants; jackals, venomous creatures, and all serpents, including those with poisonous fangs and *goṇāsas*; and whatever others there may be.

6. All those village-dwelling spirits will disappear and shall never again have power. Famine, fire, drought, and terrible calamities arising from weapons, water, sorcery (*kākhorda*), and the ruin of homes—these shall not affect the body. Whether it be a mole, a birthmark, or a pimple, all these afflictions shall be cured by the wise Vidyādharas; they will be clearly manifested and successfully pacified. There is no doubt in this matter. O Blessed One, by the mere recollection of me, the *Amogharājahṛdaya*, one will remember the Vidyādhara; then—

7. "In an instant, O Blessed One, I shall appear before the vidyādhara; I shall fulfill all his desires, I shall grant all boons as they have been described, I shall accomplish all his tasks, and I shall bestow the attainment of Amoghasiddhi. With my vow of truth, I shall maintain the samaya. By the empowerment of the Tathāgata and authorized by the word of the Tathāgata, O Blessed One, I shall do all that.

1. I shall bestow [this] upon them, provided that the Vidyādharas perform the ritual accomplishments (*sādhana*) according to the prescribed manual (*kalpa*). O Blessed One, if the *dhiṇi*-mudrās are set in motion, then by means of this mudrā being employed, one will become endowed with a great mass of merit; one will be empowered by the prophecies of all Bodhisattvas; one will be protected by all the deities; one will be uniquely honored by the whole world; one will be the sole object of veneration for all sentient beings; and [one will master] the chapter on the manuals of all maṇḍalas and mudrās...

2. He will have entered the samaya; he will have immeasurable life; he will be a vidyādhara of Amoghasiddhi; his speech will be authoritative; he will possess mindfulness, intelligence, and confidence; his intellect will be unimpeded; he will be a granter of boons by the noble Avalokiteśvara; there will be a constant desire to see him; and he will constantly be a bestower of boons; [he will be] always [victorious over] all enemies and adversaries—

3. He shall be victorious over all enemies and all who are wicked or malicious. He shall be ever victorious everywhere. He shall become invisible to all yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, vighnas, vināyakas, asuras, and nāgas. He shall be entirely fearless among all noble beings. All kings, royal ministers, and their retinues including the ladies of the inner court shall remain under his control. He shall possess a single form everywhere; he shall possess a single [voice] everywhere.

4. He will become one who stands firm; he will be long-lived and liberated from all diseases. He will be free from all faults, impurities, stinginess, and envy. He will possess excellent mindfulness and a perfectly pure body. At the time of death, he obtains a vision of the Great Tathāgata, and Āryāvalokiteśvara grants him a vision. They all encourage him, saying: "Come, my son, to the world of Sukhāvatī."

5. Following the element (dhātu), he will pass away with well-established mindfulness; all the gates to the hells will be closed for him, and he will be liberated from going to any state of woe. This will be his final birth from a womb. He will constantly possess the recollection of his births in every life. Everywhere he will be born spontaneously from lotuses. He will travel from buddha-field to buddha-field until he reaches the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍala).

6. Regarding the phrase "from wearing": Now I shall proclaim the insignia-seal (*cihnamudrā*) fashioned by Lokeśvara. Whether it be a drawing on all sides of a mandala or simply a hand-held weapon, by the mere sight of which there will be joy and satisfaction; one is liberated from all sins and attains accomplishment (*siddhi*) in reality. By this, one will always be armored and perpetually clad in mail; one is eternally armored in the blazing Dharma and is forever resplendent.

7. It shall be so. The accomplishment of all rites and the supreme accomplishment of all mantras are attained. By the mere drawing of the mudrā-maṇḍala, the yakṣas and rākṣasas flee, and all seizing spirits (*graha*) perish; this is certain upon merely seeing it. One is liberated from all afflictions and all diseases, even those that have arrived there. It is invincible against all enemies, whether in the enemy’s army or one’s own army; it constantly brings victory and is auspicious. It is a constant destroyer of demons and a source of perpetual accomplishment.

1. It becomes the supreme [attainment]. For the sake of the happiness of the Vidyādharas, accomplishment occurs in accordance with reality. Regarding the mudrā of the noble Avalokiteśvara, as well as his insignia and weapons—all activities that are appropriate, wherever they are employed, there the mudrās are formed. That which is called the "Blossoming Lotus" (*padmavikasita*) and that which is adorned with lotus petals—according to the ritual manual (*kalpa*), all of them should be made surrounded by a garland of flames; all of them are mudrās of life. All of them...

2.
