Hereafter, I shall explain the Amoghamudrā, which brings accomplishment and is for the benefit of all beings; indeed, the Amoghamudrā is preeminent. Having formed the Vajra-añjali gesture with the fingers joined at their middles, the little fingers and thumbs extended, and the index fingers slightly bent—this is proclaimed as the Mahāmoghā Viśvarāja Padmamudrā. This is the Mudrā of All Actions (*sarvakarmika*), well-suited for all rites. Enter the mudrā thus described! Sa-...

2. This is the supreme *Ratnamaṇḍala*. As soon as this supreme seal (*mudrā*) and mantra are grasped, the *Vidyādharas* who provide protection indeed enter the supreme liberation-maṇḍala that follows the three times; thus, the highest accomplishment (*paramasiddhi*) will arise. [92] Oṃ vajre vajrādhiṣṭhitapadme viśvarūpadhare dhara dhara hūṃ praviśatu stri(strya)dhvagatāṃ dhiri tuṭi svāhā. When this seal is grasped, the Buddha-fields of the ten directions are desired for the sake of the accomplishment of reality (*tattvasiddhi*); of this there is no doubt. The lotus blazes—

3. There will be great joy for the body and hands; indeed, with a face constantly smiling, the sight of the Vidyādhara stands before him. The gates of the heavenly realms of the Buddha-fields are opened on all sides. In the thirty-two abodes, the gods remain with their gates unbarred; in the thirty-three abodes, they all remain with their gates unbarred; the gates of the Sukhāvatī world-system remain unbarred, as do all the abodes.

4. By the mere grasping of this mudrā, one enters [the state of liberation]. This mudrā removes all sins, utterly consumes all afflictions (*kleśa*), liberates one from all suffering, and destroys all transgressions. Merely by the performance of the mudrā, one is freed from the sixteen hells and the eight terrifying fears; all misdeeds perish, the gates to hell are closed, and one has crossed over those terrifying fears. Indeed, by the mere sight of this mudrā, one becomes a *vidyādhara*.

5. "They shall be liberated from all evils, even those committed as the five acts of immediate retribution; they shall always be beloved by all sentient beings, for they are indeed empowered by all the Tathāgatas. This very mudrā is formed by curling the tips of the thumbs and holding them at the tips [of the fingers], placing the middle fingers in the form of a lotus bud (*jaṭā*) upon the crown of the head; this is the *Padmajaṭā* mudrā. It is renowned as the *Amoghahasta*. Reciting the mantra for it for the benefit of all sentient beings: OṂ AMOGHAPADMAJALE.

6. *Viśodhaya hūṃ viri viri vimale svāhā*. Having placed [the hand] upon the head with the mudrās, one should bathe [the disciple] with the auspicious *dhāraṇī*. When the mantra has been recited one hundred and eight times, by the mere act of bathing, those skilled in mudrās and mantras attain purification from impurity; thus indeed is impurity purified. Through these [mudrās], even those who do not practice celibacy become celibate, and those who are not silent become silent. A divine mass of merit blazes forth, resplendent like the sun and moon. He—

7. He is eternally beloved by the world; there is unsurpassed accomplishment of the mantra. Indeed, through the reality of the Amoghasiddhi [mantra], one attains the accomplishment of the Amoghapāśa. All deities come for the sake of protection—of this there is no doubt. The Noble Lord Avalokiteśvara is the bestower of boons upon pure beings; he always grants boons everywhere and appears day after day. There is constant freedom from disease and words [of health], as well as contentment and nourishment. Every rite is accomplished everywhere, and one is liberated from all diseases.

1. It is said: "This wonderful bath, which liberates one from all obscurations and is the supreme of all auspicious things, is indeed the unsurpassed Amogha-bath. Firmly joining the two hands, one should bring the jewel and lotus [mudrās] together; with the two index fingers slightly contracted and all [fingers] evenly composed, this is the Samādhi-mudrā. Having assumed the cross-legged posture (paryaṅka), one should sit. When this mudrā is employed while reciting the mantra with a concentrated mind, by its mere grasping, one becomes equal to Mount Meru in the cross-legged posture.

2. Encircled on all sides and invisible to all obstructors and Vināyakas—whether Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Asuras, or Garuḍas—all of them flee far away to the cardinal and intermediate directions. Without obstacle, the rite of the reciter succeeds; there is no doubt. [94] *Oṃ amoghavajradṛḍhapadmeśvara hūṃ*. Having formed the *samāñjali* mudrā, the two index fingers are pressed against the middle fingers; the forefingers are white, and the thumbs are at the tips of the lotus petals.

3. The mudrā of Amogheśvararāja: One should perform the mantra-mudrā in the presence of the noble Avalokiteśvara. *Oṃ padmeśvara amoghavarada bhiri bhiri svāhā.* First, one should recite this twenty-one times. Then, while binding the mudrās, one should recite the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa with a single-pointed mind and an intention directed toward reality (*tattva*). By merely reciting it once, the three times (*tryadhvan*) that have always followed her are shaken.

4. Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as numerous as the sands of hundreds of thousands of millions of Ganges rivers, will grant their approval to that vidyādhara; they will comfort him and shower that vidyādhara with various rays of light. As soon as he calls to mind the Noble Lord Avalokiteśvara, the latter appears before him. Then, by the mere act of grasping [the mantra], the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) are fulfilled.

He becomes endowed with the ten perfections; he becomes endowed with the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; he becomes endowed with the ten powers of a Tathāgata; he attains the four grounds of self-confidence; and he attains the complete purity of the noble eightfold path. By the mere grasping of this seal and by the mere recollection of the Amogharāja-hṛdaya, one obtains these great benefits and praises of virtue.

By reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times and performing one hundred and eight mudrās, through a single fast and recitation, Noble Avalokiteśvara will appear before the vidyādhara in his own natural form and grant him his approval, saying: "Excellent, excellent, O vidyādhara! This is the supreme recitation. Extending his right arm, he places his hand upon the head of the vidyādhara and comforts him, saying: "Come, my son; choose a boon for whatever purpose you desire."

"I give [it] to you. Having been thus favored and empowered, he said: "May you become my eldest son among the Vidyādharas! "O accomplished Vidyādhara, may you remain steadfast through the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, the *Vimokṣamaṇḍala*, the *Mudrāpaṭala*, and the *Kalparāja*! With a mind of great compassion, act for the sake of all sentient beings! This is your final dwelling in a womb; upon passing away from here, you shall go to the world-system of Sukhāvatī and be born spontaneously within lotuses."

Adorned with all the major marks and minor signs, he shall possess an immeasurable lifespan until the very end at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍala*). Therefore, by reciting [the mantra] one thousand and eight times and performing one hundred and eight mudrās, when the one thousand and eight [recitations] are completed from a state of non-attachment, he arrives through the sky. He will become a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) of the pure maṇḍala of unfailing miraculous transformations, [surrounded by] eighteen *koṭis* of vidyādharas...

2. He will have a retinue of one hundred thousand niyutas; his lifespan will be immeasurable; and he will exercise the supernatural power named Mahāmogha-vipula-prabhāsa. By the majesty of that supernatural power, he travels through the triple-thousand great-thousand world-system merely by the slight movement of bending and extending his arm. When the mantra is recited one hundred thousand times, one hundred thousand mudrās are set in motion; by this, even in this very life, [one attains the state of] Noble Avalokiteśvara.

3. He becomes like nectar; through the illusion-like samādhi, he performs transformations and attains the divine, unerring, and utterly pure eye. He displays various forms, such as those of Īśvara, Maheśvara, Brahmā, the sons of the gods, Rudra, Vāsava, Soma, Āditya, Kumāra, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and so forth, even displaying the forms of various nāga kings. In whatever way the discipline of sentient beings requires, in that very way does he manifest his form.

4. He shows this: through one hundred thousand recitations as a worldly means, by means of one hundred thousand supramundane recitations, he sees all the buddha-fields in the ten directions and beholds all the Tathāgatas face to face. He receives the prophecy from all the Tathāgatas and will be empowered with the empowerment of non-retrogression, until the very end at the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍala). [This is] held by means of the mudrā.

5. Seated in the full lotus posture, with a mind characterized by compassion for all beings and consisting of loving-kindness (*maitrī*) and mercy (*karuṇā*), one shall recite the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* mantra even once. At the very moment of that recitation, it becomes as if eighty-eight recitations have been performed; all the Tathāgatas will grant their consolation and infuse one's body with mindfulness, intelligence, and vigor. By the mere recitation of the *padya*, the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*)—

6. There will be no enemies for him, and from that cloth-painting of Duṣyapa, rays of light will issue forth. They will grant him a vision of the noble Avalokiteśvara in his perfectly pure form in a dream. They will bestow all boons upon him. All his karmic obstructions will become purified; all his sinful obstructions will go to their complete exhaustion and total disappearance. All diseases and all worldly affairs—

7. Through these means, supreme accomplishment will arise. One should cultivate the recollection of the Buddha (*buddhānusmṛti*). Having firmly joined the palms in the *samāja* gesture, the tips of the fingers are slightly curved and placed at the mouth; the little fingers are spread apart, while the middle fingers resemble a lotus. Recite this mantra: [96] *oṃ turu turu padme amoghasiddhiṃ hūṃ*. This *amoghasiddhi* mudrā brings accomplishment in all rites. While this is being performed— 14b (P23a3, D.24a4)

One who knows all attains success quickly; one will swiftly be granted a vision. He sets in motion the supreme boon, the unfailing success that is most difficult to obtain, both mundane and supramundane. Indeed, one is liberated from all evil, and a mass of merit increases eternally; auspicious sounds resound constantly, and the gods always provide protection. One should always maintain the vajra-bind, the firm bind, and a steadfast mind. Extending the heart [hand] while curling the index finger, with the unfailing lotus—

2. The heart-mantra of the Padmamaṇḍala-mudrā is known as Padmeśvara; this mudrā accomplishes all ritual purposes. Having uttered this mantra, one should then utter the Amogharāja: Oṃ amoghahṛdayapadme dhara dhara padmadhara mahāmaṇḍalahṛdaya hūṃ. This mudrā is set forth as the heart of the Holder of the Lotus (Padmadhara). Indeed, the accomplishment of the Amogha-heart is the very reality; there is no doubt about it. Everywhere, all rites are accomplished; there is no hesitation in this regard.

3. One should guard the secret mudrā through the recitation of the well-guarded mantra. You should maintain a state of being well-bathed, wearing clean garments, and possessing a pure mind; you should be one who has become compassionate toward all sentient beings. Always be devoted to the Guru. Constantly intent on faith, remain ever delighted in Padmapāṇi. Thus, rites will be swiftly accomplished; one will swiftly attain Buddhahood; one will swiftly obtain Lokeśvara; and one will swiftly come to be endowed with the welfare of all sentient beings.

4. Having extended the left arm just so far, [the hand] is positioned in the shape of a lotus from the mouth. Turning the hands upward, one should bend the ring finger and the thumb, and extend the right arm. Contracting the fingers into the shape of a lotus mandala, with the thumb and middle finger joined, he is Mahāmoghaśāntanetra, possessing a mind of loving-kindness (*maitrī*) and a nature of compassion (*karuṇā*) for all sentient beings. He uttered this mantra:

5. Haraḥ. Oṃ! You who hold the noose of Paśupati, whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of rays, O attractor, awakener, perfect awakener, bhuru bhuru, you who have accomplished the Amoghapāśa, hūṃ! These mudrās and mantras should be recited twenty-one times. Then, while reciting the Heart of Amoghapāśa, one should cast the hand-gesture (mudrā) of the noose from the right hand, and again hold it in its proper place seven times.

One should recite this seven times and cast it [into the fire]. One who possesses a pure intention should recite the *Amogharāja* [sūtra]; by the mere act of reciting it, the great seal of the unfailing noose (*pāśamudrāmahāmogha*) which attracts all the sources of awakening (*bodhyākarṣaṇa*) brings about the state of Buddhahood immediately. Whatever other various tasks one contemplates in the mind, they are all immediately attracted; there is immediate, unsurpassed accomplishment (*anuttarasiddhi*). Devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, and kinnaras—

7. All the Rāma-horagas shall immediately come into the sight of the vidyādhara; all the Buddhas in the ten directions will look upon him and grant their vision in reality. The bodhisattvas will assemble for the purpose of paying homage to the vidyādhara, and the noble Lord Avalokiteśvara, the Bestower of Boons, will place his hand upon the head of the vidyādhara. With a completely purified body, he will immediately grant his vision, even if [the practitioner] has fallen into the Vīci hell.

1. Those beings who have committed the five acts of immediate retribution, those who revile the noble ones, and those who reject the true Dharma—even they, upon seeing this mudrā and through its application and so forth, instantly purify all their evils. By the mere sight of it, the Leader will immediately grant [his presence], and all activities shall be accomplished by the mere grasping of the mudrā. This mere sight of the mudrā, while the mantra is being employed, is equal to the sight of a Vidyādhara; one beholds the face of the noble Avalokiteśvara.

2. One should not look [at it]. The obscurations of sinful karma accumulated over hundreds of thousands of successive births—all this is purified by the mere sight of grasping the seal (*mudrā*); there is no doubt in this matter. The wise one, having firmly joined the fingers in the shape of a lotus, making the index fingers like jewels, slightly bending the middle fingers, and raising the arms high with the tips of the great *cintāmaṇi* banners, should place the consecration upon the head while reciting this mantra: [99] *oṃ stryadhvānuga-*

3. May they consecrate [you] with all the consecrations of the three times: *Padmamaṇi Supadme Amoghe Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhite Hūṃ*. By this mere consecration, the Vidyādhara shall be consecrated by all the Tathāgatas; he shall receive the hand-consecration of the Noble Avalokiteśvara; he shall become a Great King of Vidyādharas; he shall attain the accomplishment of all vidyās; and he shall be purified of all afflictions and obscurations.

4. "He shall become wise; he shall become the sole preeminent one in all the world, standing above all. Having extended the head of the *vajrapadmabandha* from the crown of the head, with the tips of the fingers always [joined], the index finger in the shape of a hook, and the face itself with a frowning expression—this is the mudrā of the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*), which accomplishes all rites. This mudrā brings about all attainments (*siddhi*) and is the supreme means for all practices. Recalling this mantra, it is the supreme means for all practices: [100] Oṃ krodharājamahāmo-

5. *Gha hana hana sarvaduṣṭāṃ hūṃ*. This is the mudrā merely by being brought to mind. It possesses the great power of mantra; all the wicked are indeed shattered, even Mount Sumeru would crumble. When this mudrā is grasped, all evil beings, wicked nāgas, and wicked obstructing spirits (*vighna*) and leaders (*vināyaka*)—all of them are pacified merely by grasping the mudrā; they all remain under one's control, including gods and humans.

6. Śramaṇas, Brāhmaṇas, Śūdras, and Kṣatriyas alike—everyone is always under her control; she remains present here as "This One. Always composed, having joined [the hands] with the thumbs level and the middle fingers likewise raised, one should slightly bend them upward. This is the supreme mudrā of the goddess Mahāpadmatārā; it brings about unsurpassed accomplishment everywhere. Having formed a bud-like lotus with the other [fingers], one should extend the thumbs and slightly bend only the little fingers; this is Mahāśvetā.

7. The divine seal (*mudrā*) is the supreme accomplishment of all attainments (*sarvasiddhi*). Having formed the *vajrākāra* [gesture] with the left hand, one should encircle it with the right hand in a firm bond; the face should likewise be knit in a frown (*bhṛkuṭī*). This is the Great Frowning Seal (*Bhṛkuṭā-mahāmudrā*), which bestows all desires. Having extended both hands in the gesture of reverent salutation (*añjali*), one should extend the middle fingers and bend them inward between the palms. Then, extending the little fingers, one should form the shape of a chain (*śaṅkalī*) and a lotus (*padma*), placing it at the location of the heart. This is the seal (Mudrā 15b).

1. This *mahāmudrā* shall be employed for all the deities dwelling within the maṇḍala; all the deities of the maṇḍala will be satisfied. All will arrive with equal impartiality and all will provide protection—of this there is no doubt. And this *mudrā* is proclaimed as that of the *dūtīs* and *yakṣiṇīs*: having extended the hands in the gesture of reverent salutation (*añjali*) with the palms facing like a lotus, one places them at the position of the heart. Having firmly bound the *vajramuṣṭi*, one bends the middle fingers, while the remaining [fingers] and the thumbs—

2. For the sake of welfare, this lotus-shaped seal is prescribed for the face. This seal, beginning with the seven stars, grants supreme accomplishment everywhere. All evils are dispersed; all afflictions and all diseases are destroyed—of this there is no doubt. It is successful in all rituals and is the supreme Amoghasiddhi. Placing both hands level, one should form the lotus gesture in the shape of a vajra; by bending the index fingers and pressing the thumbs against the eldest fingers (the little fingers), this is the Hayagrīva seal, the best among all mantras.

3. Having formed the *añjali* in the shape of a lotus, one should join the two index fingers at the middle joints; then, extending one of the middle fingers like a hook (*kuśa*), this is the *Amoghapāśa* mudrā. This indeed is the *Vaḍavāmukha*; it was spoken by Vajra as that which accomplishes all rites and bestows all unsurpassed attainments. This mudrā consists of the index and thumb joined together, while the remaining fingers are contracted into the shape of a lotus and placed at the heart; this is the *Nīlakaṇṭha* [mudrā].

4. The Mudrās for those skilled in all ritual manuals (*kalpa*): Placing the two hands in the lotus-fist (*padmamuṣṭi*) gesture, with the left and right hands positioned [so], one should maintain a gentle facial expression. With eyes directed toward loving-kindness (*maitrī*), this eleven-faced mudrā is unimpeded everywhere. Likewise, with the thumbs level and the tips of the fingers slightly contracted, the two index fingers formed in the shape of a lotus—this is the *Īśvarā* mudrā, which pierces through [all obstacles]. This same mudrā, when the middle fingers are bent into the shape of a crescent moon, is [the next].

5. Extending the left index finger is the *Maheśvara-mudrā*, which reveals all spirits (*bhūta*). Having firmly joined the two hands in the *śaṅkalī* [fist] gesture, extend them; then, placing them again at the heart, this is always the *Yama-mudrā*. Extending the left hand, one should bend the fingers slightly upward; keeping the right hand at the heart, one should cross and bend the thumb (*jyeṣṭhāṅguli*); extending the remaining fingers, this is the *Varuṇa-mahāmudrā*, [which subdues] all *nāgas*.

6. The Lord’s Ploughing [Mudrā]. Firmly joining the two hands and curling the fingers in opposite directions, one should place the right and left thumbs tucked into the hollow of the heart. This is the mudrā called Kuberaka; it shatters all yakṣas. The right hand is raised with the index and thumb fingers bent inward; the left hand is extended with its fingers pointing upward. This is the Brahmānviṣa mudrā, which accomplishes all rites everywhere.

7. With this very same mudrā, bend the little finger of the right hand; this is the mudrā of the host of ṛṣis, which is honored by all the gods. Firmly binding both hands together, this is the Sudarśana wheel-mudrā; it is called the Viṣṇu-mudrā, which destroys all asuras. Make the right hand the shape of a citron and the left hand the form of a trident; bend the thumb and the little finger [of the right hand]; this mudrā is declared to be that of Rudra, which rends all bhūtas. [The right hand—] 16a (P.25b1, D.26b6)

1. Forming a fist with the left hand, extend the index finger; having bound the fist at the hip region, stand with the left leg extended. Always maintaining a fierce gaze, perform this mudrā called Kumāra; it is likewise the mudrā of Devasena-pati. Extending both hands upward, extend the three fingers; pressing the thumb with the index finger, this is the Āditya mudrā, which emits a thousand rays. This same mudrā, however, is formed by pressing two pairs of the three fingers together.

Extending [the hand] with the name of Soma, this mudrā is resplendent with a host of stars. In that regard, there are these great mantra-words, which accomplish the realization of the purpose of all activities, remove all sins, and destroy all afflictions; they serve for the purification of all obscurations, bring about the exhaustion of all karma, and achieve unfailing success as the accomplisher of unfailing actions: [101] Oṃ padmatāre turu turu hūṃ. [102] Oṃ mahāpadme.

3. *Śvetāṅge huru huru svāhā* // [103] *Oṃ bhṛkuṭi padme tara tara hūṃ* // [104] *Oṃ padme pāṇḍaravāsini kuṇḍa kuṇḍa svāhā* // [105] *Oṃ amoghapadmavarade sidhya sidhyatu hūṃ* // [106] *Oṃ sarvatra gāmini āvāhayaraudriṇi hūṃ* // [107] *Oṃ amoghinivāre tāraya padmabhuje hūṃ* // [108] *Oṃ dārutarulapadme amogha hūṃ* // [109] *Oṃ vaḍavāmukhe nikṛndaya duṣṭā hūṃ* // [110] *Oṃ padme*...

4. *Nilakaṇṭheśvara* bhuru bhuru hūṃ // [111] *Oṃ somyavadane prasīda śāsaya* hūṃ // [112] *Oṃ padmeśvari sādhaya* hūṃ // [113] *Oṃ amogheśvari* hūṃ // [114] *Oṃ samari tare tare* hūṃ // [115] *Oṃ nāgapadmani* hūṃ // [116] *Oṃ yakṣādhipati muru muru* hūṃ // [117] *Oṃ amoghe brahmārate* hūṃ // [118] *Oṃ ṛṣivarade amoghabhuje* hūṃ // [119] *Oṃ amoghaviṣṇurājapadmanābhe sarasamantabhu-*

5. *Je svāhā* // [120] *Oṃ rudra tuṭi mili svāhā* // [121] *Oṃ śaktidhare amoghavati svāhā* // [122] *Oṃ sahasrakiraṇe hūṃ turi svāhā* // [123] *Oṃ somaprabhe hūṃ* // The mudrās and mantras have been thus declared. O Vidyādhara, always accomplish each mudrā and each mantra separately. One should perform all activities as described without delay, being pure, clean in conduct, well-bathed, and wearing clean garments.

6. Ṇi Dhāraka: While anointing one’s arms and hands with fragrant perfumes and ointments, one should perform each mudrā one by one. As each mudrā is performed, and through the recollection of the mantras, these mudrās shall be performed hundreds of thousands of millions of times. While performing the mudrās, one will be endowed with a great mass of merit and will be empowered by the prophecy of all the bodhisattvas.

7. He will be protected by all the deities; he will be honored by all the world; he will become the sole teacher of all sentient beings; he will have entered the ritual manual (*kalpa*) chapter on the pledges (*samaya*) of all ornaments and mudrās; he will possess an immeasurable lifespan; he will be a Vidyādhara of unfailing accomplishment; his speech will be authoritative; he will be confident in his mindfulness and intelligence; and he will be unimpeded.

1. And his intellect shall be awakened; he shall become a granter of boons like the noble Avalokiteśvara; he shall always have a desire for [the vision of] the Noble One; and he shall always be a bestower of boons. He shall always be victorious over Śakra, adversaries, enemies, and all wicked and malicious beings. He shall always be a giver of victory everywhere. He shall be visible even to all yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, vighnas, vināyakas, asuras, and nāgas. All the noble ones and great...

2. He becomes autumnal [pure]. All kings, royal ministers, harems, and retinues will abide in peace under his influence; he will become one single form everywhere; and he will be the sole object of veneration for all. He will be long-lived, free from all diseases, and devoid of all faults, impurities, stinginess, and envy. His mindfulness will be excellent and his body perfectly pure. And at the time of death, there will be a vision of the Great Tathāgata.

He attains [this]. Then, Āryāvalokiteśvara will grant him a vision; he comforts them all, saying: "Come, my son, follow me to the world-system of Sukhāvatī. At the moment when mindfulness is well-established, he shall act, and the gates of all hells will be closed. He becomes liberated from going to all miserable destinies. This will be his final dwelling in a womb and his final birth; and always, regarding birth—

3. By recollecting [this], one attains [the following]: everywhere one will be born from spontaneously produced lotuses; one will proceed from buddha-field to buddha-field until reaching the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa).

Amoghapāśakalparāja – Part II 16b4 (P.26b3, D.28a3) 4. Now I shall explain the symbolic seals (*cihnamudrā*) emanated by Lokeśvara, as well as the hand-gestures (*hasta*) and weapons (*praharaṇa*) to be drawn all around the mandala; by the mere sight of which one will become joyful and satisfied, and be liberated from all sins.

5. From these, accomplishment (*siddhi*) arises in reality; by this, one will be eternally armored and always clad in mail. Being armored with the blazing Dharma, one shall be perpetually and constantly radiant. The supreme accomplishment of all ritual manuals (*kalpa*), the accomplishment of all mantras, and the written mudrās, maṇḍalas, and mantras—[before them] even the yakṣas, rākṣasas, and all seizing spirits (*graha*) flee; upon merely seeing [this], they perish, of this there is no doubt. One is liberated from all—

6. Whether against all diseases or even all illnesses; against all invincible enemies or the armies of others and one's own; it is always auspicious and brings victory. It is a destroyer of *rakṣas* at all times, and constant success shall arise. For the sake of the happiness of the *vidyādharas*, this supreme accomplishment truly occurs. The mudrā of the noble Avalokiteśvara, as well as his insignia and weapons—all these are appropriate wherever they are employed; in each such place, the mudrā becomes manifest.

7. And [the mudrā] called Padmavikaśitā, adorned with lotus petals—these should all be made surrounded by a garland of flames according to one's choice. All those mudrās consist of living beings; they are all bestowers of fruit. [They are]: Phalavajra, Triśūcīvajra, Tomaravajramaṇḍali, Padmavajra, Padmamālā, Vajrāṅkā, Padmapratiṣṭhita, and Padmaśvāsa. A lotus should always be on both sides, as well as the Padmasādhukāra and the Padmamuṣṭi. 17a (P.27a2, D.28b2)

1. Or the lotus-pointing gesture (*padmatarjanī*); the lotus-yawn (*padmavijṛmbha*), the lotus-hook (*padmāṅkuśa*), and the *añjali* [gesture]; and indeed the lotus-lattice (*padmapañjara*). The lotus-joint (*padmasaṃkalī*) always brings accomplishment; and the lotus-contemplation (*padmacintā*) is likewise always [efficacious]. [The mudrās] named Maṇipadmā and Suvajrā, as well as Amoghapadma; the lotus-bell (*padmaghaṇṭā*) and the lotus-sword (*padmakhadgā*). [The mudrās] called the trident (*tṛśūla*), the holding of the club (*musala*), the jewel-staff (*maṇidaṇḍa*), the flower-staff (*puṣpadaṇḍa*), and likewise the holder of the seven nooses (*saptapāsa*); the holding of the sea-monster (*makara*), the half-discus (*ardhacakra*), and the conch (*śaṅkha*). The citron (*bījapūra*) and the pomegranate (*sadāḍima*); the moon-holder (*candradhara*), and so forth.

2. [The deities] below that [are]: the one holding a mallet, the one with a tooth-stick, the one with a flower-basket, the one with a rosary, the one with a five-pronged [vajra], the one with the Amoghapāśa, and Amoghasiddhi. In all these cases, this lotus should be established [as their seat]. These hand-gestures (hasta-mudrās) should be depicted wherever they are prescribed. This is the forty-fourth mudrā for one who performs the drawing of the hands. They should be made with flames all around and adorned with jewel ornaments. Merely by seeing these on cloth or within a mandala, one should perform [the rite].

3. Whether on the wall of a rampart or anywhere else whatsoever, [this practice] always removes all sins merely by being seen. Those residing even in the Avīci hell, as well as those who have committed the five acts of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*), are all instantly and completely liberated; they are known as "pure beings" (*śuddhasattva*). They shall become non-retrogressive (*avaivarttika*) and established upon the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) of a bodhisattva. This state is irreversible through the vision of the Mudrā-maṇḍala of Noble Avalokiteśvara.

4. The Lord, the Giver of Boons, always holds his hand upon the head; he constantly shows his face directly before one, as the Lord of the World, the Giver of Boons. Whoever beholds this mudrā attains a state equal to that [of the Lord], and is even more distinguished. One who constantly recollects these thirty-five-word mantra will always attain all siddhis; such a person never goes to an evil rebirth. They shall quickly, very quickly, behold the maṇḍala of liberation and attain Buddhahood. He is the eldest son—Ami-...

There will be no doubt regarding his attainment; he shall be the eldest son of the Lord of the World, born from his very breast and from his mouth. Born of the Dharma through the Dharma, this leader has been prophesied. He will have planted roots of merit in the presence of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges. His merit will be immeasurable and incalculable in its transformation.

6. One attains the aggregate [of merit]. For whomsoever these words of the mudrā-mantra shall come into their hands, for them this great mudrā is proclaimed to have such vast benefits. In that regard, the mantras are as follows: [124] Oṃ amoghamañjalī mili cili hūṃ. [125] Oṃ āśvāsaya kṣaṇavigate hūṃ. [126] Oṃ abhayavarade tuṭi hūṃ. [127] Oṃ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhite bhiri bhiri hūṃ. [128] Oṃ padmahṛdayamuṣṭi hūṃ. [129] Oṃ visara visara sarvamalān tarjjaya hūṃ.

7. // [130] Oṃ vijṛmbha huru huru hūṃ // [131] Oṃ aṅkuśāmogha karṣaya hūṃ // [132] Oṃ kavacaya turu turu hūṃ // [133] Oṃ amoghasaṃkalī miri miri hūṃ // [134] Oṃ amoghacintāmaṇi tuṭi turu hūṃ // [135] Oṃ amoghamani ciri ciri hūṃ // [136] Oṃ vajra tuṭi cili hūṃ // [137] Oṃ amoghahṛdaya cara cara śuddhasatva hūṃ // [138] Oṃ ghoṣavati viṭi viṭi hūṃ // [139] Oṃ vidyākhadga cchindaya śatru hūṃ //

1. Oṃ tṛmalapariśuddhe bhiṭi hhiṭi hūṃ // [141] Oṃ suru suru hūṃ // [142] Oṃ maṇi maṇi hūṃ // [143] Oṃ puṣpavatijaye hūṃ // [144] Oṃ bodhicittapāśa dhara dhara hūṃ // [145] Oṃ padmapāśaviśuddhe hūṃ // [146] Oṃ vajrapāse bhavatu muru muru hūṃ // [147] Oṃ cintāmaṇipāsavarade hūṃ // [148] Oṃ cakrapāśāsuranirghātaka dhuru dhuru hūṃ // [149] Oṃ triśūlīpāśa vilokaya tāraya hūṃ // [150] Oṃ nāgapāśa //

2. Bind! Drag! O evil nāga-noose, strike! HŪṂ // [151] Oṃ, O you born from the water, rend, rend! HŪṂ // [152] Oṃ, O you of stainless moon, purify, O best of rays that dispel darkness! HŪṂ // [153] Oṃ, O Śrī, awaken! HŪṂ // [154] Oṃ, O supreme full victory! HŪṂ // [155] Oṃ, O you born from fruit, TURI! HŪṂ // [156] Oṃ, O perfect mandala, conquer! HŪṂ // [157] Oṃ, O you with a thousand rays of light! HŪṂ // [158] Oṃ, strike down and subdue all the wicked! HŪṂ // [159] Oṃ, O Mind, purify, O stainless one! HŪṂ // [160] Oṃ, O Puṣpavatī, well—

3. Oṃ gandhavare hūṃ // [161] Oṃ śatasahasraguṇite kṣaṇa kṣaṇa hūṃ // [162] Oṃ vajrotkṣepasūcīmukha ciṭi ciṭi hūṃ // [163] Oṃ amoghāpratihatapāśahaste hūṃ // [164] Oṃ sarvatrāmogha sidhya sidhya sādhaya hūṃ // These are likewise the hand-gestures (*mudrā*). Merely by performing the recitation once, and by the mere display of the gestures, all sins are instantly removed; one quickly attains Buddhahood. Quickly... śī-

4. One indeed meditates for an eon upon the Amoghapāśa-vimokṣa-maṇḍala for the sake of supreme accomplishment. In that regard, there are the weapon-mudrās: the jewel-gem, the flower, the lotus, the water-pot, the jewel-garland, the rosary, the conch, the wheel, the mace, the spear, the thunderbolt, the trident, the *pāṭṭisa* (javelin), the transverse thunderbolt-axe, the double-trident, the jewel-thunderbolt, the jewel-trident, the action-thunderbolt, the wish-fulfilling gem, and the staff with a blade and a hammer.

5. Maheśvara’s trident; sword and noose; goad and elephant; tree; coral; axe and discus; axe and mace; hand-flame; jewel-lamp; radiance; rays; pestle; blue lotus; axe and vessel; water-pot; stone; mountain; Meru; serpent-circle; parasol; banner; makara; fish; tortoise; *nandyāvarta*; knowledge-circle; knowledge-seal; trident-circle; sword; *kaṭṭā*—

6. Raka; Padmamālī; Tṛśūlākhya; Subhūṣuṇḍi; Bhiṇḍipāla; Daṃṣṭra; Caturmudra; Caturdaṃṣṭra; Gulaka; Śaṅkhacakra; Vajraśaṅkha; Tṛśūlākhyaśaṅkha; Maṇiśaṅkha; Padmaśaṅkha; Rudhā; Paṭala; Siṃhamukhī; Jīvaṃjīva; Kalaviṅka; Haṃsa; Sārasa; Krauñca; Mayūra; Yamadaṇḍa; Caturmukha; Caturmaṇḍalikā; Tṛśūlākhya; Pūrṇakumbha; Ardhacandra; Sūryamaṇḍala; Candraprabha.

7. The trident, the ocean, the flower-basket, the book, the deer-skin, the thunderbolt (*kulisa*), the chain (*śaṅkalī*), the adamantine chain (*vajraśaṅkalī*), the archway (*toraṇa*), the bowl, the robe, the water-strainer (*khakhoraka*), the bamboo stand (*vedikā*), the waist-band (*kāyabandhana*), the topknot (*cūḍa*), the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), the garland (*vaḍamāla*), and the triangle surrounded by vajras—these are the weapon-mudrās as described for the Leader of the Leaders of the World. This secret maṇḍala of liberation is known as the *Amoghapāśakalpa*.

Whether on cloth, on a leaf, on a wall, or wherever else it may be drawn—clearly defined, well-composed, and skilled in the application of colors—with all [deities] established upon lotuses, forming mudrās with universal flames; all those mudrās consist of life-force (*jīvamaya*), bestowing the accomplishment of all aims. They instantly remove sin and grant the fruit to those who possess them. All these are empowered by the leaders, the Lords of the World (*Lokeśvara*), and are empowered by all the Buddhas, the Śākya Kings, and the Tathāgatas. Therefore, with all effort—

2. By constantly upholding this, the wise one becomes beloved by the Buddhas; he is undoubtedly the eldest son. He who upholds this supreme chapter on mudrās—the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, the secret liberation-maṇḍala that is unsurpassed—will swiftly attain success through this supreme dhāraṇī, mudrā, and mantra. Now I shall proclaim the seven nooses (*pāśas*) in accordance with the various desired rites of the *Amogha* [sādhana], according to the ritual procedure as it is to be accomplished.

3. Just as the means are in reality, so all these [materials], each distinct and appropriate, should be understood according to their characteristics and according to the reality of the means. The five types of thread are established by the reality of the means for the noose: silk thread, lotus thread, sun-thread (arkasūtra), hemp thread, and bark thread. Having spun these threads, one should fashion the noose according to the ritual procedure for the means (*sādhanavidhi*). It is accomplished immediately by the mantra of seizing; there is no doubt in this matter.

4. From this [thread], one should always take a silk thread and cut it to the proper measure. Having fasted, wearing clean garments, well-bathed, and observing celibacy, and having eaten food that is "three-white" (tṛśukla) in a pure place, one should, with a mind of loving-kindness, briefly cause [the mantra] Amoghapāśahṛdaya to be recited. Then, having divided it into eight parts, one should weave it with great concentration. [The images of] the half-body of the King Amogha, with hands joined in *añjali* and holding a lotus, should be made.

5. That [image] should be well-finished, measuring four finger-breadths in height, adorned with a crown of matted hair (*jaṭāmakuṭa*) and decorated with all ornaments. Three types of forms should be made: the gentle form, the frowning-faced one, and the Wrathful King (*krodharāja*). It should be made of silver or gold. Then, a noose should be bound [to it], sixteen thousand *hasta* in length. On the second side of the face, a trident and a *sāmalaka* fruit should be bound. Then...

6. On the full moon or the eighth day of the lunar fortnight, the Vidyādhara, having fasted for a day and night, having bathed well and wearing clean garments, should sit cross-legged and perform worship to the Buddha according to the prescribed ritual. Remaining silent, he should recite [the mantra] one thousand and eight times over the noose (*pāśa*). Then, when the count is complete, he should prepare a divine seat one thousand and eight times, and place the noose upon it. He should consecrate it with the Amoghapāśa mudrā.

7. It should be said: "Divine worship is to be performed with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, cloth, and so forth. Incense of agaru, candana, and turuṣka is to be offered; lamps are to be offered. Then the vidyādhara, having recited the mantra over mustard seeds twenty-one times, should scatter them above the noose. The noble Avalokiteśvara is to be worshipped with a cloth painting (*duṣyapaṭa*), according to one's means and whatever is available. Then the vidyādhara [should perform] the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) of that noose... [18b] (P29b2, D.31a4)

1. Having performed the morning twilight worship while seated cross-legged with a composed mind, the recitation (*jāpa*) should be performed. Having recited over a single mustard seed, it should be thrown into the noose. This should be done daily until eight thousand are completed. The morning twilight recitation should be performed according to one's ability, and worship should be offered by one who avoids bad food. One must avoid what is left-over from others and what is not left-over; one should wear clean garments. When the eight thousand are complete, the noose blazes. If it is worldly—

2. Regarding accomplishment (*siddhi*): if it blazes with the color of fire, it is supramundane accomplishment (*lokottarasiddhi*). If it blazes in various colors, that body of unerring nature (*amoghaśarīra*) blazes and emits this sound: "Excellent, excellent, Vidyādhara! You have accomplished this supramundane noose of the thought of awakening (*bodhicittapāśa*), and you have drawn forth the unsurpassed thought of awakening. Having fulfilled the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*), you are included within the ten perfections. Therefore, this mundane means of accomplishment (*laukikasādhana*) shall become a wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇi*) that fulfills one's intentions according to how one thinks in the mind."

3. By the mere raising of the hands in prayer, everything is accomplished; everything is drawn in. Wherever one casts [the hands], one should recollect the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* seven times toward that direction; all intentions are fulfilled in an instant. Even if one has committed the five acts of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*) and is destined for the Avīci hell, it will clearly succeed for them. One should not give rise to doubt or uncertainty in this matter. Wherever one casts the face with a frown (*bhṛkuṭīmukha*), [there too it succeeds].

4. All those gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, being constantly drawn [by this], shall approach the presence of the vidyādhara; they will serve him as his slaves for as long as they live. All kings, along with their ministers and the retinues of their harems, shall stand [before him]. He will become one who is greatly honored by all the world. Whatever purpose he casts the noose for, that purpose of his shall be accomplished. This is the noose of the Krodharāja.

5. Having recited the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*) twenty-one times, it should be thrown. At the very moment it is thrown, all obstructors (*vighna*), leaders of obstacles (*vināyaka*), and wicked beings become bound by a noose. By his will, they remain bound for a year, a hundred years, a thousand years, or even a hundred thousand eons (*kalpa*). When he generates loving-kindness (*maitrī*) and compassion (*karuṇā*), the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa should be recollected three times; then they are released again. [Even] from the midst of an army—

6. If one casts it [into the enemy ranks], the soldiers become bound by nooses. If one casts it into the midst of battle, all weapons, missiles, bows, arrows, spears, clubs, mallets, *musuṇḍi*-spears, discuses, lances, arms, shields, and armor—all become bound by nooses. Water mustard seeds (*jalasarṣapa*), having been consecrated seven times with recitation, should be cast [into them]; they will be released. One should worship the noose day after day according to one’s means; whatever one intends for its purpose, all that shall be accomplished. This is the accomplishment of the Amoghapāśa.

7. No ritual procedure is required. Alternatively, if one desires invisibility, while performing the practice, one should take the mudrā in the hand of Amoghapāśa; grasping the previously mentioned noose with the right and left hands, by reciting the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya one hundred and eight times, one becomes invisible. By reciting it one hundred and fifty-six times, one travels through the sky and becomes a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) among the Vidyādharas of Amoghapāśa, with a retinue of hundreds of thousands of millions of Vidyādharas.

He becomes [successful]; he lives for ten million years; his hair becomes curled and ringed; he possesses unimpeded strength, vigor, and prowess. If one desires rain, by worshipping her, it rains according to one's wish. By worshipping her while restraining excessive rain, one stops the rain. For one who wishes to pacify all calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions, and all Māras, the Vidyādhara must bathe, remain pure, and be clothed in clean garments. Pāśa-...

2. Having ascended to a high place with haste, one should take hold of a noose with the Amoghapāśa mudrā and recite the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya seven times while facing the four directions. As the noose is raised, all quarrels, strife, conflicts, and disputes; all internal and external armies, adversaries, and enemies; as well as all fears, enmities, calamities, afflictions, great plagues, famines, and the perils of wilderness travel—all these are pacified by mere remembrance. Excessive rain, untimely rain—

3. Drought, cold, wind, heat, and the fear of fierce fires are pacified. A great boundary-binding is established for a hundred yojanas in every direction. Just as one intends in the mind, so everything is accomplished. One should perform worship; the Amogharāja mantra should be recited; it should be honored. Merely by the act of worship and supplication, everything is immediately attained. One should not entertain doubt or uncertainty in this regard. As prescribed in the ritual manual (kalpa)—

4. Whatever is to be done according to the ritual procedure for accomplishment should be performed accordingly. Then, in that very instant, all of that will be accomplished immediately. One should cultivate loving-kindness (*maitrī*), compassion (*karuṇā*), sympathetic joy (*muditā*), and equanimity (*upekṣā*). One should be intent upon compassion for all sentient beings. One should worship the noble Avalokiteśvara. One should possess reverence for the Three Jewels. One should possess guru-reverence through mental attention toward all the Tathāgatas. [One should maintain] pure and clean conduct—

5. One must possess pure ethical discipline (*śīla*). This is because of the reality of the practice for the *Cintāmaṇi-amoghapāśa* which draws forth awakening. Now, therefore, I shall proclaim the ritual procedure for the wheel-noose (*cakrapāśa*), the entry into the reality of the practice of the Vidyādharas, the supreme means of entering all subterranean caves (*bilas*), the entry into the abode of the Asuras, the entry into the abode of the Kinnaras, the entry into the abode of the Gandharvas, the entry into the abode of the Devas, and the movement through the sky.

6. [There is] the entry into the abode of the Thirty-three, up to the entry into the abode of Akaniṣṭha; the entry into the abode of the Naga kings, the entry into the abode of Pātāla, the entry into the abode of the Sun, the entry into the abodes of the stars and constellations, the entry into forests, the entry into mountains, and the entry into great rivers. In whatever way it is directed by the mind, in that very way—whether mundane or supramundane—it is accomplished with little hardship and little effort through this method of the *pāśa* sādhana.

7. In this matter, no doubt or hesitation should be conceived. The *vidyādhara*, having become pure, having bathed well, and wearing clean garments, should eat the three white foods (*tri-śukla-bhojana*). He should recite the *Buddhānusmṛti* with faith, reverence, and sincerity. Establishing a mind of loving-kindness (*maitra-citta*), with an intention of compassion and a pure mind, he should begin on the thirteenth day until the moonlight is full and clearly manifest, according to the prescribed ritual. And the ritual for worship at the three times of day should be performed as follows... [as in 19b (P31b1, D.33a5)].

1. One should always perform the recitation (*jāpa*) according to one's means; one should always perform it one hundred and eight times during the three periods of the day—namely, at the three junctions of the day and likewise at the three junctions of the night. Having prepared the three types of thread, one should fashion the unsurpassed wheel-noose (*cakrapāśa*). One should make a silk thread, a lotus thread, and a *arkka* thread, tripled and of proper measure, thirty-six cubits (*hasta*) in length. One should fashion a threefold wheel, four finger-breadths (*aṅgula*) in both diameter and width, complete with a hub (*nābhi*), a rim (*nemika*), and spokes (*ārā*) all around, made of gold or silver.

2. Regarding that which is made of copper: having set out a divine seat, a Dharma-seat well-adorned, provided with a fragrant mandala, strewn with flowers, and arranged with full vases as well as water-offering bowls; having placed [the image] facing the cloth [painting], and having placed a wheel-noose above the Dharma-seat, one should perform worship at the three junctions of the day according to one's intention, reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times. Then, on the fifteenth day, having fasted for a day and night and remaining silent, [one should worship] upon the noble Avalokiteśvara cloth-painting.

3. Worship of Īśvara must be performed. Three kinds of offerings should be presented. Seated facing the cloth painting of the Dharma-seat, one should recite the Amoghapāśahṛdaya eight thousand times with agallochum, sandalwood, and guggulu incense. Reciting it over each individual mustard seed, one should cast them into the noose. When the eight thousand are complete, the noose blazes; a wheel remains suspended in the sky, and the body of the Vidyādhara blazes and whirls upward.

4. Rays of light issue from the head, and the sound of the word "Excellent! (*sādhukāra*) resounds from the cloth painting. Then the Vidyādhara should know: "The Amoghapāśahṛdaya and the ritual of the Great Wheel-Noose (*mahācakrapāśavidhi*) have been accomplished. Thereupon, the Vidyādhara should perform a great worship. Having recited the Amoghakrodharāja one thousand and eight times, the Vidyādhara should then take hold of the noose; he should grasp the wheel in the form of a mudrā in his left hand.

5. One should hold the noose-seal (*pāśamudrā*) in the right hand, shaped like a wheel, and while grasping it, one should recollect the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* mantra and cast it in the four directions. Then, one should recite the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*) ten times in each of the ten directions. After that, one should rotate it seven times in the manner of consecrating one’s own body. By the mere act of rotating it together with the seal-form, one will be consecrated as a Universal Monarch (*cakravartin*) of the Vidyādharas. This is the Great Sword—

6. He will become supreme in his spiritual powers (*ṛddhi*). Sudarśana, the great wheel-turning king (*mahācakravartin*), will appear in his own form and stand before him. He will bow his head at the feet of the *vidyādhara* and speak thus: "O *vidyādhara*, what do you command? I shall do it. Whatever purpose he states, all that shall be accomplished. He will exist as a servant and perform tasks everywhere. Then, when the *vidyādhara* desires to enter the palace, from there—three... [times].

7. Having remained overnight, one should hold a noose in one’s hand; wherever there is the entrance to a cave, one should whirl the noose around three times. The Amogharāja mantra should be recited, and the noose should be cast. As soon as it is cast, all the doors of the caves and dwellings are flung open. All mechanical devices, bolts, gaps, great rivers, mountain peaks, and the evil paths of yakṣas and rākṣasas are brought down and shattered.

1. The locks, door-bolts, and mechanisms become shattered and scattered; they fall apart and perish. They appear utterly pure, stainless, and as miraculous manifestations of vast celestial palaces (*vimāna*). A palace and celestial mansion made of the seven jewels is seen, variegated and adorned with various gems, and embellished with various jewel-trees. A celestial mansion of divine fragrance is seen, featuring gardens of various flowers. Then, by the Vidyādhara holding a noose in his hand—

2. Having made the wheel facing toward the form of the mudrā, one should recollect the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*. One should enter; as soon as one has entered, that excellent palace shakes in six ways—it trembles, quivers, rattles, roars, and thunders—and it becomes illuminated by great divine rays. Then the vidyādhara should enter. Thereupon, the medicinal herb named *Amoghaviśuddhavimalā* appears in the form of a divine woman.

3. Adorned with ornaments, decorated with divine garments and jewelry, and endowed with a supreme, abundant, and beautiful complexion, she comes possessing a divine and magnificent form. She holds a *bījapūraka* fruit. And that medicinal herb, upon being seen by one who has assumed a female form, draws forth all seeds and all powers from within a distance of one *yojana*. Then, by the *vidyādhara*, the foremost noose of the *Amoghapāśacakra*—

4. It should be maintained. Upon merely seeing it, their strength, vigor, and vitality are withdrawn; they become weak. Then that woman laughs. One should press with the syllable *oṃ* and remember the King of Wrath (*Krodharāja*). She falls face down and water flows forth. That water must not be touched; one should remember the Unfailing King (*Amogharāja*). Then she gazes with a sidelong glance. She should be struck with the noose of the Vidyādhara.

5. ... [the syllable] VYAM. From it, nectar-water flows forth; it should be taken up and touched. By the mere touch of it, one travels through the sky and ascends upon the first wind-element. One should anoint the eyes; then one sees all the Tathāgatas residing in the ten directions, together with their retinues of bodhisattva hosts, and all the manifestations of their buddha-fields, celestial palaces, and abodes. They are seen as clearly as if they were in the palm of one's hand. And those who remain... [are seen].

6. They endure and maintain themselves. Those who have attained final nirvāṇa, those who are past, those who are future, and those who are present—whatever Buddhas there are, as well as the great reliquaries (*mahācaitya*) containing the *dhātu* and the *kūṭapūpa* stūpas—all of these he shall see within the mere circle of his own household assembly. He should protect himself; by merely anointing himself with this unguent, he will come to possess a divine, golden-colored skin; and he will have deep blue, curled, ringlet-like hair. Divine blue—

7. He will possess eyes as excellent as those of a peacock. His lifespan will be a divine hundred thousand *kalpas*. He will have a retinue of one million eight hundred thousand *vidyādharas* as his universal monarch (*cakravartin*). He will have a retinue of two hundred and seventy million *apsaras*, *kinnarīs*, and *vidyādharīs*, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā. [Whatever he intends in his mind,] by the mere thought of his desire, [there shall be] a hundred flavors...

1. First, excellent divine food appears; a supreme, divine great drink of ambrosial flavor appears. Until the very end at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*), the great king of the Sudarśana wheel rolls before one. It crushes all enemies, all obstacles, and all obstructing spirits (*vināyaka*); it destroys, cuts, rends, causes them to cease, shatters, and grinds them down. Alternatively, all the hair of that woman who is ill must be combed, and her body-bound [garments]—

2. It should not be made [of ordinary materials]; it should be bound, and that in which it is bound shall consist of the seven precious gems. Wherever he enters, he becomes invisible everywhere. All the deities will become established in his service. All the nāgas, all the devas, all the kinnaras, and all the vidyādharas—all of them will remain under his command. All of them, together with their retinues, will follow closely behind him until the attainment of enlightenment.

3. Now, when a Vidyādhara wishes to enter the palace and subsequently wishes to exit again, he must neither speak to nor touch that woman of medicinal herbs. With a noose-seal (*pāśamudrā*) in his hand, he should enter the excellent palace; then all the inhabitants of the palace—men, women, boys, and girls—will emerge and stand before him. Some will have full water-jars in their hands, some will have parasols in their hands, and some will have divine [objects].

4. Some were wearing garments; some were wearing divine great jewels and gems; some were carrying perfumes, some flowers, some garlands, and some various and wonderful ornaments and decorations. Some were carrying ointments, some fragrant powders, some vessels filled with scented water made of the seven precious gems, and some divine fruits of various kinds. Some held various divine flowers, such as the *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka*.

5. Some bear *nandana*, *mahānandana*, *mañjūṣaka*, *mahāmañjūṣaka*, *roca*, *mahāroca*, *atimuktaka*, *campaka*, *vārṣika*, *nīla*, *mahānīla*, *kadamba*, *sumanā*, *yūthikā*, *nāgapuṣpa*, *kontagandha*, and *vārṣikapuṣpa* flowers; some bear divine incense; some bear *gośīrṣa* and *uragasāra* sandalwood incense; some bear *agaru*, *turuṣka*, and *tamālapatra* incense; some [bear] peacock-feather fans; and some—

6. Some have swords in their hands; some have spears in their hands; some have thunderbolts, axes, *tomaras*, spears, clubs, tridents, and *musuṇḍhis* in their hands. Some, clad in armor, mail, and protective garments, have assembled for the purpose of guarding him. Some hold various jeweled vessels—golden vessels, silver vessels, golden flowers filled with jewels, and silver flowers. All of them offer these to the *vidyādhara*. By the *vidyādhara*... the Great...

7. One should practice mental attention through loving-kindness toward all beings, mental attention toward the Buddha, and mental attention toward the noble Avalokiteśvara who holds the unfailing noose (*amoghapāśa*). With a mind intent on compassion, one should remain vigilant and silent while providing consolation. One should enter by way of the enemy-path and, standing facing the lion-throne, place the unfailing wheel-noose (*amoghacakrapāśa*) upon the eastern lion-throne. Then, the knowledge-holder (*vidyādhara*) himself—

1. One should sit down; having gone upward, one should pay homage to all the Tathāgatas and bow to the face of the Noble Avalokiteśvara. Then, one becomes victorious over all enemies. If one bows with the face turned downward, then the opposing Vidyādhara is decapitated by a wheel. Immediately upon sitting down, the abode of the Vidyādhara undergoes sixfold transformations, a great roar arises, a sound of great clamor manifests, and divine five-fold musical instruments—

They play musical instruments, and from the sky, deities in a great celestial palace (vimāna), wearing turbans and crowns, consecrate the head of the Vidyādhara. At the very moment he is consecrated, a rain of the seven precious gems appears; a rain of gold, prosperity, and garments appears; a rain of various wonderful divine flowers—golden flowers and silver flowers—descends; and a rain of divine ornaments descends. Then, Apsarases arrive with vessels made of the seven precious gems, [filled with] ambrosia (amṛta).

3. By means of the *tarasāyana*, one brings forth the essence (*rasa*). It must be grasped by the *vidyādhara*; the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* should be recollected. Then it is to be touched by the *vidyādhara*. As soon as it is touched, the *vidyādhara* obtains the purification of a divine body. His skin becomes the color of gold. His hair becomes exceedingly dark blue, and his eyes become like divine lotuses, purified with divine vision. [He remains] for hundreds of thousands of millions of *kalpas*.

4. The lifespan becomes ten million years (*niyuta*). If one who desires to depart takes that supreme elixir (*rasāyana*) and enters into the midst of divine water scented with sandalwood according to his wish, bathing therein, then as soon as he has bathed, he stands at the entrance of the cave. He appears in the form of Maheśvara; he shall become the sole object of worship for all the world, standing above it, just like the noble teacher Avalokiteśvara.

5. This vidyādhara shall become like one who is honored, revered, and held in high esteem. Therein, he may touch this supreme elixir (*rasāyana*), and it shall become as pure as great Jāmbūnada gold. Whether he touches a wall, a mountain, a pillar, a tree, a vessel, a jar, a pot, a *vaṭṭākā*, or a clod of earth, it shall become as pure as great Jāmbūnada gold; it shall remain so for as long as required. Then, vi—

6. When a daughter of the nāgas of the lower world, or a daughter of the apsarases, or a daughter of the kinnaras approaches, then the vidyādhara must be pure, wearing clean garments, and well-bathed. On the eighth, fourteenth, or fifteenth day, he should worship the noble Avalokiteśvara on the cotton-painted cloth. He must remain fasting for a day and night. This great wheel of the supreme seat (cakramahāpāsa) [should be worshipped] by one adorned with the divine seat and the Dharma-seat.

7. Having established the image, one should perform a great worship before it alone without speaking. One thousand and eight recitations are to be performed. With each recitation, a single mustard seed should be cast onto the noose. When the one thousand and eight are complete, that noose will coil itself like a serpent. A wheel in the form of a hooded snake will remain; then the *vidyādhara* should seize the noose. [Whether it be] in the abode of the *nāgas*, or in the abode of the *surendras*, or in the abode of the *kinnaras*, or in the abode of the *apsarases*—[he shall seize it].

1. Or, having stood [there], one should recollect the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*. A noose should be cast into the interior of the dwelling. As soon as it is cast, one should further act in this manner: whatever object one has in mind, that object becomes bound by the noose. "Act according to my intention! One may [command] other things according to the mental intention, such as wealth, or gold, silver, jewels, pearls, beryl, conch, crystal, coral, silver, refined gold, clothing, ornaments, or other [possessions].

2. Just as you desire the manifestations of celestial palaces (*vimāna*), the noose (*pāśa*) must be cast everywhere; wherever it is cast, there it draws [the object] forth very clearly. Thus, it fulfills the intention of the mind, and the state of being will not be otherwise—whether in a royal family, a brahmin family, or a kṣatriya family, or whoever has such an intention, whether woman, man, boy, or girl—with the mere taking of their name.

3. By the mere release of the noose, those who are bound by the noose will be drawn forth; even including all beasts, birds, lions, tigers, elephants, and buffaloes, he draws them in. If one should cast [the mantra] into the midst of battle, whoever has their name cast therein shall stand before him, bound by the noose. Everything is accomplished exactly according to the intention of the mind. One who desires to cause the moon and sun to descend should face the moon and sun—

4. Standing in the sky, one should recollect the Amogharājahṛdaya seven times and cast the noose toward the moon and sun. Then it should be drawn back; the moon and sun will become bound by the noose. They descend from the sky and stand before the vidyādhara, accomplishing all tasks exactly as desired. Alternatively, for one wishing to go to the abode of the moon and sun, [one should take] the noose...

5. When the mudrā is held in the hand, one should recollect the *Amogharāja-hṛdaya*; the Vidyādhara then flies up into the sky and enjoys the seats of the moon and sun for as long as he desires. Then, remaining in his own place, he descends by means of an unbroken and uninjured throw [of the mudrā]. One who wishes to enter a forest cave must be pure, wearing clean clothes, and well-bathed; he should [recite the mantra] twenty-one times at the entrance of the forest cave.

6. One should recite [the mantra] and release the noose; by the mere act of releasing it from the hand, all the *nāgas* in the forest caves and celestial palaces (*vimāna*) shall appear, and they will all stand before the *vidyādhara*. They will say to the *vidyādhara*: "Enter this excellent great palace of the *vidyādharas*. Then, the *vidyādhara* should call to mind Amogharāja. With the noose-mudrā in his hand, he should enter the forest cave. As soon as he has entered, the forest abode undergoes a sixfold transformation.

7. At the edge of the central grove, there is a lotus pond made of the seven precious gems, possessing a divine sandalwood fragrance; its water is neither too cold nor too hot, and its surface is pleasant to the touch and sweet to the taste. It is like the essence of ambrosia (*amṛta-rasāyana*). Then, having consecrated a mustard seed twenty-one times with the *Amogharājahṛdaya*, it should be thrown into the center of the pond. As soon as it is thrown, a maiden with a form like that of a divine jewel-woman (*strīratna*), whose body is half-submerged, emerges. 22a (P36a2, D.38a1)

1. She holds a full jar made of jewels, adorned with various kinds of divine flowers, and offers it to the Vidyādhara. With her head bowed and feeling bashful, she says to the Vidyādhara: "O Lord Vidyādhara, enter the palace; do not delay. Then the Vidyādhara must utter these three words of accomplishment: "I seek the next world," "Vidyādhara-hood," and "Worldly accomplishment of practice. Wherever he desires his own happiness, he should say: "I am sent by my mother and brother. Then—

The Vidyādhara should say: "Sister, I am seeking the sake of the next world; give me [entry] so that I may enter. She says: "Be gracious, O Vidyādhara; enter the palace. Then the Vidyādhara, with the noose-mudrā in his hand, should enter while reciting the *Amogharājahṛdaya*. Thereupon, a magnificent great palace is seen, with celestial palaces made of the seven jewels, adorned with nets of divine bells, and draped with hanging silk streamers of various colors; and that maiden, a great jewel—

He gives it. Having taken hold of that great jewel-gem which is desired by the Vidyādharas and those seeking the next world, the Vidyādhara should then grasp it; he should prepare a seat, a noose that is perfectly circular, and stand upon the seat. He should stand upon that great jewel-gem noose. Flowers and incense should be offered. The Heart-mantra of Amogharāja should be recollected. As soon as it is recollected, the noose together with the great jewel-gem blazes forth.

4. That great maṇi-jewel exudes milk-water (*kṣīrodaka*). That milk-water must be taken by the vidyādhara; it must be touched. By the mere touch of seven handfuls of that milk-water, his entire body becomes stainless and completely pure. He obtains a ray of light called "The Net of Radiance from the Great Maṇḍala of the Amoghaprabhāsa Jewel. He will become established in the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) and irreversible (*avaivartika*). Unsurpassed—

5. One attains the path to supreme enlightenment. One attains the miraculous manifestation of the noble Avalokiteśvara’s illusion-like samādhi. With a perfectly purified body, the Vidyādhara Amoghapāśa, the most excellent one, stands before them. Placing his right hand upon their head, he comforts them, saying: "You are my eldest son; you have attained the state of a Vidyādhara. By you, the Buddha-body of the Great Liberation Maṇḍala..."

6. Regarding "completely pure": he sees all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions. They all utter the sound of "Well done! Well done! saying, "Excellent, excellent, Great Being! You have entered; you have attained the path to enlightenment; you are a Buddha. This is the practice for the path to liberation (*mokṣamārga*). Alternatively, if you seek the state of a Vidyādhara, then [the deity] gives a golden flower which must be taken; one should stand upon the head of that very maiden. By pressing with the syllable *Oṃ*, immediately upon being placed above, *Oṃ*—

When the word "kāra" is well-proclaimed, a drop of water flows from the two eyes of that maiden. Then, it must be seized and touched by the Vidyādhara; as soon as it is touched, he will become a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) of the Vidyādharas. With his hair curled in locks and a noose in his hand, he travels through the sky. He will have a retinue of eighteen thousand million Vidyādharas and will remember seven thousand past births. [Vidyādhara] 22b (P37a1, D.38b7)

1. The means of accomplishment (*sādhana*). Alternatively, when he provides the worldly method of accomplishment, it happens as follows: the Vidyādhara takes from my treasury and then that maiden, with her own hands, plucks her hair. He gives it to the Vidyādhara; all the hair must be taken and spun threefold. Twenty-one thread-knots must be made and bound upon the head. Just as one intends in the mind, so does he display a magical illusion (*indrajāla*), fulfilling all desires.

2. He displays flowers and fruits; as he desires, he displays them along with spirits (*bhūta*). Having tied [the mantra] around his neck, he becomes invisible. All *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, *bhūtas*, *piśācas*, *kumbhāṇḍas*, *mahoragas*, humans, and non-humans remain under his control. Having tied it between his eyebrows, all gods and *nāgas* remain under his control. One should bind it on the right arm; one will possess the strength of ten *nāgas*. One will become invincible in power and wheel-like [in prowess], overcoming all wicked adversaries and enemies. Vā-

3. One should bind the great arms; [then] the people of the fourfold world remain under one's control. Having bound the left hand, whomever one touches shall become submissive, both in person and with their wealth. One should bind the right hand and strike at the eastern city gate for three *praharas*; then the king, along with his harem, retinue, city, kingdom, and the women, men, boys, and girls of the royal capital, remain under one's control, both in person and with their wealth.

And furthermore: those born in the animal realm—birds, fierce beasts, venomous creatures, and other beings accompanied by poison—will remain under one's control. One should bind the right thigh. Wherever one enters—whether into a forest, a cave, a mountain glen, a grotto, or a wilderness sanctuary—as soon as one has entered, all substances, all medicinal herbs, and all deities will appear in their own forms and stand before one, [offering] their feet and calves.

5. One should bind the *kṣiṇapāda* [to the foot]; they will cross the Mahāsamudra-maṇipāda. However, as for other great rivers, the water will reach only the height of the shanks (*jaṅghā*). One should bind the left shank; one travels a hundred *yojanas* day by day and returns again without rest. One should bind the left thigh (*vāmoru*); one shall enter the great cremation ground (*mahāśmaśāna*), and all who dwell in the cremation ground will become naked. All will remain under one's control.

6. Then, while the Vidyādhara takes his delight in that very palace, he should take a full jar with his left hand and grasp that maiden with his right hand. He should enter the great, excellent palace. There, in the center of that excellent palace, is a lotus pond strewn with flowers; there, in that lotus pond, he should bathe both of them, and that water should be touched. As soon as they have been bathed and touched by it, he becomes a Vidyādhara Wheel-turning Emperor (cakravartin) of the Cakra-Vidyādharas.

7. He will have a retinue of seven thousand million *vidyādharas* and a lifespan of ten thousand *kalpas*. His hair will be curled in locks. He will become a sovereign king over twelve hundred forest-dwellings, palaces, and celestial mansions. If you give him to me as a mother, he will protect your son; he will enjoy wealth, grain, clothing, ornaments, jewels, pearls, coral, silver, and gold. Thus [he will be] a sister in all matters of necessity.

1. She will maintain freedom from deficiency; she will not take away even a portion [of one's merit]. Day after day, she brings a celestial woman adorned with divine ornaments; she provides the enjoyments of a celestial mansion; she provides a divine house and palace. Wherever you direct her as a servant, there she goes—whether to the abode of the gods, the abode of the nāgas, or the abodes of yakṣas, rākṣasas, or bhūtas. She performs various other tasks as a servant according to whatever one desires in one’s mind.

2. // The Procedure for Entering the Forest // Now, a Vidyādhara desiring to enter the underworld (pātāla) must bathe, remain pure, and wear clean garments. Having smeared a square maṇḍala in a secret place on a pure patch of ground, anointed it with various fragrances, and set out offerings of various flavors, he should burn agallochum incense. Having fasted for three nights and recited the Amogharājahṛdaya mantra eight thousand times, with the Cakrapāśa mudrā in hand, when [the night] is full—eight...

3. From the center of the mandala, incense appears. The Wrathful King should be invoked seven times. Then, a great black man emerges from the center of the mandala; his body is half-formed and deformed, with terrifying fangs, hair standing erect and flaming at the head, red eyes, red tongue and lips, red nails, blue-black hair, firm and hard arms, a protruding belly, a white sacred thread, five heads, venomous snakes, and a flickering tongue.

4. [One sees him] clothed in a tiger skin, with an axe and a club in his hands, surveying the ten directions. Then, the vidyādhara must not be afraid; he must remain firm and call to mind the King of Wrath (Krodharāja). He should release the wheel-noose and cut off [the opponent's] head, from which great blood flows. That blood should be smeared over the entire body of the vidyādhara; by the mere act of being smeared, his own body will be empowered as being composed of vajra. Fearless—

5. Having cut out the [sun’s] disc and produced his own eye, he should wipe it and anoint that eye; he will become one with divine vision (*divyacakṣus*). Having extracted the marrow and touched it, he will have a lifespan of ten thousand *kalpas*. He will become a repository for an ocean of learning (*śrutisāgara*). In birth after birth throughout a hundred thousand *kalpas*, he will remember his past lives (*jātismara*). If he should eat the heart for a *kalpa*, he travels through the sky. Having made a sectarian mark (*tilaka*) with the heart-blood, he becomes invisible.

6. He becomes one whose sword cuts off tongues; he effects the crushing of all enemies. If one desires to enter the netherworld (*pātāla*), then having recited the *pāśacakra* mantra one hundred and eight times with the Wrathful King (*krodharāja*), one should take the noose in the form of a mudrā and strike the ground of the circle. One should deliver three strikes. Thereupon, the gates of the netherworld become opened. One should enter as if entering one's own home, going back and forth repeatedly. As for others—

7. Perform all activities; all those dwelling in the netherworld remain under one's control. Therefore, by one desiring to enter the sky, looking upward, one should recite the *Amogharājahṛdaya* eight thousand times. Having consecrated *kuṭu*-oil eight thousand times, one should protect oneself with it. With the *pāśamudrā* in hand, one travels through the expanse of the sky and becomes enveloped in the nature of space. By one desiring to go to the abode of the gods, having gone to a temple, [one should perform this] before the deity... 23b (P.38b6, D.40b5)

1. One should tie a cord around one's neck eight thousand times while reciting the *Amogharājahṛdaya*. For whomsoever the gods have bound [the cords], that god descends and stands before the *vidyādhara*. Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara will say to the *vidyādhara*, "What do you request, O *vidyādhara*? Then the *vidyādhara* should say, "I shall go to the celestial realm. If they have other intentions, they grant them all at once. Thus, there is the attainment of going to the celestial realm.

2. Having grasped it with the sound, one travels through the sky to the celestial abode by means of divine power. There, one shall enjoy the great divine palanquin (vimāna) according to one’s desire; or, if one does not so desire, one descends again from the celestial abode. Other activities, performed according to one’s own mental inclinations and intentions, shall be accomplished everywhere. One should not give rise to doubt or hesitation in this regard. This is the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the Wheel-Noose (*cakrapāśa*). Following this, one should accomplish the Lotus-Noose (*padmapāśa*) of the Vidyādhara.

3. Out of desire, that *vidyādhara* must be pure, having bathed well and wearing clean garments. Having fasted for three nights, or five nights, or one night, the *vidyādhara* should prepare a cord or thread. It should be made of silk thread, lotus fiber, or the color of lapis lazuli, dyed with red pigment. It should be twenty-one cubits long. And he should fashion a lotus from the three jewels, with petals fully opened and measuring four finger-breadths.

4. On a cloth of gold, a cloth of silver, or one made of lapis lazuli or sapphire, a lotus seed-vessel (padmakarkaṭikā) should be fashioned, surrounded by pearls; then a noose should be bound [to it], and on the second side a noose-seal (pāśamudrā) should be bound. Then, it should be beautifully adorned with a divine seat and a Dharma-seat. A cow-dung circle (gomayamaṇḍaka) should be made. Above the maṇḍala, a lotus made of fragrance should be visualized, and above the maṇḍala, the Dharma-seat.

5. Having established [the image], it should be performed with a full water-jar (pūrṇakumbha) prepared. A scattering of flowers should be offered, and incense of agaru, candana, and turuṣka should be burned; the argha and pādya offerings should be set out. He [the practitioner] should stand upon a Dharma-seat (dharmāsana) above a lotus and noose, with Noble Avalokiteśvara in front. Seated cross-legged as a vidyādhara, while reciting the Amoghapāśahṛdaya ten thousand times, one should recite [the mantra] over each individual mustard seed and cast them upon that [image]. When the ten thousand are complete—

Then, on the full moon day, having fasted for a day and night, one should worship Noble Avalokiteśvara and worship that noose. Holding it with the Amoghapāśa mudrā, one should recite the Amogharāja-hṛdaya one hundred and eight times. Then, reciting the Krodharāja one hundred and eight times at the three junctions of the day and night, the worship should be performed.
