7. When the sound "dhu-m" issues forth, various colored rays of light will emanate from the noble Avalokiteśvara. Then, the vidyādhara, seated in the mudrā-paryaṅka posture, with unblinking eyes and a smiling face, should maintain a mind of great compassion. Looking toward the face of the noble Avalokiteśvara, he should recite the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya three times. Then, [he beholds] the noble Avalokiteśvara with his divine body—

He approaches with his true nature (*bhāva*) and extends his right arm; he places it upon the head of the *vidyādhara* and gives him a cry of approval (*sādhukāra*), thus consoling him: "O *vidyādhara*, you are my eldest son, born of my own body (*aurasa*). This great rite of recitation (*jāpa*) and this great rite of worship have become for me a supreme worship. This is the supreme rite of recitation and the supreme accomplishment (*sādhana*). You have accomplished the *Amogharājahṛdaya*; you have accomplished the *Mahāpadmapāśa*. Be gracious."

2. "A boon according to your mental aspiration has been fulfilled by you; you are liberated from all desires. You are completely freed from the prison of the fear of *saṃsāra*, and released from the terrible horse of birth, old age, death, and sorrow. You are completely freed from the sixteen terrible great hells, and you are completely freed from the eight great fears and the painful sensations of suffering. This is your final birth; having fallen away from the terrible sufferings of dwelling in a womb, you shall be born spontaneously from lotuses in the world-system of Sukhāvatī, the realm of the Vidyādharas, until [enlightenment]."

3. ...and the culmination of sovereign power. You have planted [the seeds]; you have planted eighty-four thousand *koṭis* of great roots of merit, equal to the sands of the river Gaṅgā. You are endowed with a great mass of merit; you have become a Vidyādhara. Many transformations have been performed by you. You have been prophesied as a Great Vidyādhara, liberated from all the terrible obstacles of the hells and the past. Grant a boon according to what dwells in your mind. Then, by the Vidyādhara...

4. "Just as you have intended in your mind, so shall I grant it to that man. Then the vidyādhara should take hold of the lotus-noose. In a pure place, he should perform a grand worship with reverence. When the task is to be performed, he should grasp the noose with his hand; thus all tasks are to be accomplished. Having placed the lotus in the left hand of Noble Avalokiteśvara and grasped the noose in the right hand, one should recite the Amogharāja-hṛdaya one hundred and eight times.

5. [Recite] this: by the mere recitation of the name of whichever sentient being [is intended], the deity attends upon that Bodhisattva at the head [of the rite] when one hundred and eight recitations have been completed, and grants all desired boons. Then, a Vidyādhara who wishes to request the prophecy of enlightenment (bodhivyākaraṇa) should become pure, put on clean garments, bathe well, and having fasted for a day and night, [offer] a magnificent [oblation] to the Blessed Buddha Śākyamuni.

6. Having performed worship, that lotus-noose should be placed into the hand of the Blessed Buddha. On the second side, it should be tied around one’s own neck; the *Amogharājahṛdaya* should be recited eight thousand times. When the eight thousand are completed, the Blessed Buddha appears before the *vidyādhara* with a body of golden hue and places his hand above the *vidyādhara*’s head. He comforts him, grants him a prophecy, and fulfills all his heart’s desires. He—

7. They exhaust the sins that constitute obstacles, accumulated over hundreds of thousands of lifetimes; they go to destruction without remainder. Their body shall become completely pure. They shall be free from stains, having departed from stinginess and envy. This will be their final dwelling in a womb and final birth; they shall experience the glory of the divine world. Among all sentient beings, they shall be the sole teacher; they shall be worthy of worship and stand in the place of a guru. At the time of death, [they shall see] the Tathāgatas of the ten directions...

1. They take heed of them and comfort them, and show them the excellent path. They stand before the noble Avalokiteśvara and comfort him. He raises his right hand; with mindfulness well-established before him, they cast off their bodies. As soon as they have cast them off, through that very cultivation, they will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī. They will be born from lotuses of miraculous appearance, adorned with all ornaments and endowed with the primary and secondary marks.

2. His body will be adorned, and he will become one who remembers his births; he will recollect his births throughout hundreds of thousands of kalpas. And this Amoghapāśahṛdaya—the manual of the chapter on the mudrās of the *Vimokṣamaṇḍala*—will remain at the tip of his tongue in its entirety. Thus, he will be established in the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*), irreversible, and non-retrogressive. Through the great miraculous power of supernatural transformations and the attainment of great supernormal faculties, he will [pervade] the ten directions with divine peaked palaces, celestial mansions, and excellent abodes.

3. He approaches every buddha-field, continuing until he reaches the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*). Now, if a knowledge-holder (*vidyādhara*) desires to see the world-system of Sukhāvatī in this very life, that knowledge-holder—whether in a pure location, a house, a forest, a monastery, a circular pavilion (*maṇḍalavāṭa*), a walking path (*caṅkrama*), a peak, or a small hut—should, on a pure, level, and smooth patch of ground, demarcate a square mandala.

4. Or else, construct a hand-sized mandala, well-proportioned, square, with four corners on all sides... [smooth, well-spread, made of] *śatarttaka* grass, soft and green; having divided it all around, the wise one should trace the mandala with a thread. Having divided the center of the middle mandala, [he should draw] a very beautiful lotus, variegated with colors, one hundred and eight-petaled, along with its seed-vessel (*karkaṭikā*). Around the entire perimeter of the lotus, [he should adorn it] with various ornaments that beautify the mandala.

5. One should draw beautiful lotuses of various colors, measuring four finger-breadths [in size]. Within the inner corners of the lotuses, one should draw pure blue water-lilies. Around the perimeter of the altar (*vedikā*) and the circle of jewels, one should depict an ocean, divided by divine waters and adorned with celestial palaces (*vimāna*) made of various gems. It should be strewn with various water-born flowers and frequented by various birds, such as swans, cranes, curlews, ruddy geese, and *jīvaka* birds.

It should be adorned with various flocks of birds; it should be filled with fish, sea-monsters, and crocodiles, and fashioned in the form of an ocean. Various jewel-trees, flowering trees, and fruit-bearing trees should be made, along with a railing (*vedikā*). Outside that, one should construct a circular railing (*bahivedikā-maṇḍala*) and draw hand-gestures (*mudrā*) and weapons. At the four gates, the Four Great Kings (*caturmahārāja*) should be depicted. Then, divine seats should be prepared upon the lotuses in the central maṇḍala, and the Blessed One Amitābha should be placed upon them.

And [one should worship] Āryāvalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta. It should be prepared with full vases arranged for the mandala; it should be strewn with flowers and anointed with perfumes. Various divine banners should be displayed. A white offering should be presented, as well as water for the feet and water for the guest-offering (*argha*), and garlands of lamps should be made. Amitābha, with a lotus-noose in his hand, should give a lotus. The *vidyādhara* should be pure and wear very clean garments, having bathed well.

1. Having been touched by that [mixture] of the five products of the cow, having fasted for a full day and night, and having sat facing east with legs crossed in the *paryaṅka* posture, one should hold the *pāśamudrā* with the hand and perform the recitation (*japa*). One should be possessed of a mind of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), intent on compassion, and become one who is compassionate toward all sentient beings. The *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* should be recited until, at the end of the night, Amitābha blazes forth and rays of light issue from that great maṇḍala.

2. It moves; the body of the vidyādhara trembles and blazes. Then, at the time of twilight, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ārya Amitābha—possessing a golden-colored body like that of a Tathāgata—stands before the vidyādhara as a heap of gold. He places his right hand upon the head of the vidyādhara, consoles him, and will fulfill all his heart’s desires. Then he vanishes, [entering] the sleep named Suviśuddhanirmalāvabhāsa.

3. He attains that by which, merely upon falling asleep and merely closing his eyes, he beholds the world-system of Sukhāvatī with its celestial palaces and abodes, filled entirely with the people, lands, and assemblies of bodhisattvas; he beholds that Tathāgata teaching the Dharma, and all those circles of assemblies offer him consolation. He beholds the miraculous display of supernatural power consisting of the transformations of all the celestial palaces. This is his final birth.

4. He will be born in a thousand *sukhāvatī* world-systems; he will remember his births from lifetime to lifetime. He will recollect seven thousand lifetimes, and then, having awakened, by reciting the *pāśa* [mantra] one thousand and eight times, and holding the *pāśa* in his right hand, he flies up into the sky. He lives for ten thousand years and becomes a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) over all the accomplished *vidyādharas* of the *pāśa*. Eight—

"He shall have a retinue of ten thousand. This is the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the Lotus-Noose (*padmapāśa*). Therefore, a Vidyādhara desiring to accomplish the Vajra-Noose (*vajrapāśa*) should take bark, silk thread, and cotton thread, and fashion them together with a chain (*śaṃkalī*) into a single cord measuring twenty-one thousand units. A Vidyā-staff (*vidyā-karttavya*) made of white sandalwood, four finger-breadths in length, should be fashioned; it should be five-cornered and [represent] the head of a *bhūta*.

6. One should fashion the Naga kings Nanda and Upananda as being bound and encircled by bonds, and they must be bound with a noose adorned with garlands of flames. The Vidyādhara must be pure, wearing clean garments; he must have bathed well and be sprinkled with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), seated upon a seat of *darbha* grass. Facing the cloth painting (*paṭa*), he should grasp the noose with his right hand and recite the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa ten thousand times.

7. By reciting the mantra of the Wrathful King one thousand times, that noose then blazes. Grasping it, one flies up into the sky. All those belonging to the Vajra family, the Tathāgata family, the Maṇi family, and the Padma family—all of them remain at the tip of one’s mouth. One will possess a form, strength, vigor, and prowess equal to Vajrapāṇi. One becomes a lord of the vidyādharas equal to Vajrapāṇi. One lives for twelve thousand divine years. This Vajrapāśa performs all rites.

1. The Destroyer of All Enemies: Wherever one casts the noose—whether upwards or downwards—it brings back everything that is bound, whatever dwells in the mind. It should be cast toward the cardinal or intermediate directions by the King of Wrath (Krodharāja). Whether it be women or men, or others anywhere else, he quickly brings them all back, bound by the noose; of this there is no doubt. Whether it be a god, or a nāga, yakṣa, rākṣasa, gandharva, asura, garuḍa, kinnara, bhūta, or mahoraga—he swiftly draws them all in.

2. "They will undoubtedly be bound by the noose. Having recited the mantra over the noose twenty-one times with the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*), on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, during the dark of night, the noose should be cast in the four directions. At the very moment it is thrown, all obstructors, Vināyakas, and wicked Yakṣas and Rākṣasas become bound by the noose; they stand before the Vidyādhara, become performers of all his tasks, and remain under his control for as long as they live, becoming his servants. This applies to all malevolent spirits (*graha*) through the mere sight [of this] and through resolute conviction (*adhimukti*).

3. Having recited the mantra over the noose one hundred and eight times with the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*), and holding the noose in his hand, he enters the cremation ground and becomes invisible. All the doors of the palaces will be opened. Having gone to the entrance of a subterranean cave (*biladvāra*), he should strike the opening with the Vajrapāśa; all the openings of the caves will be opened, all the mechanical bolts will burst apart, and all wicked men, non-human beings, evil rivers, and venomous snakes—all shall [be overcome].

4. All species of venomous creatures will disappear. Having entered one's dwelling by way of a straight and direct path, one shall accomplish all tasks; then, exit the house once again. This is the ritual procedure for the Vajrapāśa, the performer of all rites. Now, one who desires to accomplish the Vidyādhara of Maṇipāśa must seek out a gem: either a diamond (*vajra*), lapis lazuli (*vaiḍūrya*), crystal (*sphatika*), ruby (*marakata*), or sapphire (*indranīla*).

5. Or [the length] should be one *hasta* or more than the measure of a finger-joint. It should be made of very pure and perfectly refined gold-work, adorned with golden flowers and encircled by pearls, and with *kulita* filaments. Just as a *campaka* flower [is formed], so it should be made; a divine silk thread, well-dyed with beautiful colors, cut to the proper measure of twenty-one *hasta*s, and having the size of a middle finger, should be used. Having fixed the jewel on one side, on the second side a golden *saṃkusīmaṇi* should be made, like the tip of a hair (*vālāgra*). Then, by the Vidyādhara—

6. One must be pure and wear clean garments; one must be well-bathed and have applied the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). Then, facing the cloth painting (*paṭa*), a mandala of all fragrances should be prepared, square in measure and adorned with full vases and incense burners. Incense made of agalloch, sandalwood, and *turuṣka* should be offered. In the central mandala, a divine seat—the seat of the Dharma—should be properly decorated according to the measurements, strewn with flowers, and provided with perfumes and musical instruments. The practitioner of the mantra (*vidyādhara*) must subsist on the three white foods.

7. One must avoid food that has been placed in a broken vessel, food made from poor-quality cloth, and that which is defiled by refuse, as well as leftovers. While reciting the *Amogharājahṛdaya* twenty-one thousand times, one should place a noose upon the Dharma-seat with the right hand and hold it firmly. Then, once the twenty-one thousand recitations are complete, the Vidyādhara—having reached eight thousand [recitations]—should consecrate each individual mustard seed while reciting the *Krodharāja*. Once those eight thousand are complete, the Vidyādhara should perform a magnificent worship of the noble Avalokiteśvara.

1. On a cloth of *ra*duṣya, one should depict the Blessed One Amitābha, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni; a grand worship (*udārapūjā*) should be performed. Then, on the full moon of the fifteenth day, the Vidyādhara, having stayed awake for a day and night, should perform a grand worship of the noose (*pāśa*). Whatever ritual of worship there may be, all of it should be done individually. The Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa should be recited twenty-one times for each [offering] and presented. Then, sitting cross-legged, while reciting the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa throughout the entire day and night, one thousand and eight [recitations]—

2. One should crush *kaika* mustard seeds; when one thousand and eight have been completed, a great trembling will occur. From the cloth painting (*duṣyapaṭa*) of Noble Avalokiteśvara, rays of light of various colors will issue forth, and those [rays] will cause the jewel-noose (*maṇipāśa*) to blaze. It blazes upon the body of the *vidyādhara*. As soon as it has blazed, the *vidyādhara*, grasping the jewel-noose with his right hand, will let out a great roar. Then Noble Avalokiteśvara will appear before the *vidyādhara* in a divine form. Amitā-...

Then the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and the Tathāgata Avalokitaprabharāja, with bodies the color of gold, remain in the sky through miraculous power. Bestowing their approval upon the vidyādhara, they extend their golden-colored arms and place their hands upon the crown of the vidyādhara’s head. They comfort the vidyādhara, saying: "Excellent, excellent, O vidyādhara! You have attained success; the Great Cintāmaṇi Amoghapāśa is purified; you have attained success!"

4. This is the unsurpassed ritual procedure for accomplishing mundane and supramundane activities. O Noble Avalokiteśvara, you who hold the Great Wish-Fulfilling Jewel and the Unfailing Noose (*Amoghapāśa*) for the sake of the Vidyādhara’s fulfillment of all desires—by means of this very body, through diligent effort, grant the accomplishment of the Great Wish-Fulfilling Jewel and the Unfailing Noose; manifest the accomplishment of various mundane and supramundane tasks according to the mental intentions of the practitioner, and bestow the miraculous transformations of various supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*).

5. O Vidyādhara, depart! You have fallen; follow after the world-system of Sukhāvatī. For one who desires to see Sukhāvatī, who desires to worship it, and who desires to worship the Tathāgatas with divine clouds of offerings worthy of a Tathāgata—namely, with divine flowers, divine perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, ornaments, decorations, and garments—if that Vidyādhara wishes to initiate such worship of the Tathāgatas, he [should perform this] upon his head...

6. In battle, one should prepare a fragrant mandala and offer flowers and incense. Holding this Great Unfailing Lasso (Amoghapāśa) which possesses the wish-fulfilling gem (cintāmaṇi), grasping the Amogha-cintāmaṇi-holder in the right hand while [the other] rests in the left hand, and placing the right knee upon the ground, one should meditate with great mindfulness (*mahāmāsikāra*) according to one's intended mental focus. Thus, meditating and recollecting the Heart-mantra of the Unfailing King (*Amogharājahṛdaya*), one should perform the salutation seven times. This is for the Great Wish-fulfilling Gem, the Vast Unfailing...

7. When setting out on a journey, one should call to mind the Heart of Noble Avalokiteśvara. With a heart pervaded by great loving-kindness and great compassion, and being intent on mercy toward all sentient beings, one should recollect the mantra one hundred and eight times. *Namas* to the oceans of the vast expanse of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas established throughout the three times. *Namas* to the Saṅghas of all Pratyekabuddhas and noble Śrāvakas of the past, future, and present. *Namas* to those who have gathered together in the right assembly.

Homage to those who have entered the path; homage to Śāradvatīputra, the great lord of giving; homage to the noble Maitreya and the others, the foremost inhabitants of the excellent Tuṣita heaven together with their excellent retinues. Homage to the noble Tathāgata Amitābha, who dwells in the maṇḍala of Sukhāvatī. Homage to the Triple Gem. Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the great compassionate one. Homage to Viśvarūpāvalokita, Brahmā, and Viṣṇu.

2. The sons of the gods, headed by Maheśvara and Īśvara: Oṃ, Padme, great wish-fulfilling gem, jewel, jewel, unfailing jewel; excellent jewel, great jewel; great unfailing jewel that is the ornament of all Tathāgatas; move, move, move about, lord of those who move at night; you whose arms hold the great lotus; granter of boons, greatly compassionate one; bearer of the great and beautiful form; most excellent Great Bodhisattva; holder of the lotus, seated upon the lotus, crowned with the lotus, wearing a garland; as white as a lotus, your body adorned with lotuses.

3. Thousand-armed one, thousand-eyed one; adorned with various wondrous weapons and mudrās, O thousand-armed one! Victory, victory! O you whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of rays! Bear, bear! O wearer of variegated ornaments! O you whose body is adorned with jewels, gold, diamonds, lapis lazuli, emeralds, sapphires, and rubies! Move, move! O you of variegated feet! O Great Bodhisattva, granter of boons! O you who assume the forms of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara! O Lord of the Lotus (Padmeśvara) Lo...

O Keśvara, Ananteśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Kuvera, O you who assume the forms of the hosts of ṛṣis and Kumāra the commander-in-chief! Dha-ra dha-ra, dhi-ri dhi-ri, dhū-ra dhū-ra! O you who assume the forms of the great elements, consecrated by all the Tathāgatas, remember the pledge! O Blessed One, fulfill them! Deliver them to the further shore! Establish sentient beings! Threaten the wicked! Cast down the obstacles! Slay the stains of the three poisons! Sara sara sara! Drive away evil! Būṃ būṃ būṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ! Accomplish, accomplish! O Great...

5. O jewel among men, holder of the unfailing noose, accomplish for me vast success! Grant it to me, O goddess of the three worlds! O Great Compassionate One, awaken, awaken! Enlighten, enlighten! Fully awaken! O great Paśupati, wearer of the disguise! Display your infinite power of miraculous transformations! *Turū turū*, cross over into the sky! O revealer of the vast celestial palaces, homage be to you! O holder of the vast treasury of merit, O great Amoghasiddhi, *būṃ būṃ*! May they consecrate me throughout the three worlds!

6. *Nadevyā vipulakīrttikare svāhā* // *Bhuvaḥ svāhā* // *Bhūr bhuvaḥ svāhā* // *Amoghavipule svāhā* // *Mahācintāmaṇisiddhe svāhā* // *Sarvasiddhivarade svāhā* // *Oṃ vipuleśvara lokeśvara maheśvara mahācintāmaṇi mahāmoghasiddhe būṃ phaṭ svāhā* // Immediately after reciting this one hundred and eight times, O Vidyādhara, the great unfailing jewel-noose (*mahāmoghamaṇipāśa*) blazes throughout the entire body; [you become] Amoghapāśahasta Avalokiteśvara.

7. He travels through the expanse of the sky by means of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*). He displays a great miraculous transformation (*mahāriddhivikurvvaṇa*) that is like an illusion. He beholds the world-system Sukhāvatī; he beholds the Tathāgata Amitābha together with his assembly and retinue, the mandala of great bodhisattvas, and his excellent celestial palace (*vimāna*), as well as the miracle of supernatural power. A rain from clouds of great offerings will manifest. For all the inhabitants of Sukhāvatī, there will arise great clouds of offerings of light from the Tathāgata Amitāyus.

1. All of them will grant their approval to that *vidyādhara* from the inhabitants of Sukhāvatī and to that Tathāgata Amitāyus. That *vidyādhara* shall hear all those sounds and behold that great rain of offerings. If the *vidyādhara* desires to descend from the sky, he descends by the mere thought of it. If he does not desire it, he remains right there in the sky among all the *vidyādharas* who have attained accomplishments in the firmament and who hold the wish-fulfilling jewel of unfailing and vast success.

2. He shall become a supreme universal monarch (*cakravartin*). His retinue of *vidyādharas* shall be immeasurable. His lifespan shall be eighty hundred thousand great eons (*mahākalpa*). Then, when he descends [to earth], he shall live for ten thousand years. He shall be an object of great worship and reverence, equal to Lokeśvara. He shall be the singular embodiment of all the world. Even the gods shall descend; they shall perform vast and excellent worship for that *vidyādhara*. All sentient beings shall regard him as if he were their only son.

He will be worthy of praise; he will be worthy of worship; he will be worthy of veneration, protected by all the hosts of deities; he will become a great accumulation of the ocean of sacred learning. O Vidyādhara, this applies to all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions and the three times, together with their retinues of Bodhisattva assemblies, as well as the communities of Pratyekabuddhas and noble Śrāvakas, along with the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas within the Buddha’s teaching.

4. With those who are deeply devoted and desirous of making offerings; wishing to fulfill the great mass of merit of all the Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions and the three times; wishing to plant great roots of virtue; wishing to satisfy with the most excellent divine food, possessing the finest of tastes and flavors, and the most sublime divine elixir, the assemblies of all the Tathāgatas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Noble Śrāvakas; and wishing to give a great, magnificent gift—day after day, indeed, one should offer...

5. That Vidyādhara, desiring to perform the *jāpa*, having bathed well, being pure, and wearing clean garments, should prepare a maṇḍala as it is available—O Blessed One, it should be square—in front of the noble Avalokiteśvara. Flowers and incense should be offered while kneeling with palms joined in reverence; he should maintain mindfulness of all the Tathāgatas. And this [is] the Noble Avalokiteśvara’s *Mahācintāmaṇivipulāmoghapūjāpravartana*...

6. One should recollect the *Śvarahṛdaya* seven times with an expansive and vast mental attention (*manasikāra*), performing great clouds of offerings and great gifts of alms, including food, drink, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, garments, ornaments, decorations, and musical instruments such as cymbals, drums, and lutes. While maintaining mental attention upon jewel-trees, fruit-trees, lamp-trees, and wish-fulfilling trees (*kalpavṛkṣa*), one should chant the mantra-dhāraṇī and cause the noose to revolve through the ten directions.

7. Whatever one conceives in the mind and prays for, then, throughout the ten directions and across the three times, within the mandalas and before all the assemblies of the Tathāgatas—as numerous as mustard seeds—a rain of great clouds of offerings will manifest, with every requisite for the retinue being complete and according to one's wishes. In this way, there shall appear an abundance of all requisites for great worship. Such is the great power of this *dhāraṇī* for the performance of the vast and unfailing jewel-offering.

1. The Heart of Avalokiteśvara. If one should recollect this dhāraṇī three times daily at the junctions of day and night, by that, all the mustard-seed mandalas belonging to the Vidyādharas of the three times will be propitiated; they will be honored and revered. One will be planted with a great accumulation of merit and a great root of virtue. All those Tathāgatas of the three times, along with their mustard-seed mandalas, will bestow upon the Vidyādhara the power of memory and intelligence, as well as vigor and vitality, day after day, in every respect.

They will behold the Tathāgatas; they will be constantly sustained by the Tathāgatas; they will be perpetually followed by the noble Avalokiteśvara; and he will always grant them the boon of vision. In this very life, the sufferings, fears, and terrors of saṃsāra that cause them to tremble with fear will be pacified. Furthermore, they shall not fall ill; there shall be no fever, no poison, no artificial toxin, no sorcery, no weapon, no fire, and no water; nor shall any calamity assail their bodies. There shall be no fear of enemies, nor of foreign armies.

There shall be no fear; no fear of enemy armies, no fear of adversaries or enemies, no fear of gods, and no fear of yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, rākṣasas, ḍākinīs, or those who take any form at will (kāmarūpin) or yoginīs. Within a distance of a single yojana, it will not be possible for them to hold [the practitioner back], and they will flee far away. Furthermore, no obstacles shall arise for him. Even if there should be some being who has committed the five acts of immediate retribution, or who has reviled the noble ones—[for such a person, this shall likewise be so].

4. Even for one who has rejected the True Dharma and whose body is enveloped by the karmic obstructions accumulated over hundreds of thousands of kalpas, all of these shall, upon seeing [this], reach total exhaustion without remainder and he shall be liberated—if he performs the recitation of the *anāpatti* (non-offense) mantra one thousand and eight times. It should be recited even with a single fast and a single session of recitation; such a person shall turn back from saṃsāra for hundreds of thousands of millions of births and kalpas, and shall be completely liberated from the karmas resulting from the recitation of the dhāraṇī.

The evils accumulated over thousands of kalpas from former actions are destroyed; one is no longer defiled by the faults of saṃsāra. Like a lotus, one remains unstained; like a lotus, one becomes untainted. From all the obscurations of evil, one attains the five stages within this very life. By practicing while abiding in the rules of the recitation ritual, one attains the stage of non-retrogression. By mere remembrance, one will become perfected in the six perfections.

6. He will come to follow the ten perfections. By reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times day after day, he attains the state of Samantabhadra in this very life. He enters into all mantra rituals (*kalpa*), mandalas, and mudrās. He will enter into all pledges (*samaya*) and become bound to the realization of all accomplishments (*siddhi*). Merely by the sight of a Vidyādhara, the sins that lead to rebirth in the Avīci hell are destroyed. Even if a Vidyādhara enters a cemetery, whether it be a dead bone, a corpse, or a bloated carcass— [The text continues: ...he becomes empowered. By merely seeing him, one is liberated from all suffering. He becomes a master of all mantras and a possessor of the power of the Vidyādharas. He shall never again fall into the lower realms. He will be followed by the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and rākṣasas. He will be honored by all beings. He will be protected by all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. He will be beloved by all women. He will be respected by all kings. He will be invincible to all enemies. He will be successful in all his undertakings. He will be free from all diseases. He will be endowed with great strength and vigor. He will be long-lived. He will be handsome and of noble appearance. 7. Even if it should happen that the shadow of a *vidyādhara* falls upon a corpse, oil, discarded offerings, or a wall—wherever those beings may be, even if they are destined for hell, they shall be liberated from that very moment and will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī. One should not entertain any doubt or uncertainty regarding this. How much more so for those who perform extensive service! Whether it be a son of good family or a daughter of good family, or a monk, a nun, a layman, or a laywoman—[whoever performs this service].

Whether it be one who follows by faith (*śraddhānusārin*) who upholds these dhāraṇīs, recites them, reads them, studies them, reflects upon them, cultivates them, worships them, writes them, or causes them to be written—such a person will certainly become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). In this very life, they shall obtain hundreds of thousands of great and vast qualities. And by means of this very dhāraṇī, in this very life, they shall [attain] the accumulation of all roots of virtue and the roots of virtue devoted to the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*).

It will become complete. This very dhāraṇī alone is sufficient to fulfill all requisites; what need is there for the exhaustion of performing many tasks? Then, having accomplished the Amoghacintāmaṇipāśa of the Vidyādhara, one should perform all activities according to one's mental intentions, and everything will be accomplished. All tasks to be done will be successfully achieved. Just as the direct vision of the noble Avalokiteśvara provides a prophecy and bestows boons, so too does this Amoghacintāmaṇi.

3. One should regard it as a noose; one must not entertain any doubt in this matter. Then, having tied the Vidyādhara-noose around one's neck, taken the jewel in the right hand, and grasped the hook with the left hand, one becomes invisible and enters wherever one desires. By the radiance of the jewel's rays, night shall become like day. One enters everywhere: into the realm of the gods, the realm of the nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, or the realm of the mahoragas, as well as into wind-channels, mountains, and trees.

The doors of the netherworld (pātāla) shall open; he enters everywhere invisibly and emerges again at will, accomplishing whatever he desires. He lives for a hundred divine years, which is equivalent to a human lifespan. All the stains, faults, and impurities of the afflictions (kleśa) will be eliminated. Now, if a Vidyādhara wishes to perform the knowledge (*vijñāna*) that accomplishes his purpose, he should, on the full moon, the eighth day, or the fourteenth day, be well-bathed, pure, and dressed in clean garments.

5. Or, it should be performed in a clean location, purified with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) using cow dung and dried cow manure. In that place, a fragrant mandala should be prepared in the center of another area; it should be strewn with flowers, adorned with full water-jars, and the site should be perfumed with various fragrances and incense. Then, in front of the noble Avalokiteśvara, having arranged a divine seat, one should be well-composed and surrounded by a circular enclosure in the form of a nāga.

6. One should stand at the place in the middle of the jewel; one should stand there. Then, the Vidyādhara should perform worship. He should recite the *Amogharājahṛdaya* twenty-one times. He should recite the *Krodharāja* twenty-one times. He should recite the *Amoghacintāmaṇihṛdaya* one hundred and eight times. Then, incense of agallochum, sandalwood, and turuṣka should be offered. The jewel should be gazed upon; all of that [vision] will be seen within the middle of the noose-jewel—either the vision of a Tathāgata, or the vision of a Bodhisattva, or the vision of a Deva, or the vision of a Nāga.

7. Or [he may have a vision of] yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, or mahoragas; or a vision of battle or combat; or a vision of weapons; or a vision of exhausted weapons; or a transition through births; or a vision of sovereignty; or the acquisition of a village, the acquisition of a district, or the acquisition of a city; or a vision of silver, gold, jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, silver, refined gold, clothing, ornaments, and decorative finery; or a discourse on the elements; or a magical illusion (*indrajāla*). 28b (P49a1, D.50b4)

Whether it be talk of travel, talk of hidden treasures, talk of grain, the acquisition of a maiden, the success of ritual actions (*karmasiddhi*), the success of mantras (*mantrasiddhi*), subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*), or the attainment of sovereignty—all of that is seen clearly through the center of the jewel, whether auspicious or inauspicious; all of this is seen therein. Whether there will be rain or no rain; disturbances, calamities, or epidemics; death, great mortality, death of cattle, death of goats, death of horses, or death of elephants; or fear of great terror, whether from one's own army or an enemy army—all that is seen exactly as it appears in the mirror of the jewel. Whatever one thinks of, whatever one prays for—si-

Whether it be prosperity or failure, good or bad—everything is seen here, and there shall be no doubt, no uncertainty, no hesitation, nor any other state of mind. During a time of excessive rain, one should place a *maṇi* jewel in a lake; then the rain will fall according to one's desire. To stop excessive rain, one should show the "sky-jewel" (*ākāśamaṇi*); the excessive rain is pacified. At sunrise, one should show the sun from a position facing it; the sun descends and grants all boons. One should show the new moon from a position facing it; the young moon descends.

3. It bestows the boons of all desires. It shall show the middle of a great river, where great jewels appear. It shall show a forest glade, where all medicinal substances stand before one in their own forms; whatever one prays for, one should take it. It shall show a mountain cleft, where all medicinal herbs blaze, to be taken according to one's wish. It shall show a heap of grain, where all types of grain are transferred; they appear wherever one desires. In the place of the Mother, it shall show Mahākāla.

4. One should stand with the head bowed; Mahākāla, together with his retinue of the assembly of Mothers, will appear in his own form before one and become subject to one's will. He will perform all tasks and activities. One should present him to the king; [the deity will show] the king along with his excellent fourfold army, his circle of ministers, his harem and attendants, as well as gold, bullion, jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, silver, and refined gold, and the wonders of garments, ornaments, decorations, and celestial palaces.

They remain under one's control and shall serve [the practitioner] for as long as they live. While brandishing a noose in the midst of a great multitude, one should recollect the *Amoghasiddhi-cintāmaṇi-dhāraṇī* and cause a rain of flowers, fruits, and celestial palaces (*vimāna*) to fall according to one’s desires. Having fixed it upon the top of a banner and established it as a refuge at the head of the palace of an anointed Kṣatriya king, one must observe the noble eightfold fast (*āryāṣṭāṅgopavāsa*) and be intent on compassion for all sentient beings. The *Amogharāja-hṛdaya* [is to be recited] twenty-one times—

6. While reciting [the mantra] one hundred times, one should call to mind the twenty-one wrathful kings (*krodharāja*). Then, while reciting the *Amoghasiddhi-cintāmaṇi-dhāraṇī* one hundred and eight times, if one recites it with a loud voice for a full eight hundred times, rain will manifest according to one’s mental wish. It rains down wealth, grain, clothing, ornaments, flowers, and fruits. All strife, quarrels, conflicts, disputes, famine, the perils of wilderness travel, and calamities—by the power of that noble Avalokiteśvara—[shall cease].

7. It does not come to an end; all shall attain peace; it shall grant fearlessness to all sentient beings; they shall be liberated from all fears and enmities; all the wicked, even down to the most ferocious wild beasts, shall dwell in loving-kindness (*maitrī*); all sentient beings shall become free from deficiency; and all their heart's desires shall be fulfilled. This concludes the *Amoghacintāmaṇimahāpāśasādhana*. Now, for one who wishes to accomplish the *Vidyādhara-khaḍgapāśa*, that practitioner— 29a (P.50a3, D.51b4)

1. A sword sixteen finger-breadths in length must not be made of iron; its hilt must be made of silver, and it must have a golden flame. A bark-cord, a *arka*-cord, and a *kośa*-cord—each sixteen cubits long on one side—must be fashioned as a perfectly complete means for accomplishing the task; they must be of correct measure and tripled. Then the *vidyādhara*, being pure, wearing clean garments, and having bathed well, must attach the noose and sword; standing upon a circular platform, he should grasp them with his right hand.

2. [The practitioner], wrathful with a face fierce with a frown, seated in the paryanka posture, facing the cloth-painting (paṭa) of Noble Avalokiteśvara, should recite the mantra eight thousand times while acting as the Wrathful King (Krodharāja). Upon the completion of the eighth thousand recitations, the sword blazes; the Vidyādhara flies into the sky and shall become a sovereign universal monarch (cakravartin) over all accomplished Vidyādharas of the sword-mantra. He will possess unimpeded strength and prowess and shall live for eighteen thousand years. Alternatively, holding a noose in his left hand with his right—

3. Taking the sword with a wrathful *hūṃ* sound and pressing it down, one will become invisible. One will become the sovereign king, a universal monarch (*cakravartin*), over all those who have attained the power of invisibility, including the *pāśa-khaḍga-vidyādharas*. One’s lifespan will be ten thousand years. Therefore, by brandishing the sword with a wrathful *vidyādhara*, all obstacles, *vināyakas*, wicked *yakṣas* and *rākṣasas*, and all spirits will be severed. If one brandishes it once in the midst of battle, all the warriors—

Various weapons will be severed; they will be paralyzed. All things in the ten directions will tremble. While wandering through the midst of the cremation grounds, the [weapons] of all those fierce-behaved beings dwelling in the cremation grounds will be severed. All naked dwellings will be [severed]; while wandering through the openings of the chasms, all mechanical door-panels will be severed. All door-bolts will be severed. All evil—

5. They will become obstructors and destroyers of those who move among non-human beings; they will utterly perish, and all other activities will be performed according to one's desire. This is the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the *khaḍga* (sword). Now, by a *vidyādhara* who wishes to accomplish the *nāgapāśa* (serpent-noose), that *vidyādhara* should first accomplish five threads, dye them with five colors, have them woven, and then accomplish the well-prepared and well-perfected [noose] of the correct measurement.

6. Then, one should combine divine flour made of food, honey-flower, juice-flower, *manacchilā*, lotus-stamen, *nāgapuṣpa*, and *arkakṣīra*, together with vermilion (*hiṅgula*), all in equal proportions; having ground them very finely and well-mixed, one should have a circular snake-mandala made, measuring eight hundred and eight [units], shaped like a three-headed hood, using gold for its covering, which should be bound wherever the sixfold supreme noose has fallen by the Vidyādhara who has recited the *Amogharāja* mantra.

7. Having become pure, having bathed well, and wearing clean garments, one should prepare a square maṇḍala of cow dung according to the proper measure. One should perform worship with fragrant scents, scattering flowers and arranging full vases. The central area of the maṇḍala should be adorned with banners. One should set out a divine seat; upon that, one should place a circular *nāgapāśa* (serpent-noose). In the center of the serpent’s hood, one should have [the figures] face the east and offer three white *bali* offerings. One should present the three white *bali* offerings, as well as water for the feet (*argha-pādya*), incense, lamps, and various kinds of perfumes.

1. One should prepare a maṇḍala strewn with *lāja* (fried grain), sesame seeds, aloeswood (*agaru*), and frankincense (*turuṣka*). Having placed the noble Avalokiteśvara facing [the practitioner], the Vidyādhara, seated in the cross-legged posture (*paryaṅka*), should perform great worship and carry out the great procedure of recitation (*jāpavidhi*). Having recited the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya eight thousand times—reciting the supreme recitation of the Krodha one thousand and eight times—one should recite over each individual sesame seed and scatter them upon the head of the Nāga. When all tasks are fully accomplished, the Nāga will always blaze forth. [One should place] the noose at the site...

2. It will move; it rises from the seat to the height of four finger-breadths. Then it must be grasped by the *vidyādhara*, and he becomes invisible. "Go to the abode of the *nāgas*; having stayed at the *nāga* lake, the gates of the *nāga* abode will be opened. The *vidyādhara* should enter, recollect the King Amogha, and whirl the *nāga*-lasso three times. Then the *nāga* king, together with his retinue and harem, will come and pay homage to the *vidyādhara*. They say: 'Enter, O *vidyādhara*. Then the *vidyādhara* enters.

3. The practitioner of the spell (*vidyādhara*) should enter while grasping the serpent-noose (*nāgapāśa*) and whirling it; then that practitioner of the spell will no longer see those faults of the serpents (*nāgadoṣa*), and they will become invisible. All the mechanical devices, doors, and bolts shall be severed and broken. As soon as he has entered, a divine Naga maiden arrives—beautiful, pleasing, adorned with all ornaments, and wearing garlands of jewels. She offers herself to the practitioner of the spell, who should then take hold of her.

4. Having established it, as soon as it is established, the Naga maiden rises into the sky together with him; two breasts flow with milk, which must be caught and drunk by the Vidyadhara. His lifespan will become twelve thousand years. His hair will be curled like a ringlet, and he will become a universal monarch (cakravartin), the sovereign lord of all Naga kings. He will possess great strength, vigor, and prowess. Therefore, having reminded the Vidyadhara of the heart-mantra of the Naga-noose, [one should act] with a sprig of Karavira.

5. One should honor the noble one. Whatever one draws forth, if one contemplates it with the mind, all of it is accomplished in an instant. During a time of drought, one should whirl the nāga-noose in a high place; by merely whirling it once, a great torrent of rain falls. During a time of excessive rain, having lowered the nāga-noose in a high place, the excessive rain will be pacified. During a time of cold winds and frost, at dawn, one should whirl the nāga-noose in the four directions.

6. Lightning falls for a hundred *yojanas* all around; all cold winds and lightning bolts become bound. Grasping the *nāga*-lasso with the right hand and holding a *nāga* with the left hand, whether in spring, autumn, or during the rainy season, one should remember the Wrathful King while whirling the lasso. It should be cast into the sky. Whatever flowers and fruits are produced, they are all taken away; these become divine, well-ripened, and perfectly transformed foods that fall from the expanse of the sky to the earth. If [one does this] once...

7. While the King of Wrath is being set in motion and rotated twenty times, all the palaces, ornaments, garments, decorations, and finery of the *nāgas* fall to the ground. If a *vidyādhara*, even once, rotates [the wheel] without hesitation while recollecting the King of Wrath, then the *nāgas*, together with their retinues and their palaces, fall to the surface of the earth. If a *vidyādhara* desires to bring a king under his control, along with his inner harem and retinue, he should place a noose and eight thousand mustard seeds [there].

1. Having recited the *Amogharāja* mantra over a staff, strike [the enemy]; then, taking up the serpent-noose (*nāgapāśa*), whirl that noose specifically toward whichever direction King Rājagṛha lies. The king, together with his harem and retinue, will become submissive and shall remain so for as long as they live. When fighting in battle, one should recite the *Krodharāja* mantra and throw the noose into the midst of the fray. A great venomous serpent (*āśīviṣa*) will appear—fierce-eyed, with a flickering tongue and eyes glowing like burning coals—at the mere sight of whom the fourfold army, in every direction and sub-direction, [will be overcome].
They flee away. Whatever task is present in the mind, perform all those tasks accordingly. Thus ends the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the Nāgapāśa.

Amoghapāśakalparāja – Part III 30a2 (P52a7, D.54a1) 2. Then, one who wishes to accomplish the noose of Bhūteśvara should have the hair of a yak-tail (*camarivāla*) and a large lock of hair (*mahākeśa*) woven together into a trident three *aṅgulas* in length. It should then be made of iron. Thereafter, while reciting the Heart-mantra of Amogharāja one thousand and eight times, and while reciting the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*) one thousand and eight times, one should fast for a day and night.

3. One must be clean, wearing pure garments, and well-bathed. It should be accomplished on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight throughout the day and night. Then, having taken a trident-noose, one will become like Bhūteśvara in form. As the lord of all *bhūtas*, one lives for eight thousand years. One will become the master of all the palaces of the *bhūtas*. One should enter the cremation ground with a noose in hand; then all those dwelling in the cremation ground stand before one at the gates of all their abodes.

4. "The gates are opened; enter as you please and do whatever you wish. One should bind this [mantra] around the neck of the deceased while recollecting the Wrathful King Ākaṭṭaya. Then he approaches the deceased and says whatever one desires; he does whatever one commands and is released, being set free. A yakṣa image should be bound around the neck while recollecting the Wrathful King Ākaṭṭaya with a wrathful mind; that yakṣa will appear before one. [The mantra of] the Vidyā—

5. Dharas speaks: "Command me, O Lord; I shall do it. The Vidyādhara should say: "Be my servant and messenger for as long as you live. [She replies: "So be it. Then, day after day, he should command her, and she will do everything. One should bind the neck of the Yakṣiṇī while recollecting Krodharāja; the Yakṣiṇī comes and stands before the Vidyādhara. She gazes at the Vidyādhara with unblinking eyes and says: "What do you request? The Vidyādhara [should say]: "By the Vidyādhara..."

One should say: "Perform for me the three means of accomplishing my purpose. If it is the mother, she protects like a son with food, drink, bedding, clothing, wealth, and grain. If it is the wife, she provides all requisites, grants sovereignty and lordship, and moves about in play. If it is the sister, she fulfills all desires and wishes; she will perform all tasks, run everywhere, and return day after day, giving ornaments, garments, and decorations.

Day after day, he brings another celestial woman for the sake of play. One should bind [the mantra] around the neck of Vaiśravaṇa; while reciting the *krodhamantra* with anger and pulling [the cord], Vaiśravaṇa then arrives. Day after day, he gives a thousand *dināra*s and gives a thousand pieces of gold. Day after day, gifts must be given and meritorious deeds performed. It should be bound around the neck of Mahākāla; having recited the *krodharāja* seven times over the right hand, one should strike Mahākāla with a slap while angry, causing him to cry out.

1. The Vidyādhara must not be afraid; rather, he should strike him again while enraged. Then [Mahākāla] sheds tears. The Vidyādhara should take those tears and apply them as a *tilaka* (forehead mark). He will become invisible and see all treasures (*nidhāna*). Then the Vidyādhara should strike him again with a slap. Thereupon Mahākāla vomits blood. The Vidyādhara should touch it, and he will travel through the sky and become a great lord of the Yakṣas (*mahāyakṣādhipati*). Having offered *guggulu* incense and recollecting the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*), [Mahākāla] appears before him in his own form.

2. By [this] method, she grants all boons as desired; the entire host of mothers and their retinues remain under one's control. All other tasks that are to be performed according to one’s will should be carried out. This is the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the Triple-Spear Noose (*triśūla-pāśa*). Now, I shall explain the ritual procedure of the Chapter on the Noose (*pāśa-paṭala*), the unsurpassed method for the accomplishment of reality (*tattva-sādhana*). Displaying the various colors and forms of the Lord of the World through the miraculous power of the illusion-like (*māyopama*) samādhi, he manifested his universal form (*viśvarūpa*), possessing a thousand arms and a thousand eyes, and infinite—

3. The vision [of him] is the vision of the three worlds; his form is the manifestation of various kinds of forms for the sake of disciplining those to be trained. Manifesting this most secret form, the accomplishment of the noose is for the sake of compassion toward all sentient beings; the attainment of the vidyā is the inner reality in truth. Therefore, O wise King of Vidyās, for one who follows to the next world and seeks Buddhahood, and who desires the vision of all the Tathāgatas, and wishes to see Lokeśvara, the Protector who transcends the world, in truth—this [is] for him.

4. For one who practices supreme devotion toward this King of Rituals (*kalparāja*), may there arise faith, reverence, truthfulness, and the highest grace. For one who desires various forms of liberation, various manifestations of form and various means are revealed. This is the unsurpassed *Amogharāja-kalpa*. One attains the unfailing accomplishment (*amoghasiddhi*) and the highest unfailing fruit; the unfailing supramundane accomplishment (*lokottarasiddhi*) is empowered by all the Buddhas. It is the unfailing [teaching] of the Lord of the World (*lokanātha*), which bestows the boon of worldly sovereignty; it is the unfailing mundane accomplishment (*laukikīsiddhi*).

5. For one who desires a boon according to their wish, there is the unfailing and vast miraculous display of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*) within the junctures of transformations. Therefore, with every effort, purify yourself according to the prescribed ritual manual and in accordance with the cloth for the painting (*paṭaduṣya*). Constantly perform the recitation (*jāpakarman*) and always behold the painting. [Therein are] nooses of various forms, as well as the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*), the King of Knowledge (*vidyārāja*), the deities of the mandala, the deity of fire, the fire-oblation (*homa*), Vāyu, Varuṇa, and those of fierce form.

And the gentle forms of deities, the appearance of nāgas, and the forms of yakṣas and rākṣasas; bhūtas, asuras, gandharvas, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas—all these he displays to the Lord of the World, the bestower of boons. He displays Yama, Kubera, Agni, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Kumāra, Īśvara-deva, and Maheśvara; the Sun, the gentle forms, the lunar mansions, and the deities of the lunar days—these various kinds of forms the Lord of the World displays out of a desire for the welfare of sentient beings, for the sake of their discipline, and for the path of liberation.

7. Since [the Lord] reveals himself to sentient beings, one should never entertain doubt. According to the nature of the task, according to the means, according to the type of cloth for the painting, and according to the appropriate method of binding with cords; in whatever place he is worshipped, wherever the mind rejoices; by whichever mudrā he is visualized, and by whichever mandalas are arranged—everywhere, from the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the Protector, the Savior, the Leader, and the Guru, one obtains unfailing accomplishment (*amogha-siddhi*), which bestows unfailing fruit. Unfailing everywhere...

1. And he shall touch the feet of the Sage who turns the supreme Wheel of Dharma. [This is] the ritual procedure for accomplishing the binding of fetters and the wearing of rags. Now, I shall explain the rite of *homa*, which accomplishes all purposes of action unfailingly; it immediately removes all sins, destroys all obscurations, crushes all enemies, annihilates all obstacles, wards off all malevolent beings, is the most excellent destroyer of all impurities, and one is liberated from the sufferings of the sixteen hells. It always removes the eight terrible fears and is the supreme subduer of foes. It is the best of many...

2. It is a protection that immediately removes all diseases; it pacifies strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes. It wards off famine and the perils of wilderness travel, and destroys calamities and misfortunes. It draws forth divine happiness and the like; because it is the reality that accomplishes Buddhahood, it is the supreme means for achieving all siddhis, the unsurpassed awakening of a Buddha. It is common to all sentient beings, yet the granting of its boon is extremely difficult to obtain. The deities are always pleased, and the nāgas find joy in it. The Tathāgatas constantly look upon it day and night.

3. There is no doubt about this: the Bodhisattvas, being well-composed, will always rejoice; and Lokeśvara, the Bestower of Boons, will eternally abide here—of this there is no doubt. Furthermore, the four Great Kings, together with their retinues and ministers, will be constantly attached to him for the sake of protection at all times. Then, the Vidyādhara should perform a fire-oblation (*homa*) here, having gathered at a wise and pure location, in a secluded spot on clean ground, free from disturbance.

4. From this [tantra], one obtains the rites of pacification (*śāntika*), enrichment (*pauṣṭika*), and subjugation (*abhicāruka*). The *śāntika* rite is for the benefit of all sentient beings and the pacification of all evils. Through the *pauṣṭika* rite, one attains prosperity; everything shall be free from deficiency. Through the *abhicāruka* rite, there is the suppression of enemies, wicked Vināyakas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Guhyakas, as well as those of fierce mind who are terrified and trembling with fear. This is the unsurpassed accomplishment of mantra. The ritual procedure for the fire-oblation (*homa*) is prescribed for both this world and the next. [Next is] the invocation (*āvāhana*).

5. The fire-god, the deities, the *nāgas*, and likewise the *vidyādharas*—one should always construct a trench in the shape of a lotus and draw a lotus within it. One should construct the trench for the central filament of the lotus according to the prescribed rule; one should have the trenches made either square or circular. One should make it well-finished, very white, well-concealed, well-proportioned, and well-praised; one should perform [the rite] on an auspicious lunar day and under a favorable constellation. Having made it extensive and rich in auspiciousness, one should perform a most beautiful *bali*-offering with incense and flowers.

6. Having established the divine [fire] with celestial [mantras] on all sides, first perform the invocation (*āvāha*) of Agni, and afterwards cause the fire-offering rites (*homakarman*) to be performed. Having become pure, the Vidyādhara—having bathed well and wearing clean garments—should perform the ritual of mantra-recitation (*mantrajāpavidhi*) and have the binding of the boundary (*sīmābandha*) performed here. Likewise, he should perform self-protection, the binding of the topknot (*śikhābandha*), protection of others, the binding of the maṇḍala, and the protection of his companions. Always kindling firewood from the *arka* tree and indeed from fragrant woods, he should consume ghee, mustard seeds, and parched grain as his "food of fire" (*agnibhojana*).

7. Twenty. Then, having invoked the deity Agni: Oṃ namaḥ! O Agnijvāla, Mahājvāla, Jyotsnyā-prabhāmaṇḍala, Sarvavit! You are the recipient of the *āhuti* and *prahuti* offerings; you are the fire of heat, the blazing flame, the smoke, the breath, and the radiance from your mouth. You are the sharp-rayed forest fire and the lightning; you are the chief consumer of oblations (*hutāsana*). O foremost of all gods, O great hero among all yakṣas, O Great Victor, O one of great strength, O irresistible one! You are the one who causes all things to blaze forth, the one who is like the sky, the one who is like a cloud, and the one whose orb is worshipped and honored. 31b (P55a3, D.56b5)

1. O you who are skilled in the divine form that pervades everywhere; O invoker of all-pervading deities, O consumer of oblations, O fire! O dispeller of darkness, O you who are freed from the gloom by your rays! O you whose food consists of the fragrant Priyaṅgu fruit and the finest of delicious flavors! O you who are subtle, sharp, and the reviver of the dead, O beloved! O you who wear ashes as flowers, ashes as clothing, and who serve with garments of ash, always covered in ash! O you who consume smoke and are filled with it! O you who possess the perfection of digestion and the finest of tastes, who rains down preeminence everywhere! O you who are everywhere irresistible, who are eternally touched and bitten, yet do not perish...

2. <Muñcasi>. O God of thirty-two forms, deity whose face is fire, you who possess the power to dispel lack of appetite and disease, great Atharvan, expert among gods, O God of Gods: accomplish the noble rite quickly and according to reality. *Oṃ jvala jvala tiṣṭha samayaṃ huru huru hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. With this, one should worship the fire; one should consecrate it seven times with the mantra. One should offer guggulu and mustard seeds smeared with clarified butter by the handful—seven handfuls in total. Likewise, the water for honor (*argha*) and the water for the feet (*pādya*) should be offered, as well as handful after handful of perfumes and unguents.

3. One should not offer incense; rather, one should offer a handful of fruit. Then, one should sprinkle with water and perform the ritual sipping (*upaspṛśana*). [One should worship] the deities in their proper sequence. Then the *vidyādhara* should commence the fire-offering (*homakarma*) with well-purified fragrant wood: *plakṣa*, *udumbara*, *sumanā*, *campaka*, and *karṇikāra*; likewise *padma*, *utpala*, *devadāru*, fragrant *candana*, and the wood of the *bodhi* tree, as well as other fragrant woods.

4. Or else, one who is confident should prepare wooden planks for the rites of pacification using *śamī* wood, as well as *argha* and *darbha* grass. Having kindled the fire with these, one should perform the *homa* rituals. Having gathered together in one place sandalwood powder, *agaru*, *turuṣka*, and so forth, as well as *kunda*, *urusaturuṣka*, *spṛkā*, *gandhamāṃsī*, and *priyaṅgu*, and having mixed them with ghee and fresh butter, one should offer them into the sacrificial fire while reciting the *Amogharāja* mantra one hundred and eight times. One should thus perform the oblation.

5. When eight thousand [recitations] have been completed with the noble Avalokiteśvara before him, at the middle of the night he rises up, blazing in the form of the deity Agni. Well-established, he surveys and gazes upon the ten directions all around. He grants his approval to the knowledge-holder (vidyādhara), saying: "Excellent, excellent, O knowledge-holder! I am well-pleased; you have accomplished it, O knowledge-holder. Speak the supreme procedure for the fire-oblation (homavidhi); I shall grant everything. Then the knowledge-holder should request a boon according to his desire.

6. He gives everything according to your request. Then the *vidyādhara* should offer water for the feet (*arghapādya*) and present the ritual offering (*balikarma*). Thereafter, the *vidyādhara*, having kindled a fire with fruit-wood, should offer a large oblation (*piṇḍa*) smeared with ghee while reciting the *Amogharājahṛdaya* one thousand and eight times. When the full one thousand and eight recitations are completed, a man half the size of a human emerges from the middle of the chasm. He presents a silver vessel filled with food the size of a thigh. The *vidyādhara* should take it; as soon as it is taken—

7. One leaps into the sky. From the body of the *vidyādhara*, rays of fire-flames issue forth. Having consumed that, one will have a lifespan of ten thousand years. One will become a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) among the *vidyādharas* who move through the sky. For ten eons, one will remember former births. The *amogharāja-kalpa-vimokṣa-maṇḍala* will abide at the tip of one’s mouth. If one does not grasp the vessel, then one should offer oblations twenty-one more times; a great trembling will occur. [Then one will appear in the form of the noble Avalokiteśvara. 32a (P56a2, D.57b4)

1. He does not stand before [the practitioner]. He consoles the *vidyādhara*, saying: "Excellent, excellent, *vidyādhara*! Well done by you, *vidyādhara*, regarding the ritual of the fire-oblation (*homavidhi*). Speak your boon; I shall grant it. Then the *vidyādhara* should state his boon according to his desire, and then [the deity] grants everything. The noble Avalokiteśvara takes a vessel from the presence of the man and hands it over with his own hand to the *vidyādhara*. Having taken it, the *vidyādhara* eats that ball of food; as soon as it is consumed, he travels through the sky by means of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*), amidst flames—

The body within the womb blazes; flames of various colors appear. He will become an Amogha Vidyādhara Cakravartin. His retinue of Vidyādharas will consist of ninety-two hundred thousand billion *koṭiniyuta* Vidyādharas, equal in number to the sands of the river Ganges. Ninety-two hundred thousand billion palaces and celestial mansions, equal to the sands of the river Ganges, will appear as abodes established by Amogha. All these shall be celestial mansions of the seven jewels, together with mountains.

3. With forests containing trees and fruit-bearing trees laden with flowers, some with various wonderful creepers, branches, leaves, roots, and sprouts; some with golden flowers, some with silver flowers, and some with flowers made of the seven various jewels; and adorned with palaces by means of merits and various wonderful divine flowers—such as *śāla*, *tāla*, *campaka*, *latā*, *tāla-gandha*, *vārṣika*, *sumana*, *yūthikā*, *taraṇaka*, and *kupya* flowers—as well as groves, gardens, delightful places, and celestial mansions (*vimāna*).

It will come to pass. Their desires will be delightful. There will be divine rivers, streams, lakes, ponds, and pools filled with water scented with divine sandalwood; there will be palaces made of the seven precious gems, adorned with divine lotuses—blue, red, white, and yellow—and strewn with golden sands. It will be a palace frequented by hosts of divine apsarases, goddesses, kinnarīs, and gandharvas, as well as by gods, dānavas, gandharvas, nāgas, and vidyādharas.

Surrounded by hosts of kinnaras and endowed with divine enjoyments and celestial palaces, he sports, delights, and enjoys himself in every abode until he reaches the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*). Seated at the seat of awakening, he maintains this single measure of lifespan from the turning of the wheel of Dharma until his final nirvāṇa. Such is the unsurpassed great accomplishment; the Noble Avalokiteśvara remains constantly attached to him until the end of awakening.

6. *M* // Thus, this method for obtaining alms-food, which is exceedingly difficult to find, shall cause one to go to the assembly of all Tathāgatas throughout all Buddha-fields in the ten directions. One shall hear the Dharma in the presence of all Tathāgatas. And that garland of light-rays illuminates the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system. This is the Heart of the Noble Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa, which is honored by all Bodhisattvas, and the chapter on the mantras, mudrās, and ritual procedures for the maṇḍala of liberation.

The entire collection of all ritual procedures for accomplishment (*sādhanavidhi*) and the sublime maṇḍalas of all the kalpas will abide before his very face. Hundreds of thousands of millions of nāga kings will remain under his control at all times; all the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, and kinnaras will remain under his control. Up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, the gods will always follow that vidyādhara, and he will have a great retinue constantly and perpetually at his service. Effortlessly, [he will possess] divine flavors, the finest tastes, and food and drink.

1. It will manifest through celestial palaces (*vimāna*) of various kinds; likewise, it will manifest as celestial palaces adorned with diverse garments, ornaments, and decorations. Such are the procedures for the fire-oblation (*homavidhi*). One obtains the accomplishment of manifestation, which is an unfailing means of attainment (*amoghasādhana*). Alternatively, even for those of meager fortune who lack the seeds of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, by merely holding the vessel together with that [substance], one obtains royal sovereignty. One experiences divine and human splendor. Merely by being touched, one attains a divine lifespan of eighty-four thousand years.

It will open [the gates of liberation]. Furthermore, diseases shall no longer prevail over him, nor shall there be the obscurations of evil or the afflictions (*kleśa*). All adversaries, enemies, and those who are wicked or malicious shall be rendered powerless. He will be completely liberated from all realms of hell, the animal womb, the world of Yama, and the domain of hungry ghosts (*preta*). He will become uniquely worthy of worship by all sentient beings. Men, women, boys, and girls will long to behold him, and he will be victorious everywhere. He will obtain speech that is never in vain and is always accepted.

3. At the time of death, they will have the desire to behold all the Tathāgatas; they will obtain the direct vision of the noble Avalokiteśvara. With mindfulness well-established, they will pass away. Having passed away, they will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī through its co-existent nature. They will be born from lotuses of miraculous birth. In every birth, they will remember their past lives. Furthermore, they will never again go to the lower realms, nor will they ever again [enter] a mother’s [womb].

4. He will be reborn from womb to womb; and he will constantly travel from Buddha-field to Buddha-field in order to behold all the Tathāgatas and all the Bodhisattvas. One should make a *tilaka* on the forehead, and one will become invisible everywhere through the mantra. By the mere act of remembering the deity of fire (*agnidevatā*) a hundred times, she appears before one in her own form; she will grant all boons and accomplish all tasks. Now, for one who wishes to accomplish the *Amoghapiṇḍa*:

5. That vidyādhara should prepare a ball of cooked rice mixed with boiled grain (*kulmāṣa*), the size of a *bilva* fruit, and containing balls of ghee, molasses, sugar, and honey. Then, having kindled a fire of *karavīra* wood, he should offer each ball into the middle of the fire after reciting the mantra over it seven times; he should offer one hundred and eight oblations. This should be done three times a day for three days. Thereafter, the vidyādhara should take mustard seeds and flowers as they are available, mix them together, recite the mantra over them twenty-one times, and cast them into the middle of the fire.

6. One should consecrate *lāja* and mustard seeds seven times with the King of Wrath (*Krodharāja*). Then, from the midst of the fire, the deity of Fire (*Agnidevatā*) emerges with half of her body and presents to the Vidyādhara a vessel made of the seven jewels, filled with a *piṇḍa*. [She says: "Accept this divine great *piṇḍa* of the Vidyādhara! O Siddha, the ritual procedure for the *piṇḍa* has been accomplished by you. Thereupon, the Vidyādhara should take that vessel of *piṇḍa*; as soon as he touches it, an elixir (*rasāyana*) begins to work. He leaps into the sky, and his hair becomes curled and ringed.

They shall be released; his complexion shall become pure; he shall become a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) of the *vidyādharas*. He shall have a retinue of sixty-eight thousand *vidyādhara* universal monarchs. The fire deities, together with their abodes, celestial palaces, and retinues, shall remain under his control. They shall perform all his tasks. Whosoever’s alms-bowl he touches, that person shall become a great accumulation of an ocean of learning. And this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, honored by all bodhisattvas, is a maṇḍala of liberation.

The entire chapter and ritual manual of the *Samudramantra* will remain before his very eyes. Day by day, he will recite a thousand verses and master them. In a future birth, he will go to the world-system of Sukhāvatī; he will be born from spontaneously appearing lotuses and will possess the recollection of his past lives. Furthermore, there shall never again be any loss of his memory; his words will be authoritative, he will be beloved by all sentient beings, and he will be worthy of great honor. Having made a *tilaka* on his forehead, [he will attain] invisibility...

2. He will become one who has mastery over all spirits, yakṣas, and rākṣasas. All palaces will stand with their doors opened wide. For anyone seeking a wife or a son, by eating that alms-food (piṇḍa), there will be the attainment of a son—one who is handsome, pleasing, and beautiful to behold, endowed with the most excellent and abundant complexion, long-lived, intelligent, and wise; one who is proficient in all treatises. Therefore, one who desires to feed a hundred thousand people should prepare milk-rice (pāyasa) in a pure place, free from [impurities].

3. In the family [of the practitioner], while performing the ritual with *karavīra* flowers, one should recollect the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya-mantra* until it is accomplished. Then, one should sprinkle water mixed with white mustard seeds over which the *Krodharāja* has been recited. Next, one should place a food offering (*piṇḍa*) inside a single pot of milk-rice (*pāyasa*). Then, in the first portion, the Three Jewels should be presented with the food offering. After that, one should offer it to the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara; then, one should offer it to the noble Mañjuśrī. Then, the śramaṇas—

It should be given to Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras; to women, men, boys, and girls; and to the wretched, the needy, travelers, and beggars. Even if hundreds of thousands of people eat as much as they desire, no decrease or increase will be perceived in that vessel, nor will there be any exhaustion therein. And all those who have eaten that food shall be freed from all previous obscurations, sins, and defilements; they shall be free from all diseases; and [free] from all calamities and all adversaries—

5. They shall not be overcome by the fear of enemies; they shall not be overcome by the fear of any spirits, yakṣas, or rākṣasas. Their bodies shall become supple and delicate. They shall be resounded by the divine, sweet, soft, and gladdening songs of the kinnaras. They shall be eternally free from all evil and suffering. And for as long as they live, they shall be constantly endowed with happiness. In every future birth, they shall all go to the state of the Sugata. And that bowl-full of milk-rice [should be placed] in a high place.

6. Having prepared a mandala in an open space and placed that bowl upon the mandala, one offers it to all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions. As soon as it is offered, before each of those hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas—equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā—in every single buddha-field of the ten directions, there appears divine food of a hundred flavors and a divine bowl filled with alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*). Divine sandalwood mandalas appear, strewn with divine flowers. Thus he—

7. All the Tathāgatas residing within the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, together with their circles of assemblies, including the hosts of bodhisattvas and the communities of śrāvakas, are fully satisfied by that excellent divine food of a hundred flavors. Consequently, all those Tathāgatas, along with their circles of assemblies, the hosts of bodhisattvas, and the communities of śrāvakas, purify the merit-offering (*dakṣiṇā*) for that vidyādhara and his patron (*dānapati*). By means of that purified merit-offering, through the power of cultivation, he shall obtain great sovereignty in this very life or in another birth. Great—

1. He will become enriched with the gold of spiritual accomplishment (*sādhana*); he will become enriched with abundant treasuries and granaries; he will be attended by all the Tathāgatas; he will have a desire to behold all the Bodhisattvas; and all the deities will provide him with protection, defense, and guardianship. Now, one who wishes to bring a king, his harem, and his fourfold army under control, that Vidyādhara must be pure, wearing clean garments, and well-bathed. With a vessel made of *aneya* wood, [he should offer] ghee-soaked...

2. One should offer one thousand and eight oblations. Having kindled the fire with fuel-sticks of *devadāru* and *arka* wood, by means of this full thousand-and-eightfold oblation, the king—along with his harem, retinue, and fourfold army—remains under one's control, as do [all beings] through wealth and person. By practicing for three nights, all the nāga kings remain under one's control together with their abodes and retinues. By practicing for five nights, all bhūtas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, together with all their retinues, [remain under one's control].

They remain under one's control. By practicing for seven nights, all the vidyādharas remain under one's control. By practicing for seven nights, the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven headed by Śakra, along with all the hosts of apsarases and the auspicious celestial maidens, descend; they remain under one's control and shall serve one for as long as life lasts. Beginning from the full moon until the eighth day and the fifteenth, at the three junctions of the day, one should offer oblations twenty-one times with fuel-sticks of *arka* wood into the fire.

Having kindled [the fire] on the full moon of the fifteenth day, he appears before the practitioner in the form of the noble Avalokiteśvara. He gives his approval to the knowledge-holder (*vidyādhara*), saying: "Excellent, excellent, O knowledge-holder! I am well-pleased with you, O knowledge-holder; speak a boon, and I shall grant it to you. Whatever purpose you have, I shall grant it all—whether it be the discourse on treasures (*nidhivāda*), the discourse on mineral essences (*dhātuvāda*), the discourse on sacred fields (*kṣetravāda*), the power of traveling through the sky, invisibility, the discourse on mantras, or the accomplishment of ritual manuals (*kalpasiddhi*)—I shall grant all of that."

5. Whether it be kingship, or the office of a minister, or mastery of speech, or the acquisition of a village, or the acquisition of clothing, or the acquisition of cattle, horses, buffaloes, camels, or sheep; or the acquisition of wealth, or the acquisition of grain—I shall bestow all of that upon you. Or whether it be the power of traveling through the sky, or invisibility, or the attainment of supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*), or the attainment of meditative concentration (*samādhi*), or the attainment of mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇī*), or the ritual procedures (*kalpa*) and means of accomplishment (*sādhana*) for seals (*mudrā*) and maṇḍalas, or the raising of a *vetāḍa* (vampire), or the state of a perfected *vidyādhara*, or the state of a minor *vidyādhara*—or whatever [it may be].
