6. Whether it be the state of a *vidyādhara*, entry into a hidden place (*hila*), entry into a forest, entry into a mountain, or entry into a cremation ground—I shall grant all of that. Then, whatever the *vidyādhara* may desire in his mind, he gives it all. Merely by the sight of the *vidyādhara*, one obtains the purification of the body called the "Stainless and Unfailing Gaze" (*vimalāmogham avalokitam*). In a future birth, one proceeds to the world-system of Sukhāvatī, arising spontaneously from the center of a lotus calyx.

7. He will beget offspring, and he will possess the recollection of his births from lifetime to lifetime. And this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*—which is honored by all bodhisattvas, which is the mandala of liberation, the chapter on the ocean-mandala, complete with its ritual manual (*kalpa*), and entirely perfected—shall abide upon the tip of his tongue until the final end at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍala*). Therefore, a knowledge-holder (*vidyādhara*) who wishes to accomplish the rite and practice of the *modaka* oblation should prepare food-modakas. Then, one thousand and eight [of these]... [34a] (P.60a3, D.61b6)

1. While reciting the Amoghapāśahṛdaya one thousand and eight times, the vidyādhara must then become pure, wearing clean garments and having bathed well. Then, having kindled a fire with fragrant wood fuel-sticks, he should offer oblations of sweetmeats (modaka) smeared with ghee, one thousand and eight times until the fire is full. From the midst of the fire, a boy arises and offers a vessel full of divine sweetmeats. Then the vidyādhara should sprinkle that boy with mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited seven times; truly, that boy will speak to the vidyādhara.

2. What do you seek from the Vidyādhara? The Vidyādhara should say: "Grant all desires. She says: "Accept this bowl of sweetmeats (*modaka*), O Vidyādhara; these will be the means for accomplishing your immeasurable tasks. Accept this supreme elixir (*rasāyana*), O Vidyādhara; this will be your ultimate accomplishment. Then the Vidyādhara should take that full bowl and say to that boy: "Be my companion. The boy says: "I shall be your companion in every task."

3. For success: when there is a task for a Vidyādhara, then one should offer oblations of guggulu mixed with sandalwood, soaked in ghee and mustard oil, using the Amoghāṅkuśa mantra recited seven times. Having kindled a fire with *arkka* wood, by the mere offering of the oblation, I shall be summoned; I will come immediately, accomplish all tasks, become a performer of all rites, attend upon you for as long as life lasts, and carry out the service of attendance. All—

4. I ward off the Vināyakas, Bhūtas, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas. Then, the Vidyādhara must touch that sweetmeat (*modaka*); he will fly up into the sky and overcome all the families of Vidyādharas. He will become the universal monarch (*cakravartin*) of all Vidyādharas; his retinue will consist of eighteen *koṭis* of Vidyādhara universal monarchs. His lifespan will be sixty thousand divine eons (*kalpas*), and his hair will be curled and ringlet-like.

5. It will overflow. Having placed a sweetmeat (*modaka*) in the middle of a vessel and set it before the noble Avalokiteśvara, and having consecrated it with the Amogharāja-krodha [mantra], one should then give and eat it among all śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, as well as among women, men, boys, and girls; it shall never be exhausted. It will appear again and again. As long as the sweetmeat remains in the middle of the vessel, so long will it continue to function, even for hundreds of thousands of people in great abundance.

6. And it will be given away, yet there shall be no depletion. Having recited the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* over a sweetmeat (*modaka*) seven times, wherever it is thrown, that [place] becomes divine gold. Having recited [the mantra] over a sweetmeat seven times, it should be cast into the abode of the *nāgas*. Then, as far as the limits of the great ocean, all the *nāga* kings together with their retinues will remain under one's control. What need is there to mention [ordinary tasks]? They will become doers of one’s bidding; if one commands them regarding drought, they cause rain to fall; if one commands them regarding excessive rain—

7. They hold back excessive rain; by the mere utterance of the command, they hold back all winds, cold, heat, and lightning. Having recited the mantra seven times over a sweetmeat (*modaka*) and struck it at the entrance of a cave, all the entrances of the caves remain opened; all mechanical devices, bolts, and doors burst open; they cause all the inhabitants of the dwelling to emerge and stand before the *vidyādhara*, becoming his obedient servants. [The same occurs for] forest thickets, mountain clefts, and the doors of dwellings.

The doors of the abodes of all *bhūtas*, *yakṣas*, and *rākṣasas* shall be opened. All *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, and *bhūtas* will become naked; they will all remain under one's control, obedient to one's commands, and will attend upon one for as long as life lasts. One should bathe an untouched corpse with scented water, recite the mantra over a sweetmeat (*modaka*) twenty-one times, and cast two sweetmeats into the midst of a great cremation ground.

2. It should be given [to him]. Wrap the corpse in a white cloth; with the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*), sprinkle it seven times with water and mustard seeds. Whatever you ask about, they will tell you all of it: whether there is security or famine, pestilence, calamity, misfortune, fear of foreign armies, adversaries, enemies, or death; they tell all of that. They tell of rebirth in the world of the gods or rebirth in a Buddha-field. They tell of birth in hell. They tell of short life or long life. They tell of untimely death.

3. He speaks of the movement of treasures; he speaks of the discourse on elements (*dhātu*), or fields (*kṣetra*). He speaks of sorcery (*indrajāla*). He speaks of the accomplishment of rituals (*kalpasiddhi*), the accomplishment of mantras (*mantrasiddhi*), and the accomplishment of mudrās and maṇḍalas. He speaks of the accomplishment of eye-salve (*añjana*) and the accomplishment of medicinal pills (*gulikā*). He speaks of all these: traveling through the sky, invisibility, the raising of a *vetāḍa* (corpse-demon), the dispatching of fevers, the subduing of enemies, and the bringing under control (*vasīkaraṇa*). He speaks of means (*upāya*); he speaks of loss; he speaks of increase. Even unto the end of the eon (*kalpāntara*), [he speaks of] the past and the future...

4. It tells of the present. Then, one should moisten the face with water provided by a vidyādhara; taking a *modaka* (sweetmeat), the deceased falls [back to life]. Having recited the mantra over the *modaka* twenty-one times, one should sit at the king’s gate; the king, together with his harem and retinue, remains under one's control, as does one’s own wealth. If one sits at the city gate, all the inhabitants of the city—men, women, boys, and girls—remain under one's control. One will become greatly honored.

5. One attains the accomplishment of the arrival of great wealth. Having recited the mantra seven times over a sweetmeat (*modaka*) of the Great Goddess Śrī, it should be placed in [the person's] hand; they will come under the control of the Great Goddess Śrī and attend upon them. She bestows great riches, and this shall continue for as long as one lives. Having recited the mantra one hundred and eight times over a sweetmeat, it should be placed in a small pouch and worn on the hip. As long as one wears it, one will become invisible. One enters wherever one desires. [One becomes] single-minded...

6. Wherever there is a stream of water, one should empower a sweetmeat (*modaka*) by reciting [the mantra] twenty-one times and consecrate it with the Wrathful King (*krodharāja*). Sitting at the foot of a tree, [the practitioner should know that] those who can assume any form at will will remain under his control. They will attend to him and serve him with all desired things according to his wishes, attending upon him for as long as he lives. Having empowered a sweetmeat twenty-one times and placed it on the head of Mahākāla in the Mother’s abode, one should then consecrate it with water and white mustard seeds over which the Wrathful King has been recited seven times; from that, everything...

7. All the yoginīs and ḍākinīs will attend upon [the practitioner] and come under their control; they will become messengers who perform all activities. By placing a *modaka* (sweetmeat) for Mahākāla at the navel center while reciting the mantra twenty-one times, the entire host of Mothers will appear before one in their own forms; they will grant all boons and become performers of all tasks. Having consecrated a *modaka* with the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*) by reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times, one should place it within the bowl of Noble Mañjuśrī. Up until the *modaka*... [35a] (P62a1, D.63b6)

1. While the vessel remains in the midst of the ten directions before all the Tathāgatas, various flavors and the most excellent tastes, as well as divine and great jewels, manifest; the assembly of Śrāvakas and Bodhisattvas within the great maṇḍala of the great assembly shall be fully satisfied. And all those Tathāgatas and those hosts of Bodhisattvas, together with the Saṅgha of Śrāvakas, purify the dakṣiṇā for that Vidyādhara. Having recited the mantra over the sweetmeats one hundred and eight times and having consecrated them with the King of Wrath (Krodharāja), [he sprinkles] water with the King of the Hook (Aṅkuśīrāja).

2. While reciting the mantra, one should bind the boundary around the fire-pit. Then, having kindled it with *arka* fuel-sticks and placed that sweetmeat (*modaka*) in the center of the fire in the pit, one should offer one hundred and eight oblations of ghee, mustard seeds, and curd-whey. When the one hundred and eight oblations are completed, the deity Agni appears before the *vidyādhara* in his own form and says: "Excellent, excellent, *vidyādhara*! I have been fully gratified; I am well-pleased, *vidyādhara*, and supreme joy has been attained by me. Speak, *vidyādhara*, I shall grant you a boon according to your heart's desire."

3. A desire for the syllable *si* arises. Whatever boon the Vidyādhara wishes for in his mind should be spoken; he grants it all. The deity Agni attends to him and comes under his control. He bestows the accomplishment of all tasks. One may enter and emerge from the midst of a mass of fire as cool as the Himalayas, as if through water. With the hand, one effects the release from fire within the mandala; even if one places a blazing [fire] upon the head, not even a single hair is burned, nor does one come under the power of fire.

4. It enters [the mouth]; one holds it flaming in the mouth, yet not even the slightest heat falls upon the body. Just as sandalwood is cool and refreshing, it will perform various other tasks. If one binds it with the hem of a garment, it does not burn; if placed in the midst of water, it does not sink. It appears in its own form through every rite of *homa*. When employed in any task, it bestows the accomplishment of all undertakings in each respective case. Everywhere it teaches the ritual manual for the accomplishment of mantras and maṇḍalas.

5. The flame, driven by the force of the incense wind, travels a thousand *yojanas* and returns again. It instructs one in all tasks; it shall perform all tasks; it bestows accomplishment (*siddhi*) everywhere. Therefore, for one desiring to accomplish the fire of Unfailing Flame (*Amoghajvālā*), which is the supreme divine blaze, possessing a majesty equal to the rising sun and like a wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇi*), it illuminates all around in the ten directions and accomplishes various [aims].

6. The task is the accomplishment of the supreme transformation (*pākasiddhi*). This is the most excellent and best elixir (*rasāyana*), the unsurpassed discourse on the elements (*dhātu-vāda*). They accomplish various other transformations that are unsurpassed; by night one sees as if divine, and by day one is like the sun. One should perform the accomplishment of the task once; one should well-mix the jewel-substance, well-prepared. Pure through the practice of recitation (*jāpa*) and with conduct of purity, one should accomplish it with fire of unfailing flame. I shall describe the firewood for the fire, which has a radiance equal to a blazing fire; one should prepare it all in one place.

7. One should prepare all these as fuel for the unsurpassed rite: sandalwood, *kadara*, *pataṅga*, and *karavīra*; wood from the *arka*, *samī*, and *vaṃśa* trees; *śirīṣa*, *karṇṇakārika*, the Bodhi tree, milky trees (*kṣīravṛkṣa*), *plakṣa*, *sumana*, *gandhavārṣikā*, *padmanāḍa*, and its leaves; *kumuda*, *puṇḍarīka*, and *utpala*—their roots, leaves, and flowers; *bilva* wood, *bījapūraka* wood, *sinduvārī*, *campaka*, *drākṣāṇī*, *picumanda*, *sahavālaka*, and *citraka*. Having gathered these woods, one should prepare them with fuel sticks.

1. [One should] cause a small image to be made. With mustard seeds, ghee, curd, honey, and parched grain as oblations; with three *palas* of divine copper, twice that amount of vermilion (*hiṅgula*), *kiṃkuṣṭha*, one *pala* of white *kāñcana*, ten *palas* of sandalwood, and one *pala* of realgar (*manaḥśilā*)—these substances combined with twice as much yellow orpiment (*haritāla*)—one should fill a crucible and place it in the midst of a fire prepared in a pit. One should offer eight thousand oblations, clearly manifest and well-composed, being pure in conduct, wearing clean garments, well-bathed, and perfumed with fragrant scents. Having set out an offering of various flavors, flowers, and fruits...

And when eight thousand recitations and burnt offerings have been completed, one should then present the bali-offering, flowers, and incense, and offer the *argha* and *pādya* water. Having prepared the crucible with milk and clarified butter (*agnikṣara*), the Vidyādhara should strike it with mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited one thousand and eight times. It should then be consecrated twenty-one times with the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*) mantra. Thereupon the crucible blazes. Then the Vidyādhara should worship that crucible; [he should place] that jewel in a copper casket or a silver casket within the crucible.

3. Having taken it, one should place it there in a casket. Just as the *cintāmaṇi*, so shall this *Amoghajvāla* be of great and supreme power. At night it displays the luster of the moon; during the day it displays the luster of the sun. When the time for cooking arrives, by placing that jewel [there], one accomplishes the cooking of all desired objects. When one performs the fire-oblation (*homa*), one should place it in the middle of the sacrificial pit and offer the oblation; then a great flame of fire manifests. In every case, it serves as a lamp for all rites.

4. He will achieve this: in the midst of a great battle and conflict, a heroic man—having bathed well and wearing clean garments, and having girded himself with armor—should place that great jewel upon his head. Then, he alone shall enter the battle; that man will become like a single blazing fire. Consequently, the enemy forces in the battle and conflict will be defeated; they will flee in confusion toward the ten directions. And never again shall there be any fear of an enemy force.

5. There will be no fear from either [source], nor will there be fear of enemies or adversaries. Holding the jewel in one's hand, one should enter the cave-dwelling; all the doors of the dwelling will remain open, and all the inhabitants of the dwelling will stand before one. Having gone to the entire Naga realm and holding that jewel in one's hand, one should enter the middle of the dwelling; all the water will no longer exist. Then all the Nagas will stand before one. O you who are true to your vow—

They do not remain [independent]; for as long as they live, they will become servants under one's control and remain obedient to commands. All crops, grasses, shrubs, and trees will grow with ease; they will become soft, smooth, and tender. They will be full of vitality and mindfulness, and free from illness. And all those sentient beings who consume that grain, flowers, and fruits will perform many other various tasks. [This is] the Great Jewel, the Unfailing Radiance, the Great Fire-Flame. Therefore, by the power of the Unfailing Radiance...

7. [The ritual for] the summoning of the insect [is performed] by one who desires to see the noble Avalokiteśvara in his own form. Then, the vidyādhara must be pure and wear clean garments; he must be well-bathed, with his body perfumed with scented water. Then, he should kindle a fire with fuel-sticks of *arka* wood. He should offer eight thousand oblations of mustard seeds, *agaru*, sandalwood, curd, honey, and ghee mixed together. Then, with *amoghāṅkuśa* and *guggulu*, he should offer twenty-one oblations. The noble Avalokiteśvara will then appear before him in his own form.

He remains present; he fulfills all excellent intentions and grants boons according to one's desired mental aspirations. Then, the vidyādhara should request a boon with his desired mental aspiration, and thereafter Āryāvalokiteśvara grants everything. Then, by one who wishes to accomplish the eye-salve (añjana), that vidyādhara must be pure, wearing clean garments, and well-bathed. Having fasted for one night, he should place [the ingredients] in a copper casket, and then [add] sovīrāñjana mixed with double the amount of haritāla.

2. It should not be filled; therefore, it should be recited one thousand and eight times. Then, one should stand in the middle of a trench. Upon that, having kindled a fire with *arka* wood, one should offer one thousand and eight oblations of *uśīra*, mustard seeds, and sandalwood, smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. When the one thousand and eight [oblations] are complete, one should then take the collyrium and grind it into fine powder upon a stone slab. One should then consecrate it with manaḥśilā, camphor, and musk, and further recite the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* one hundred and eight times.

3. Having recited the Amogha-aṅkuśa King of Vidyās twenty-one times, one should then perform the rite for summoning everywhere. Thereafter, one should be consecrated by the King Amogha. Then, sealing it seven times with the Amoghapāśa mudrā, one should apply it as collyrium to the eyes; one will fly into the sky and become the sovereign of all vidyādharas. One’s hair will become curled in ringlets, and one will live for ten thousand kalpas. By applying a tilaka-mark on the forehead, one becomes invisible.

It will come to pass. One should apply collyrium to the eyes while remaining silent. One may enter the royal court, where one stands having brought the king, along with his harem and retinue, under one's influence. One will become greatly honored and highly esteemed. One attains the accomplishment of great purpose and gain, whether at the time of the ritual practice (*sādhana*) or the time of recitation (*jāpa*). By applying this collyrium, one becomes invisible to all obstructing spirits (*vighna*), leaders of obstacles (*vināyaka*), and all deities belonging to the host of Māras. Furthermore, no heart-obstructing impediments or interruptions shall arise. Well—

5. By means of this, one will accomplish the method of attainment (*sādhanavidhi*). One should apply collyrium to the eyes and enter into the midst of a great multitude; they will all become submissive. There will be success regarding great wealth, grain, clothing, ornaments, and decorations. By gazing at a woman with unblinking eyes, she will become submissive, whether by means of oneself or by means of wealth. One should apply collyrium to the eyes and enter a great forest; there will be no fear of any thieves, rogues, robbers, fierce beasts, venomous serpents, poison, or fire. One will be safe and well.

6. If one applies this ointment to the eyes during all quarrels, disputes, conflicts, and legal cases, one will be the superior speaker; one will be victorious in every instance. When engaged in battle and standing in the midst of combat, if one applies it to the eyes, one will be victorious everywhere and shall overcome all fears. For one bitten by any venomous creature, if one applies it to the eyes, one will become free from poison. For all fevers—whether quotidian, tertian, quartan, or those occurring every fourth day—if one applies it to the eyes, one is completely liberated from all fevers.

7. For one who has drunk poison or been affected by a toxic agent, one should apply [this ointment] to the eyes; he will become free from poison. For one seized by any of the planetary spirits (*graha*), one should apply it to the eyes; he is liberated from the eighty-four thousand planetary spirits. At the mere application of the ointment, eye-pains are released, as are headaches and hemiplegia. One is immediately liberated from the seizure of *brahmarākṣasa* spirits and from the seizure of *apasmāra* (epilepsy). By the mere application of the ointment to the eyes, one is liberated. Even when a king is enraged, or those who are being led away as fit for execution, they are liberated by the mere application of the ointment to the eyes. This is the Great Kāla, which removes all fears.

One should apply collyrium to the eyes; it stands at one's head and grants all boons. It will accomplish every task. One will bring all the hosts of Mothers under one’s control. One should apply collyrium to the eyes and gaze with unblinking eyes upon the Great Goddess Śrī while reciting the *Amogharājahṛdaya* three times; thus one stands before the Great Goddess Śrī. She will grant every undertaking and bestow abundant, abundant wealth. At the time of sleep, one should apply collyrium to the eyes and go to bed; one will see abundant, abundant divine and great dreams.

2. He grants a vision in his own form as the noble Avalokiteśvara and bestows all boons. Great mindfulness and intelligence arise. If one applies collyrium to the eyes or causes it to enter the body, one receives great worship. By applying collyrium to the eyes while holding an image of the noble Avalokiteśvara, one will constantly be a granter of boons and will always have a desire for his vision. Having mixed it with *rocanā*, one should apply it to the eyes; if one enters a royal court, there will be a great increase in sovereignty.

3. He shall obtain [success]; there will be the attainment of great wealth; there will be the accomplishment of great purposes; he will be dear to all the king’s harem, the assembly of ministers, and the council; they will all remain under his control. One should apply collyrium to the eye of an image of Mahādeva; one will become the sovereign of all spirits (*bhūta*), and they will all remain under one's control. Servants and laborers [will obey]. One should apply collyrium to the forehead-eye of an image of Mahākāla; one will have mastery over all *yakṣas*.

4. It will become effective. If one anoints the eyes of a corpse, it rises up. One should anoint the eyes of those afflicted by all spells, poisons, and *khaṛda* (sorcery); all [effects of] poisons, *khaṛda*, and spells will be neutralized. They shall never again cause any harm. If one anoints the eyes of a hungry person and enters a city, he obtains food and drink effortlessly. If one anoints the eyes of a mendicant (*piṇḍapātika*) as he goes for alms, he receives a vast amount of food of various flavors from the right [donors]. All—

5. All eye diseases—such as *pilla*, *paṭala*, *timira*, *arbuda*, *kācara*, night-blindness (*rātryandha*), itching (*kaṇḍūya*), slimy discharge (*picchila-srava*), *kaṇṭaka*, pustules (*piṭaka*), and the growth of flesh (*māṃsa-rohaṇa*)—are destroyed by this [remedy]. They become healthy. Among all eye diseases, it purifies the divine eye, making it as clear as the vision of Suparṇin. One obtains sight and joy; all remain under one's control. One gains wealth in grain, success in one's aims, and unsurpassed sovereignty. Now, therefore, [concerning] all wealth, grain, clothing, ornaments, and decorations—

6. I shall now proclaim the *Vibhūṣaṇākarṣaṇavṛddhi-amogha-agnidevatāvāhana-vipulahoma*, which is the unsurpassed means for attaining all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhi*), the achiever of all aims, immediate, and supremely gladdening to the wise. One shall immediately obtain sovereignty and an abundance of enjoyments. One must not harbor doubt, hesitation, or uncertainty. Being pure, wearing clean clothes, and having bathed well, one should perform the rite. For this fire-offering (*homa*) is inconceivable, vast, and the unsurpassed increase. [One should offer] the root of the *karañja* tree, together with its stalk, leaves, flowers, and fruits, as well as the *arka*...

7. Having kindled the fire with fuel sticks of *plakṣa* wood, one should offer a full eight thousand oblations of the seven seeds, rice grains, parched grain, sesame, and mustard, anointed with curd, honey, ghee, and pungent oil. When the eight thousand are completed, while being consecrated by the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*), one should then recite the great queen of vidyās, Amoghāṅkuśī, one hundred and eight times and offer oblations of *guggulu*, *caṇḍabījaka*, and ghee-anointed substances. When this is finished, all tasks will be accomplished; thereafter, food, drink, bedding, seating, and medicinal requisites for the sick will appear spontaneously.

There will be an increase in bedding, requisites, wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses; various garments, ornaments, decorations, and embellishments, as well as flowers, perfumes, garlands, and ointments, will appear effortlessly. One will obtain great sovereign power and majesty and shall live for the duration of one's life. Then, on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, having fasted for a day and night, one should prepare collyrium. Reciting the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* mantra ninety times, consecrating it with the King of Wrath (*Krodharāja*), and sealing it with the *Amoghapāśa-mudrā*, one should apply the collyrium to the eyes.

2. He travels through the sky by means of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*). He shall become the sovereign king and universal monarch (*cakravartin*) of all those who have attained success through ointments (*añjana*) and all the *vidyādharas*. His hair will be curled and ringlet-like. He lives for ten thousand eons. By applying this ointment to his eyes, he sees at night as clearly as during the day. He becomes invisible and can enter the abodes of all *bhūtas*, *yakṣas*, and *rākṣasas*. He manifests everywhere. One should apply this ointment to the eyes and enter the Mother’s Abode (*mātṛsthāna*); there, he shall remain with unblinking eyes.

3. Having beheld the foremost deities, one should then recollect the Kings of Wrath (*krodharāja*) once; thereupon, all the Mother Goddesses will stand before one. They will become bestowers of all boons, performers of all rites, and attendants for as long as life lasts. One will become beloved by all the assemblies of Mothers and their retinues, and they will remain constantly attached for the sake of protection, defense, and guardianship. Now, I shall proclaim the ritual procedure for the *gorocana* accomplishment and fire-offering (*homavidhi*), which brings happiness to the Vidyādharas and is perfected.

4. ...the accomplished, supreme *Amogharāja*, worshipped by gods and *dānavas*, which accomplishes all aims, brings about subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*), and is the best for traveling through the sky; it is exceedingly difficult to attain, yet it grants entry into strength, as well as entry into forests, mountain caves, and the depths of the underworld (*pātāla*); likewise, entry into the abodes of *nāgas* and lakes, crossing great rivers, the production of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*), accomplishment (*siddhi*), the warding off of all fears, the pacification of all diseases, and [the removal of] all sins...

5. O Destroyer of Arrows! It bestows victory in battle and conflict, eternally crushing all enemies; it eradicates the hosts of all planetary spirits (grahas), wards off all fevers, and destroys previous obscurations and all sins. It grants sovereignty and enjoyment, increases wealth and grain, and pacifies strife, quarrels, disputes, and litigation. It shatters all bonds, fetters, and shackles, and brings before the king those wicked ones deserving of death who are filled with wrath. For one who now serves this—of the man...

6. Like a son to his father, he speaks with joy; he is liberated from all calamities, and he shall be honored everywhere. Wherever he goes, he will always be dear to embodied beings. He will always be beloved by the king, along with the queens and their retinues. Likewise, the brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras—all women will always be fond of him, as will men, boys, and girls—whoever constantly uses this unsurpassed *gorocana*, [consecrated] by the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the Giver of Boons. Always.

7. Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, who are eternal bestowers of boons, shall remain day and night for the sake of protection. Furthermore, many other gods, powerful Nāga kings, Bhūtas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Kuṣmāṇḍas, Kinnaras, Mahoragas, Gandharvas, Asuras, and Garuḍa lords of great supernatural power—all of them shall stand day and night for the purpose of protection over this son, once he has been thus empowered by the most excellent, potent, and perfected *gorocanā*. Then, the Vidyādhara, having become pure, having bathed well, and wearing clean garments, [should take] the cow-...

1. Having obtained yellow orpiment (*rocana*) and indeed great red lead (*mahālohita*), and having combined them with saffron (*kuṅkuma*), one should fill a copper vessel in front of an image of Amoghapāśa. Having recited [the mantra] eight thousand times, one should cover it with new white cloths. Then, having kindled a fire with fuel-sticks of *khadira* wood and *arka* wood, one should offer oblations one thousand and eight times, mixing parched grain (*lāja*), mustard seeds, *guggulu*, rice, and sesame seeds, anointed with curd, honey, and clarified butter. When the one thousand and eight [oblations] are complete, once the fire has subsided, one should take the fine, pacifying ashes and cast them into that vessel.

Then, having recited [the mantra] one hundred and eight times and having been consecrated by the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*), one should perform the consecration with the mudrā. Then, having applied a tilaka of *ūrṇā*-hair, one flies up into the sky. One will become a great *vidyādhara*, a universal monarch (*cakravartin*); the lord of all *vidyādharas*. His hair will be curled like earrings. He lives for ninety-nine thousand years. All the doors of the celestial abodes remain perpetually open for him. Having made a tilaka on the forehead, he becomes invisible; he exists everywhere.

3. He enters into them; he shall become the sovereign lord in every abode. The dwellings of all *bhūtas*, *yakṣas*, and *rākṣasas* stand with their doors flung open. All the *bhūtas*, *yakṣas*, and *rākṣasas*, together with their armies and retinues, will come and attend upon him. For as long as he lives, they will be his servants. If one applies collyrium to the eyes at night, one sees as if by divine sight. One sees great treasures everywhere. One sees the gates of the netherworld (*pātāla*) in the fissures of the earth opened wide. One sees the palace of the *pātāla*.

Having performed all the activities of the underworld (*pātāla*), he emerges once again and enters into the midst of the waters of a great river. There he beholds a celestial mansion (*vimāna*) as if it were his own house; he beholds a mansion adorned with the seven precious gems. All those who dwell there in the water remain under his control. Just as one enters and exits his own home, he enters and exits the abode of the *nāgas* and *śarabhas*. Having anointed his entire body [with the ointment], when he enters the midst of battle and combat, he is seen wearing armor and equipped with mail, granting victory everywhere.

5. It will come to pass: holding it at the mouth, one may enter a royal court; the king, together with his harem and retinue, shall remain under one's control. Whatever one speaks with one's voice, all that they will do; whatever one asks for, all that they will give; whatever one commands, all that they will obey. Having wiped one's face, wherever one goes, there women, men, boys, and girls shall attend to one, remaining under one's control, whether by means of oneself or through wealth. One should smear [the mantra] upon the right hand.

6. Whomever it touches, that person will become more prosperous; wealth, grain, gold, female slaves, male slaves, laborers, and servants will remain under their control, ready to do whatever they are told. By anointing the right forefinger and standing facing a cloud that is thundering during a time of storm, one can threaten it and thereby pacify all cold winds; they will not approach within a league. During excessive rain, if one displays the palm of the right hand toward the clouds, the rain is pacified. During a time of drought, [one should display] the palm of the right hand.

7. Regarding the application [of the ritual] at a lake in the abode of the *nāgas*: one should strike the water three times with the palm of the hand. At that very moment, the *nāga* king will release great torrents of rain. If he does not rain within that instant, then he should be struck five times; then all the *nāgas* will release torrents of rain. If they do not rain, then all the *nāgas* will suffer from diseases of the head. If one strikes seven times, all the *nāga* kings will fall into calamity; it will result in the destruction of the lineage of all the *nāga* kings for those possessed by *grahas*.

1. One should apply collyrium to the eyes of all; by the mere act of applying it, the eighty-four thousand types of seizures are pacified. By making a *tilaka* on the forehead of those suffering from fever, all fevers—whether quotidian, tertian, quartan, or quaternary—are pacified. For those afflicted by all diseases, bathing [with this] brings immediate liberation from every ailment. One is freed from leprosy, skin eruptions, scabies, pustules, and ringworm. By the mere application of an ointment, one is liberated from all swellings, hemorrhoids, fistulas, erysipelas, *gaṇḍamāla*, *mālā*, and so forth. For all those bitten by venomous creatures, the *li-*... [is applied].

By merely drinking it, one becomes free from poison; by merely drinking it, one is liberated from every poison-mantra. For all those suffering from abdominal diseases—such as intestinal tumors (*gulma*), dropsy (*jalodara*), splenic disorders, pain in the flanks, heart-pain, bladder-pain, hemorrhoids, diarrhea, urinary disorders (*prameha*), cholera (*visūcikā*), indigestion, and upward movement of gases (*udāvarta*)—these shall be pacified by merely drinking it with warm water, and they shall never again recur. Having placed a *rocanā* pill on the head, standing near the entrance of a cave or opening, and having smeared the right hand [with it], one should strike the door with the palm; [this applies to] all poisons.

3. Through that means, the gates shall be opened. One may enter without fear; henceforth, there will be no further obstacles. All those who dwell in that abode shall come before one and become subject to one's will. There will be the great accomplishment (*mahāsiddhi*) for the fulfillment of all tasks. Having smeared both feet [with the mantra], if one enters into the midst of a blazing fire, the deity Agni will appear in his own form and stand before one, taking hold of the hand. He says to the *vidyādhara*: "Enter my palace and celestial chariot (*vimāna*), O *vidyādhara*; [here] is your command."

4. One should know that by saying "I shall perform all tasks, O Vidyādhara," the Vidyādhara will then carry them out. If one anoints both arms, one will possess the strength of seven nāgas. If one anoints both thighs, one becomes an invincible wrestler. If one anoints the shanks, one gains the depth of a great river and crosses to the other side. Having anointed the throat and entered a forest glade, the doors to the dwellings within the forest glades will open; all substances and medicinal herbs will appear before one in their own forms, whatever one desires.

5. Having taken that, and having held a pill of *rocanā* (bezoar) at the tip of the mouth, one should enter mountain caves and deep ravines and cry out loudly three times. Those who dwell there in the mountain ravines and caves, whose secret doors of their abodes are opened, and those inhabitants there—all of them will stand before [the practitioner] in their respective forms. They will become performers of all tasks; and whatever grasses, shrubs, trees, substances, and medicinal herbs are there, they will stand before [him] in their own natural forms.

6. [The juices] will flow; those excellent juices will flow forth, and those guardians of the juices will present themselves in their own forms as foremost. They will all come under one's control. One should perform all tasks at will and without fear. Having made the heart a *tilaka*, whatever is in the heart—hopes, desires, thoughts, intentions, and actions—all that is accomplished at that very moment. Having made the belly a *tilaka*, one obtains food, drink, and sustenance according to all one's wishes; everything is achieved effortlessly.

7. By smearing [the ointment] on both sides, one obtains garments as desired; by smearing it on the backbone, one obtains a bed or seat according to one’s mind; by smearing it on the ears or on the vital points (*marmasthāna*), one obtains ornaments and decorations according to one’s intention; by smearing it on the region of the forehead, one obtains a horse-vehicle. Day after day, without speaking, at dawn, one should consume one pill of *rocanā* while reciting the *Amogharājahṛdaya*, and thus [attain] the first [result].

On the first day, one recites and retains a thousand verses; day by day, one recites and retains them, doubling [the amount]. After seven nights, a great range of hearing increases. By practicing for two weeks, one’s voice becomes like that of a *kinnarī*. By practicing for three weeks, there will be a collection of a great ocean of learning, and one will possess a voice that is smooth, sweet, deep, and resonant like the call of the *kalaviṅka* bird. For those desiring a son, it should be given with ghee; even women who have borne only daughters will obtain a son. For those in prison, shackles, and fetters—

2. One should smear a chain of *rgaḍa* (scorpions); as soon as it is smeared, it shatters into pieces and perishes. On the eighth, fourteenth, or fifteenth day, one should bathe a pill of *rocanā* (bezoar) with scented water while reciting the *Amogharājahṛdaya* seven times; one should then personally consecrate it with the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*). As soon as it is bathed, all sins and all previous obscurations (*āvaraṇa*) are destroyed. Having bathed for three nights, one attains the accomplishment (*siddhi*) of this mantra and mudrā practice. All adversaries, enemies, and wicked, malevolent beings have no power over one. Ka-

3. Furthermore, he will everywhere be completely liberated from all fear, and shall never again be stained by the impurity of evil. Having rubbed a pill of *rocanā* with oil and anointed his face, if he stands facing a king and embraces him as a son, he will experience great joy; it pacifies all fear and the king’s wrath. If one anoints the entire body [with it], even for one deserving of execution, the weapon shall not strike the body; it will shatter into pieces and not penetrate the body.

The bow breaks. If one ties a pellet of gorocana around the neck and enters a forest, wilderness, mountain thicket, or difficult terrain, there will be no fear of any thieves, rogues, robbers, yakṣas, rākṣasas, humans, non-humans, fierce beasts, or venomous serpents; they shall vanish. If one ties it on the right arm, one becomes invincible everywhere and shall be greatly honored everywhere, possessing everywhere unimpeded great strength, vigor, and prowess.

It will come to pass. One should bind [the mantra] on the left arm; one will become beloved by all women, men, boys, and girls. All will desire to see him. He will become worthy of great honor. There will be the attainment of great and vast wealth. One should bind it on the right calf; one travels a thousand *yojanas* without rest. Taking a pellet of *gorocanā* in the mouth and holding a mustard seed with the right hand, while recollecting the "Infallible Hook" (*Amoghāṅkuśa*) without speaking, that place—

6. Having mounted it, one should scatter mustard seeds in whichever direction there is a woman, man, boy, or girl; they will be summoned instantly and will come. Even if they are situated at a distance of a hundred *yojanas*, they will certainly arrive within three nights—of this there is no doubt. By binding a pellet of *gorocanā* to the right or left hand, wherever one touches it, [there will be] wealth, grain, gold, gems, pearls, conch shells, crystals, coral, silver, refined gold, clothing, and ornaments.

7. It becomes one that draws in and moves everything; wherever one desires, there it shall move. Having entered the kitchen, a slap should be given on the door-panel (*capeṭa*); all the uncooked rice, water, and food will be drawn forth. Wherever one desires, there it transfers; go to the perfumer’s shop and it transfers all the shop’s equipment. A slap should be given on the door-panel of the liquor-shop; it transfers everything from the jars of wine. A slap should be given on the storehouse; it draws forth all the grain.

1. Having entered a sugar-refinery and touched the wheel, one transfers all the molasses, liquids, sugar, and candied sugar [there]. One sends it wherever one desires. If one places a *capaṭa* (box/container) at the city gate, at the time of twilight, all the inhabitants of the city will be rendered asleep. If one buries it at the gate of an enemy, their expulsion is accomplished. If one throws it into an armory, all weapons and arms will become paralyzed and broken. If one buries it at the royal gate, all adversaries, enemies, and wicked beings will be bound and paralyzed.

2. They shall become paralyzed. One should smear a conch shell and fill a high place; as far as the sound is heard, all those who cause strife, quarrels, conflicts, disputes, sorcery, poison, and disease shall be completely liberated from them. Filling the city gate, it pacifies all calamities, misfortunes, and plagues. Filling a cow-pen, all the milk shall be taken away; it transfers [the effect] wherever one desires. Filling and transferring it into a herd of cattle, all the milk of the cattle shall be taken away. He who—

3. He desires to transfer [the power] there; filling the midst of the great multitude, all shall become naked and there shall be the stripping away of all garments. One should smear a drum with [the substance]; while sounding it on a high mountain, it arrests all cold winds and [other elements], causing them to perish so that they shall have no further power. It wards off lightning for hundreds of yojanas in every direction. While sounding it throughout a city or kingdom, all diseases, calamities, afflictions, and misfortunes are pacified. All strife, quarrels, and conflicts—

4. Disputes shall be pacified; all fears of famine among gods and men shall be stilled; they shall perform various other tasks; it is useful everywhere. This [mantra] is common to all sentient beings, bringing peace and prosperity, pacifying all diseases, destroying all sins, calming all calamities and misfortunes, quelling all famines and wildernesses, and eliminating all bhūtas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, grahas, and epilepsy. I shall explain [it] for the vidyādhara...

5. Having become one who wears pure garments, with his body well-bathed and perfumed with fragrant scents, having established a variegated mind infused with the fragrance of scented water, and being intent on compassion for all sentient beings—with a heart born of great compassion—one should perform this fire-offering (*homakarman*). Using fuel sticks made of *arka* wood, or wood from a milky tree, or even wood from the Bodhi tree, one should kindle the fire with these sacrificial woods and offer parched grain, mustard seeds, lotuses, lotus stalks, and leaves, along with curd, honey, and ghee.

6. One should offer oblations one thousand and eight times with the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*. Then, one should perform the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) one hundred and eight times with the *Amoghapāśakrodharāja*. Then, sealing it one hundred and eight times with the *Amoghapāśamudrā*, once the great fire-offering (*mahāhoma*) is completed, immediately within a radius of one *yojana* all calamities, misfortunes, portents, diseases, severe famine, dangers from one's own army or foreign armies, fears of adversaries and enemies, and [fears of] all thieves, rogues, robbers, and fierce wild beasts—[shall be pacified].

7. The fears of venomous snakes, wicked spirits, scorpions, ants, and small creatures shall be pacified; they shall have no power for a hundred *yojanas*. There shall be no fevers, no ailments, no diseases, no *yakṣas*, no *rākṣasas*, *bhūtas*, or *grahas*; these shall have no power. All strife, quarrels, disputes, riots, tumults, threats, sieges, imprisonments, and beatings shall be pacified. There will be security for all sentient beings. There will be abundance of food, it will be delightful, crowded with many people, filled with men, and rich in flowers and fruits.

There will be food; there will be an abundant production of wealth, grain, and crops. All things—grass, shrubs, medicinal herbs, trees, and plants—will be delicious, well-ripened, and fully developed, including their stalks, roots, fruits, and growth. Furthermore, throughout one's life, no report of punishment or even of verbal censure will be heard in that realm. The ascetics, brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, women, men, boys, and girls in that realm will be constantly healthy and possessed of pleasant touch.

They will become joyful in mind with delight and pleasure; they will dwell with minds of loving-kindness (*maitrī*) and compassion (*karuṇā*). And all those gods, *nāgas*, *yakṣas*, *gandharvas*, *asuras*, *garuḍas*, *kiṃnaras*, and *mahoragas* will remain well-guarded; they will provide protection, defense, and concealment for a full hundred *yojanas* in every direction. They will perform protection, guardianship, peace, and auspiciousness. Furthermore, the four Great Kings, together with their armies and retinues, will provide protection, defense, and concealment, and will guard [the area], warding off all malevolent beings.

The sons of the gods, Īśvara and Maheśvara, will constantly and perpetually provide protection, defense, and guardianship. Indra, king of the gods, together with his retinue of thirty-three sons of the gods, and Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, together with their retinues of all the hosts of gods, will ensure that the territory is well-guarded there. They will infuse vital energy (*ojas*) into all sentient beings and will protect and preserve them for a distance of one *yojana*. All śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, as well as all women, men, boys, and girls—

4. For what purpose will they provide protection, defense, and concealment? By the power of this rite of pacification (*sāntikarma*), all sentient beings shall become completely liberated from all evils and obscurations. All Tathāgatas will attend to that realm; all Bodhisattvas in the ten directions and the entire host of Bodhisattvas will assemble there. They remain desiring to grant consolation and a vision to all sentient beings. The sun and moon, together with the hosts of stars, will move in harmony. [This is for the] complete protection of all sentient beings.

5. For the sake of [all beings], Noble Avalokiteśvara constantly and continuously provides consolation as if to an only son for all women, men, boys, and girls; he protects them and will fulfill all their desires and hopes. He will grant them repeated visions. Then, having mixed that *homā* ash with scented water, one should sprinkle it in all four directions; thus a great boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) is established. In the case of all diseases, one should touch [the patient]; [thus] all diseases—

6. One pacifies [fevers] by means of the name. By making a *tilaka* mark in all fevers, one is liberated from all fevers. Perform a ritual bath with scented water and ashes, and the obscurations and sins of all beings will be purified. For those who have fallen into captivity or are in prison, one should smear [the substance] on their garments; they shall break free. For anyone bitten by any venomous creature, one should smear it on the edge of the mouth, and they will become free of poison. The procedure for the invocation of fire and the *homa* sacrifice is complete. Now, therefore, here begins the [procedure] for the Lotus Family (*padmakula*).

7. In the noble Avalokiteśvara’s Great Lotus Array, I shall proclaim the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, the maṇḍala of liberation, the great king of ritual manuals (*mahākalparāja*). These [rites] will accomplish hundreds of thousands of actions even if they have not been previously mastered. On an auspicious lunar day, under a favorable constellation, at a most propitious and supremely pure time, having bathed well and wearing clean garments, one should be composed with a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*) and compassion. Compassion is the supreme ornament for all sentient beings. [Thus begins] the *Amoghapāśa* Great Vidyā... 40a (P71b8, D.74a5)

1. The supreme accomplishment of the Royal Ritual (*rājakalpasiddhi*): It will perform all tasks accomplished through recitation; of this there is no doubt. O Padmapāṇi, the Giver of Boons, he who always holds the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*) of the Teacher of the World within his heart shall always be surrounded by all embodied beings. A heap of merit as vast as hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas, equal to the sands of the Ganges, increases for him. He accumulates roots of virtue and will perform the deeds of a Buddha. By means of a single fast and a single recitation, the wise man—whether a monk, a nun, or a lay follower—should practice.

2. Who, as an *upāsaka*, shall thus quickly go to Sukhāvatī, liberated from the terrible sufferings of afflictions (*kleśa*)? He will constantly obtain the vision of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; of this there is no doubt. Now I shall explain the procedure for recitation (*jāpa*), according to the rule for the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa. One should perform the rites of recitation for the attainments of the reality of the Vidyādharas. Having made a square cow-dung mandala all around in front of the image of Amoghapāśa, one should delineate the square with conch powder and gold thread.

3. One should decorate with white sandalwood a supreme mandala that is square, four-cornered, with four gates, and divided in the center. One should worship a hundred-petaled lotus with saffron; one should place a lotus in the center, a seed-vessel (*karṇikā*), and a flask filled with scented water together with mustard seeds. While burning agalloch incense and placing full jars, having arranged various flowers and set out four vessels for the *argha* and *pādya* offerings, the Vidyādhara, having become pure and wearing clean garments, [should observe] the *poṣadha*.

4. Furthermore, one should maintain the practice of eating only the three kinds of pure food and remain moderate in eating. One should perform the recitation (*japa*) of the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* mantra eight hundred times during the three periods of the day. Facing the noble Avalokiteśvara, one should sit in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*). One should assume the mudrā of recitation and hold a rosary. Extending the index finger and the thumb, one should become peaceful and self-controlled, possessing a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*), concentrated, and established with the body poised in meditation, gazing tranquilly.

5. Without attachment, the recitation (jāpa) should be performed; by the mere act of simultaneous recitation, there will be a great trembling of the earth. One should take hold of the Amoghapāśa mudrā and perform prostrations, and a great earthquake will occur. One must not be afraid; one should remain firm in mind and be devoted to compassion for all sentient beings. Fixing one's gaze upon the feet of the Noble Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa, one should cause the Wrathful King to be invoked seven times. By the mere act of invoking him seven times, there will be a great trembling—

6. A sound will arise. Rays of light will issue forth from the forehead of the Noble Avalokiteśvara, illuminating everything all around. That vidyādhara will experience a heart full of great joy; his face will be smiling and the hairs on his body will stand on end. Then he should look up at the face of the Blessed One. Simultaneously with that very act of looking up, O Blessed One, a voice of "Well done! will issue forth from the right side of the Noble Avalokiteśvara. As soon as the voice of "Well done! issues forth, his eyes will move. Immediately upon the issuing of that voice of "Well done," [the eyes will move].

7. He shall attain the purification of all obscurations of the lower realms. He will be endowed with a great purity of body. He will have planted roots of merit under hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas. He will be worthy of being beheld by all Bodhisattvas. His body will be soft, delicate, and supple. His hair will be curled and ringlet-like, and he will speak words that are smooth, sweet, and melodious. Furthermore, he attains purity of vision, as well as purity of body and purity of mind.

He will be free from wrinkles and grey hair. He attains the samādhi named *Sarvasattvāvalokitaviśuddhi* (Purity Beheld by All Beings). Until dawn, Noble Avalokiteśvara appears in his own form, offers consolation, places his right hand upon the head, and grants all boons—whether it be the power to travel through the sky, invisibility, the attainment of the divine eye, a vision of Buddha-fields, the attainment of samādhi, the attainment of dhāraṇīs, or the accomplishment of the ritual manual (*kalpa*) for the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*. [This is] the instruction of the Teacher.

2. Or the discourse on spells; or the retention of what has been heard; or the discourse on hidden treasures; or the discourse on the elements; or sorcery (*indrajāla*); or going to the world of the gods; or entering a chasm; or entering the abode of the *nāgas*; or the discourse on sacred fields (*kṣetra*); or the summoning of *yakṣas*; or the summoning of *rākṣasas*; or the raising of a *vetāḍa*; or entering a forest; or entering a mountain; or entering a city; or the demonstration of entering [the power of] medicinal herbs; or the state of being a sword-bearing *vidyādhara*; or the state of being a perfected *vidyādhara*; or the status of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*); or the attainment of kingship.

3. Whether it be the acquisition of sensory objects, sovereignty over a realm, the crushing of great armies, the power of movement, or plunging into the ocean—he grants all of that. He grants the accomplishment of every purpose; he protects according to one’s desires wherever they may be. By constant recitation, he purifies the five acts of immediate retribution. One attains the samādhi called "Purification through the Vision of All Beings Free from Obstructions. For one desiring to accomplish the ointment (*añjana*), on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, [one should take] realgar...

4. Having placed ink in a copper vessel, one should draw a mandala of sandalwood. Having placed it facing toward the noble Avalokiteśvara, the practitioner, having bathed well and wearing clean garments, should sit cross-legged facing the noble Avalokiteśvara and recite [the mantra]. One should perform the binding of the boundary with the Amoghapāśa mudrā, and the King of Wrath (Krodharāja) should be invoked seven times. One should consume the three white foods and remain without eating [other food]. For whichever son of good family or daughter of good family... the noble Aṣṭā-... [text continues]

5. One must observe the fast (upavāsa) according to the prescribed limbs. The recitation (jāpa) should be performed; as soon as it has been recited, [the vessel] blazes in a copper bowl, becomes hot, and froths. Taking that [substance], one should apply it as collyrium to the eyes. One travels through the air by means of supernatural power (ṛddhi). One beholds all the Buddha-fields. One beholds the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, in the ten directions. One will become a universal monarch (cakravartin) of the great holders of vidyā. One beholds all the abodes of the *vilas* opened up. All treasures (nidhi) leap forth—

They shall see them; they shall see all the celestial abodes with their doors opened, and wherever they desire, there they go. They will become invisible to all yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, grahas, humans, and non-humans, as well as to adversaries and enemies. On the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days, one should perform the recitation without speaking. One should offer eight thousand recitations while facing the noble Avalokiteśvara, seated in the cross-legged posture; by the mere completion of the recitation, [one shall see] the noble Avalokiteśvara in his divine...

7. He does not appear before [the Buddha] in his own physical form (*ātmabhāva*), but places his right hand upon his head. He attains the samādhi named *Vimalodgatāvalokitavikurva* (The Manifestation of the Purely Arisen Gaze), and he attains the supernatural power (*ṛddhi*) named *Sarvatathāgatavyavalokitādhiṣṭhānavyūhasandarśanaprabhāsa* (The Radiance of the Display of the Array of the Empowerment of the Gaze of All Tathāgatas). He attains a lifespan of a thousand divine aeons. He will obtain a divine body and behold all the Tathāgatas, including the Tathāgata Amitāyus, the Arhat, the Samyak-saṃbuddha.

1. He will gather the true Dharma and will not cause it to be confused. Having attended upon all the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dwelling in Sukhāvatī, he stands before them; he becomes possessed of a divine form. His hair will be curled and ringlet-like, and he obtains a celestial palace in the form of a peaked tower named *Padmaprabhāsavimalā*. Therefore, by that Vidyādhara who desires to obtain for his own body a physical existence with a core of diamond-hard essence (*vajrasāragarbha*), he should recite [the mantra] over that jar filled with scented water sixty-two thousand times, and then [offer it to] Noble Avalokiteśvara...

2. Before the Bodhisattva Tejorāja, having remained for a day and night fasting, one should bathe [the image]. At the very moment of bathing, his physical body will become composed of vajra; all the Tathāgatas will gaze upon him. His lifespan will be a thousand divine years. All yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, and grahas will become subject to his command. All devas and nāgas will appear before him. He will accomplish all mundane rites of siddhi. By the mere act of recollection, by the mere arising of the thought [of him], all—

All the grahas and all the apasmāras enter [the practitioner] and tell everything—whether true or false, whether real or unreal, whether possible or impossible, whether an occurrence or a non-occurrence, or whether there is prosperity and abundance or peace and plenty—they shall tell all that. They will perform all such tasks and duties. All the workers remain constantly like slaves. Then, one who desires to deliver each and every person in the world, and who desires to establish everyone under one's own control, [should proceed].

4. Desiring to liberate all beings from the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama; desiring to attain the samādhi named Amoghajñānavyūha; desiring to accomplish the maṇḍala of liberation; desiring to accomplish the ritual manual (kalpa) of the Amoghapāśahṛdaya; and desiring to accomplish the Mahāmoghapāśahṛdaya—that practitioner of the vidyā-mantra must individually fashion a reflected image of the noble Avalokiteśvara in his Amogha-form, [wearing] a crown of matted hair...

5. [He should be depicted as] smiling, wearing an antelope skin and the attire of Paśupati, adorned with all ornaments. He should be shown either seated in the *paryaṅka* posture or standing with his right knee bent and fallen toward Sudhana, while looking up at the face of the Wrathful King (*krodharāja*) on his left. The Wrathful King should have six arms and a wrathful appearance. Amitābha should be placed upon his crown. He should be adorned with all ornaments, and all [the figures] should be made with relics (*sadhātuka*). A lotus seat situated upon a mountain should also be fashioned. By one who is pure, wearing clean clothes, having bathed, for a day and night—

6. One must become a Vidyādhara who has been sprinkled with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) and consecrated by an ablution of water and mustard seeds. With a heart encompassed by great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), one should look [upon the rite]. If one does not perform the ritual in this manner, [the mantra] succeeds merely upon being recited; how much more so through the performance of the recitation-rite? And whichever Vidyādhara would worship eighty-eight koṭis of Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā—

7. Whether it be a vidyādhara, a monk, a nun, a layman, a laywoman, a king, a queen, or anyone else of such a kind who desires to see [the deity], who wishes to plant great roots of merit, who wishes to establish all sentient beings in roots of merit, and who wishes to effect the purification of all evils—that person should fashion an image of the noble Avalokiteśvara made of gold, representing Amoghapāśa.

1. According to one's means, whatever is available should be used. Then, one should stand facing east and prepare a square *kuṅkuma* mandala, well-proportioned and marked out with vermilion lines. In the center of the mandala, a garland of lotuses should be made, and in the middle of that lotus garland, a water-pitcher (*bhṛṅgāra*) should be placed. It should be fashioned with various flowers, and four jars filled with scented water should be set out. Decorated with flowers according to one's means, it should be arranged with five offering bowls (*arghapātra*). One should burn incense using five incense burners, burning *agaru* (aloewood) incense.

2. Sixteen lamps of fragrant oil should be lit. One should worship the noble Avalokiteśvara with flowers, incense, perfumes, and garlands, and offer them to Lokeśvara while sitting cross-legged facing him. Having bound the Amoghapāśa mudrā, one should consecrate oneself, recollect the King of Wrath (Krodharāja) once, and, having focused the mind upon all the Tathāgatas, pay homage by mentally bowing toward the ten directions. One should bind the mudrā for recitation and perform the recitation. By reciting it one hundred and eight times—

3. There will be a trembling of the earth; he rejoices within himself and sees it blazing. And all those Tathāgatas manifest the vision of their faces. It blazes within the matted locks of the noble Avalokiteśvara, and the sound of the word "Well done! issues forth. By the second recitation of one hundred and eight [times], it displays the signs of great accomplishment (*mahāsiddhi*). The noble Avalokiteśvara extends his arm and places it upon the crown of the head of the knowledge-holder (*vidyādhara*). This is called "The Surveying of All Tathāgatas."

He attains meditative concentration (*samādhi*). He will become a holder of the Amoghapāśa vidyā-mantra. At dawn, those Tathāgatas will grant him a vision; they will reveal all Buddha-fields, and he will become endowed with the roots of merit of all the Tathāgatas. By the third recitation of the eight hundred [mantras], at the time when the sun is rising, the Noble Avalokiteśvara appears before him in his own form. He gives him the noose named Padmavivara and bestows all accomplishments (*siddhi*). These—

5. He gives his approval to those who possess the Jina. Furthermore, whoever shows this form of the noble Avalokiteśvara will have planted roots of merit before sixty-four thousand Tathāgatas. All the deities, headed by Brahmā, as well as the divine sons Īśvara and Maheśvara, will always desire to see him. He will be free from all diseases. And all [beings] will provide for his protection, defense, and guardianship, being constantly bound to him with the fulfillment of every excellence. All—

6. One becomes free from evil. Then, an image of the Noble Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa should be made as before. A mandala of white sandalwood should be prepared, filled with water scented with white sandalwood and perfumes, and five vessels for the offering (argha) should be set out. Various flowers should be strewn about while burning incense of white sandalwood. The Noble Avalokiteśvara should be worshipped, and forty-two lamps fed with fragrant oil should be lit. Four incense burners should be placed [around the mandala].

7. The King of Wrath (Krodharāja) should be invoked twenty-one times. The Vidyādhara must be pure and wear clean garments. The mudrās of Amoghapāśa should be performed seven times, and the mudrā for recitation (jāpa) should be assumed. Seated in the cross-legged posture (paryaṅka), one should extend the index finger. With the left hand formed in the shape of a lotus, the recitation should be performed one hundred and eight times. When the one hundred and eighth is completed, the sound "Sādhu! issues forth from the eastern direction. One sees oneself delighted, [surrounded by] all kings, ministers, and courtiers...

1. They become submissive along with their retinues and cities. By merely uttering their names, they come from a thousand *yojanas* away; all remain as servants, remaining as those who carry out one's commands. Whatever you command, they will do; she herself will become your mistress. One will become greatly honored. By reciting [the mantra] two hundred and eight times, Śakra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and the others will become submissive; they remain as executors of one’s orders. Whatever you command, they perform. And the four Great Kings, together with their hosts and retinues, the hosts of Yakṣas and Rākṣasas—

2. [The following] become manifest: by reciting one hundred and eight times, the Moon and Sun descend from the sky and stand before [the practitioner]. The deities of night and the deities of the sky descend and stand before [him]. All those who perform services as servants remain present. By reciting one hundred and eight times for the fourth [deity], all *nāgas* remain under control; indeed, all [of them], beginning with Nanda and Upananda, the *nāga* kings of the ocean, remain under control. One should fashion an image of the noble Avalokiteśvara out of copper and a small mandala out of red sandalwood.

3. One should scatter red flowers and burn incense from four incense burners. Furthermore, one should light fifty-two lamps of ghee and burn incense. Five vessels for the *argha* offering should be set out. One should worship Noble Avalokiteśvara. The King of Wrath (*krodharāja*) should be recited twenty-one times. The Amoghapāśa mudrā should be performed twenty-one times. One should sit cross-legged before the cloth painting (*duṣyapaṭa*), focusing the mind upon all sentient beings.

4. One should bring to mind the Tathāgata Rūpa and look out in the four directions with a gaze of loving-kindness (*maitrī*). One should bring to mind all the realms of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, and asuras; one should bring to mind the eight great hells and look upon them with a mind of compassion (*karuṇā*). One should form the *padma*-shaped mudrā for the recitation (*japa*) and perform the recitation. When one hundred and eight [recitations] are completed, there will be a great earthquake in the four directions and a thunderous roar. And those who have gone to all the hells—

5. Those beings who are liberated—by this, all the gates of hell are opened, recited, and reduced to ashes. Those beings in the hells shall go to a happy destination until the final attainment of enlightenment. Furthermore, all those in the hells shall themselves be liberated from the experience of suffering and their bodies shall be adorned with divine marks. And all those beings who see [this] shall become non-retrogressive. By a second recitation of one hundred and eight times, [the power reaches] the subterranean realms (pātāla).

6. Those beings who are devoid of light, by the power of this Amoghapāśahṛdaya, become free from darkness. Rays of light issue forth; those beings are completely liberated. They will be born by spontaneous transformation (*upapāduka*) in the abode of the Noble Avalokiteśvara. They will be entirely freed from old age and death until the end of awakening. They attain the samādhi called Samantaprabhāvodgatavimalā and shall have a lifespan of one eon. Having passed away from there, they will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī.

7. It is split; it remains at the very foot of that [statue] until the end of enlightenment. And he shall become free from all sorrow. Having made fine powders of white sandalwood, kāstūrikā, camphor, and various other kinds of fragrant substances, they should be ground well again. They should be mixed with water containing the essences of kunduruka and sarjarasa, along with white *gahana*, and ground into a fine paste. An image of the Noble Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa, measuring eight finger-breadths and adorned with all ornaments, should be fashioned.

1. One should fashion [the deity] adorned with a crown of matted locks, wearing the attire of the Lord of Creatures (Paśupati) consisting of an antelope skin, four-armed, holding a single lotus in one hand, a noose in the second, a trident in the third, and a gesture of reassurance (*āśvāsana*) in the fourth; seated upon a lotus throne, adorned with a fathom-wide halo of light. To the right, Noble Tārā should be made, and to the left, Vimalamati. Below Lokeśvara is the King of Wrath (*Krodharāja*), and above is Abhidhābhajin. Then, the Vidyādhara, having become pure and wearing clean garments, bathing at the three junctions of the day and wearing three sets of rags, should perform the recitation (*japa*) at the three junctions.

It should be performed one hundred and eight times, from the eighth day until the full moon on the fifteenth. A mandala should be smeared with various perfumes and outlined with five colors. In the center of the mandala, the deity of the Amoghapāśa-vidyā should be painted, kneeling with her gaze directed upward. In the four corners, Īśvara, Maheśvara, Yama, and Varuṇa should be painted. It should be divided into four doors. One should place vessels filled with perfume in the four corners, and at the four doors, one should place jars filled with fragrant offerings and *triśukra*.

3. One arranging the eight *bali* offerings and the vessels for the *argha* water should fashion them adorned with various flowers; one should burn incense of agalloch and sandalwood; one should light one hundred and twenty-eight lamps of fragrant oil; and it should be made beautifully decorated with banners. One should perform worship to the Bodhisattva Noble Avalokiteśvara and stand facing east upon the mandala. A thread for the cloth painting (*paṭasūtra*) sixteen cubits in length, made of five-colored threads, should be tied at one end to a golden ring. [Mukti-]

4. A *kuṇḍalika* (coil) should be bound; it should be made completely encircled and wrapped like a snake. Having formed it into a coil, it should be placed within the central mandala and covered with a clean cloth by one who is pure. The Vidyādhara, seated cross-legged facing the mandala, should perform the Amoghapāśa mudrā thirty-two times. Having performed self-protection (*ātmarakṣā*), he should perform the binding of the mandala and the binding of the directions. The King of Wrath (*krodharāja*) should be recited one hundred and eight times. Then, by the Vidyādhara—

5. With a smiling face, one should clearly manifest the mudrā of recitation (*jāpamudrā*) and perform the recitation (*japa*). One thousand and eight recitations should be offered. Having consecrated each individual mustard seed with the mantra, they should be cast upon the thread for the cloth painting (*paṭasūtra*). This must be done without speaking. When the eighth thousand is completed, the cord of the cloth thread will burst into flames. Various rays of light will issue forth, and the sound "Excellent! Excellent! will resound: "Well done, well done, O Vidyādhara! You have attained success (*siddhi*). Take this Amoghapāśa!"

6. Perform all your activities; this supreme, perfected Great Cintāmaṇi-noose will accomplish both mundane and supramundane tasks for you. And that Noble Avalokiteśvara will blaze forth. From the body of Lokeśvara, great clouds of fragrance will issue forth, pervading an area of six *yojanas* with their scent. Merely by smelling that fragrance, one will be freed from all diseases. Through the application of the powder of the "dust" of all sufferings, obscurations, and poisons, they shall be destroyed. All sentient beings—

7. They will become followers. Then, the vidyādhara, having taken that cintāmaṇi-noose and placed it in a copper casket, should set it at the feet of the noble Avalokiteśvara. When there is a task to be performed, he should be well-bathed and pure; it should be taken up and the task performed. It must be worshipped three times every day. That vidyādhara becomes a traveler through the sky; with a purified body, he sports together with the vidyādharas of former times, and all are brought under his control.

1. [They] will exist. Their lifespan will be one thousand years. Having passed away, they will be born through spontaneous birth (*upapāduka*) upon the calyxes of lotuses in the world-system Sukhāvatī together with those who are to be born there. They will become universal monarchs (*cakravartin*) of all the vidyādharas. Their lifespan will last for one hundred thousand kalpas until the end at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍala*). And merely by seeing that Noble Avalokiteśvara, they will exhaust the five deeds of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*) and so forth. Having recited the *sumana* flower mantra one hundred and eight times, [one should offer] one by one to the Noble Avalokiteśvara...

2. It should be known that when one hundred and eight [recitations] are complete, all the kings, their kingdoms, hopes, inner circles, and furthermore their retinues, will become submissive. By means of this, the practitioner himself, along with his gold, grain, female and male slaves, and laborers, will come under his control. Taking jasmine flowers and remains of offerings (*nirmālya*), together with fragrant *pṛyaṅgu*, *tagara*, *kuṣṭha*, *sadā*, saffron (*kuṅkuma*), *māṃsī*, *sāmaka*, *spṛka*, *nalada*, *bola*, *sadā*, and mustard seeds (*sarṣapa*)—this fine powder, made into pills, should be infused with divine water; it is the supreme *arghada* known as the "Lotus," which brings fame and glory.

3. At the outset, it removes all diseases, subdues fevers, [and cures] spider-bites, swellings, erysipelas, scabies, leprosy, and ailments of the blood; thus, they declare that through this ointment one becomes happy, and all those diseases are destroyed. Having bathed, the sages declare it to be a remover of sin. By applying this auspicious *tilaka*—which bestows long life and royal fortune—one always achieves victory when entering battle. For women, it is a source of great delight and the supreme means of subjugation. It destroys the effects of *kākhorda* spells...

4. Neither poison nor venom, nor powdered substances, nor the application of mantras, nor ointments, food, bathing—none of these are ever required for one who constantly and perpetually crosses over to happiness. Thus spoke Lokeśvara to the world: for headache, an ointment; for eyeache, collyrium; for toothache, holding [the mantra] in the mouth; for abdominal pain, warm water; for side-pain, an ointment of ghee; for pain in the limbs and minor members, an anointing; for subjugation, an ointment on the palm of the hand; for great illness, massaging and bathing; and for seizure by yakṣas—

5. By burning the hand-act (*hastakarman*) with incense, one is liberated from all planetary seizures (*graha*). A *tilaka* marked on the head of those who are sealed [by these spirits] cures heart disease. When mixed with warm water and salt, it pacifies the planetary seizures; when combined with parched grain (*lāja*) and smeared with clarified butter (*sṛta*), there will be great peace. In all cases, having recited the mantra twenty-one times, one should prepare a cow-dung mandala in all instances of strife, quarrel, conflict, and dispute, scattering flowers upon it and placing four powders of fragrance. One should also place four vessels filled with milk.

6. One should offer four *argha*-bowls and four incense burners, burning incense of *agaru* and *turuṣka*. Having recited [the mantra] over *guggulu* resin twenty-one times, one should burn it as incense. One should worship the Noble Avalokiteśvara made of fragrant substances. Having recited the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*) one hundred and eight times and having consecrated mustard seeds with the recitation, they should be scattered in the four directions. The *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* should be recalled ninety-one times. In all cases of strife, quarrel, conflict, and dispute, one will be the victor. He—

7. Victory shall prevail in battles and conflicts with all armies, whether one's own or those of an enemy; he shall conquer the fourfold army even if the enemy is Śakra himself, let alone those who are merely human. One who desires to invoke Śakra should recite [the mantra] over one hundred and eight lotuses, offering each one to Noble Avalokiteśvara while uttering the name of Śakra. Having consecrated bdellium (*guggulu*), clarified butter, and mustard seeds one hundred and eight times, he should offer them as an oblation into a fire made of *arka* wood.

1. Having lit the fire on the fourteenth day of the lunar month, the ritual of recitation (*jāpavidhi*) should be performed in its entirety. Śakra, the lord of the gods, together with his army and vehicles, will descend; they will stand before one, become obedient to one's commands, and all will remain under one's control. Whatever one seeks, he grants it—except for the position of Śakra himself, which this mind cannot endure. One should recite while treading upon the foot of Brahmā. When one hundred and eight recitations are completed, at the completion of those one hundred and eight, Brahmā appears before one in his own form. He offers all boons according to one’s desire.

2. It dwells in the mind.
