Having recited the *Nārāyaṇa* mantra ninety times over *guggulu* resin, one should first offer it as incense with water and *sarṣapa* seeds over which the mantra has been recited twenty-one times. Nārāyaṇa appears before one in his own form. He becomes a performer of all rites (*sarvakarmakara*) and grants even the form of Viśvarūpa. He bestows a village upon the donor of gold. One will possess the great strength and speed of Nārāyaṇa. Having looked at the face of Maheśvara, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times into the right ear; then, with *sarṣapa*...

Having recited [the mantra] twenty-one times, one should offer it from the head; incense of guggulu should be offered after reciting it seven times, and the water for the guest-offering (argha) and the water for the feet (pādya) should be presented. Thereupon, the image of Maheśvara moves, and the sound of "Well done! (sādhukāra) issues forth. Then he appears before one in the form of Maheśvara, and he stands with his entire host and retinue under one's control. He grants all desired boons. For one wishing to invoke Mahākāla, [one should take] eight hundred and... guggulu.

4. Having recited [the mantra] one hundred times, blood and liquor should be offered. Having recited [the mantra] twenty-one times over mustard seeds, they should be thrown toward Mahākāla; he will be summoned. He will become a servant, he will become a performer of all tasks. Wherever he is sent, there he goes. He will be accompanied by his own retinue and attendants. All the abodes of the yakṣas will have their doors opened. Whatever he desires, that he performs. He will be equal to all grass.

5. ...they will appear. They become providers of all joy; they perform every action through recitation twenty-one times at the three junctions of the day without speaking [to others]. The night deities, together with their hosts, retinues, and attendants—those gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans who roam by day and night—all shall come under one's control. They will perform every task; they will all constantly stand before one in their own forms throughout the night. All night-long enjoyments...

6. [The deities] present celestial palaces to one who is pure, clothed in clean garments, well-bathed, truthful, established in a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*), always possessing compassion for all sentient beings, and constantly performing the recitation (*jāpa*) while relying upon great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*). Thus ends the Chapter on the Procedure for Recitation (*Jāpavidhipaṭala*). Now, therefore, I shall explain the procedure for the fire-oblation (*homavidhi*), which accomplishes all rites—auspicious, pacifying (*śānti*), nourishing (*pauṣṭika*), and malevolent (*abhicāraka*), providing protection, removing all diseases, and effecting subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*).

7. One who desires the protection of the household should always perform the following: having kindled a fire with fuel of *arka* wood soaked in bitter oil (*kaṭutaila*), one should offer one hundred and eight oblations. One should recite the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* one hundred and eight times, and the *Krodharāja* seven times. Thus there will be great protection for the household. [This applies] in all cases of strife, quarrel, conflict, and dispute; against all adversaries and enemies; and against all diseases, all fevers, and all... (44a).

1. All calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions—all planetary spirits (*graha*), all famines, wildernesses, deaths, great deaths, and [the afflictions of] men, women, boys, and girls—will be pacified. All deities will provide him with protection, defense, and guardianship. Īśvara and Maheśvara will be constantly and perpetually bound to him. And the noble Avalokiteśvara will always and continuously desire to appear before him. By means of oblations of ghee, mustard seeds, and *guggulu*, through one thousand and eight burnt offerings (*homa*), there shall be great peace throughout all regions, kingdoms, cities, villages, hamlets, and districts.

2. They shall come to pass. Before the noble Avalokiteśvara, on the full moon day, one should offer one thousand and eight oblations of white flowers, *gandha*, *priyaṅgu*, and *tagara*, anointed with pungent oil. The king, his ministers, the inner court, and their retinues, as well as the villages, cities, towns, districts, elephants, horses, cows, and buffaloes, will become submissive. One should offer one thousand and eight oblations of *apāmārga* fuel-sticks, anointed with curd, honey, and ghee, along with white flowers. One obtains a thousand villages from the noble Avalokiteśvara.

3. One should offer one hundred and eight oblations of lotus-stalk fuel sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee before the deity. Within three nights, one obtains eight hundred *dīnāras*. Having kindled a fire with *khadira* wood, one should offer one thousand and eight oblations of white water-lilies (*kumuda*), including their stalks, roots, and leaves, smeared with mustard seeds; thus one is liberated from all *vināyakas*. On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, having fasted and put on white garments, one should become pure and well-bathed. [One should apply] sandalwood and *priyaṅgu*—

4. One should offer water mixed with ghee and mustard seeds one thousand and eight times at the time of midnight; then a yakṣiṇī will come. She bestows five thousand *rūpakas*. On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for a full day and night, one should go to the bank of a river flowing to the ocean, kindle a fire with *bilva* wood, and offer eight thousand *bilva* flowers smeared with ghee and honey. Then a yakṣa maiden, adorned with all ornaments, will arrive; she comes at midnight.

5. He holds a jewel casket; it must be seized by that vidyādhara and must not be looked at with the mouth. Again, one hundred and eight recitations are to be performed. Having set down the vessel, she falls at his feet, saying, "I shall serve the vidyādhara. Then the vidyādhara, having recited the King of Wrath twenty-one times, whatever task there may be, a recitation of one hundred and eight times is to be given at midnight. A yakṣiṇī arrives and will perform all tasks as a servant.

6. [They] will become performers of all rites. On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, wherever a treasure (nidhi) is located, one should go there and recite [the mantra] one thousand and eight times, and remain performing the offering ritual (balividhāna). Worship of the Noble Amogharāja should be performed; having offered one thousand and eight oblations of *sarṣapa* seeds mixed with ghee—using jasmine flowers, fruit, leaves, and *sarṣapa*—one should empower water with *sarṣapa* seeds twenty-one times and strike the earth. Then all treasures will rise up. Having taken them, a portion should be given to the Three Jewels, and the remainder may be taken by oneself.

7. It should be performed as follows: having kindled a fire with Vibhītaka wood, one should offer one thousand and eight oblations of sesame seeds and rice grains smeared with ghee. The king, together with his harem and retinue, along with his fourfold army, his wealth, grain, gold, and bullion, will become submissive and remain so for the duration of his life. One should offer one thousand and eight oblations of white mustard seeds, Campaka flowers, and lotuses smeared with ghee; all the men, women, boys, and girls residing in the entire realm will become submissive. [One should offer] rice husks...

1. One should offer salt ninety-one times; the people of the four castes will become submissive. Having kindled a fire with *agasti* wood, one should offer one thousand and eight *arka* flowers smeared with honey and ghee. One should perform worship of the noble Avalokiteśvara daily; one obtains a hundred *dīnāras*. One should offer a thousand *palāśa* leaves, parched grain, and fuel-sticks; one obtains a thousand pieces of gold. Worship of the Three Jewels must be performed; it reappears when distributed again. On the full moon of the fifteenth day, having fasted for a day and night, [one should go to] a river flowing to the ocean...

2. Having descended to the waist-deep water in the river Minyānandī, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times over mustard seeds. Having consecrated them twenty-one times, one should strike the river with those wrathful [seeds]. Then, a maiden emerges from the midst of the water. She bestows a great abundance of jewels. Having taken them, one should offer half the portion to the Three Jewels and perform worship to the noble Avalokiteśvara. On the full moon day of the fifteenth, having fasted for a day and night and performed worship to the Blessed One, the noble Avalokiteśvara, one should [offer] *apāmārga* wood-fuel smeared with honey and ghee and *sarjarasa*...

3. Having recited [the mantra] over flour-cakes (*saktu*) one hundred and eight times, one should offer them into the fire one thousand times. One’s own name should be invoked; one will be liberated from all sinful obstructions. One will be freed from all afflictions and all diseases. All adversaries and enemies shall perish. One should offer fuel-sticks of *arka*, sesame, mustard seeds, and *guggulu* resin soaked in clarified butter (*ghṛta*); there will be great peace (*mahāśānti*). For the rite of nourishment (*pauṣṭika*), one should offer parched grain (*lāja*) soaked in milk, mustard seeds, and white sandalwood (*śvetacandana*) soaked in clarified butter, one hundred and eight times.

4. [For] Rama, the auspicious one: on the fourteenth day, one should perform an *abhicāruka* (malevolent rite) using *karavīra* flowers mixed with seven kinds of salt, with fuel-sticks of thorny wood smeared with pungent oil. One should offer oblations (*juhūyāt*) twenty-one times after reciting [the mantra] over lotus, sandalwood, and mustard seeds smeared with clarified butter, and one hundred and eight times; one should cause the Krodha-mantra to resound seven times. Then, during a drought, a great rain will fall. As long as the command is maintained, it will rain. Taking those ashes, reciting the mantra over them twenty-one times, and throwing them into the sky, there will be excessive rain.

5. One pacifies a plague. If one throws [the offering] in the four directions, there will be a binding of a great boundary (*mahāsīmābandha*). If one throws it toward a cloud, all winds, clouds, and thunderbolts will have no power. For the immobilization of an army, one performs a *homa* with sesame and rice. For the repelling of a hostile army, one performs a *homa* with the seven grains. For the accomplishment of a cave-dwelling, one performs a *homa* with moths. One should offer *arkka* leaves with clarified butter; then all the openings of caves become opened. For entering a forest, [one should offer] lilies (*kumuda*), *tagara*, and mustard seeds smeared with clarified butter; [then] the entire forest—

6. The openings [of the underworld] become unsealed; all substances and medicinal herbs remain in their natural forms. Having kindled a fire with leaves and wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of black pepper (*marica*); Śakra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, and the others descend and stand before one. One should offer eight thousand oblations of golden flowers, *karṇikāra* flowers, and blue lotuses smeared with clarified butter; the moon and sun descend, grant all boons, and one travels through the sky. One should prepare fuel-sticks of *rājavṛkṣa* wood and [offer] a hundred flowers—

7. By offering twenty-one oblations of *tāvarī*, moth-sandalwood (*pataṅgacandana*), and mustard seeds smeared with barley-oil at the three junctions of the day for seven days, one gains mastery over the great kings, including their harems and retinues. This subdues all spirits, grahas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas. With rice, mustard seeds, and salt as the offering, it should be performed everywhere while employing the Amoghapāśa mudrā. In all cases, one should recollect this mantra while using the Krodha mudrā. This is the procedure for the oblation. Next, the Amoghapāśa... [45a] (P82a5, D.84b4)

1. I shall now proclaim the ritual procedure for the cloth painting (*paṭavidhāna*) of the *Śrīhṛdaya*, the Great King of Ritual Manuals (*mahākalparāja*). By the mere sight of it, even one who has committed the five deeds of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*) extending to the Avīci hell is purified. One should have a cloth made measuring two cubits in length and width, with uncut fringes and free from defects. It should be made of *arbuda* wool, very smooth and well-cleansed, and perfectly square on all four sides. The painter must be pure, observing the vow of silence (*maunīvrata*) and the fast (*poṣadha*), wearing clean garments, eating only the three white foods, bathing three times a day, and using non-staining pigments in a new vessel.

2. On a clean, new, and pure *kūrca* (grass mat), one should paint the noble Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa—either standing, sitting, or seated in the *paryaṅka* posture. He should be depicted adorned with a crown of matted hair (*jaṭāmakuṭa*), wearing the attire of the Lord of Creatures (*paśupati*) with an antelope skin (*eṇeya-carma*), and embellished with all ornaments. He should have sixteen arms, a gentle face, and a smiling countenance and eyes. He wears a crown of the Victorious One Amitābha, faces the south, and has a fresh moon within his crown. His two hands are raised in the *vajrāñjali* gesture in the form of a lotus.

3. Two hands below should be formed with the *samantamukha-mudrā*. With two hands, the *jāpa-mudrā* should be made by extending the right index finger and holding it in the shape of a lotus; a rosary (*akṣamālā*) should be held between them, and the two [hands] should be formed with the *amoghapāśa-mudrā*. With one hand [the deity holds] a trident, with the second a lotus, with the third the *amoghapāśa* scripture, with the fourth the *amoghapāśa* itself, with the fifth a breath (*āśvāsa*), with the sixth a water-pot (*kuṇḍikā*), and with the seventh—

4. With the eighth [offering], one should prepare a vessel filled with various jewels and a basket of various flowers, adorned with a fathom-wide radiance. His body should be depicted as beautified by various flowers. One should construct a gabled pavilion (kuṭāgāra) for Potalaka, well-proportioned, square, with four pillars, beautiful on its base, inlaid and variegated with various jewels, adorned with garlands of lotuses, fashioned with circles of vajras, and beautified by various flowering branches and plantain trees. On the right—

5. The sun is not above; the moon is on the left, to be fashioned by the sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm. With various flowers and silken banners in their hands, they worship the Blessed One. The mountain should be made in the shape of a lotus, adorned with a pedestal, beautified by a pond with its staff, and strewn with fish. It is filled with crocodiles, swans, cranes, jīvañjīvaka birds, and cakravāka ducks. On top of the mountain, a lotus throne fashioned from various jewels and gems should be made, as well as a lion throne.

6. On the right side of the enclosure, Īśvara should be depicted. Outside, in the position of the *kuṭi*, Maheśvara should be on the left, adorned with all ornaments. Inside, to the right of Noble Avalokiteśvara, Noble Tārā should be depicted. To the left [of Tārā] are Vaśatāṅgī and Śalajja; [and further left] Vimalamati, with her hand in the gesture of consolation (*āśvāsahasta*). Sudhana should be depicted kneeling at her feet. In the position of the central *karkaṭika* (pedestal), the Wrathful King should be depicted, four-armed, with a wrathful form and holding weapons.

7. One should depict [the deity] with a hand holding a noose and a sword, with a trident and a lotus in his hands, seated in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*) upon a lotus seat with his body slightly bent. His head should be turned upward, and sages should be made to be praising him from the right and left. Below that, on the right and left, one should make Mahāvajraśikhara and Mahāvajrapāśahasta. The hosts of gods—Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Vāsava—should be depicted within the lotus pond; on the left side, Śakra and Brahmā should be made, as well as the four Great Kings.

On the left side, they should be depicted wearing armor and bound with girdles. Below them, the goddesses of the Lotus family, the messengers (dūtīs), and those with busy hands should be made; likewise Śrī, Sarasvatī, Bhīmā, the deities of night, the deity of the earth, and the deity of crops. On the side of Īśvara, Bhṛkuṭī should be made, and Pāṇḍaravāsinī between the messengers of Maheśvara. Ekajaṭā and the Rākṣasī should also be included. A lotus mountain, square on all sides and inlaid with the seven jewels, should be made; it should be filled with various trees and creepers, adorned with flowers, and graced by lotus ponds.

2. It should be strewn with various flowers. To the left, one should depict lions, tigers, kumbhāṇḍas, and young nāgas, as well as the five great guhyakas. Below, the five great nāga kings should be depicted everywhere upon the mountain seat, holding various flowers and jewels in their hands, gazing up at the face of the Blessed One. At the feet of Noble Avalokiteśvara, the vidyādharas should be depicted prostrate on their knees, holding flowers, incense, and camphor in their hands, gazing up at the face of the Blessed One.

3. One should depict the Victor Amitābha, the Śākya King, the Lord of World-Kings, the Great Sage, as the head of the world. By the mere sight of this cloth painting, all those who have committed the five acts of immediate retribution and have accumulated sins in the Avīci hell for hundreds of thousands of births—all these shall perish and be destroyed; and they shall all be completely liberated. How much more so for pure beings who are devoted with faith and seek the worship of the Jewels: for them, there will be great fruit and great benefits in this very life.

4. One should expect that he will be endowed with roots of merit in the presence of six hundred and forty million *koṭī-niyuta-śata-sahasra* of Tathāgatas, equal to the sands of the river Gaṅgā; he will have planted roots of merit. By the mere sight of this cloth-painting (*duṣyapaṭala*) containing the single vision of the Noble Avalokiteśvara and the Amoghapāśahṛdaya, the Noble Avalokiteśvara takes heed of him. [The sight—]

5. And if one recites it, by the mere act of crying out [for help], he immediately gazes [upon them] and causes all obscurations to be cast away; the *Amogharāja-dhāraṇī-hṛdaya* becomes accomplished. For one who is ill, tormented by a great disease, and distracted by hundreds of thousands of sufferings from various ailments—all those [afflictions] are completely liberated upon the mere sight [of this], and all diseases, all sufferings, and all illnesses will be gone, and they shall be free from obscurations and disease.

6. Even those who have fallen into the womb of animals are liberated merely by seeing it. Having adorned this cotton cloth (*duṣyapaṭa*) with great honor and respect, with a great retinue, with great musical instruments and cymbals, and with parasols, banners, and flags, one should cause it to enter a great city, a royal palace, a monastery, a district, a house, or a village. As soon as it has entered, the cotton cloth [dispels] all strife, quarrels, conflicts, disputes, and famine.

7. Deserts and wildernesses will be pacified; fear of one's own army and the armies of others will be stilled. All yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, pūtanās, kaṭapūtanas, skandas, apasmāras, and chāyās will be pacified. There will be security, abundance, delight, and great happiness for many people. They will exist with great joy and mental well-being. Following the six perfections, all who pass away through the mere sight of this [sūtra] will be reborn in the world-system Sukhāvatī.

1. ...all sentient beings shall become those who go to the [Pure Land of] Sukhāvatī. For seven million eons, in birth after birth, they shall possess the recollection of their past lives (*jātismara*). The Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas shall attain the samādhi not yet attained, named *Padmaprabhāsavimalaviśuddhirāja*. They shall also attain the status of a Universal Monarch of Vidyādharas named *Padmapratiṣṭhita*. This is the ritual procedure for the preparation of the cloth-painting (*paṭavidhāna*).
Amoghapāśakalparāja – Part IV 46a1 (P84a3, D.86b3):
1. Now, therefore, I shall explain the great ritual manual (*mahākalpa*) and mandala of the Amoghapāśahṛdaya. [The river...]

2. On a riverbank, or at a lake abounding in lotuses and water-lilies, or in a flower garden, a fruit grove, or a celestial palace situated on pure ground; having thoroughly cleansed a portion of the earth that is free from grass, chaff, hair, husks, ashes, charcoal, heaps of refuse, and potsherds, and devoid of stones, gravel, hard clods, bones, skulls, skeletons, and the corpses of the dead; and where there is a pool or spring on a level plot of land with a stream flowing from the north to the south, and which is well-proportioned toward the southwest and northeast, where there is a tree—

3. Adorned [with these], and having reached that place which is delightful and endowed with the splendor of a mind of excellent color, one should indeed recite the mantra and scatter water and mustard seeds all around; this is the supreme purification of the ground. Having recited it thirty-one times over the mustard seeds, they should be scattered while reciting the King of Wrath (Krodharāja). In the four directions, there shall likewise be a binding of the quarters, a binding of the mandala, and a binding of the boundary for a hundred yojanas all around. All evil ones and all obstructors and leaders of obstacles shall depart; they will not remain even for a moment.

And they go forth into the ten directions; wicked spirits, wicked beings, and those wicked, fierce wild animals—all these attain pacification. All the deities protect that site and region; the wise know that the maṇḍala must not perish there. Having measured a square maṇḍala thirty-two cubits on each side near the water, well-proportioned with four corners, level, adorned with divisions, with four gates and provided with four archways, one should then draw the maṇḍala with powder of five colors after tracing it with a five-colored thread—starting from the white [corner].

5. On the auspicious eighth or fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, under a favorable lunar mansion and on a propitious date, one should have an excellent maṇḍala drawn using stakes of white sandalwood. One skilled in the proper distribution of sections should first [draw] with a white line, the second with red, the third is known to be yellow, the fourth likewise blue (ākāśaka), and the fifth black like collyrium; in the center, within the womb-maṇḍala (*garbhamandala*), one should draw a lotus with a thousand petals upon nine vessels placed on a base of nine tufts of grass.

6. On all sides, it has the form of a raised altar (*vedikā*), and it is adorned all around with garlands of lotuses and variegated colors. Therein, in the center, one should place the Blessed One, the King of the Śākya Buddhas, the Great Sage; to the right, Amitābha, the Tathāgata, King of the Lords of the World; and [to his right] Lokeśvaranātha, wearing the guise of Amoghapāśa, following the mantra. To the left is Vajrapāṇi, holding a fly-whisk and a vajra in his hands, with a frowning face and a core of flames. Following after Āryāvalokiteśvara are the goddess Tārā and Vimalagati.

7. They should be depicted. Beneath Avalokiteśvara, Mahāgaurī, Pāṇḍaravāsinī, and Maheśvarī (Mahāśvetā) should be depicted, holding a staff and a water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*) in their hands. Beneath her, Ekajaṭā-Rākṣasī should be made. She should be depicted with distorted teeth, wearing a garland of skulls, standing firm, wearing the sacrificial thread (*yajñopavīta*), four-armed, holding a vajra and an axe in her right and left [hands], and threatening the finger-guards, Asuras, and Vināyakas with her left fingers. To the left, one wearing the attire of Brahmā should be depicted, O Noble Avalokiteśvara.

1. [One should depict] Īśvara, adorned with a crown of matted locks (jaṭāmakuṭa). To his left and right, Īśvara and Antakeśvara should be made. Below him, the goddess Śrī, the deities Sarasvatī and Rātri, and the deities of the crops and fruits should be made. Below that, all around, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and the others should be made; and the sages, adorned with crowns of matted locks, should be stationed. In the four corners, the four Great Kings, equipped and bound in armor, should be stationed. In the intervals between them, the goad, axe, vajra, staff, noose, and spike should be depicted.

2. Outside the interior of the maṇḍala are Brahmā, Rudra, and the goddess Umā; on the side of Brahmā is Sarasvatī in the form of Bhṛkuṭī. Between them are a staff and a water-pot. In one corner is the *Amoghapāśahṛdayavimokṣamaṇḍala*, a discourse on the Dharma. In another [corner] is Śivāvahā, and then Hayagrīva, the wrathful deity, should be placed. At the eastern gate, Mahābhairavanetra should be stationed. To the south, the Vajra-Vināyaka named Mahākelikila should be depicted, holding a vajra, an axe, and a noose. To the west is Padmakulasundara—

3. A female messenger (dūtī) should be made with her left hand holding [an object]. To the north, a Gaṇa named Mahāvajraśikhara should be made, holding a vajra-noose in his hand. Then, at the entrance door, a flask filled with scented water should be placed; it should be well-bound with Chinese silk within the central maṇḍala, and the flask should be positioned so as to be covered with gold according to one's intention. Having placed it with water of sandalwood, saffron, kastūrikā, and camphor, it should be adorned with all ornaments. It should be covered with fine Chinese silk and [adorned] with flower garlands.

4. It should be adorned with a golden ring; four incense burners should be placed upon it. While burning agalloch incense, a cord made of five-colored silk threads should be fashioned there according to the measurement of a sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*). A golden trident should be fastened to the ring, and on the second side, a lotus water-pot (*padmakuṇḍikā*) inlaid with pearls and gems should be fastened. A vessel for the circular enclosure should be placed above, and an offering of worship should be performed. Amoghapā-...

5. It should be recited one thousand and eight times with a sincere heart. An offering of unbroken grains (akṣata) should be prepared using mustard seeds, sandalwood, camphor, musk, or fragrant powder. Fragrance should be diffused at the four gateways, and jars filled with incense should be placed there. Thirty-two vessels for the guest-water (argha) should be set out; vessels of gold and silver should be provided. Eight jars filled with incense should be placed, and eight jars filled with fragrant white substances.

6. It should be established. Eight vessels filled with various flavors and fragrances should be set out; eight vessels filled with the fragrance of scented curds and milk should be set out. There are eight offerings. With sixty-four types of offerings and the like, the *bali* should be prepared—purely by one who is pure—and it must be free from meat, blood, onions, garlic, pungent foods, and foul-smelling flowers. It should be strewn with various flowers and adorned with various parasols, banners, cloths, and streamers. Thirty-two incense burners should be set out, burning various kinds of diverse incense. One hundred and eight...

7. Those fragrant oil lamps should be lit. A garland of lotuses should be painted all around the mandala. The vidyādhara, being pure, should wear clean garments; he should eat only three meals a day and wear three pieces of clothing. He must follow a pure companion. Until the rite of entry is performed, one should be consecrated with the Amoghapāśahṛdaya. As soon as one is consecrated, one is embraced by all the Buddhas and empowered by the Lords of the World, [entering] the great mandala of the Lotus Family, the Holder of the Lotus, through the Amogha-hṛdaya.

1. When accomplishment (*siddhi*) becomes manifest, whatever one contemplates, all tasks are accomplished exactly so. Having entered the unfailing pledge (*samaya*) of all, one attains the *dharmasamayasiddhi*, which is the maṇḍala of liberation through the true nature of all phenomena (*sarvadharmanatā-vimokṣamaṇḍala*). Being completely freed from all karmic obscurations, one experiences divine and human prosperity that accompanies all happiness. One becomes followed by the hosts of gods, asuras, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, who offer garments and enter the sphere of yoga (*yogamaṇḍala*). Furthermore, [the powers of] beating, quarreling, pinning, burning, scorching, casting down, killing, and subjugating have no power over such a person.

2. And those who perform [this rite] against him, upon their very bodies a hundred-thousandfold [blow] falls upon their heads. Neither *pratyaṅgirā* nor any other power can release [the victim], except for that *vidyādhara* to release them. Then, having placed the cloth-painting facing the mandala, one should recite the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* one thousand and eight times; with the *Amoghapāśamudrā*, it should be performed one hundred and eight times. The *Krodharāja* should be performed twenty-one times. Then, the image in the mandala...

3. Rays of light stream forth; that vase blazes with various colors, and that cloth-painting, its colors fully perfected, blazes. A great trembling occurs, and the Vidyādhara is seized. From the cloth-painting, the sound "Well done! Well done! issues forth: "Well done, well done, O Vidyādhara! By you, the Heart-mantra of Noble Avalokiteśvara, Amoghapāśa, has been mastered. This noose of yours is accomplished. This Cintāmaṇi-noose is supremely accomplished by you; perform all rites."

4. O you who have attained supreme accomplishment, having taken that petitioner and a full vase, one should recite [the mantra] over it eight hundred times; he should then be bathed under the Puṣya constellation on an auspicious white lunar day. Merely by being bathed, he obtains the complete purification of all impurities of the body. He obtains the purification of the fivefold self-nature, the purification of the five ears, the purification of the five eyes, the purification of the five noses, the purification of the five tongues, and the purification of the five consciousnesses.

5. Purity: One attains the purification of the five faculties. The noble Avalokiteśvara will constantly grant boons. There will be a constant desire for his vision. One will behold all the Tathāgatas. One will always be attended by Bodhisattvas. All the deities, including Śakra, Brahmā, and the others, as well as the four Great Kings with their retinues, will provide protection, defense, and guardianship for this person. They will approach him.

They shall approach that region of earth and constantly and perpetually provide for its protection, defense, and guardianship. Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, Maṇibhadra, and many hundreds of thousands of secret deities shall provide for its protection, defense, and guardianship. They shall perform rites of peace and well-being. One shall obtain unfailing knowledge, unfailing wisdom, and unfailing success in hearing, morality, and vigor. One shall obtain the status of an unfailing giver of gifts. One shall be endowed with an unfailing mass of merit; that is to say, there shall be the fulfillment of the six perfections.

7. He will be skilled in immeasurable supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*); he will possess the ritual manuals (*kalpa*) of perfected vidyās; his strength, vigor, and prowess will be unfailing; and he will possess the perfect array of qualities of an unfailing Buddha-field. He will bring to completion and gather together roots of merit equal to sixty-four hundred thousand times ten million *niyutas* of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. He will be worthy of worship and honor by all sentient beings; all will come under his influence; and he will be worthy of veneration, like the very heart of a shrine (*caitya*). // //

47b (P86b7, D.89b2) 1. The Ritual for the Mandala. Then, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, and knelt with his right knee upon the ground. Approaching the Blessed One, he circumambulated the Blessed One three times, bowed his head at the Blessed One’s feet, and addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, within this ritual manual for the liberation mandala of my Lotus family, in this ritual manual for the chapter on great vidyās, there is the Amoghapāśahṛdaya."

2. "O Blessed One, I shall now proclaim this Great King of Vidyās here in the midst of this assembly before the Blessed One. Then, the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, with a smiling face, looking up at the Blessed One, spoke this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*: "Homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas established throughout the three times. Homage to the assemblies of all Pratyekabuddhas and Noble Śrāvakas of the past, future, and present."

Homage to those who have correctly gone; homage to those who have correctly entered upon the path. Homage to Śāradvatīputra, the one of great intelligence. Homage to the excellent assembly of noble Bodhisattvas, headed by the noble Maitreya. Homage to the noble Amitābha, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha. Homage to the Three Jewels. Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, Mahāsattva, the Greatly Compassionate One. To them—

Having paid homage to the great ṛṣis and the most excellent assembly of noble ones, I shall now recite this *Amogharāja-hṛdaya*, which was uttered from the mouth of the noble Avalokiteśvara and spoken by the Tathāgata himself in the midst of a great assembly. May it be successful for me! May there be protection for me in the glorious *Tri-bhuvana-devikā* and in all my bodies against all fears! It is as follows: Oṃ cara cara ciri ciri curu curu Mahākāruṇika! Viri...

5. Viri piri piri ciri ciri, O you of supreme great compassion! Siri siri piri piri ciri ciri, O you who hold the great lotus in hand! Kala kala kili kili kulu kulu, O you who are the supremely pure being! Ehy ehi, come, come! Budhya budhya, awaken, awaken! Dhāva dhāva, run, run! Kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu, O you who are the supremely pure being! Kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru, O you who have attained great power! Cala cala sañcala sañcala saṃvicala vicala eṭaṭa!

6. Eṭaṭa bharabharabhiri bhiri bhurubhuru, come, come, O Great Compassionate One! You who wear the guise of Mahāpaśupati! Dhara dhara sarasara caracara harahara! Hāhā hāhā hīhī hīhī hūhū hūhū! You who wear the guise of Brahmā of the syllable Oṃ!

Dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru / tara tara / sara sara / para para / cara cara / vara vara / to him whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of excellent rays; jvala jvala / tapa tapa / O Blessed One, [homage] to Soma, Āditya, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Brahmā, and Indra...

7. O you whose feet are worshipped by the hosts of ṛṣis and the hosts of gods; suṛu suṛu cuṛu cuṛu puṛu puṛu; muṛu muṛu, O Sanatkumāra, Rudra, Vāsava, Viṣṇu, and Dhanada; you who assume many various guises as the leader of divine ṛṣis; dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru; thara thara ghara ghara yara yara lara lara; hara hara; mara mara vara vara, O bestower of boons, Great Lord Maheśvara, whose gaze surveys all worlds, O Blessed Noble Avalokiteśvara—muhu muhu muṛu muṛu muya muya muñca muñca!

O Īśvara, protect, protect me, Śrī Tribhuvanadevī, from all fears, from all calamities, from all misfortunes, from all planetary influences, from all diseases, and as the deliverer from all killing, imprisonment, kings, thieves, robbers, fire, water, poison, and weapons! Kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu! Move, move! O illuminator of the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the four noble truths! Tama tama dama dama! Sama sama! Masa masa! O dispeller of the great darkness of ignorance, fulfiller of the six perfections! Mili...

2. *Mili*! Then: *ṭaṭa ṭhaṭha ṭhaṭha ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭuṭu ṭuṭu ṭhiṭhi ṭhiṭhi ṭhuṭhu ṭhuṭhu*, you who have made a girdle of deer-skin! Come, come! O destroyer of the hosts of spirits belonging to Īśvara and Maheśvara! Act, act! Pass, pass! *kaṭa kaṭa maṭa maṭa*, you who dwell in the pure realm, O Great Compassionate One! You who wear a white sacrificial thread and a garland of jewel-diadems; you upon whose head is placed the crown of the Omniscient One; you who possess the great wonder of the lotus in your palm; you who are unshakable through meditation, concentration, and liberation; you who bring peace to many beings...

3. O you who mature the three [realms], the Great Compassionate One, the purifier of all karmic obscurations, the liberator from all diseases, the fulfiller of all hopes, the consoler of all sentient beings—homage be to you, svāhā! Then, as soon as this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* of the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara was spoken, while it was being recited, this great assembly and the mandala, together with the mountains, forests, and groves, shook in six ways.

The great earth shook, illuminating the world; a great rain of flowers appeared, including divine *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, *puṇḍarīka*, and *māndārava* blossoms, falling as high as the knees. Great musical instruments and cymbals were sounded. From the sky, divine beings adorned with ornaments released a rain [of flowers] upon the Blessed One. And all the gods dwelling within the circle of the assembly—

5. The *gandharvas*, *kinnaras*, *mahoragas*, *guhyakas*, and all those others gave their approval, saying: "Excellent, excellent! O Great Pure Being, this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*—this great wish-fulfilling gem (*mahācintāmaṇi*)—is most difficult to encounter. This rain of great jewels has been poured down by you who have spoken it. This supreme king of rituals (*mahākalparāja*) that you have spoken is the ultimate accomplishment. Now, for one who has accomplished the recitation, all rites are effective. By reciting at the three times of day, wearing clean garments, and bathing three times, [the practitioner attains success].

6. One who eats only three white foods should perform a hundred-eight recitations before the noble Avalokiteśvara, having established an image of the goddess Śrī and performed worship. Having consecrated each individual mustard seed with the mantra, it should be offered to the great goddess Śrī. From the fourteenth day until the fifteenth, one attains divine prosperity. It purifies the five sins of immediate retribution; the noble Avalokiteśvara grants a vision, and all evil is purified. While burning incense of agallochum and sandalwood—sī-

7. For the great [demon] Māhandha, one should perform a rite of pacification using ashes and mustard seeds, and a stake of *khadira* wood should be driven into the ground. In all fevers, a thread spun by a virgin should be recited over twenty-one times and tied on; one is liberated from all fevers. In all diseases, ghee and oil should be consecrated with recitation and placed in a copper vessel. A lotus with its stalk and filaments—these, when empowered, [should be used] for drinking, eating, and anointing; through these very rites, one is liberated from all diseases by means of twenty-one recitations. 48b (P.88b1, D.86b3)

1. For the destruction of *kākhorda* (sorcery), one should recite [the mantra] over ghee and honey twenty-one times and protect the body. One should rub [the body] with *āḍhaka*. Having removed the impurities of the body, one should fashion an image; having recited [the mantra] over a lump of clay twenty-one times, it should be cut with a weapon. All *garaka* and *kākhorda* spells will be severed. One is liberated from all diseases. Great *kākhorda* sorceries are destroyed. Having recited [the mantra] twenty-one times over a protective thread, knots should likewise be tied; this constitutes great protection.

2. For one who is terrified by all fears and trembling, there shall be no further fear. For abdominal pain, salt water that is pleasantly warm should be given after reciting [the mantra] seven times; the abdominal pain will be destroyed. For the destruction of poison: water should be given after reciting it seven times, and all poisons will be destroyed and rendered non-toxic. For eye diseases, a white thread should be tied to the ear, and all eye diseases will be destroyed. For any malignant poison, earth should be consecrated with recitation and applied as an ointment, and one becomes free from poison. For toothache...

3. Having consecrated with mantras a tooth-stick of *karavīra*, a tooth-stick of *sumana*, or a tooth-stick of *gulgulu*, one should chew it; this pacifies toothaches. In all cases of binding a boundary (*sīmābandha*), a five-colored thread should be used. Having consecrated it twenty-one times and tied it to four stakes of *khadira* wood, they should be driven into the ground in the four directions; thus there is a great binding of the boundary. In all planetary afflictions (*graha*), a five-colored thread [is used]; having consecrated it twenty-one times, one is completely liberated from all planetary afflictions. [In cases of] all insects and metals...

4. For those seized by *liṅga* and *galagraha*, an ointment of honey and *pippalī* should be applied to the spiders (*lūtā*). For *galagraha*, one should apply an ointment or [administer] warm water; thus they are liberated from all seizures. For eye diseases, one should bathe [the patient] with scented water (*gandhodaka*). Having recited the mantra seven times over water for the *palāśa* tree, over *palāśa* flowers, and over licorice water (*madhuyaṣṭī*), one should bathe [the patient]; they are liberated from all eye diseases. For earache, one should cook oil in a copper vessel; having added *śatapuṣpā* and filling the ear with it, one is liberated from earache. [It cures] all strife, quarrels, and...

5. Having recited [the mantra] seven times over water used for washing away the afflictions of spirits and disputes, one should wash one’s face; victory will be attained everywhere. In all cases—against all armies, wheel-turning kings, foreign realms, all adversaries, and all enemies—in all battles, one should prepare a circular mandala of cow dung and place four full jars [of water]. Being pure and dressed in clean garments, one should offer incense of *agaru* (aloe wood). Having performed worship to the noble Avalokiteśvara, this—

The *Amoghapāśahṛdayasūtra* should be honored and recited; it brings about great peace (*mahāśānti*). One will possess a mind of universal loving-kindness and a disposition of loving-kindness. It will be victorious everywhere and bring about great tranquility. One should sprinkle that water all around. One should apply a mark of sandalwood (*tilaka*) upon one's own heart after reciting [the mantra] twenty-one times. By remembering it a hundred times, all heinous crimes (*ānantarya*) are destroyed, and there is protection for the entire household. [This is the] *argha*-offering of the *Padmanākulī*.

7. One should offer flowers soaked in ghee as an oblation; thus great protection for the house is established, and protection from all spirits and planetary influences is secured. Alternatively, for one seeking to accomplish the jewel-mantra (*maṇi*), having gathered materials suitable for all rites and made them into equal portions, and having prepared this well-distributed mixture, one who is pure and wears clean garments should perform all activities while reciting the Heart-mantra one hundred and eight times. [The substances are: *jayā*, *vijayā*, *nākulī*, *gandhanākulī*, *cāriṇī*, *abhayapāṇi*, *idrapāṇi*, *gandha*, and *priyaṅgu*.

1. One should have tagara, cakrā, mahācakrā, somarājī, and sunandā made into a fine powder. It should be infused with divine water and sandalwood water mixed with saffron. Having washed [the object], one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times. Placing the jewel before the noble Avalokiteśvara and reciting it twenty-one more times while fumigating it with agalloch incense, one should place it at the feet of that very Blessed One. One should dry it in the shade and cover it with a cloth. Then, it should be taken up again seven times.

2. The *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* should be recited three times; the *Krodharāja* should be set in motion three times. If one holds it upon the head, the king together with his harem and retinue will perform a great worship; all will come under one's control. All the people of the four castes will remain submissive. By means of this alone, one will become weighty [dignified]; all the deities will bestow vital energy (*ojas*) upon him, and the noble Avalokiteśvara will be constantly beheld. And Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara—

They will follow after him; they will be granters of boons at all times; and all adversaries and enemies will constantly pursue him, yet remain under his control. All evil spells, *kākhordas*, poisons, and powders shall have no power over him, and they shall all be destroyed. He will always be endowed with glory, majesty, merit, fortune, and the accumulation of wholesome roots. All the Tathāgatas will look upon him, and they will always desire to see him. He—

4. It shall be a bringer of victory at all times and in every place; his unimpeded good fortune shall increase. His arms shall be invincible, and he shall possess the strength of a great nāga. In all battles and conflicts, he shall achieve great victory; he shall possess great vigor, heroism, and prowess. For the vidyādhara, there shall be the accomplishment of a great kalpa. He shall be unassailable by any yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, grahas, or apasmāras. [He shall be freed from] all evil dreams and ill omens...

And those [afflictions] shall vanish from him; they shall never have power over him. It should be worn around the necks of children; all seizing spirits (*graha*), all fevers, and all diseases shall have no power over them, even those that take away life at birth. Constantly and perpetually, for a long time, Mahākāla, together with his retinue of mothers and his constant followers, will provide protection, defense, and guardianship. One shall live long and possess a full lifespan. For women, one should perform a ritual bath and, having put on clean garments, [wear this].

6. Worship should be performed for the Noble Avalokiteśvara; it brings supreme good fortune, pacifies misfortune, and results in a husband who is favorable for a hundred years. One will have sons and wives, and one's offspring will be excellent. One will be pleasing in appearance to all, and the faults of women will no longer arise for such a person. This shall be expected to be the very last female existence. Upon passing away, one will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī. When bound with this jewel, protection is established everywhere.

7. [Poisons] do not arise; neither poison, nor weapons, nor fire will take effect, and no poisonous action occurs. When this jewel is bound on, one becomes free from poison. [The poison] will be quickly pacified; it does not produce pain, and one recovers with ease. For the suppression of wind-storms, clouds, and lightning, one should cast water over which the mantra has been recited seven times into the sky; all wind-storms, clouds, and lightning will be suppressed. A fence should be constructed using pomegranate vines and oleander vines. [This is for] the increase of mindfulness, [spoken by] the Noble Avalokiteśvara.

1. In front of a Śiva image, without speaking, one should recite the Amoghapāśahṛdaya seven times and drink the jewel [powder] with warm water; one will become a great ocean-like accumulation of learning. One will grasp and recite a thousand verses. For one who desires to bring under control the entire royal court and its retinue within all kingdoms and nations, it should be smeared upon them; wherever one enters, they will remain submissive. If one smears it on both knees, one will cross to the further shore of a great river that is knee-deep. Having fixed it at the top of a banner, in battle or...

2. Whether in battle or in the midst of a caravan; when they have entered mountain caves, ravines, or remote valleys in the middle of a forest, they should be anointed [with this substance]. They will cross over in safety and well-being. All fears of thieves, rogues, robbers, and fierce wild beasts shall have no power over them; they shall become invisible. For those who have fallen into all kinds of bonds, it should be smeared [upon them]; all shackles, fetters, and stocks shall burst asunder. If one anoints oneself, one becomes invisible and the bonds are released. If one applies it to the eyes at the time of sleep, one sees a great dream.

3. It reveals whatever has been thought of or prayed for; it grants a vision of the noble Avalokiteśvara and tells everything. No eye diseases shall prevail against him. If one holds [the mantra] at the mouth and gives it as a gift to someone, that person will become submissive. If one anoints the forehead of one possessed by a spirit, as soon as it is anointed, [the spirit] enters and tells everything. If one anoints the palm of the hand and touches an elephant, it will come under one's control. Wherever you send it...

4. One goes there; having made a mark from the circle of hair (ūrṇākośa), one becomes greatly honored by the whole world. If one anoints the throat, all brahmins become submissive like Śiva (Nīlakaṇṭha); they will become servants and attendants. If one recites the mantra over the eyes with milk at night, one sees as if by divine vision; one sees the dwellings of all yakṣas and rākṣasas opened up; all hidden treasures will be extracted. Having thrown [the substance] into a lake in the abode of the nāgas, the great nāgas...

5. They release a torrent of rain. When there is excessive rain, one should cast [the substance] mixed with water into the sky; they will cause it to subside. One should cast the stream toward the clouds; the thunderbolt (aśani) will not fall. One should bind the hands; wherever one touches, there it becomes inexhaustible. One should bind the feet and shanks; one may enter into the midst of fire, yet the fire does not step upon one—it will become like a slab of sandalwood. One should smear a sword and enter into a battle; the entire body will become a single mass of flame.

6. All enemy armies will flee; victory shall prevail everywhere. For one who is severely afflicted by a great illness, one should administer the powder, and the severely ill person is liberated. For those suffering from dysentery or those with impaired digestion (*grahaṇī*), it should be administered with warm water, and they are immediately liberated. In cases of pain in the sides, it should be administered with buttermilk (*takra*), and it subsides. For all diseases, one should prepare it with ghee and oil. Through massage, food, drink, medical treatment for the nose (*nasta-karman*), and ointment, all diseases are destroyed. Not...

7. They may never prevail. One should smear [the area] all around the entrance of the hole with [the mantra] and rotate the Heart Mantra seven times; the Amoghapāśa mudrā should be assumed, and the Krodha mantra recited once, then one should enter. Just as if it were one’s own home, all magical devices (*yantra*) will shatter, all malevolent beings will be warded off, and all obstacles and impediments (*vighna-vināyaka*) will vanish. Holding [the text] in one’s mouth, the Heart Sūtra should be recited; without speaking, it should be repeated one hundred thousand times.

They will become adorned; they will be endowed with the roots of merit of all the Tathāgatas. One should smear an axle-pin [with this]; it will grant victory in all battles. One should consecrate it in a shop; it will be sold for a great price. One should wash the face of a maiden; she becomes easily wedded. Having made a *tilaka* on the heart [with this], one becomes invisible everywhere. This great jewel (*mahāmaṇi*), which grants all desires and accomplishes all rites, wherever one employs it, there it acts. Through recitation (*jāpa*), there is protection of oneself and protection of others, and one becomes invincible everywhere.

2. By offering water with sesame seeds over which the mantra has been recited seven times for the sake of the *vighnas* and *vināyakas*, all *vighnas* and *vināyakas* are pacified. To destroy misfortune, one should have an image of Noble Avalokiteśvara in the form of a mandala painted on a cloth; then, while remaining silent, one should perform extensive worship before it and recite the mantra eight thousand times. One must be pure and wear clean garments. Incense of *agaru* should be offered, and a lamp of scented oil should be lit. As soon as the recitation is completed, all misfortunes [are destroyed].

They perish. For the purpose of destroying poverty, and because of its lack of success [otherwise], one should fill a water-pot with fragrant water to destroy evil dreams, ill omens, and obscurations; having consecrated it one hundred and eight times with either gold or silver, one should sprinkle [the person], and all those [afflictions] will perish. One experiences great worldly prosperity. The subduing of all planetary influences (*graha*) is accomplished by an oblation (*homa*) of sesame seeds and rice. To destroy all diseases and ailments, one should give water after reciting the mantra over it. Untimely death—

4. By reciting [the mantra] one hundred times three times a day for a full year, one pacifies untimely death. By reciting it eight hundred times every day, there is the breaking of bonds, shackles, and fetters. For the subjugation of a king, by reciting it eight hundred times on the royal road, the king together with his retinue becomes submissive. For the paralyzing of thieves and robbers, by offering a *homa* of seeds of *rājākośātaki*. For the paralyzing of fire, having cast pieces of *khadira* wood into the fire while reciting, the fire becomes paralyzed.

5. For the freezing of water, one should throw the seed of the *salyakī* plant into the water; the water will become frozen. For the destruction of poison, one should recite [the mantra] over a peacock feather and throw it; for the neutralization of weapons, one should recite [the mantra] over the ashes of a tree struck by lightning and throw them. All weapons will be neutralized. For the accomplishment of meditative absorption (*samādhi*), one should bind the *samādhi-mudrā* and recite; one attains a thousandfold meditative absorption. By that Vidyādhara—whether he be a monk (*bhikṣu*) or a nun (*bhikṣuṇī*)—who desires to bring the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*) to fulfillment...

6. Whether they be laymen (*upāsaka*) or laywomen (*upāsikā*), a square *gomayamaṇḍala* should be prepared with well-defined divisions. It should be honored with sandalwood, saffron, musk, and camphor; having thus worshipped it, it should be strewn with various flowers. Having placed the noble Avalokiteśvara facing [the practitioner], four vessels filled with perfumes should be set out, as well as four bowls for the water of offering (*arghapātra*) and four incense burners. A vase of scented water should be placed in the center. Upon that vase, the Blessed Lady Prajñāpāramitā—

7. One should establish [the image]; it should be adorned with all ornaments. Four fragrant lamps should be lit, and a magnificent worship should be performed. A maṇḍalaka should be prepared, beautifully decorated with banners. Sitting cross-legged in front of the maṇḍala, one should perform the recitation. One thousand and ten times the Krodharāja should be recited, or one hundred and eight times; thus the six perfections become fulfilled. One obtains the vision of the Noble Prajñāpāramitā and the accumulation of all roots of merit.

1. He fulfills [the vow]. One who desires to subdue many hundreds of thousands of beings and to crush all wicked ones, such as the Māras, by means of reciting one thousand and eight times on a mountain peak, should recite over a vajra or a trident one thousand and eight times. Having cast it with the Amoghapāśa mudrā and bound it with the Tarjanī mudrā of the Wrathful King, he should recite it twenty-one times while angry and throw it into the sky, whirling it; thus all wicked ones, such as the Māras, will be crushed. This is for the sake of the accomplishment of all rites and the accomplishment of all mantras.

2. One who desires to accomplish and fulfill all wishes should bind the Amogharāja-mudrā and recite it one thousand and twenty times; great accomplishment will arise. One who desires to obtain the consecration of all Tathāgatas should recite it one thousand and thirty-two times; all the Tathāgatas will consecrate him. Likewise, he should be consecrated with a pitcher of scented water. Having gazed upon an image of the Tathāgata containing relics, he should recite it ten thousand times; he attains the state of a Tathāgata. Standing at the feet of the noble Avalokiteśvara—

3. One should recite it ten thousand times, and one becomes equal to Avalokiteśvara. By one who desires to summon Vajrapāṇi, while grasping Vajrapāṇi, it should be recited one thousand times and incense of guggulu should be offered; the Noble Vajrapāṇi will then appear before one in his own form. In all cases, the King of Wrath (Krodharāja) should be remembered. In all cases, the Amoghapāśa mudrā should be employed. Even if not previously accomplished or mastered through recitation, it is accomplished throughout infinite kalpas. [One should cultivate] compassion, sympathetic joy, equanimity, modesty, shame, loving-kindness, and wisdom.

4. And when one is thus endowed, this is declared to be the accomplishment; it is armored against other accomplishments, and one attains success everywhere. Masses of merit blaze forth. First, for those reciting with the King of Wrath, there shall always be the binding of boundaries (*sīmābandha*). There is the binding of the directions (*digbandha*) and the binding of the mandala (*maṇḍalabandha*), which are extremely difficult for *rākṣasas* to overcome. One becomes consecrated by all the Tathāgatas and the sons of the Victors. One is eternally armored and consecrated in all the excellent accomplishments of the ritual manuals (*kalpa*). One becomes a knower of the commitments (*samaya*) everywhere.

5. O Mogharāja, one quickly attains accomplishment and becomes comforted. One should constantly recite this for the sake of obtaining the boon from Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara; if you desire the consecration of the Wrathful King (Krodha), all the Victors (Jinas) shall consecrate you as a Tathāgata who has seen the Truth. I shall proclaim the supreme ritual manual (kalpa) of the Unfailing King (Amogharāja), the Wrathful King. Being pure and wearing clean garments, endowed with wisdom and awakening—one should practice. This accomplishment and its means have been prophesied by all the Tathāgatas. Homage!

To all the Tathāgatas, the Noble Avalokiteśvara, and the Vajradharas: Oṃ cara cara / curu curu / Mahākāruṇika! Ciri ciri biri biri, Mahāpadmahasta! Kala kala kulu kulu, Mahāsthāmaprāpta! Cara cara / cara cara Niśācareśvara! Ehy ehi sidhya sidhya budhya budhya dhāva dhāva kiṇi kiṇi! Paramaśuddhasattva! Kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru, Mahāpaśupativeṣadhara! Hāhā hīhī hūhū! Oṃkārabrahmave-

O bearer of the six [perfections], O you whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of excellent, supreme, and most excellent rays; blaze, blaze! Heat, heat, O Blessed One, whose feet are worshipped by the hosts of lunar and solar deities, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Brahmā, Indra, and the ṛṣis; O you who are well-praised, well-praised, firm, firm; O leader of the gods, ṛṣis, and lords—Sanatkumāra, Kumāra, Rudra, Viṣṇu, Vāsava, Dhanada; O wearer of many various guises; sustain, sustain! You who look upon all things with your gaze; Lord of the World, Great Lord! Release, release! Release, release! 51a (P92b8, D.95b4)

1. You who deliver others from execution, imprisonment, beating, kings, thieves, fire, water, poison, and weapons; you who proclaim the *kaṇa kaṇa* [jewels], the factors of awakening (*bodhyaṅga*), and the four noble truths (*caturāryasatya*); *tama tama*, *sama sama*, you who pacify the darkness of great ignorance; *mili mili*, you whose girdle is made of *eṇeya* deer-skin; come, come! *maṭa maṭa*! You who dwell in the pure realm; you who possess great compassion (*mahākāruṇika*), wear a white sacrificial thread (*yajñopavīta*), and bear a jewel-crested crown; you who place your joined palms upon the head of the Omniscient One (*sarvajña*), and are unshakable through meditation, concentration, and liberation; you who [practice] the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*)...

2. Ripūraka! O ripener of the continuums of many sentient beings! O crusher of all Māras and all malevolent ones! O fulfiller of the attainment of all siddhis! Having been consecrated by the consecrations of all the Tathāgatas, O Blessed One Amogharāja! HŪṂ PHAṬ! Homage be to you, SVĀHĀ! This very one, through the preliminary ritual application of the mantra, is the supreme, perfected, and all-purposeful wrathful deity named Amoghapāśa, effective for all rites. [169] Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Amitābha, the Tathāgata! Homage to the noble—

To Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One; to the one who grants unfailing boons, who holds a noose in his hand, the Great Pure Being: Come, O Blessed One, lotus-handed! O you whose granting-finger is the bestower of boons, lotus-armed one, wearer of the guise of Maheśvara! Be gracious! Come quickly, O you of great speed, adorned with rays of light! Ha ha! Amoghaśuddha! Sara sara! Cala cala! Come, come, O Blessed One Avalokiteśvara, for my sake!

4. Accept this offering of perfumes, flowers, and brooms by the truth of the Three Jewels: *Amoghasiddhe svāhā*. With incense of *agaru* recited twenty-one times, perform the invocation for the noble Avalokiteśvara and all those who dwell within the maṇḍala. Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One, whose supreme arm is unfailing and perfumed with all fragrances.

5. O you who are beloved by all perfumes, garlands, and ornaments; O you whose head is adorned with the crescent moon; O you who delight in perfumes, flowers, and ointments—accept this from me, O Excellent One, O Bestower of Boons! Svāhā! [The incense should be offered after reciting this seven times. Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One! It is as follows: *Hili hili mili mili mahāprabhāsvaravimale brahmaveṣadhare suma...*

6. *Tivara-de*, *turu turu* O you adorned with variegated garlands! *Hara hara*, *mara mara*, *turu turu*! Grant joy to my unfailing heart! Accept this excellent flower of mine, *svāhā*! Seven sets of seven flowers should be offered. Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One, the Bestower of Boons to the Great Bodhisattvas! Remember, remember, Blessed One, the pledge of all the Tathāgatas!

7. *Śvāsite* / O Blessed One, who beholds all sentient beings, you whose hand holds the unfailing noose! Accomplished one, accomplished one, you whose vows are accomplished! By the power of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha: *bhuru bhuru*, O true commitment, *svāhā*! This is the vidyā-mantra for the recollection of the noble Avalokiteśvara. Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! It is as follows: *dhure dhure*, O Vajradhara! (51b) (P93.b4, D.96b1)

1. Padmajaye! O you who have departed from obstacles! Vēga vega! Dhuta dhuta! O you who are dear to all seeds! By the truth of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṃgha: mili mili svāhā! This *balividya* should be given after being recited seven times. [174] Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One! O Blessed One, whose body is the unimpeded gnosis of the Tathāgata! Bring forth, bring forth! O you with the lotus-throne and lotus-arms! O white-bodied one with white arms!

2. O you adorned with white garlands! *Dhuma dhuma*, blaze forth! By the truth of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, *svāhā*! [175] This lamp-mantra is empowered by reciting it seven times. Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! It is as follows: *Oṃ vīra vīra padmapāṇi! Āgama āgama amoghatatvasiddhe! Sarvatathāgatagaganaraśmisamcodita sarvavidyādharaviśodhane amoghajvalasiddhe svāhā!* *Sugandha-*...

3. One should bathe [the image] with a jar of scented water over which the *snāna-vidyā* has been recited seven times. *Namo ratnatrayāya*. Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One! It is as follows: *dhume dhume dhudhume / padme padmanirbhāsa śuddha śuddha kāñcanaprabhāsavimale / śuddhasārāgryo śuci śuci gocaraśuddhe / padmāṅgavati / prāvaraṇi svāhā*. This is the *vastra-vidyā*; it should be recited seven times.

4. By means of this recitation: Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! It is thus: *śāme śāmaya śānti me śrītribhuvanadevyārakṣasvastyayanaṃ kuru śāntośi me sarvapāpāṃ śāntaśuddhakalyāṇaviraje jayasiddhe bhagavann āryāvalokiteśvara sara sara svāhā*. [This is for] sleeping and sitting.

5. Having consecrated it with this mantra, one should go to sleep; one will not see any bad dreams or evil omens. Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One. It is as follows: *nāgaprakarṣaṇe*, *divyajale*, *jalavāhe*, *jalasaṃkhyābhayaḥ*, *yan nāgajalasaṃśodhani*, *padmasare padmaviśuddhe*, *pāṇijale saṃśodhaya*, *ātman vara vara sa-* [178] One should sleep after having recited this over [the water]; one will not see any bad dreams or evil portents. Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage! To the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One. It is thus: *nāgaprakarṣaṇe*, *divyajale*, *jalavāhe*, *jalasaṃkhyābhayaḥ*, *yan nāgajalasaṃśodhani*, *padmasare padmaviśuddhe*, *pāṇijale saṃśodhaya*, *ātman vara vara sa-*

6. *Lile svāhā* // Regarding the science of water: bathing, seizing, and sprinkling—these should be performed everywhere with [the mantra] recited seven times. Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One, the benefactor of all beings, the one who grants unfailing boons, the giver of food and drink to all beings, the provider of various delicious flavors as sustenance for gods, nāgas, and others. O Purifier of the entire world, O Excellent One, satisfy [all beings]!

7. *Śuddhe svāhā*! This is the *vidyā* for the offering. Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One, who is worshipped by all gods and asuras; to him who completely fulfills all things; to him who is unsullied by any fragrance; to him who is pure as the sky; to him whose radiance is liberation; to the Victorious One, the Conqueror, who accepts the removal of faded flower offerings; to the Purifier of flowers, garlands, and fragrances; O Purifier of all Tathāgatas, purify! O Purifier of the lotus! (52a)

1. Svāhā! The Vidyā for the Removal of Withered Offerings. Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! It is as follows: *Dharaṇindhare dharaṇibandhe / bandha bandha śukraviśodhani / śuklamāliliṅgini / śukraviśodhani / śukravimale svāhā!* Having recited this twenty-one times over either *kuśa* grass, cotton threads, or youth-cord (*kumārasūtra*), twenty-one knots should be tied; this effects the binding of semen (*śukra*).

2. [182] Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One. It is as follows: *Jvala jvale vimalo jvale prabhāvaviraje sūryavati | jaya padmamālādhare svāhā*. If one recites this seven times over ashes during the fire sacrifice (*agnihotra*) and scatters them all around, no obstacles or obstructing spirits (*vināyaka*) shall ever have power [to cause harm]. [183] Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One...

3. *Kāya*: Tadyathā: *jale jale jalavati jalaprabhāvani nāgaśraviṇi divyavāriṇi mili mili svāhā*. This is the *upaspṛśana-vidyā* (the mantra for ritual ablution). Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! Tadyathā: *hāriṇi hāriṇi piṅgala piṅgali hiri hiri bhagavan niścala pracala pratiṣṭha rakṣa rakṣa śrītribhuvanadevyāḥ*.

4. By the truth of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, svāhā! Having consecrated the bundle of kuśa-grass seats with this, it is the *āśana-vidyā* (seat-mantra) recited seven times. [185] Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the deities who dwell in all maṇḍalas! Homage to the knowledge-deities (*vidyā-devī*) who have attained perfection in all ritual manuals (*kalpa*)! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! Come, O Blessed One, Padmasundarī, Great Knowledge-Deity! Move! Move!

5. *Padmasundari*, *Vegavati*, *huru huru svāhā*. Every day, having worshipped the Rākṣasī Ekajaṭā—the Kṛtyā—of Padmasundarī with flowers, incense, offerings, perfumes, and so forth, the recitation of the Kṛtyā-mantra should be performed seven times; by this, all obstacles shall never prevail. [186] Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the King of Wrath! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One!

6. Of the one who possesses the attire of all families of vidyās: Tadyathā: Oṃ, O you whose power is the unerring heart! O pacifier of all obstacles! Bring forth! Gather together! O you seated upon a lotus throne! O you adorned with jewels and gold! O you whose arms are like lotuses! Cross over, cross over! Remove the evil! O Unerring Heart! O Victorious One, O Three-eyed One! O you whose arms grant boons! Remember, remember the commitment (*samaya*) of the Blessed One and of all the Tathāgatas! Bear, bear! Bhuru, bhuru! O wearer of the Brahma-attire! O you whose body is adorned! O remover of great fear! Behold!

7. *Lokayasarvvasatvāvalokani vara vara varade svāhā*. This is the vidyā for all rites; it should be practiced especially at the time of accomplishment (*sādhana*). Protection must be performed by many vidyās and by all the attendants residing within the maṇḍala. [187] Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! It is as follows: *para para mara mara bandha bandha samantena amoghapāśah*.

1. *Tiṣṭha tiṣṭha*! By the truth of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, *svāhā*! With ashes, having recited [the mantra] twenty-one times, one performs the binding of the maṇḍala with the Amoghapāśa mudrā. Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! It is as follows: O Binder of the Directions, O Unfailing One, O Unobstructed One! *Muru muru suru suru turu turu*, destroyer of all obstacles! O You adorned by the lotus lake! By the truth of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha! Bind, O supreme deer-skin one! *Bandha ajinavarade*.

2. Svāhā! After those who have been invoked, the binding of the directions (diśābandha) should be performed. Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! It is as follows: *hili hili mili mili / siri siri piri piri / cara cara pracara vimānadhara / dara dara / gaccha gaccha / O Blessed Noble Avalokiteśvara, go to your own abode! *turu turu amoghapadme svāhā!* With a handful of whatever flowers are available—

3. Having recited it twenty-one times, it should be given; thus the rite of dismissal is accomplished. This concludes the ritual procedure for the chapter on the *vidyā*-kalpa. Now, therefore, I shall proclaim the procedure for the cloth-painting (*paṭaka*), which is the means for easy accomplishment—the supreme practice of the Great Wrathful One, the King of Unfailing Power (*Amogharāja*). This is the king of wrathful ones who accomplishes the ritual manual; it is the highest attainment. I shall proclaim this *vidyā*, the supreme and unfailing accomplishment, by the mere activation of which there is unsurpassed success in all ritual manuals. [It is the power of] hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas...

4. They shall behold the Buddhas; they shall behold the Perfectly Awakened Ones. Like the sands of hundreds of thousands of Ganges rivers, they plant roots of merit before millions of Buddhas, the Tathāgatas—an unsurpassed mass of merit that pacifies all evils and increases strength and vigor. It is effective for the accomplishment of the reality of all mantras throughout every eon without fail. By the mere act of recollection, the surface of the earth trembles; the thirty-three gods, together with the *asuras*, the oceans, and Mount Meru, tremble; and the *nāgas* quiver and flee.

5. In the battle between the gods and the asuras, the supreme Vidyārājas, along with Vajrapāṇi and the yakṣas, together with their armies and mounts—all whose bodies were wreathed in flames—trembled violently. Yet the four Great Kings did not shake the supreme world. They all gathered together and went for refuge to Lokeśvara, saying: "Save us, O Blessed One, our Protector! Save us, O Compassionate One! Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, toward the Blessed One...

Having approached the Blessed One, he said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, I possess the Amoghasiddhi-hṛdaya, a king of vidyās, by the mere recitation of which the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya is more swiftly accomplished. By its mere recollection, the Noble Avalokiteśvara grants a vision of himself in his divine form and bestows all the supreme siddhis. Therefore, Blessed One, I shall proclaim it here before the Blessed One in this circle of the assembly."

7. [190] Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage! To the noble Amitābha, the Tathāgata; homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One. It is thus: Oṃ, lotus, lotus, you whose arms are adorned with the lotus-holder! Move, move, you who wear the garb of Brahmā! Carry, carry, you who wear a variegated crown! Your body is adorned with jewels, gold, vajras, and lapis lazuli! Cross, cross, ferry across, O Blessed One, O Blessed Lady, to the further shore! Support, support, you who hold the unfailing noose in your hand! Grant, grant, O bestower of boons, in every way—

1. O Avalokita, Great Bodhisattva, Giver of Boons, pale as a lotus, seated upon a lotus throne! Blaze, blaze! You who are consecrated by the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas; O Great Compassionate One! Strength, strength! Possessor of great strength and speed! You whose face is deformed and formidable with fangs! Possessor of great majesty! Giver of boons through vast wisdom! Great Compassionate One! Wearer of the guise of the Great Lord of Beasts (Paśupati)! Move, move! Accumulation of the most excellent merit! You who possess the meditative concentrations and absorptions of the Sugatas! Sovereign of Universal Observation! Great Lord! Tamer of the wicked, fierce tamer of the dissolution! King of Wrath!

2. Wearing a great garb, O you who are equal, equal, and have attained great power! O you whose radiance surpasses the moon and sun! O impurity-cleanser, purifier of all impurities! You who possess a lineage of sages among all hosts, wearing the form of Mahāmaheśvara! Adorned with matted locks graced by the Victorious One Amitābha, your head adorned on the right by the moon! Crush, crush! Destroyer of all hosts of yakṣas, rākṣasas, and bhūtas! Cross over, cross over! Adorned like the host of stars, wearing a garland of constellations, the one who brings about the destruction of all obstacles! O you of supreme loving mind, Great Compassionate One! Pass beyond, pass beyond, completely fulfilled—

3. O you who possess the bliss of the maṇḍala of jewels! You who fulfill the six perfections! *Mili mili*! You who wear a garment of eneya deer-skin and bear an upper robe of tiger-skin! You who are beheld by all the Tathāgatas! Three-eyed one! Wielder of the trident! Wielder of the blazing vajra! You who hold the unfailing noose (*amoghapāśa*) in hand and assume the forms of Yama, Varuṇa, and Kuvera! You who assume the form of the Lord of Nāgas! You whose body is stainless and pure! You who pacify all sins, purify all obscurations, and destroy all defilements! [O Lord of] the three worlds...

4. O you who bring all beings under your power, the purifier of all sentient beings, the bestower of the boon of awakening and of bodhisattvas, empowered by all the Tathāgatas: Oṃ, O pure one adorned with the lotus! Dhiri dhiri! Look upon me! Sama sama! Accomplish all my actions! O you who have attained the accomplishment of the heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa! O dweller in the secret place, bestower of boons, hūṃ phaṭ! Homage be to you, svāhā! As soon as this was spoken, all those hosts of spirits and yakṣa-kings—this King of Vidyās, Amoghasiddhi—[became manifest].

5. All obstacles and impediments were cast headlong down; all the palaces became ablaze, becoming a single mass of flame. Then Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, his hair standing on end with thrill, was filled with terror. All the hosts of gods—Śakra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, and the four Great Kings—were terrified, as were the gods and dānavas. All the ṛṣis were cowed, as were the nāga kings dwelling in the great ocean. They produced a torrent of water—

6. And those gods and nāgas dwelling in the water, the deities of the agitated great ocean, and those who dwell in the city of Laṅkā; all the vidyādharas from the universal monarchs down to the deities of the Śuddhāvāsa realm and the deities of the sky—all these ascended into the air. With divine flowers of various kinds—lotuses, kumudas, utpalas, puṇḍarikas, māndārava, and mahāmāndārava—they began to rain down upon Mount Potalaka, showering it with divine ornaments and decorations.

On Mount Talaka, [the earth] had subsided to the depth of a knee for the purpose of worshipping the Blessed One. And for the sake of worshipping that Bodhisattva Āryāvalokiteśvara, they played celestial musical instruments and songs. They raised a great tumultuous roar and a great shout of joy, proclaiming this great gift. "O Blessed One, this is a Great Vidyā spoken by Āryāvalokiteśvara for the benefit of all sentient beings. Then Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, [approached] where Āryāvalokiteśvara was...
