The Being, the Great Being, having approached him and circumambulated him three times to the right, covered him for the sake of worship with a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand. "O Blessed One, this supreme ritual manual (*kalpa*) has been spoken, the unsurpassed Great Knowledge (*mahāvidyā*), the Amogharāja, the Heart of Great Knowledge, O Great Sage, Lord of the World! Speak, O Blessed One, the entire ritual manual of the unsurpassed accomplishment of Amogharāja; may you teach the perfect accomplishment of all rites. Then, from that point, the Blessed One [spoke] the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya of the Noble Avalokiteśvara.

2. We shall explain the ritual procedure for the King of Vidyās, Amoghasiddhi, and the unsurpassed method for the cloth-painting (*paṭavidhāna*). One should have a square cloth made, well-proportioned on all sides, with its fringes uncut and free of hair. A painter who is pure, has bathed well, wears clean garments, observes the *poṣadha* vows, and uses non-sticky pigments kept in nine vessels, should paint [it]. In the center is the Blessed One, the Noble Avalokiteśvara, adorned with a crown of matted locks and decorated by the Victor Amitābha, [holding] a fresh moon in his right—

3. He wears a crown that is not fixed [to his head], is clothed in a garment of deerskin, and bears the attire of the Lord of Creatures (Paśupati). Adorned with all ornaments, he has three heads, three eyes, and four arms. Seated upon a lotus, he is mounted on a mountain; in the center, his face is gentle, with a smiling countenance; on the right side, his face is fierce with a frowning brow; and on the left side, at the peak of the new moon, his face is fierce, terrifying with protruding fangs, and distorted. His crown is adorned with Amitābha. With one arm he holds a lotus, and with the second [he holds] a trident.

4. *Laṃ*. Third, [one should visualize] Amoghapāśadhara, whose body emerges from half [the lotus], with a frowning face, his hand bearing the Amoghapāśa mudrā, gazing at the Blessed One, and fourth, Āśvāsabhuj, who has a mass of flames all around him, endowed with a fathom-wide halo. On the right side, the goddess Tārā should be depicted modestly with her body slightly bent, gazing at the hand that displays the boon-granting gesture (*varada-mudrā*); on the left, Padmasundarī should be made likewise modest, according to the appropriate proportions, gazing at the hand of Tārā which holds the Amoghapāśa.

5. Ekajaṭā and Padmasundarī are to be depicted as rākṣasīs; between them, Vimalagati is to be depicted above the goddess Tārā. Bhṛkuṭī is to be depicted on the second side, and Śvetā is to be depicted [there]. Below Padmasundarī, Kṛtyā is to be depicted according to the mantra. Below Ekajaṭā, the great goddess Bhīmā is to be depicted. Above, the sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm are to be depicted, and Śakra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are to be depicted. [They are adorned with] various flowers—

6. [The Blessed One] should be depicted being honored. Beneath him, the Four Great Kings should be made. Beneath Noble Avalokiteśvara, Noble Vajrapāṇi should be made in the form of a fierce, loud laughter; the wrathful Amogharāja should be made in a state of combat. By the mere sight of this painting, one should know that Noble Avalokiteśvara, his excellent celestial palace, and Mount Potalaka are being manifested before one's eyes. By the mere sight of it, one is liberated from the eight great hells; one is liberated from the eight great fears. Pa-

7. Even one who has committed the five deeds of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*) is completely liberated; one who rejects the True Dharma (*saddharma*), having been rejected by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, is purified merely by seeing [the deity]. Although destined for the Avīci hell and without end, such a person is completely liberated. They will plant roots of merit (*kuśalamūla*) equal to a hundred thousand great Brahma-merits. They will obtain all worldly and divine happiness. Furthermore, at the time of death, Noble Avalokiteśvara will appear before them face-to-face and provide consolation. Having passed away, they will go to Sukhāvatī...

He will be reborn in the world-system of Vaidūryanirbhāsā. Free from all obscurations, he will remember five hundred thousand births. This shall be his final birth until the culmination of enlightenment; by the mere sight of this [teaching], he will be endowed with a mass of merit. How much more so if he performs further service? He should be known as irreversible from the realization of unsurpassed enlightenment. This applies whether it be a son of good family or a daughter of good family, or a monk, a nun, a layman, or a laywoman.

2. Whether it be a king, a royal minister, a woman of the inner court, or the chief queen, if they should recollect this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* in the presence of this painted cloth ritual (*paṭavidhāna*) and worship that Blessed One Avalokiteśvara, you should know that for them it is multiplied a hundred thousandfold. Furthermore, if one should recollect the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* while performing the great recitation ritual, and if one should recollect the Blessed One’s *Amoghapāśakrodha* three times without speaking, and sprinkle water [upon oneself], you should know that for them all the Tathāgatas are likewise [present].

3. All those bodhisattvas will be consecrated until the end of enlightenment by means of this Amoghasiddhi-mahākalpa-dhāraṇī. Before the image of the noble Avalokiteśvara, standing face-to-face with palms joined, having recited it seven times, having performed seven circumambulations, and having offered water for the feet and guest-water along with flowers and incense, they pay homage. By that, they should know that each of the hundreds of thousands of various dhāraṇīs will have been recited seven times. A-

4. And when this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, the *Vimokṣamaṇḍala*, the great Dharma-discourse, has been recited one hundred thousand times, the *Amoghapāśa-mudrā* should be performed. Gazing upon the face of the noble Avalokiteśvara, touching him with both right and left arms, and placing them at the location of the heart, by means of this yoga, they become as if performed with a single mudrā for each of those one hundred thousand recitations. O Blessed One, whichever son of good family or daughter of good family, or monk or nun—

Whether it be a gambler or a female gambler, a king or a queen, the chief consort, or the attendants of the inner harem and the great royal ministers—should one desire to perform one hundred thousand times ten million recitations (*jāpa*) of this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* of Noble Avalokiteśvara; or desire to consecrate (*abhiṣeka*) hundreds of thousands of millions of Tathāgatas; or desire to set in motion this *Vimokṣamaṇḍala* until the completion of the entire ritual manual for hundreds of thousands of millions of times; or desire to [perform] this *Amoghapāśamudrā* for hundreds of thousands of millions of times—

6. One who desires to cause the stream [of the teaching] to flow must consecrate this cloth-painting (duṣyapaṭa) in each respective place. Having placed it facing oneself in a pure place, in an uncluttered dwelling, on a walking-path (caṅkrama), or in a forest retreat; in a cave, on a mountain peak, in a monastery (vihāra), or even in a house; having made a clean and pure room smeared with well-prepared yellow cow-dung and sprinkled with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), one should prepare a circular mandala made of white sandalwood, two cubits in measure, in front of the painting, anointed with various fragrant ointments.

7. It should be adorned with saffron; it should be worshipped with musk and camphor. Having filled a water-pot with scented water and various diverse perfumes, it should be placed in the center of the central maṇḍala and covered with a cloth. One should place fragrant flowers, incense, offerings, and twenty-one garlands. Eight vessels filled with perfume should be placed in the four directions. Eight bowls filled with milk should be placed. On the pedestal below the eight bowls, there should be milk-rice, rice-gruel, sugar-candies, various sweets, and boiled rice.

1. Bowls filled with honey, sugar, and clarified butter should be set out. Incense burners containing black aloe-wood incense, white sandalwood, camphor, kunduruka, and śrīvāsaka should be placed there. An oblation of aloe-wood fuel should be performed. It should be performed on an altar adorned with various flowers; thirty butter lamps should be lit. Then the Vidyādhara must wear clean garments and be well-bathed. This should be performed from the fourteenth day until the full moon of the fifteenth day. The image of Noble Avalokiteśvara should be worshipped. Then the Vidyā—

2. He should be sprinkled seven times with scented water by Dhareṇa Krodharāja. The Amoghapāśa mudrā should be performed twenty-one times. Then, while seated cross-legged and remaining silent, one should form the *jāpa* mudrā and perform the recitation (*jāpa*) of the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya one hundred and eight times. Thereafter, the Amoghasiddhi-vidyārāja should be recited eight thousand times. Then, seventy rays of light will issue forth from the cloth painting, illuminating everywhere and circumambulating it three times to the right.

3. <ḥ> / They enter through the eye on the forehead of the noble Avalokiteśvara. As soon as they have entered, a great *dhāraṇī* will arise; the *vidyādhara* will rejoice and horripilation will occur. His complexion and skin color will become perfectly pure. From the fingers of the noble Avalokiteśvara’s boon-granting arm, divine water flows; from his two feet, milk flows. The *Amoghapāśa* in his hand blazes; the lotus leaf in his lotus-hand trembles; the trident blazes. She—

The sound "Dhu" issues forth: "Excellent, excellent, noble son! You have accomplished the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*; perform all rites. By you, the supreme accomplishment of the *Mahākalparāja* has been achieved through Amoghasiddhi. Then, he reveals his form as the noble Avalokiteśvara and grants the most excellent fulfillment of all desires. This is the supreme, unsurpassed accomplishment; even without being personally mastered, it performs those rites. Therefore, one who wishes to perform the rite of subjugation [should recite] the lotus [mantra] one hundred and eight times.

5. Having recited [the mantra], it should be placed into the hand of Noble Avalokiteśvara. Whomever one gives it for by name, that person will become submissive. One should recite over a *sumanā* flower one hundred and eight times and offer it to Noble Avalokiteśvara. Furthermore, having consecrated it seven times, one should present it as an offering. Whomever one gives it to, that person will become submissive. If one gives it to someone seized by a planetary spirit (*graha*), they will be liberated from all planetary spirits. If one gives it to one who is ill, they will be liberated from all diseases. At the royal gate—

6. One should scatter [the powder] over a king together with his harem and retinue; he will become submissive. One should throw it upon a funeral pyre, and that being is liberated from hell. If one throws it at a moment for a being situated in the Avīci hell, they are liberated in an instant. Having placed it at the head of one who has gone to bed, one sees a great dream; it grants a vision of the noble Avalokiteśvara and speaks all one’s heart’s desires. Whether a woman or a man, whoever one scatters it upon will become submissive and thereafter follow after one. [One should scatter it] over a king...

7. If one should cast [the powder] into water, she will become a slave. By establishing an image of a deity and invoking it, one will be summoned; [the practitioner] becomes a performer of all rites. For one desiring to accomplish the eye-salve (*añjana*): having recited the mantra one thousand and eight times over realgar (*manaḥśilā*) eye-salve before the cloth painting (*paṭa*), three signs appear: it blazes, froths, and emits smoke. When one has applied that salve to the eyes, one becomes invisible. One sees all treasures; one sees all the abodes of the *yakṣas*. [One should apply it] on the forehead... (55a) (P.100a1, D.102b4)

Having made a tilaka on the forehead, one enters all that is stainless; all doors and all mechanical devices shall burst open. By touching limb to limb, one flies up into the sky. Having made a tilaka on the head, the Noble Avalokiteśvara becomes eternally granting boons. By applying [the ointment] to the neck, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, and other gods become eternally bound to one's service; they grant the accomplishment of all undertakings. If one applies it at night, one sees as if by day. All treasures shall spring forth; having placed [the vessel] face down, one causes it to vomit [its contents].

2. By anointing one’s own body with this, for as long as one lives, the body becomes armored; all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and others will become invisible to one; one becomes a performer of all rites; and one’s lifespan will be a thousand kalpas. Alternatively, having extracted the heart [of the substance], it should not be consumed; one will become possessed of a form according to one’s great desire (*mahākāmala-rūpin*). One displays the forms of all deities; indeed, one displays the forms of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, and the Great Universal Form (*mahāviśvarūpa*); one displays the moon and the sun. [The substances are: *manacchilā*, *gorocana*, *sauvīra*, *kuṅkuma*, and *kuṃkubha*.

3. Likewise, one should recite the *Amoghasiddhi* mantra ten thousand times; the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* one thousand and eight times; and the *Krodharāja* one hundred and eight times—all these without speaking to anyone. It should be ground in front of the noble Avalokiteśvara. Facing the cloth painting (*paṭa*), being pure and wearing clean garments, having fasted for a day and night on the full moon of the fifteenth day, one should grind it into a fine powder again. Then, with the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* and the *Krodharāja*, [one should recite] one hundred and eight times—*a-* [the text here is incomplete].

The Vidyārāja Amoghasiddhi should recite [the mantra]. Then, he should remain in the hand of Noble Avalokiteśvara; a great worship should be performed, and the cloth painting (paṭa) should be worshipped. Having fasted for a day and night, one should sit cross-legged before the cloth painting. One should rotate the Amoghapāśa mudrā twenty-one times. The Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya should be recited twenty-one times; it should be performed by means of the recitation-mudrā (jāpamudrā). The Krodha-mantra should be recited seven times.

Then one should mutter the *Akṣīṇya* mantra. The *Amoghasiddhi-dhāraṇī* should be set in motion; then, immediately upon having applied the ointment, one beholds the Noble Avalokiteśvara on Mount Potalaka, together with his celestial palace (*vimāna*), his assembly of bodhisattvas and their palaces, and the inhabitants of Potalaka. One beholds the world-system Sukhāvatī and sees the Tathāgata Amitābha teaching the Dharma. One hears that teaching of the Dharma and [beholds] all the Tathāgatas in the ten directions.

6. He purifies all the assemblies of bodhisattvas and the community of śrāvakas, and he sees them together with their buddha-fields and celestial palaces. He hears the speech of those proclaiming the teaching of the Dharma. Even for one born in a family of outcasts, or even for one who has committed the five acts of immediate retribution destined for the Avīci hell, if the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One, through the empowerment of the Tathāgata, directs his attention toward him, he grants a vision in a dream. He purifies all sinful obscurations and all veils. Da-

7. It bestows the accomplishment of the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*. One lives for a full thousand divine years and experiences divine bliss. One should apply [the ointment] against all diseases; it pacifies all diseases and removes all fevers. By the mere act of applying it, one becomes free from all poisons. One should apply it against all fears, and one will become invisible. One will become invisible among all adversaries, enemies, rogues, thieves, and bandits. Among those who are exalted... [55b] (P101a6, D.103b3)

There will be no fear in battles. One should apply it in all quarrels, strife, conflicts, and disputes; everywhere there will be victory. One will be the superior debater. One should apply it in all wars; in military engagements, victory will be achieved. One will cross over the vanguard of the enemy forces. If one enters the royal court and applies it to the eyes, the king together with his harem and retinue will become submissive; all will come under one's control even without speaking. If one enters a city, all the inhabitants of that city—men, women, boys, and girls—will [be subdued].

2. They will become submissive. If one anoints the right eye, all those whom one sees with the eye of the fourfold world (*cātuvarṇṇa-loka*) will become submissive. If one anoints the left eye, all harlots (*raṇḍā*) become submissive. Taking hold of the right arm of the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the King of Vidyādharas Amoghasiddhi should be recited one thousand and eight times, and worship of the Noble Avalokiteśvara should be performed. For him, [the rites] of that Amoghapāśahṛdaya, of the Wrathful King, and of all the Kings and all the Dhāraṇīs [should be performed] separately.

There will be hundreds of thousands [of beings] who have turned [toward enlightenment] individually. Twelve thousand koṭis will have planted roots of merit in the presence of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One. And all of them, having taken up his name, will have propitiated thousands of Tathāgatas; they will obtain a face-to-face vision of sixty-eight thousand Tathāgatas. All worldly activities will be accomplished for them.

4. Those situated in the Avīci hell of the eastern enclosure are purified. Furthermore, there shall never again be a going to the states of woe; in birth after birth, he will be one who remembers his former lives. All the gods will grant him boons, and they will constantly provide for his protection, defense, and guardianship. While supporting the left arm and reciting [the mantra] one thousand and eight times, by the mere act of reciting, all the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and so forth, are summoned.

5. They will be released; they all remain under one's control. When a task arises, the Vidyārāja Amoghasiddhi should be recited seven times. Then all the gods, nāgas, and others will become performers of every action. They will not merely follow one constantly and uninterruptedly, but by taking hold at the navel, one shall conquer all the nāgas and others. They will release showers of rain and satisfy the entire Jambūdvīpa. One should perform the whispered recitation (*karṇajāpa*) one hundred and eight times. Wherever the mind is directed—

6. Having gone to that very place, whether it be a woman or a man, a king or a queen, a śramaṇa or a brāhmaṇa, or a lay follower (upāsaka)—whatever you intend, whatever you seek to attain, all that activity shall be accomplished. If one holds the head [of the person] and recites [the mantra], they will come under control as far as the Brahmā world; all shall become obedient and subject to one's will. One should recite eight thousand times, beginning from the outset. When one recites while pressing [the person down], ten thousand recitations should be performed, until those who have gone to the underworld (pātāla) come under one’s control.

7. ... [all] will become laborers; all will become servants. Having recited the mantra eight thousand times over a lotus, one should cast it into a lotus pond; an inexhaustible lotus will appear. It will be a lotus that blooms at all times. Having recited the mantra seven thousand times over a blue lotus (*utpala*), it should be thrown into a pond of blue lotuses; inexhaustible blue lotuses will appear. They will bloom at all times and never perish. In the same way, [one may treat] *sumana*, *gandhavārṣika*, *yūthikā*, *navamālikā*, and other flowers...

They shall produce flowers at all times and they shall become inexhaustible. Having recited [the mantra] one hundred and eight times over fruits and flowers, and having cast them into a garden or within a forest, the flowers and fruits shall become inexhaustible and shall bloom at all times. One who desires to attract great prosperity (*mahāśrī*) should fashion an image of the Great Goddess Śrī out of beeswax. She should be depicted sitting in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*), adorned with all ornaments, with graceful limbs, holding a lotus in her hand, with a full chest, and fashioned as if composed of fruits and flowers. She should be made—

2. One should worship with *rūpaka* musk and white sandalwood. It should be placed before the cloth painting (*duṣyapaṭa*). The previously described mandala ritual should be performed, and it should be made of white sandalwood. Incense of *agaru* should be offered to Noble Avalokiteśvara on the cloth painting; incense of white sandalwood should be offered to the Great Goddess Śrī. Worship and honor should be performed for both. An offering of white food and scented water should be presented. Eight vessels for the guest-water (*argha*) should be offered. The Vidyādhara, being pure and having bathed well—

One must be pure, wearing clean garments, and seated facing forward in the paryaṅka posture. One should recite [the mantra] seven times with the Amoghapāśa mudrā. Having consecrated whatever garlands and flowers are available one hundred and eight times with the Amoghapāśahṛdaya, they should be tied upon the head of the Great Goddess Śrī. An offering of water (argha) and flowers should be performed. Having recited over incense one hundred and eight times, white sandalwood incense should be offered. Then, by the vidyādhara, one hundred and eight—

4. The *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* should be recited one thousand times. Reciting it over each individual mustard seed, they should be offered to the Great Goddess Śrī. When the one thousand and eight have been completed, the Great Goddess Śrī blazes forth. Rays of light issue from the forehead of the Noble Avalokiteśvara. All the requisites and the mandala will become golden in color. Divine and great prosperity (*divyamahāśrī*) is summoned; it does not depart for as long as one lives. Divine prosperity—

5. Whatever you shall enjoy, day by day, you must perform the great three-times-daily worship (*triṣkālapūjā*) with the hand of the noble Avalokiteśvara and the goddess Śrī, and an offering vessel (*arghapātra*) must be presented. Worship of the Three Jewels must be performed; [the offering] must be given; [the food] must be eaten; merits must be cultivated; and the great goddess Śrī must be worshipped at the three times of the day. Alternatively, for one who wishes to remain in the actual form of the great goddess Śrī, the *Amogharāja-krodha-hṛdaya* [mantra] should be recited a full eight thousand times.

6. One should mutter [the mantra] one thousand times over honey; it should be struck with mustard seeds eight thousand times. Then Śrī, the Great Goddess, appears in her own form, adorned with all ornaments, her body decorated with divine jewels, gold, and pearl ornaments, blazing brilliantly, with a face like a blooming lotus, eyes like blue lotuses, clearly holding a lotus, seated upon a lotus-throne with the radiance of a lotus, raining down many jewel-gems and golden lotuses, bearing hundreds of thousands of flaming jars upon her chest, accompanied by many celestial maidens and yakṣas—

Surrounded by a hundred thousand maidens and adorned with many divine ornaments, all of them radiant and complete, eight thousand moon-pillars and incense banners stood before him, bearing infinite [power]. The Vidyādhara should not be afraid; he should maintain a joyful heart. This should be recited seven times as a reminder: *Namo ratnatrayāya. Namaḥ āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya mahāmoghavaradāya. Tadyathā oṃ pa-* [191]

O Goddess, lotus-eyed one, dweller in the lotus, holder of the lotus, possessed of the lotus, lover of the lotus, as fair as the lotus, radiant as the lotus, established upon the lotus-throne; beloved of Avalokita, granter of boons, bestower of boons; be gracious, grant favor! Act, act, O Noble Avalokita, granter of boons! Huru huru, O lady of excellent limbs! Move, move, O you adorned with flowers, lover of the lotus, bearer of the variegated celestial palace; support, support, gather together, remember your sacred vow! O you who are equal to the Noble Avalokiteśvara, Goddess established in truth, granter of boons through the unfailing noose! Hūṃ! Homage!

2. *Astu te svāhā*. As soon as this is recited seven times, the Great Goddess Śrī extends her hand and places the Vidyādhara upon it. She speaks thus: "Come, noble son! You are born from my own breast. You have accomplished the Amoghapāśahṛdaya; enter the dhāraṇī named Amoghavimalaśrī, the King of Wrath, and enter my abode as if it were your own home. Perform all the rites that must be done. Then, by the Vidyādhara, again with this mantra-vidyā-dhāraṇī...

3. It should be recited three times. [192] Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage! To the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One. Tadyathā: Oṃ, Blessed Lady, Mother of the World! Bestow, bestow! O you who grant boons through your gaze! O Milky One, let it flow! O Mother, O Mother, you who bring about vast renown! O you with the most excellent arms! O you whose hand holds the unfailing noose! Svāhā! Then, from the two breasts of the Great Goddess Śrī, streams of milk—

They release it. That stream of milk must be caught with the mouth and drunk; as soon as it is drunk, one’s body will become divine—tender like a divine *padma* or *kumuda* lotus, possessing hair in curled ringlets, with eyes like blue lotuses, and speech that is clear and resonant with the sound of the *kiṃnara*. The Great King of Lotuses named Amoghasāgara-mahāmaṇi-padma-vilokita-śrīvimalā will appear before one. This is the accomplishment of a great eon (*mahākalpa*).

He shall open [the gates]. His lifespan shall be ten thousand years. He shall behold the Jina Amitābha, who is chanting the Dharma together with a host of Bodhisattvas and amidst excellent celestial palaces (*vimāna*). By means of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*), he travels through the expanse of the sky. He shall become a Great Universal Monarch (*cakravartin*) of the Great Amoghapāśa, named Mahāmaṇipadmavilokita. He shall be the sole sovereign lord of all Vidyādharas. He shall become the noble Avalokiteśvara-mudrā. He shall be a son of the gods among all the Tathāgatas.

6. He shall open [the gates]. He shall become the sole eldest son of all the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas; he shall become the only son of the four great kings. He shall possess strength, prowess, and heroism unimpeded everywhere. All the profound mudrās, maṇḍalas, chapters, vidyārājas, secret mantras, dhāraṇīs, and mantra-kalparājas of all the Tathāgatas shall manifest before him. [He shall enter] all the abodes of the gods, all the abodes of the nāgas, all the abodes of the kinnaras, and all caves...

7. The abodes of the *vivaras* shall be opened; all the abodes of the *yakṣas* and *rākṣasas* shall be opened. All shall remain under his control as servants. They shall perform worship and service toward him who is like the Lord of the World, the sole teacher and guru of all worlds. There shall be the great accomplishment of all worldly and supramundane mantra-maṇḍalas. Śrī Mahādevī herself, out of affection for her son, together with her retinue, shall personally attend upon that *vidyādhara*.

Whomever she attends upon, she will fulfill all their desires and all the tasks of their heart's wish. She presents them with all kinds of wealth and grain, silver and gold, jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, silver, and refined gold; she presents divine great maṇi-jewels, divine great Kāśika garments, and so on, up to divine food and drink, even food of the taste of nectar. Even when [the devotee] is in any place, she always follows them, constantly and continuously, as if with the affection for a son.

2. This excellent celestial palace of the Vidyādhara shall be like his own home in the capital city of Aḍakavatī; its splendor and prosperity shall be like that of Vaiśravaṇa’s abode. Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara shall constantly approach it at all times. And Vajradhara, the great general of the Yakṣas, together with the hosts of all Vidyādharas and the retinues of great Yakṣas and Guhyakas, shall provide constant and continuous protection, defense, and guardianship. Likewise, the Great Goddess Śrī, along with her retinue—

3. "They will provide protection, shelter, and guardianship day and night, surrounded by ten million *yakṣa* ascetics. Then, the *amoghapāśahṛdayakalparāja* named *Amoghapāśāgaramahāmaṇipadmavilokitaśrīvimalā*, when recited, becomes effective. It is equal to the atoms of the sands of sixty-four *gaṅgā* rivers; it belongs to hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *tathāgatas*, the Arhats, the Perfectly Awakened Ones.

4. He will have planted roots of merit in the presence of the perfectly awakened ones; he will be endowed with a great mass of merit. And whichever son of good family or daughter of good family, or monk or nun, or layman or laywoman, [should offer] divine great maṇi-jewels, seventy great maṇi-jewels, great golden flowers, silver flowers, divine garments, divine ornaments, and divine perfumes, flowers, garlands, and ointments—[doing so] with a single thought directed toward hell...

5. Suppose one were to construct [stupas] as high as the great king of mountains, Sumeru, and offer them to as many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones as there are atoms in the sands of sixty-four Ganges rivers—offering to each individual Tathāgata in this manner for every single Tathāgata—and were to present these offerings day after day until a full year has passed, performing worship and service.

6. One who kindles before each Tathāgata a lamp filled with fragrant oil the size of the great ocean will be endowed with that mass of merit and will be embraced by great roots of virtue. If one should turn this Amoghasāgara-mahāmaṇi Amoghapāśa mudrā seven times and recite the Vilokitaśrīvimalā Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya, performing eight hundred recitations, this mass of merit shall be equal [to the former].

He will be endowed [with these qualities]; he will be endowed with great roots of merit; he will be sustained by the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas; he will be embraced by all the Tathāgatas; he will never be separated from the vision of all the Tathāgatas; and he will receive the prophecy of all the Tathāgatas. Furthermore, the Great Goddess Śrī bestows all boons upon him. The Goddess Śrī shall dwell constantly in his house. Wherever the Great Goddess Śrī dwells, there— 57b (P.105a4, D.107a4)

1. Hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas, equal in number to the atoms of dust in the sands of sixty Ganges rivers, shall dwell in that very spot of earth. Because Śrī is the mother of all Tathāgatas; because the mantra-rites, mudrās, and maṇḍalas of all gods, nāgas, Brahmās, Viṣṇus, and Maheśvaras—whether for pacifying, enriching, or subjugating, or other various rites—are declared to have their origin in the Great Goddess Śrī. She is the mother everywhere, the progenitor of all Bodhisattvas; [she is] the Great Goddess Śrī. This is she—

2. Accomplished by the Great Goddess Śrī; those who grant unfailing boons; who bestow unfailing gifts; who produce unfailing and vast fame; who possess unfailing and excellent celestial palaces in the sky; who grant unfailing boons through the proclamation of their qualities; [these belong] to the Great Goddess Śrī. Those who create the light of the moon and sun belong to the Great Goddess Śrī. The thirty-two abodes of the Great Deity Śrī are declared to be supreme. Then, by a *vidyādhara* who is pure, well-bathed, sprinkled with scented water, anointed with the five perfumes, clothed in clean garments, and having consumed pure food—

3. One must be one who eats with moderation. One must avoid leftovers consisting of intoxicants, meat, onions, garlic, *gṛñjanaka*, and impure mixtures. One must be free from bad food, bad drink, bad clothing, and impurity. One must avoid association with base beings, inferior people, those who are wicked, fraudulent, cruel, malicious, ungrateful, devoid of compassion and loving-kindness, and those who are cowardly. One must avoid bad places, bad dwellings, difficult crossings, ill-consumed food, and bad shadows. [One must avoid] mutual...

4. One must avoid eating leftover food. The recitation (*japa*) should be performed while perfuming oneself with incense and fragrances, remaining silent, and with a mind of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), compassion (*karuṇā*), and sympathetic joy (*muditā*). One should be of a joyful disposition, filled with auspiciousness, and possess a heart that is thrilled, contented, and delighted. The recitation of Noble Avalokiteśvara should be performed; agarwood incense should be offered to all the Tathāgatas; frankincense (*turuṣka*) should be offered; and sandalwood incense should be offered to the Great Goddess Śrī. [The water for] the guest-offering (*argha-pātra*)—

5. And an offering must be given; flowers must be offered at the proper time. Having recited this mantra twenty-one times, it should be presented everywhere: *Namo ratnatrayāya / Namaḥ āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya / Tadyathā: Oṃ puṣpavilokite / gandhasare amoghajala saṃbharaṇi padmasaṃbhari tara tara mudite hūṃ svāhā //* By reciting this twenty-one times, [the offering of] flowers, incense, and perfumes—

6. Having presented the vessel of offering water (*arghapātra*), one should recite [the mantra] eight thousand times at the feet of Noble Avalokiteśvara. One who recites the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* seven times should recite the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*) three times. Incense of *agaru* should be offered, and flowers should be offered as they are obtained. A lamp should be lit with fragrant oil. Sitting cross-legged right there at his feet and gazing upon Noble Avalokiteśvara, while reciting the Heart Dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times, one should assume the mudrā of recitation; [then] one thousand—

7. As soon as it has been rolled, the image moves; the entire body blazes; one’s own body experiences horripilation. At dawn, it grants a vision of the noble Avalokiteśvara. It speaks all that is thought in the mind; it bestows all boons; it grants all desired boons; it provides consolation; it fulfills all heart’s desires. In this very life, one becomes free from all diseases and is endowed with the accumulation of merit and all roots of virtue.

...all obscurations and evils will be completely exhausted and brought to an end; one will be liberated from all afflictions (*kleśa*); and all adversaries and enemies will perish and shall no longer have power. Having entered into battle, this King of Vidyās should be recited twenty-one times, and white mustard seeds should be thrown into the midst of the fray; all [the enemies] will become paralyzed and stupefied. This is the Heart Mantra: Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One...

2. *Kāya*: Namely, *Oṃ amoghapāśahṛdaya padmini varade jvala jvala prasāritapadmabhuje svāhā*. This is the Heart-Vidyā. *Oṃ avalokitapadmini varāṅgiṇi turu turu hūṃ svāhā*. This is the Upahṛdaya-Dhāraṇī. By reciting this *Amoghasāramaṇipadmavilokitaśrīvimalā-amoghapāśahṛdayakalpa-dhāraṇī* one hundred times, one exhausts the five sins of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*). She will become a constant and perpetual bestower of boons by the Great Goddess Śrī. Noble Avaloki-...

3. He will always have a desire to behold Maheśvara. No poison shall affect his body, and he will be liberated from the eight great and terrible fears. No fevers or any diseases shall afflict him. Regarding all planetary seizures (*graha*): one should recite the mantra twenty-one times over a five-colored thread, tie twenty-one knots, and fumigate it with *guggulu*. It should be tied around the neck; thus one is liberated from all planetary seizures. If [the seizure is caused] by Mahākāla...

4. One who has come of their own accord and those *mātṛkā* that are sealed are liberated from all seizing spirits (*graha*). By means of a black thread, one is liberated from quartan fever (*cāturthika-jvara*). For other purposes, it should be invoked everywhere with a white thread. In all cases of strife, quarrel, conflict, and dispute, one should recite the mantra twenty-one times over *gorocana* and apply it as a forehead mark (*tilaka*); one becomes unassailable everywhere. Having applied a forehead mark on the heart, all yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, and so forth, become invisible. [The syllable] *pā-*...

5. Having applied a *tilaka* on the surface of the forehead, all the scriptures will become manifest to whomever [it touches]. Through a practice for twenty-one nights, one will become a man, a boy, or a girl. Having applied a *tilaka* between the eyebrows, kings together with their harems will become submissive. Having placed it upon the neck, all Vaiśyas will become submissive. Having smeared both arms, all Kṣatriyas will become submissive. Having applied a *tilaka* on the top of the head, all Brāhmaṇas—

By applying [the ointment] to the navel, all Śūdras will become submissive. By anointing the feet and shanks, one travels a hundred *yojanas* without rest and returns again. By anointing the soles of the feet, one crosses to the far shore of a great river, even crossing over the ocean. By anointing both arms, one will become an invincible wrestler. One should smear the knees; by the blazing radiance of a garland of fire-flames, one enters a pit of fire as if it were cool with sandalwood and *uśīra*.

7. *Yati*: One should apply collyrium to the eyes; one should infuse it with the milk of a tawny woman for a night. By this, one sees as if by day. All treasures (*nidhi*) shine forth. Even if one has been struck down for a hundred thousand eons, one leaps up. One should likewise smear the eyes with *raktākṣī*; as long as water does not touch the belly, and as long as one does not desire food or drink [one remains suspended]. One should smear the sexual organ (*indriya*); it becomes a binder of semen (*śukrabandha*). One should drink it together with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*); one’s body becomes stainless and pure. [One should be] pure and of pure conduct.

One becomes endowed [with these qualities]. All difficult crossings, ill-spoken words, evil shadows, and evil glances will cease to exist. One becomes liberated from all fears. All sinful obstructions are released. Due to the absence of all bad dreams, evil omens, and inauspicious signs, they perish; all poisons, venomous substances, and *kākhorda* spells perish. All applications of mantras and rays of light perish. In all instances of strife, quarrel, conflict, and dispute, one shall be the victor; everywhere one shall be a giver of victory.

2. There will be no fear from any adversaries, enemies, or foreign armies. One should mix [the medicine] with ghee and honey and consume it at dawn without speaking. If one recites and retains a thousand verses, through practice for seven nights, all mantras, maṇḍala rituals, and mantras of the maṇḍala sections, as well as the mudrās, will be accomplished. Through practice for only one month, one will become a repository of a great ocean of learning. Through practice for one year, one will have a lifespan of a thousand years.

3. He will become the sole teacher of the entire world; he will be beloved and his words will be authoritative. Having boiled [the substance] with oil and applied it to the head, his hair will become curled and ringlet-like, and his facial orb will become like the preeminent, full autumn moon. His body will become as soft as a lotus or a water lily, and his entire frame will be like butter, tender from being smeared with ointments. His divine hands and feet—

And there shall be ten [benefits]: one should apply it to the ears as much as desired, and the ears will grow; it should be applied even when the ritual action has been performed. All diseases involving internal fractures will perish; all phlegm and nasal mucus will no longer prevail. One will not smell divine fragrances, nor will scents that lead to further subjugation be smelled. One will become free from wrinkles and grey hair. Decayed teeth will become young teeth again. [Like] a lotus petal—

5. His tongue will become soft; he shall be liberated from all throat diseases and demonic seizures. One should fill the ears with [the substance], which brings a divine cooling refreshment to the mouth; there will be divine hearing. Only pleasant sounds and auspicious words will issue forth. Such will be the great ritual procedure for the accomplishment of *gorocana*. Now I shall proclaim the *Tejasvatī* [practice], which is perfectly accomplished, supremely auspicious, unimpeded everywhere, and established as "Brahma-gone" (*brajeta*). It is radiant—*tejasvatī*.

6. Having recited the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* twenty-one times, one should then recite the *Krodharāja* seven times. Having fully recited this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* of the Blessed One Vimalā, who is adorned with the jewel-lotus of the unfailing ocean, eight thousand times, one should—being pure, wearing clean garments, well-bathed, and having eaten white food—bear it in one's mouth by means of this vajra, receive its oral instruction, and read, retain, and master it as much as one desires.

7. Furthermore, his tongue will be as soft as a lotus, a water-lily, or a tender lotus; it will be adorned with a voice like that of the lord of the *kinnaras*; and a divine, intelligible sound will issue forth from it. To whomever he gives this charm, they shall remain as his slaves, handmaidens, servants, and laborers. Whosoever smells its fragrance shall become submissive; even those belonging to the animal realm he brings under his control. All *bhūtas*, *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, *rākṣasīs*, *pretas*, *piśācas*, and so forth, as well as those possessed by epilepsy and all who are wicked or malicious—[he subdues them].

1. All humans will depart because of that fragrance; they will flee for even a hundred *yojanas* in the four directions and remain at a great distance. All adversaries, enemies, and those with wicked or malicious minds will all depart because of that fragrance and will come under one's control through a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*). One should bind the right arm; it causes the "elephant-hand" (*hastanāga*) to fall. One will possess great strength, vigor, and prowess, and will become an invincible wrestler. One displays a strength equal to that of the Vajra-holder (*Vajrapāṇi*). [One should] bind the neck—

Furthermore, if one should enter the midst of battle, one shall alone conquer a fourfold army. When he returns again, having placed [the image] upon his head, he should enter the royal palace; the king, together with his harem, retinue, ministers, counselors, warriors, and priests, will come under his control. He will become one who stands at the very head [of the state]. With a hand whose movement is unimpeded everywhere, he may bind [his enemies]; wherever he touches, all will come under his control. [He shall obtain] wealth, grain, gold, jewels, pearls, and refined gold.

3. By the mere touch [of this], it shall become inexhaustible. Having received the sowing of the seed, it increases inexhaustibly. One becomes like Ratnapāṇi. The heap of grain and seeds increases; if one eats [from it] day by day, it becomes a great increaser of mindfulness and intelligence. One becomes free from all evils (sins). One becomes free from all diseases. It removes all fevers. It [removes] all swellings, pustules, carbuncles, erysipelas, poison-spreading rashes, scabies, and leprosy.

4. By merely smearing it with a small amount of this [ointment], one perishes; one shall never be able [to harm] [the practitioner]. By using it for only a month, all the mantra-chapters, mudrās, and maṇḍalas of every kalpa will become supremely accomplished (*uttarasiddha*). For one who constantly wears it on the body, uplifted weapons shall not strike the body. One becomes unapproachable by all thieves and rogues. One’s movement shall be unimpeded everywhere. If one boils it with oil, it cures headaches, earaches, and hemicrania (*ardhāvabhedaka*).

5. By merely casting warm [substances] into the mouth of one who causes division, all sufferings will be pacified; furthermore, no further diseases shall arise. If one fumigates with sixty-eight thousand *graha*-spirits using ghee mixed with mustard seeds, they will all flee while wailing, going off to the various directions and intermediate points. They shall never again approach that place or region of the earth. One may also perform other tasks according to one's own preference and inclination.

6. Therefore, I shall now proclaim the incense ritual for the invocation of all deities; for the summoning of the Bodhisattvas; for the exhortation of all the Tathāgatas; for the established doctrine of all Vidyādharas; and for Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Grahas, Apasmāras, Yakṣiṇīs, Pretas, Piśācas, and Skandas—it brings about the dissolution of all Ḍākinīs and the destruction of all wicked Māras. It wards off all diseases and neutralizes all evil poisons, whether from fanged creatures or those that are stationary or mobile. It is everywhere unassailable—

7. Perfected by three [recitations], it is the destroyer of all fevers, especially of quartan fever; it is the supreme brightener of the face and the most excellent incense for clothing. It is the eradicator of all spells (*mantra*) and *kākhorda* sorcery, and the most excellent means of subjugation. If a king is enraged against someone, or if executioners have raised their weapons, by fumigating with this incense, all of this is pacified. For those afflicted by artificial poisons (*gara*), natural poisons (*viṣa*), or *lūta* [spiders/scorpions], and for all wicked cattle, as well as other various living beings that are venomous and extremely fierce—by means of this incense...

1. This [incense] is a protection against all venomous creatures, whether they be snakes or scorpions. It is proven to remove all diseases, destroy all evils, and is equal to a great mass of merit. It is perfected and worshipped by all the deities. When Śakra fought with the Asuras, he burned them with this incense, and thus the Asuras were utterly defeated. By means of this King of Incense, Tripura was burnt by Rudra; Bali was bound by Viṣṇu in his dwarf incarnation as he strode across the earth; and the Lord of the Asuras, along with the planets Moon and Sun in their agitation, were all conquered by the excellence of this King of Incense. Everything is conquered.

2. But you, O Vāmana, have indeed always conquered hundreds of thousands of illusionists in the land of Bhārata; having defeated the Pāṇḍavas at the city of Dhūparāja, there is no doubt. Having conquered thousands of crores of Māras and the hosts of Kiṃkaras, the Leader, by the power of loving-kindness (*maitrābala*) and through the majesty of Dhūparāja, brought the wicked Māras to destruction. The ocean was agitated, and all those dwelling in the sea were stripped naked. Within a single vessel, in the third part, they were purified; and by means of the lost *cintāmaṇi* jewel, all purposes were accomplished.

3. By this incense, which was perfected by the Great-Souled One, he conquered [the nāgas] and returned once more to his own home. Having always raised it high upon the tip of a banner, one should fumigate with this incense for seven days and nights; for seven days and nights, rain was made to fall. Thus powerful is this incense, the accomplisher of the purpose of all rites. In the great battle, the nāgas were struck down; Nanda and Upananda of the ocean were subdued. When the great ocean was churned, Meru vomited poison, but the poison was drunk by the Blue-Throated One (Śiva) through the power of the King of Incense.

4. Enveloped [by poison], it was rendered poisonless by the power of this king of incenses; nectar was transformed [from poison]. Thus, this king of incenses destroys all poisons; of this there is no doubt. By Māndhātṛ, the four continents were conquered; by Śakra, his hair was pulled out, and he shared half the throne. By meditating upon the king of incenses, they were freed from false speech; therefore, one should speak the truth. This is proclaimed as the "Truthful Incense" by the King of Truth; it is truthful speech and the dharma of truth.

5. With a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*), one should always maintain loving-kindness, compassion, and sympathetic joy toward the entire world in brief. One should be incensed with incense; all weapons shall be neutralized. This is the incense empowered by truth, spoken by all the Tathāgatas, and by the Protector Lokeśvara, the sole teacher of the world, for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, and especially for the holders of the *vidyā*. [Even] in the sixteen terrible hells and amidst the most dreadful great fears, they shall experience the suffering of sensation—great fear... [mahābha-].

6. The most terrible sufferings of the hungry ghosts (*preta*), who are constantly afflicted by hunger and thirst and utter cries of "Alas! Alas!"—for them there is no protector. O Śāṭha, one who has compassion for all beings must look [to the Buddha]. He is the protector of the entire world, the speaker of the unsurpassed king of incenses. By means of this incense-offering, for whose sake the name is invoked, whether [intentions] are conceived with a malicious mind or with a mind of loving-kindness, they are accomplished. As soon as it is uttered and this incense is offered, all these things are always [accomplished].

They meditate upon the auspicious words of Avalokiteśvara. Whether during an eclipse of the moon or the sun, for those people afflicted by the calamities of the stars, or by Rāhu’s seizure, or by the suffering of birth—whether they be kings, women, ministers, counselors, generals, priests, kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, śūdras, vaiśyas, or any other gathering of people; when they are overtaken by misfortune, by distress, or by forms of suffering as terrible as a forest fire—if they are fumigated with this king of incenses, all of this shall be resolved at that very moment. And those people who have reached the hells shall obtain food and drink that is most delicious.
60a (P. omitted, D. 111b7)

1. Divine garments, ornaments, perfumes, garlands, and ointments, as well as clothing, vehicles, and bedding—every such embellishment for one’s dwelling arises in an instant if one applies oneself correctly. All that is desired is accomplished; all intended wishes are fulfilled. All these are always accomplished according to the word of Lokeśvara. Pretas obtain food, and supreme divine garments and ornaments constantly appear to me through liberation from all evil. One is liberated from all hells; one is liberated from the terrors of hell. Mu-

One is liberated from all sufferings and experiences a joyful birth; one rejoices happily and goes to a happy rebirth, attaining happiness everywhere. By means of this incense, one should be fumigated; one shall smell a most excellent fragrance. When this king of incenses is smelled for the sake of awakening, it dispels all darkness and mental obscurations, just as when the sun rises in the world, it dispels the darkness. By this king of incense, all suffering is destroyed; one is released from all hells and from the fear of all miserable states, and attains the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) and the divine path taught by the Sugata—all of that [is attained].

3. With diligence, one should employ the King of Incenses. Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara spoke these verses concerning the Great Kings of Incense in the presence of the Lord of the World: "Wherever this incense is burned upon the earth, this shrine becomes the abode of the Tathāgatas, eternally sustained by all the Victors. That earth is prophesied as such; there, indeed, thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abide."

4. Where one fumigates with incense, there are hundreds of thousands of millions of *vidyādharas* and *vajradharas*, as well as the four Great Kings together with their armies and vehicles; Sātā, Giri, Hemavata, Māṇibhadra, and Pāñcika; Pūrṇabhadra, Ketu, Kīla, and the great yakṣa Saṃjñeya who is borne by men; Buddhabala, Mahābala, Gavākṣapāti, Navakūpara, Prabhañjana, Aṭavaka, and Baladeva—these of great supernatural power, together with their hosts.

5. Accompanied by their armies and mounts, they remain ever present day and night; they provide protection for me, and Śrī Tribhuvanadevī always worships there with incense, where the earth is perpetually perfumed. Likewise, Vajradhara, along with the Guhyakas, the upholders of the Dharma, and the wise ones, always provide protection at all times. Similarly, Indra together with the sons of the gods, Brahmā, Rudra, and Viṣṇu—with the thirty-two gods—[provide protection].

6. All of them provide protection at all times; the moon and the sun, as well as Rāhu, the constellations, the hosts of stars, and the deities of night provide protection at all times. The deities Bhīmā, Śrī, and Śaṅkhinī, Sarasvatī, and the deities who uphold the earth; the water deities, the deities of trees and forest-tops, the mountain deities, and the deities of rivers and ponds; Yama and the gods, Varuṇa and the gods, Kuvera and the gods, Kumāra and the gods, and the great-souled ṛṣis—[all these provide protection].

May the deities of the lakes and the deities of the ponds, the rivers and the asuras of the lakes, and likewise the Moon and the Sun—may these deities always provide protection, remaining constantly bound to those who are ever-attentive day and night through this incense. May this ground be constantly perfumed with incense; may the abode of the deities on this ground be eternally presided over. May the Lord of the World, the Protector, the Guru, and the Guide—the Savior of the world and the Giver of Boons—remain forever and eternally present in that place.

1. This is the incense that, when offered as a supreme offering, allows one to swiftly attain Buddhahood by the mere scenting of its fragrance. I shall now declare the names of the substances; listen, O gods and humans, for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings and for the warding off of all sufferings. Agallochum, Tagara, sandalwood together with *nakha*, *spṛkkā*, *gorocanā*, buffalo-gallstone (*māhiṣākṣa*), *kunduru*, resin (*rasa*), *sarjarasa*, saffron (*kuṅkuma*), *nalada*, *śrīveṣṭaka* along with *harītakī*, *sāmaka*, and *gandhamāṃsī*.

And *turuṣka*, along with *pṛyaṅgu*, *kayasthā*, and *vayasthā*; *nameru* together with *musta*, as well as *kuṣṭha*, black *agaru*, camphor, and musk; the fruit of *laṅgaka* and *kanaka*; the milks of *arka*, *kanaka*, and *snuhā*; *kapāla* and *bhagavan*; *viṣṇukrāntā*, *somarājī*, *sunandī*, *ajayā*, and *vijaya*; *nākulī*, *gandhanākulī*, *brahmaputrā*, *kumuda*, the stalk of a lotus, honey, and the juice of white jaggery—these, when combined together, [form the mixture].

One should burn the supreme incense on the full moon, the fifteenth day, as well as the fourteenth, the thirteenth, and always on the eighth. The wise one, having bathed well and being pure, wearing clean garments, should maintain this for days and nights. Having prepared this incense, the discerning one employs the various mantras, mudrās, and maṇḍala-mantras. By those skilled in flowers, incense, and perfumes, this is the procedure for worship; one who is skilled in the rite of offerings (bali-karman) [should prepare] the full vessels of water for the guest-offering (argha-pātra) upon the head.

4. And [there should be] a lamp of fragrant oil, as well as the practice for a well-perfected site; and the practice for a pure site, which is well-concealed. Having sat before Amoghapāśa—the supreme disciple together with his companions—having established himself in the vow of a completely pure body and a mind of loving-kindness, and alone having cultivated compassion for all sentient beings, he should meditate on the recollection of the Buddha (*buddhānusmṛti*) and be intent upon the recitation of the mantra. Without departing from all the Tathāgatas, he should remain in the presence of the face of Lokeśvara, at the heart of Amoghapāśa.

One should recite the *Dayā* mantra eight thousand times; the *Krodharāja* mantra eight hundred and eight times; and the *Amoghasiddhi* mantra one hundred and eight times, with the syllables and phonemes clearly articulated. One should then recite the *Amoghasāgaramaṇipadmavilokitaśrīvimalā-amoghapāśahṛdaya* ten thousand times. Thereafter, one should recite this mantra one hundred thousand times: Oṃ sarvatathāgatāvalokita amoghahṛdaya cara.

6. *Cara cara mahākāruṇika sādhaya hūṃ abhiṣiñcaya amoghapāśahaste svāhā*. Then one should perform the recitation of the mantra while maintaining meditative concentration; by the mere recitation, this supreme incense—empowered by the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, the king of incenses known as the "Stainless Jewel of the Great Cloud of Vast Radiance of the Unfailing Noose," beheld by all Tathāgatas, the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the Wondrous Bestower of Boons, the Universal Monarch—[is accomplished].

7. Ma-dhūpa-rāja. First, incense should be offered to the Tathāgatas. This mantra should be recited seven times: Oṃ sarvatathāgatāvalokitamaho(moghāmo)gha jaya jaya svāhā. Then, by fumigating oneself with it, one becomes empowered by all the Tathāgatas. Upon merely being fumigated, the noble Mahābodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the bestower of boons, reveals his form; appearing in the guise of a śramaṇa or a brāhmaṇa, he appears together with me.

1. He speaks; whatever he speaks, whether he speaks or does not speak, all of that is accomplished through the visible Dharma and by one who has seen the Truth. Then, during the night, he grants a vision in his own form. He bestows all boons. One obtains unfailing knowledge (*amoghajñāna*). One becomes liberated from the eight great fears. All previous obscurations and sins leading to rebirth in hell go to complete exhaustion and total destruction. By the mere scenting [of this incense] by oneself and by the mere sight of it, everything comes under control and is empowered. Together with the kingdom—

2. They remain under the control of kings of cities, market towns, and provinces, along with their harems, retinues, ministers, counselors, soldiers, and chaplains; they become servants to all. They remain under the control of the world of the four castes. On the fourteenth, fifteenth, or eighth day [of the lunar fortnight], one who has bathed well and is wearing clean garments, having sprinkled his head with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), should draw a mandala in a sheltered place. A flower and an offering (*argha*) should be placed in a vessel, and a white sacrificial oblation (*bali*) should be set out. One should pay homage to the four directions.

3. This *mṛdvī* king-incense should be offered. By means of focusing upon all the Tathāgatas and focusing upon the Bodhisattvas, as soon as it is incensed, throughout the ten directions—in infinite and boundless Buddha-fields, numbering as many as the atoms of dust in those fields—the abodes of the Tathāgatas become completely filled; that is to say, in each single Buddha-field, there appear hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *tathāgatas* like the sands of ten *gaṅgā* rivers, [emanating] great clouds and masses of incense.

They are honored by all the retinues of bodhisattvas with the vault of the sky covered by great incense—divinely fragrant, peerless, and incomparable, consisting of uragasāra sandalwood, gośīrṣa sandalwood, uragasāra, and tamāla leaves. All the gods dwelling in the palaces of the Thirty-three, from Śakra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, up to the gods of the Akaniṣṭha heaven, are gladdened by the fragrance of that incense. So too are the hosts of lunar mansions and stars, the sun, and the moon.

5. The months will become joyful; one should not entertain doubt in this matter, nor should any hesitation arise. One should recite the Amoghapāśahṛdaya with a loud voice. And from all around, those dwelling in the Buddha-fields and the abodes of the Tathāgatas will utter the sound of "Well done! They will empower that practitioner of the vidyā through the empowerment of the Tathāgata. They will always keep him in mind and approach him again and again for the sake of seeing him. Ta—

6. Furthermore, all the bodhisattvas—headed by the noble Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, as well as those residing in Sukhāvatī under the Tathāgata Amitāyus—become joyful in heart. They grant the supreme great accomplishment (*mahāmoghasiddhi*) to the vidyādhara; they will desire to behold him. All nāgas, merely by being fumigated with this [incense], will become submissive. It holds back excessive rain; it causes rain to fall during drought; and it disperses all winds and clouds merely by being fumigated.

7. All malevolent spirits (*graha*) are destroyed; all obstacles (*vighna*) and obstructors (*vināyaka*) flee for a thousand *yojana* in the ten directions. For one who fumigates the Mother’s Abode (*mātṛsthāna*), they drive away all wind-eating clouds. By the mere act of fumigation, all malevolent spirits are destroyed; all obstacles and obstructors flee to the ten directions, and all the hosts of Mothers, headed by Mahākāla, are summoned and remain under one's control. They become performers of all tasks for one who fumigates during battle or conflict.

He shall conquer a fourfold army; everywhere, by the mere act of fumigation, victory shall be attained. It should be employed everywhere; everywhere there shall be great accomplishment. [End of] the Ritual for Incense. Now, therefore, I shall proclaim the *tilaka*, the washing of the face, and the anointing, as armor and mail-clad protection for the benefit of all Vidyādharas. Listen, O Blessed One, to the jewel of the Amoghapāśa, the Vajrapāśa, and the Mālī, by the mere application of which all supreme accomplishments are attained. [The ritual of] the sesame seed—

2. How does the wise one shine within the tufts of hair on the forehead of Kṛṣyamāṇa—within the assembly, within the midst of great people, within the community, and likewise in the midst of the group of those learned in the four Vedas—just as the confident new moon shines in the midst of the host of stars? [He is] the source of wonder for all the gods; the Lord of the World wearing Rudra’s crown; the washing from the mouth of the leader who possesses the moon-crown of Dakṣiṇamūrtti; possessing a radiance equal to the full moon; soft as a lotus petal; with eyebrows, ears, and forehead resembling the most excellent blue lotuses; his sight beloved by all sentient beings—[he is] the Adideva.

3. And they shall all become obedient and always under one's control, whoever beholds them with the eye. One should constantly touch that person [with it]; he becomes a great-souled proclaimer of knowledge, ever armored and clad in mail, with body perpetually bound, and confident. Among all beings—whether *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, or *guhyakas*—he is irresistible. Constantly surrounded on all sides by iron [strength], possessing great power and prowess, he shall always have the strength of Nārāyaṇa and the strength of a thousand serpents (*nāgas*). The deities tremble—

Those who practice [this] tremble before the ocean of the *nāgas*. If the practitioner of the *vidyā* should touch it, Mount Sumeru would immediately shake; of this there is no doubt. It possesses the strength of Nārāyaṇa, with constant power, form, and valor. This supreme king of jewels is for one who does not grasp at [worldly things]; it liberates one from all evil and destroys all defilements. Whoever has this in their hand will always obtain glory and good fortune. Liberated from all obscurations and beloved by all the world, it is as if it were born from the very mouth of the Tathāgata.

5. For one whose son has been born, that noble Avalokiteśvara—the teacher of all Tathāgatas—will be constantly and always attached to him for the sake of consolation, and likewise the speech of the *vidyā* for the sake of protection; and the great sage Lokeśvara will always be a granter of boons in his dwelling. Whoever wears this jewel shall obtain a mass of great merit equal to hundreds of thousands of millions of *koṭis* of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of sixty-four hundred thousand *gaṅgā* rivers.

6. He will have planted roots of merit in my presence. All of them will be followed by the consolation of seeing the Tathāgata; they will be endowed with all glory and good fortune. They will always possess a completely pure body, speech, and mind. They will become worthy of worship by all sentient beings. They will be invincible to all enemies. Vajrapāṇi will always stand ready for their protection, defense, and guardianship. And Padmapāṇi will always be a granter of boons to them. This—

7. By this Great Jewel Dhāraṇī of all the Tathāgatas, all the Tathāgatas have been prophesied; all the wicked ones, such as Māras, obstacles, and impediments, have been conquered and defeated, and the Wheel of Dharma has been set in motion. By anointing a drum with this and striking it, it becomes the beating of the Great Drum of Dharma. By the mere hearing of its sound, the five sins of immediate retribution are pacified for all sentient beings—even down to the beasts and birds of the animal realm—all of them [are purified].

They are liberated; those who revile the noble ones and reject the true Dharma—who were destined for the Avīci hell—are completely freed from the sixteen great hells. They are completely freed from the eight great fears. There shall be no fear of poison for them; there shall be no fear of fire, nor fear of weapons. There shall be no fear of untimely death, nor fear of any fever. Having smeared a conch shell with this [substance] and blown it, it becomes filled with the Great Dharma.

2. As many as shall hear the sound of the conch shell, they all shall become non-retrogressive (*avaivarttika*). Men, women, boys, and girls shall be completely liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, and lamentation. This shall be their final birth; having passed away, they shall all be reborn together in the world-system Sukhāvatī. They shall be born spontaneously (*upapāduka*) from lotuses, with bodies fully endowed with the primary marks (*lakṣaṇa*) and secondary characteristics (*anuvyañjana*) of a Great Man (*mahāpuruṣa*), adorned with every ornament, arising upon lotus thrones.

3. They shall hear the discourse on the Dharma in the presence of Amitābha, until the very end at the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍala). For this purpose, O Great Jewel, during the bright fortnight, this jewel should be placed upon the tip of a banner covered with a white cloth; they shall be raised up together. By the mere sight of its being placed upon the tip of the banner, it should be understood that one has seen the Tathāgata’s seat of awakening, the turning of the Wheel of Dharma, the subduing of Māra, and the raising of the vajra. Of this—

4. As soon as it has been recited, all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes shall be pacified; all calamities, plagues, famines, and wildernesses shall be pacified; all thieves, rogues, robbers, adversaries, and enemies shall perish; all internal and external armies and wicked beings shall be pacified; and all wicked venomous snakes, fierce beasts and birds, gadflies, mosquitoes, locusts, reptiles, scorpions, lice, ringworm, and hemorrhoids shall [be pacified].

5. All seizing spirits (grahas) will perish; all wicked nāgas, heat, cold, and winds will have no power; all diseases will be pacified; there will be security, delight, abundance, and the land will be crowded with many people and humans, possessing complete harmony. There will be a desire for all the teachings (dharmas); there will be the delightful pleasure of finding joy in the garden of the Dharma. Flowers, fruits, crops, food, and drink will be delicious, very soft, and perfectly ripened. All [beings] will partake of delicious and pure food and drink.

They shall be dispelled. All evil yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, ḍākinīs, pretas, and those possessed by epilepsy; the pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas, skandas, and shadows; and the ill effects of improper eating, transgressing boundaries, or looking upon things with an evil gaze—all these shall be pacified. None shall prevail, and all beings will come to possess minds of mutual loving-kindness (*maitrī*), dwelling in a state of supreme joy. Such are the great benefits and advantages empowered by this great king of jewels. Then, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara [addressed] the Blessed One...

Facing him with a smiling countenance and unblinking eyes, he said this to the Blessed One: “I shall proclaim, O Blessed One, the substances that bring accomplishment: the supreme jewel and sandalwood; those empowered and prophesied by all the Tathāgatas; my own heart-jewel, the great wish-fulfilling gem, undertaken for the welfare and happiness of all sentient beings; as well as gold, *nalada*, *gorocanā*, yellow orpiment, realgar, *manaḥśilā*, the *padma*, *utpala*, saffron, *nāgapuṣpa*, and you yourself.”

1. Having gathered tagara, the two types of sandalwood (candana), spṛkkā, vālaka, kuṣṭha, śatapuṣpā, priyaṅgu, along with hareṇuka, sūkṣmailā, lodhra, jātipatra, sumanā, sāmana, resin (rasa), sarjarasa, and the milky sap of arka—one should have these made into equal parts. It is taught that [the resulting powder] should be double the amount of gold. Under an auspicious constellation, at a lucky moment, on a well-praised lunar day, having bathed well, wearing clean garments, and established a mind of loving-kindness, one should prepare fine powders for the Amogharājahṛdaya [mantra], performing [the rite] for days and nights.

2. While reciting the dhāraṇī, one should also recite the Krodharāja one thousand and eight times. One should perform the consecration one hundred and eight times. Having mixed divine scented water with that which is called Viratā, one should fumigate it with camphor and musk. A jewel should be fastened here; using lotus seeds as the measure for its application, one should pierce it and bind it with a silk thread. Then, while reciting the Amoghapāśahṛdaya eight thousand times, [one should recite] the Krodharāja one hundred and eight times, and [the mantra of] Noble Avalokiteśvara... [the foremost].

3. It is to be accomplished as follows: while remaining silent, one should let the shadow [of the image] dry right at its base. Half, or even a quarter, of it should be covered with gold. For one by whom it is covered with gold, this performs the great ritual accomplishments (*mahākarmasādhana*)—both mundane and supramundane—such as the awakening of a Buddha, which is like the wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇi*) of the Amoghapāśa. By that which is not covered with gold, one accomplishes all mundane affairs. In all diseases, in all...

4. It pacifies seizures, scabies, erysipelas, visarpa, skin eruptions, hemorrhoids, fistula-in-ano, leprosy, various eye diseases, and headaches; [it cures] facial paralysis, lockjaw, diseases of the mouth, diseases of the nose, earache, toothache, pain in the palate, pain in the tongue, pain in the lips, heartache, pain in the sides, pain in the belly, spleen disease, backache, urinary disorders, cholera, diarrhea, dysentery, and all humoral imbalances. It pacifies all fevers.

5. It subdues quartan fevers, as well as those caused by wind (vāta), bile (pitta), phlegm (śleṣman), and their combination (sannipāta). For all diseases, it should be administered with warm water while the internal shadow [of the sun] remains. Externally, for all ailments, one is liberated from all diseases merely by anointing. When applied to the entire body in every respect, everything is accomplished; of this there is no doubt. If wrapped in gold and bound upon fire, it becomes unassailable in all cases. Pa-

6. One comes to possess strength, vigor, and prowess equal to that of Vajrapāṇi. This is declared to be the unsurpassed accomplishment of all tasks in three ways: it shall be the forehead mark (*tilaka*), the washing of the face, and likewise the anointing of the body. There is no doubt that the reality of accomplishing one's purpose is achieved through the mind and thought as intended. Kings, along with their harems, kinsmen, and ministers, will always be brought under control; they will become like slaves and remain forever as servants. Having placed the jewel within the crest of the hair—

7. Recite this mantra; it will be free from obstacles and everything will be accomplished. Having bound [the cord] between the hands with the right hand, one should recite the *vidyā*; the procedure for recitation becomes multiplied a hundred thousand times. By reciting it once, a hundred thousand recitations are increased. One should wear it tied around the neck. Even if one has not bathed, one becomes as one who has bathed. Even if impure, one becomes pure. Even if one does not practice celibacy (*brahmacarya*), one becomes a practitioner of celibacy. Even if one does not observe silence, one becomes observant of silence. Even if one does not fast, one becomes one who fasts. Even if one’s words are not authoritative, they become authoritative.

1. Success arises; non-success becomes success; for one who does not know the ritual (*samaya*), it becomes knowledge of the ritual; there arises a mental attention accompanied by loving-kindness (*maitrī*). Whatever gift one gives, even if very small, it increases into a great gift multiplied a hundred-thousandfold. One fulfills the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) by giving gold and binding it with this jewel on the right palm; whatever [object] one touches thereby becomes inexhaustible. This must not be revealed to anyone. Then...

2. All this increases. One should bind a cloth around the waist. Having entered into the middle of water, one obtains the depth of a great river. Then, by one desiring to accomplish the jewel (*maṇi*), it should be made of pure gold; it should be fashioned with thirty petals in full bloom. In the center, at the pericarp and filaments, a basket-like vessel should be made, measuring sixteen finger-breadths in size. In its center, a golden jewel should be placed. A square mandala should be prepared, provided with cow dung and cow urine.

3. It should be adorned with various colors. A lotus, perfectly circular all around, should be painted; in the center of the lotus-stamen, a silver lotus should be placed. One should prepare four full jars and four offering-pans, strewn with various flowers. It should be painted with various colorful designs. One should burn incense of agalloch, sandalwood, and turuṣka. A white offering should be set out, and it should be decorated with various variegated banners.

4. One should light thirty-two lamps of ghee. Various garlands should be arranged. Noble Avalokiteśvara should be installed. The vidyādhara must be pure and wear clean garments. Having fasted for a day and night, on the full moon, the fourteenth, and up to the fifteenth, worship should be performed at the three junctions of the day. That five-vessel set and that Noble Avalokiteśvara should be worshipped.

5. Seated in the maṇḍala facing east, one should perform the recitation one thousand and eight times. The King of Wrath (Krodharāja) should be recited one thousand and eight times; one should consecrate with mustard seeds and water. The Amoghapāśa mudrā should be performed one thousand and eight times, and likewise the Krodharāja mudrā should be performed. All rites should be carried out without speaking. Then, at dawn on the full moon of the fifteenth day—

6. At the time of meditation, that king of jewels together with the lotus becomes a single flame. A sound issues from the mouth of the noble Avalokiteśvara; the vidyādhara rejoices. A voice of applause issues from the expanse of the sky. And he beholds the great form of the Tathāgata. Then the vidyādhara must seize that flaming lotus. As soon as it is grasped with the right hand, he travels through the air. He becomes a universal monarch (cakravartin) of all vidyādharas, golden-hued like the Mahāsudarśana [wheel].

The Wheel-King stands at the forefront; he repels all wicked adversaries and enemies. He will have a retinue of twelve thousand koṭis of vidyādhara kings. His lifespan will be one thousand kalpas. He attains the samādhi called Amoghavilokitamahāmaṇidhvajāgravatī. He attains the Amoghapāśa [sūtra] known as Amoghavimalājvalitaśikhāvalokinī (or Amoghaśikhāvalokinī). Equal—63b (P.114b2, D.118b2)—

1. From within [this state], one beholds the miraculous manifestations of the Buddha-fields of all the Tathāgatas in the ten directions; and all those Tathāgatas offer words of consolation. One attains a purity of body that radiates with the power of the light from the *pariśuddha-mahāmaṇi-vajra-avalokita*. All gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and *kiṃkaras* will come under one's control. If one binds a great jewel (*mahāmaṇi*) upon the crown of the head, one proceeds toward the western direction by means of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*) to Sukhāvatī, together with its entirety, both in its collective and individual aspects, including its celestial palaces (*vimāna*).

2. He shall behold the river, the well-adorned circular enclosure (*maṇḍalavāṭa*), together with the assembly of Bodhisattvas. Those Tathāgatas shall hear from his own presence the introduction to the light of the Dharma and the great discourse on the Dharma. [The deity] displays a celestial palace (*vimāna*) with forms and ornaments like those of the noble Avalokiteśvara; having bound it around his neck, he enters all the great palaces (*vilabhavana*). Everywhere he shall become a victorious lord, a universal monarch (*cakravartin*). Sixty-four thousand doors of the great palaces stand wide open. One should bind [the mantra] upon the right arm—

3. He becomes invisible. Among all those who possess the power of invisibility, numbering as many as the sands of hundreds of thousands of millions of Ganges rivers, he shall become the sovereign king of invisibility. If one binds the left arm, all yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, and so forth, become invisible; all their abodes remain with their doors wide open. If one binds the waist, all hidden treasures emerge. If one places the knee and binds it to the right side of the thighs, [all] forest caves, celestial palaces, and abodes...
