The gates do not remain closed; all substances and medicinal herbs present themselves before him in their own forms; and all remain under his control. One should bind the feet and shanks. First, there arises a great force and speed of the wind-element; one travels ten thousand *yojanas* in the time of a single atom, and returns again within a single night and day. By the power and vigor of the great wind-velocity, one traverses the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system.

Furthermore, he returns again, and no one causes him any harm; he obtains success in accomplishing his tasks everywhere. If he binds [the mantra] to the soles of his feet, he obtains the accomplishment of the Great Pātāla (underworld). All the gates to the openings of the Pātālas will be opened for him. He may enter and exit there at his own will. If he takes it into his mouth and recites a thousand verses day after day, as soon as it is swallowed, it will become a mass like the great ocean.

6. By causing [the mantra] to proceed upon the tip of the tongue, one whose tongue becomes as tender as a lotus or water-lily will become a possessor of great learning (*mahāśrutadhārī*). If one should stroke with the hand and touch someone, that person will become a servant or slave. Men, women, boys, girls, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas—all shall remain under one's control, crying out, "I am a servant! This is the ritual procedure for the jewel (*maṇisādhanavidhi*). Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Noble Avalokiteśvara, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, I have..."

7. The Great Ritual Procedure for the Accomplishment (*mahāsādhanavidhi*) named *Amoghasiddhipravarakalaśa*. Just as the power of the *Amoghapāśahṛdayacintāmaṇidhāraṇī* is witnessed, so too, O Blessed One, shall this ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the power of Mahākāla and the means for accomplishing inconceivable transformations bring about success. It will serve for the happiness and welfare of the *vidyādharas* and for the accomplishment of reality (*tattva*). Then, one should prepare a golden vessel, or one of silver, or even of copper, or made of clay, of excellent proportions.

1. One should paint the head and neck with vermilion pigments and lotus petals, making them circular in proportion, smooth, well-proportioned in the sides, beautiful in form, well-purified, and complete in every aspect. On the neck, one hundred and eight filaments should be made, and they should be painted with petals accompanied by mantras. One should paint the Noble Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa facing east; on the south, the Eight Fears; on the north, the Mind-made [Bodhisattva]; and on the west, the Comforter—all adorned with every ornament.

2. One should depict [the deity] adorned with the sun, seated upon a lotus petal in the paryaṅka posture. The lords Īśvara, Maheśvara, Brahmā, the hosts of ṛṣis, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Vāsava, Śakra, Vajradhara, and other groups of deities should be painted. Agni, Vāyu, Sūrya, Soma, the goddesses Tārā, Bhṛkuṭī, and Śvetā, the Bhūtas, Gaṇapati, Kumāra, and the four Great Kings, as well as Rudra and Viṣṇu, should be depicted. Then, a lotus mandala with petals on all sides should be made, and a flask variegated with various colors should be fashioned; all the ornaments should be painted in gold, and musk—

3. With various jewels, each having its portion diminished, one should then construct a lotus throne made of *devadāru* wood, circular in its proportions. Upon that, a water-pot (*kalaśa*) should be placed; that pot should be filled with white mustard seeds, adorned with all ornaments, and bound with a pale-white silk cloth. On top of the mustard seeds, one should place musk, camphor, *gorocana*, and realgar. The head of the jar should be covered with a red cloth.

4. One should stand with seven pieces of precious gems. Then the vidyādhara must be pure and wear clean garments. A mandala measuring four cubits should be made; it should be one cubit high. It should be composed of clay and cow dung, well-prepared and well-praised, cleaned, and divided into four equal square sections. Then, upon that mandala, one should smear it all over with all kinds of perfumes, [measuring] one cubit all around the center of the middle mandala.

5. A square mandala should be made with white rice-porridge. One should worship a lotus with saffron and draw it with thirty-two petals; one should place a flask there in the center of that lotus. Within the central mandala, there should be various forms and banners. There should be various fragrant leaves and various ointments all around. There should be various vessels for the *argha* offering, beautifully adorned with full jars, and many kinds of incense-filled censers and various flowers should be placed [there].

6. Having placed garlands all around, one should draw the well-proportioned four gates and the symbols of the auspicious Āryā-Lokeśvarī. On the perimeter of the outer maṇḍala, one should paint a garland of lotuses all around; it should have four well-proportioned gates, and one should draw the symbols of the confident Āryā-Lokeśvarī. Having placed arrows and banners all around, one should encircle it with thread of five colors. Various flavors and various kinds of foods should be arranged—three white items as they are available—and various fruits should be set out, along with varieties of edible offerings.

7. Likewise, having scattered various flowers and garlands and so forth all around, and having placed incense burners and full jars all around; having placed four ladles and likewise four fragrant pots; having placed four sacrificial pits (*kuṇḍa*) and eight shallow bowls (*śarāva*) filled with offerings of various flavors; and likewise many kinds of white [foods]; one should offer lamps filled with clarified butter (*ghṛta*). One should scatter sixty-one times: parched grain (*lāja*), mustard seeds, liquor, meat, onions, and *gṛñjanaka* garlic.

One should avoid unrighteousness, as well as bad food and bad drink; one should avoid those who are difficult to cross over. Being pure, the virtuous ones [should wear] pure garments on the full moon day. Having performed the rite of protection for oneself in that same way, [one should perform] the binding of the topknot (*śikhābandha*), the binding of the directions (*diśābandha*), and likewise the reality of the mandala (*maṇḍalatatva*). For the sake of happiness, there is protection for oneself and likewise protection for others. Incensing with *guggulu*, mustard seeds, clarified butter, sandalwood, *agaru*, *turuṣka*, and *kunduru*—this is declared to be the supreme incense for the accomplishment of the flask (*kalaśīsādhana*). Having fasted for five nights, one should perform the supreme accomplishment of the mantra.

2. At the three junctions of the day, there shall be worship of the water-pot (*kalaśa*) and likewise worship of the Buddha, performed without conversation. Facing the mandala, seated in the cross-legged posture (*paryaṅka*), one should hold the water-pot in the right hand. One should consecrate [the disciple] with water and white mustard seeds while reciting the *Krodharāja* mantra one thousand and eight times. The *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* should be recited ten thousand times. With one-pointed attention and through the cultivation of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), one should generate compassion for all sentient beings; one should cultivate the mental focus on the Buddha and perform the recitation.

3. *Vyaḥ*. Then, during the final watch of the full fifteenth day, at dawn during the time of twilight, there occurs a great earthquake in the golden jar (*hiraṇyakalaśa*). A great sound is heard, and cries of "Well done! are heard. And that Great Kāla [image] blazes forth; rays of light of various colors issue from it. The Vidyādhara rejoices; he becomes stainless, pure, and immaculate. His complexion becomes perfectly pure, white, and as delicate as a lotus or a water lily. And that image in the jar—its own...

4. Rays of light, resembling his own body, issue forth. Then, a great and magnificent worship of the noble Avalokiteśvara must be performed by the vidyādhara. This is the successful accomplishment of the flask for the vidyādhara. Then, the vidyādhara, having empowered mustard seeds and scented water with the King of Wrath (Krodharāja) mantra twenty-one times, should consecrate the flask. Immediately upon its consecration, a sound issues from that flask: "Excellent, excellent, O Great—"

5. "O Vidyādhara, O Siddha, just as the Bhadrakalaśī and the Bhadraghaṭa are [efficacious], so too is this Great Cintāmaṇi Bhadrakalaśa of the Amoghapāśahṛdaya. May you enjoy its success according to your desire and according to what is in your mind; may all your prayers be fulfilled. Thereafter, that great celestial palace (mahāvimāna) of the Bhadrakalaśa should be honored, maintained, and worshipped. Whether it be a well-cultivated [human] aspiration or a noble (ārya) one, it will be accomplished according to one's heart's desire and all wishes.

6. Poetry, drama, mathematics, grammar, ritual manuals, discourse on mantras, the cultivation of forests, the cultivation of caves, elixirs, collyrium, metallurgy, the Vedic mantras and sūtras, songs, the Dharma and Vinaya—all these appear. For example: food, drink, clothing, ornaments, decorations, silver, gold, precious metals, pearls, beads, sapphires, emeralds, karketana stones, crystal, musāragalva, vaidūrya, blue gems, great blue gems, flowers, fruits, vehicles, garments, beds, and seats.

7. A celestial palace suitable for reliance, enjoyment, play, vastness, and sovereignty appears to the mind through mere thought. The magical net, the palace of forms, the universal form, the emanation of a Buddha, the emanation of a Bodhisattva, the emanation of a Vajradhara, the palaces of nāgas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, gandharvas, and mahoragas, and the palaces of yakṣas, rākṣasas, and lords of bhūtas—all these appear through mere thought. Excessive rain, drought, untimely rain, cold, and wind—[all these likewise appear].

1. It reveals everything, whether it be a female eater, or the warding off of water; it reveals the sight of an army, the sight of battle and combat, or the sight of a celestial palace (*vimāna*) and its splendor. In this way, all such things that are thought of or prayed for are accomplished. Wealth, grain, fruits, flowers, and celestial palaces appear; whatever one thinks of, that is fulfilled. Furthermore, taking *kastūrikā* (musk), mixing it with *gorocana* (bovine gallstone) and camphor, making a pill with the milk of the *arka* plant, and rubbing it with the milk of a tawny cow (*kapila*), one should apply a mark (*tilaka*) on the forehead.

2. One travels through the sky; one’s retinue consists of ten thousand koṭis of vidyādharas. Having made a *tilaka* on the heart, one becomes invisible. All yakṣas, rākṣasas, and bhūtas will appear before one. If one touches the tip of the tongue [with it], one recites three thousand [verses] day after day. If it is swallowed, one will have a lifespan of ten thousand years. If consumed with milk-rice (*pāyasa*), one becomes a great ocean-like accumulation of fame. It should be eaten together with the milk of the *arkka* plant; [it grants] all vidyās—

He will become a universal monarch (cakravartin). He will become the presiding authority over all ritual procedures, mantras, mandalas, and mudrās. Having applied a tilaka at the navel and entered a great river, he finds a firm footing and crosses to the other shore; he even crosses the ocean to the other shore. Having applied a tilaka on the crown of the head, one should enter into battles and conflicts, and he will conquer a fourfold army. If one eats it together with clarified butter, one gains the strength of a thousand great elephants. With one hand, [he can seize] a nāga—

4. It exists and it moves; one hurls it through the air and catches it again. By anointing this pill with one's hand, one becomes a warrior of a thousand. If one buries this pill in a temple of the gods, all the deities remain under one's control. From time to time, they pour down showers of rain; they sustain the clouds against all winds and cold. If one buries it at the king's gate, the king, together with his harem and retinue, along with his assembly of ministers, counselors, soldiers, and chaplains, comes under one's control.

5. [If one] places it at the door of the monastery, all the monks will dwell in comfort and ease; they will always dwell with a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*). If one places it within the Noble Saṅgha at the end of the row of elders, all the monks will obtain whatever food, drink, and meals they desire. Having placed it inside the alms-bowl, one should go for alms and enter the great city. One will effortlessly obtain alms-food of various flavors, the most excellent tastes, and many diverse kinds. Together with—

6. One should bury [the pills] at the site of a *caitya*, and the *caitya* is to be worshipped. As long as the pills remain at the site of the *caitya*, for that long great worship shall be performed day by day before the eight great *caityas*. One should bury them at the site of Noble Avalokiteśvara, at the feet of Noble Avalokiteśvara. Worship of Noble Avalokiteśvara is to be performed; the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* is to be recited one hundred and eight times day by day, and great worship of Noble Avalokiteśvara is to be conducted.

7. It functions as follows: if one remains keeping the pill in reserve, and buries it on a royal highway, all thieves, rogues, robbers, humans, non-humans, and fierce wild beasts become bound; they flee in every direction and intermediate point. If one buries it on a mountain peak, all substances and medicinal herbs blaze forth. As far as the peak is visible in every direction, so many women, men, boys, girls, cattle, sheep, buffaloes, horses, and so forth, shall become entirely free from fear for sixteen [years].

1. They shall be completely liberated from the fears of the great hells; they shall be liberated from the eight great fears; they shall be liberated from all diseases. A great [protection] extending for a hundred *yojanas* in every direction shall come to pass, and they shall be free from all diseases. It should be worn tied around the neck. They shall have the desire to behold the noble Avalokiteśvara; he shall always keep them in his mindful regard. If one buries it in a storehouse, there will be a great increase of grain. If one buries it at the entrance to a drinking hall, there will be a great increase of drink.

2. ...will [be accomplished]. If one buries it in the middle of a field, great crops will be produced. If one buries it at the entrance of a mountain cave, all the entrances to caves will remain open. If one smears it on the entrances to subterranean holes, all the entrances to holes will remain open. The sites of caves should be smeared; then all juices will flow forth. If one buries it in the middle of a forest, all the forest deities will appear before one in their own forms. Whatever task they desire to accomplish, they will perform. If one buries it in the middle of a lotus pond, a great [result]— (Note: The source text appears to be a fragment of a ritual manual (*kalpa*); the ellipsis indicates the sentence is incomplete.)

3. [The flowers] will appear in abundance; they will bloom perpetually; and a divine fragrance will always be emitted. One should place it at a high pitch. As many as are seen—whether women, men, boys, or girls—they all become well-protected. A boundary is established for a hundred *yojanas* in all directions throughout the ten quarters against all fears. All diseases are pacified. All sins, all enemies, all seizing spirits (*graha*), and all calamities will be quelled. All foreign...

4. [Those who are afflicted] will be pacified; they will be liberated from all calamities. If one sprinkles [the enemy] in the midst of a battle or conflict with mustard seeds mixed [with this], in that great battle or conflict, they will obtain great mutual affection. For one whose limbs are parched by a great disease, whose life is exhausted, and who is touched by a great obstacle, one should bathe them with a jar of scented water mixed with pills, reciting the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* one hundred and eight times. Worship of Noble Avalokiteśvara should be performed. Simultaneously with the bathing—

5. By means of this *pitāmātṛkā*, one is completely liberated from all ailments and all diseases; one is completely liberated from all sins and all previous obscurations (*āvaraṇa*). Furthermore, for one whose lifespan has been exhausted, life is restored again, and a body of divine form appears. Free from stains, stinginess, and envy, they become supreme. They will perform hundreds of thousands of other deeds, and by their own intelligence, these should be applied everywhere; they become possessed of all unhindered activities. He is the sovereign king over all the abodes of the *vilas*.

He shall open [the gates of liberation]. His lifespan shall be twelve thousand kalpas. Having passed away, he will be born by transformation within lotuses in the world-realm of Sukhāvatī, adorned with every ornament. His body will be embellished with jewels, gold, silver, diamond, lapis lazuli, ruby, emerald, sapphire, pearl, and coral. He will be born with hair like curled bees and ears, with eyes resembling deep blue utpala flowers, and with a complexion the color of gold. His speech will be smooth, sweet, and gentle. [The Buddha Amitābha] will extend his hand upward toward him.

7. He holds [it]; with his hand, the palm of which is like a lotus, he bestows consolation. He will become a supreme granter of boons; he will prophesy the noble Amitābha as the Buddha Amoghavilokita established upon a lotus. Then, from that mustard seed, there appear the bodily relics of hundreds of thousands of millions of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—Buddhas, Blessed Ones. He attains effortless mastery over various kinds of relic colors and forms. Together with the relics—

8. One should bury [the pills] at the site of a *caitya*, and the *caitya* is to be worshipped. As long as the pills remain at the site of the *caitya*, so long shall great worship be performed day by day for the eight great *caityas*. One should bury them at the site of Noble Avalokiteśvara, at the feet of Noble Avalokiteśvara. Worship of Noble Avalokiteśvara is to be performed; the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* is to be recited one hundred and eight times day by day, and the great worship of Noble Avalokiteśvara is to be carried out.

9. It functions as follows: if one remains having kept a pill in reserve, and buries it on a royal highway, all thieves, rogues, robbers, humans, non-humans, and fierce wild beasts become bound; they flee in every direction and intermediate quarter. If one buries it on a mountain peak, all substances and medicinal herbs blaze forth. As far as the peak is visible in every direction, so many women, men, boys, girls, cattle, sheep, buffaloes, horses, and so forth, become entirely free from fear for sixteen years.

1. They are completely liberated from the fears of the great hells; they become free from the eight great fears; they become free from all diseases. A great [protection] extending for a hundred *yojanas* in every direction shall arise, and they shall be devoid of all maladies. It should be worn tied around the neck. There will be a desire to behold the noble Avalokiteśvara; he will be constantly mindful [of them]. If one buries it in a storehouse, there will be a great increase of grain. If one buries it at the entrance to the drinking hall, there will be a great increase of drink.

2. ...will [be accomplished]. If one buries [it] in the middle of a field, great crops will be produced. If one buries it at the entrance of a mountain cleft, all the entrances to clefts will remain open. If one smears [it] on the entrances to holes, all the entrances to holes will remain open. The places of the clefts should be smeared; all essences (rasas) will flow forth. If one buries it in a forest cleft, all the forest deities will appear in their own forms and stand before one. Whatever task they desire to accomplish, they will perform. If one buries it in the middle of a lotus pond, a great [result]—

3. [The flowers] will appear in abundance; they will bloom perpetually; and a divine fragrance will always be emitted. One should place it at a high pitch. As many as are seen—whether men, women, boys, or girls—they shall be placed under great protection. A boundary-binding is established for a hundred *yojanas* in all directions throughout the ten quarters against all fears. All diseases will be pacified. All sins, all enemies, all seizing spirits (*graha*), and all calamities will be stilled. All adversaries...

4. They will be pacified; they will perish from all calamities. If one sprinkles [the enemy] in the midst of battle and conflict with [water] mixed with mustard seeds, they will attain great mutual affection even in the midst of a great war. One who is afflicted by a great disease, whose limbs are withered and whose life is exhausted, or who is touched by a great obstacle—such a person should be bathed with this jar of scented water mixed with pills, having been consecrated one hundred and eight times with the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* mantra. Worship of the noble Avalokiteśvara must be performed. Together with the bath—

5. By [reciting] this *pitāmātrā*, one is completely liberated from all afflictions and all diseases; one is completely liberated from all evils and all previous obscurations. Furthermore, for one whose lifespan has been exhausted, life is restored once more, and a body of divine form appears. Free from stains, stinginess, and envy, they become supreme. They shall perform hundreds of thousands of other deeds, and by their own intelligence, these should be applied everywhere; they become possessed of all unimpeded activities. They become lords and kings over all the celestial abodes.

He will attain liberation. His lifespan will be twelve thousand kalpas. Having passed away, he will be born by spontaneous transformation (*upapāduka*) within lotuses in the world-realm of Sukhāvatī. He will be adorned with every ornament; his body will be embellished with jewels, gold, silver, diamond, lapis lazuli, ruby, emerald, sapphire, pearl, and coral. He will be born with hair as curled as bees, eyes resembling deep blue *indīvara* lotuses, and a complexion the color of gold. His speech will be smooth, sweet, and gentle. [The Buddha Amitābha] will extend his hand toward him as he lies on his back.

7. He holds [it]; with his hand, the palm of which is like a lotus, he bestows comfort. He will become a supreme granter of boons in the future; he will prophesy the noble Amitābha as the Buddha Amoghavilokita established upon a lotus. Then, from that mustard seed, there appear the bodily relics of hundreds of thousands of millions of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—Buddhas, Blessed Ones. They possess various kinds of elemental colors and diverse forms and hues, resembling seven great precious jewels.

Furthermore, each individual relic-body shines forth like the sun; from all sides in the ten directions, rays of light issue forth. It displays various miracles of supernatural power and transformations, manifesting its own body one by one. By the mere sight of these relic-bodies, one shall become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; one must not entertain thoughts of doubt or otherwise. Lest all the Tathāgatas be distressed by this on your account, [you should act] otherwise through your own wisdom.

2. While reciting [the mantra], one should make a formal vow (*praṇidhi*) in the presence of the relics with a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*). Having contemplated one's intention, one should perform worship. Merely by the thought, everything is accomplished in an instant. Just as these are the bodily relics enshrined within the reliquary (*dhātugarbha*), so too should this auspicious vase (*bhadrakalaśa*) be regarded. The miraculous power (*ṛddhivikurvvaṇa*) of both is seen to be equal. One should not give rise to doubt or uncertainty in this regard. This is the infallible ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the vase.
Amoghapāśakalparāja – Part V 66a (P.119b6, D.123b2) 2. Then the Blessed One—

Then the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, extending his golden-colored arm and stroking the head of the noble Avalokiteśvara, said: "Excellent, excellent, Great Being! This is most wonderful. Thus is the supreme accomplishment of the rite, the attainment through the recitation of the unsurpassed and great unfailing vase, bestowed for the sake of the welfare and happiness of the world of the four castes in Jambudvīpa, and for the benefit of the Vidyādharas."

The method for the praised means of accomplishment is the unsurpassed self-consecration (*svādhiṣṭhāna*). It is the unsurpassed awakening of the Buddha through the great and unfailing miraculous transformations (*mahāmoghavikurvvaṇa*) that have been consecrated, according to the reality of accomplishing supreme siddhi. It is the turning of the wheel of Dharma at the great seat of awakening (*mahābodhimaṇḍa*), the consecration of the Great Tathāgata once he has been consecrated. For the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, I entrust to you, O Avalokiteśvara, this great consolation established throughout the entire world for all beings.

5. For the fulfillment of vows, there shall be supreme accomplishment and the success of recitation and practice; he will become one who is bound to others, a constant bestower of boons, and a constant protector. Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, with a heart of supreme joy and a smiling countenance, bowed with palms joined toward where the Blessed One was, prostrated his head at the feet of the Blessed One, and addressed the Blessed One as follows: "This one has been favored."

6. "O Blessed One, all sentient beings in the ten directions—indeed, all beings within the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system, down to every living creature, beast, and bird—are embraced by me with a mind of great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) for the sake of liberating them from all suffering and establishing them on the path to Great Enlightenment (*mahābodhi*). Therefore, O Blessed One, I shall bring about their liberation as the foremost among them all. O Blessed One, for all holders of vidyā-mantras (*vidyādhara*), the accomplishments of reality (*tattvasiddhi*) arise through my recollection; thus, O Blessed One, I am always looking upon them, always mindful of them, and always their protector. However, O Blessed One, for those who seek excellence and are devoted to the recitation, practice, touch, and worship of this *Amoghapāśahṛdayakalpa*, I, O Blessed One, shall protect them like a son of my own body and sustain them with a portion of myself. In this very way, O Blessed One, all sentient beings are embraced by me with great compassion for the sake of their liberation and the granting of boons."
66b (P. omitted; D.

124a5) 1. For the sake of conflict, for the sake of attending to all desires, O Blessed One, I do not remain indifferent, nor, O Blessed One, do I reach satiety, for the sake of liberating sentient beings, for the sake of granting boons, for the sake of protection, and for the sake of establishing all in the supreme path to enlightenment. It is a distinction, O Blessed One, if one is engaged in the recitation, accomplishment, mandala, and mudrās of this Great King of Kalpas, or if one maintains it, recites it, worships it, masters it, and applies correct mental attention (*yonisomanasikāra*).

2. O Rāma, he who contemplates [this] or hears it—even if the sound merely falls into the hollow of his ear—I, Blessed One, shall be constantly and at all times ever bound to him. I shall bestow the supreme of all accomplishments, both mundane and supramundane; the various and manifold divine great-kalpa sādhanas; and I shall establish him in the state of non-retrogression. Even for those born as animals, such as deer or birds, by the mere falling of the sound into the hollow of their ears, they shall attain non-retrogression.

3. "I shall cause them to enter the station of the Ṛttikas; how much more so, Blessed One, those whose minds are purified, who are firmly established in the four immeasurables—loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity—and who practice, recite, maintain, and read this Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya, as well as the Maṇḍala-mudrā-mahākalparāja; who remember the junctions pertaining to the three stations; and who experience various days and nights—is it not the case, Blessed One, that their bodies become non-human? Are they human—"

"O Blessed One, it should be known that this putrid body is a divine body; O Blessed One, I carry it constantly and perpetually upon my shoulder, and I bear it upon my head. Because, O Blessed One, this is a divine body, O Blessed One, it should be known as a superhuman body. Because, O Blessed One, this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* dwells within the mind of the human self-body, by that power, O Great Amogha..."

5. By the power of the heart-essence (*hṛdaya*), this putrid human body is transformed into a divine body; it should be known as a divine body. It should be known as the body of the Lord of the World (*lokeśvara*); it should be known as a body that is a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇiratna*). It should be known as a body that is the great ocean-circle treasury of the Tathāgata; it should be known as a body that is the unfailing heart-essence. It should be known as a body free from the stains of stinginess and envy, and devoid of all evil obscurations.

6. He should be known as having a body pure and stainless through the purification of the senses (*indriya-viśuddhi*). He should be known as one worthy of worship, honor, and salutation by all the gods, *nāgas*, *yakṣas*, *gandharvas*, *asuras*, *garuḍas*, *kinnaras*, *mahoragas*, humans, and non-humans. He should be known as having a body protected by the deities in the abode of the Thirty-three (*trāyastriṃśa*). He should be known as having a body endowed with roots of merit planted under seventy-two hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* of *Gaṅgā* river-sands of *tathāgatas*. Amitāyu—

7. Furthermore, his body should be known as follows: it should be known as a body that provides consolation to all bodhisattvas; it should be known as a body empowered by Vajrapāṇi’s vajra; it should be known as a body equal to the womb of the ocean’s deep waters; it should be known as a body like Mount Meru; it becomes like a great maṇi-jewel in its purity, like the great sky; it should be known as a body whose divine form is equal to the womb of the divine elements. Thus—67a (P. omitted, D.125a6)

1. [It is endowed with] majesty and great power. Furthermore, one becomes empowered and prophesied by all the Tathāgatas, and one possesses a great body. Yet, Blessed One, sentient beings are difficult to discipline, difficult to awaken, difficult to fathom, lacking in faith, envious, stingy, possessed of sinful obscurations, defiled, and full of impurity; they are also abundant in anger and abuse. Therefore, Blessed One, it is due to the continuity of their own faults that sentient beings do not succeed, and it is not my fault, Blessed One. Moreover, Blessed One, through the mere recollection of this *hṛdaya*—its reading, study, and recitation—...

2. "I shall attend to them with measure; I shall grant them my vision; I shall urge them on again and again. Yet, O Blessed One, those beings do not see me; they do not think of me, nor do they meditate upon me; nor do they apply their attention for even a moment, an instant, or a brief duration. For these beings have corrupt intentions and corrupt minds, their very bodies being filled with their own faults. However, O Blessed One, by the mere act of thinking of me, remembering me, or looking toward me, I stand before them; I abide in their sight, conversation, discourse, and company."

3. ...I shall appear. Yet those beings, nor the vidyādharas, will perceive even as much as a mere thought-conception; they will not even meditate upon [my] homage. That is to say, [they will see me] in the guise of a śramaṇa—merely wearing the tonsured appearance and saffron robes—or in the guise of a brāhmaṇa or kṣatriya, or in the guise of a great merchant, a caravan leader, a porter, or the Blessed One. Or [in the guise of] a king’s minister, a friend, a relative, a kinsman, a maternal uncle, a preceptor, a teacher, a fellow-student, a son, a daughter, a mother, a father, or a sister.

4. However, one must observe the wise person who dwells with perfected resolve through their physical form, complexion, marks, shape, speech, conversation, words, syllables, and the flow of their composition. Again and again, by how they engage in dialogue, one should know them; thus they appear as a noble being (*āryasattva*). They look at me, and I approach them with a desire to see them. By this method, I shall grant a very clear vision to all those whose minds [are longing].

5. "I shall fulfill this. In the midst of the great multitude, I shall engage in the discourse and conversation of buying and selling. In the midst of assemblies, I shall practice the exposition of treatises, poetry, the Vedas, mantras, *yukti*, grammar, sūtras, dramas, songs, and music (*gāndharva*). Regarding the topic of awakening, I shall provide instruction on logic (*naya*), discipline (*vinaya*), and the Mahāyāna *adharmas*. To the brahmins, I shall teach the Purāṇas, the Vedas, the fire-sacrifice (*agnihotra*), the *Mahābhārata*, and the *Rāmāyaṇa*. [To] the practitioners of mantras..."

6. One should know by what means I appear visibly before one; that is, when I give instruction on mantra-recitation, maṇḍalas, mudrās, ritual manuals (kalpa), dhāraṇīs, recitations, fire-offerings (homa), rites of pacification (śāntika), prosperity (pauṣṭika), and malevolent magic (abhicāruka), and so forth. It should be known through three signs: [first,] there is sweet speech; [second,] there is a smooth, tender voice with clearly articulated syllables and distinctions; and [third,] there is clear speech. He is distinguished as a superior debater in all matters. From his mouth, he exhales a fragrance like that of blue lotuses and *kapūra*. And his body—

And the scent of stūrika is perfumed; even one of loathsome form may blaze with exceeding splendor. By that *vidyādhara*, or by anyone else among the four castes of the world, he should be recognized as this Noble Avalokiteśvara. There is no doubt here, nor should any hesitation or uncertainty be produced. Even in dreams and during the four transitions [of consciousness], I shall grant visions in various forms, colors, and shapes; I shall bestow all the excellent objects of desire. Without effort, there will be a perfection of all requisites.

I shall bring to fulfillment those things that are to be accomplished; nor shall I ever cause the Blessed One to change his mind, nor shall I abandon [the task], nor shall I neglect it by withholding the granting of the boon. O Blessed One, setting aside the non-deception [of my vow], I do not perceive any other means for its success, nor will the deities provide protection or guardianship for him. Therefore, O Blessed One, we shall become the protectors, the ultimate resort, and the refuge for that suffering being; I shall certainly not be merciless, but shall surely deliver him.

"No, Blessed One! With a mind embraced by compassion, I shall deliver all sentient beings; I shall sustain them. I will certainly plant the seed of awakening within every sentient being. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and all the Tathāgatas in the ten directions, gave their approval to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara: "Excellent, excellent, Mahāsattva! You are supremely compassionate, O Pure Being, since for the sake of all sentient beings..."

3. Embraced by great compassion, [he shall enter] the great prison of the vast saṃsāra, which is exceedingly difficult to escape due to its being overwhelmed by [the afflictions of] cold, heat, hunger, thirst, and exhaustion; and it is filled with many sufferings arising from fear, terror, agitation, distress, and pain. Because of that, for such a being, the sound of the grasping and hearing of this *Amogharājahṛdayamaṇḍalamudrāpaṭalamahākalparāja* will fall upon the cavity of his ear. By that, his great and immense sufferings—

4. One is completely liberated from all evil obstructions; one becomes peaceful from all fears. Having been uplifted from the terrors of the great hells, one shall be fully released. All karmic obstructions that lead to the experience of suffering in the worldly and supramundane miserable states and hells go to complete exhaustion and total termination. One becomes empowered by all the Tathāgatas, taken into the care of all the Tathāgatas, and receives the prophecy of enlightenment from all the Tathāgatas. By the seven [vows]...

5. By merely hearing [this], that being is considered "crossed over"; they are comforted by the Tathāgata through great accumulations of merit. There will be the fulfillment of the seed of awakening—how much more so, O Avalokiteśvara, for those beings who hear, recite, uphold, read, worship, write, or cause to be written this Noble Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa Heart Sūtra, together with its maṇḍala, mudrās, chapters, and rituals, in their entirety; and who perform a great worship of it?

6. You should know that such a being is irreversible; no doubt or uncertainty should be raised in this regard. How much more so for one who holds in hand the pill, the collyrium, and the incense! That great, pure being will be embraced by all the Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions, and he or she will have pleased all the Tathāgatas. And whichever son of good family or daughter of good family—whether monk, nun, layman, or laywoman—Padmapāṇi, [who...]

7. Whoever shall worship, recite, offer, and consecrate this Heart-mantra of the Wrathful Seal of the Amoghapāśahṛdaya according to the sevenfold fasting rite, that person should be known as having seen the body of the Tathāgata in this very life. The true nature of the Tathāgata will be directly perceived; the treasury of the Tathāgata will come into one’s own hands. One must be free from doubt and devoid of all enmity and pride. Embraced by great compassion, [he shall act] for the sake of all sentient beings.

1. One should remain in my presence and perform the recitation. Those who shall proclaim the Amogha-mahāmaṇḍala and behold its vision, and who behold this great cloth-painting (mahāduṣyapaṭa), for them all the Buddha-fields of all the Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, become entered. He becomes one who has entered the heart of the Great Samaya, the secret of all the Tathāgatas. All the bodies of all the Tathāgatas become seen by him. By means of this [mantra] empowered by the King of Wrath, all the Tathāgatas—

2. He becomes consecrated. Thus he will be endowed with great benefits, praises, and a great mass of merit; he will be embraced by great roots of virtue. Such is the procedure of this Great King of Rituals (*Mahākalparāja*), which reveals great benefits, great power, and great qualities. By the mere mention of the name or the sight of this Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, this Great King of Rituals, there is a marvelous miracle in this very life, [performed by] the Tathāgata—

3. This empowerment is seen to be equal [to other practices]. One who sees this *kalparāja*, the heart-mantra of the maṇḍala, and the *dhāraṇī* of the miraculous display of the *Amogharāja*, written in a book, sees as many hundreds of thousands of millions of *tathāgatas* as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River; they are all *tathāgatas*, *arhats*, and perfectly awakened ones (*samyaksaṃbuddhas*). All these *tathāgatas* remain bound to them for their protection and consolation, standing before them to grant their vision.

4. By the mere sight of this written book, the five deeds of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya-karman*) and all previous obscurations (*pūrvāvaraṇa*) will be completely exhausted and brought to an end. In this very life (*dṛṣṭa eva dharme*), one will be endowed with many splendors, fortunes, and majesties. Upon passing away, one will be reborn through miraculous birth (*upapāduka*) within the lotuses of the *Sukhāvatī* world-system. This is the final birth for one who sees this book; when their life has ended, it will bring about the turning of a full lifespan. Free from—

5. He shall be free from diseases; he shall be free from obscurations and anger; he shall be one who has attained the great supreme accomplishment; he shall be a great accomplished master of yoga; and he shall be endowed with all qualities of prosperity. This book should be known as equal to the Tathāgata of the Dharmadhātu. Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara, having bowed with palms joined toward where the Blessed One was, spoke to the Blessed One from before him:

With a smiling face, a trembling heart, and his body blazing brilliantly, adorned with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rays of light, he addressed the Blessed One who was present before him: "Blessed One, within this great lotus mandala, there exists for me the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, the Heart-mantra of Universal Unfailing Garment and Vision. By the performance of the unfailing garment, one manifests through the illusory-like samādhi the manifestation of a thousand arms."

7. There is no manifestation of diverse forms, colors, or marks; it is not an entry through a single entry into form. For example, Īśvara, Maheśvara, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Mahāpaśupati, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, the hosts of ṛṣis, Kumāra, Sārthavāha, Vaṇij, Vidyādhara, Candra, Sūrya, and the hosts of lunar mansions and stars—all these enter into a single body. Blessed One, by the mere sight of him, all of them [enter] the samaya-mudrā of the Great Maṇḍala of Amoghapāśa.

They shall become accomplished through the practice of the Mahākalpa; they shall enter into the perfected samaya. I shall bestow the samaya of the Mahāmogha-mantra-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī for the sake of easily accomplishing the welfare of all sentient beings. In the presence of the Blessed One, I shall manifest myself for the supreme accomplishment of the recitation-practice of the Vidyādharas and for the fulfillment of all their needs. Oṃ! Homage to the Tathāgatas of the three times! Oṃ Amoghapadmapāśa-krodha, draw them forth! Cause them to enter! Great Lord of Beasts (Mahāpaśupati) — [198]

2. Wearing the guises of Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Brahmā: *Amoghahṛdayapadmakulasamayāya hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. As soon as this heart-mantra-dhāraṇī-seal was spoken, in that great assembly-circle, the earth together with its mountains, forests, and groves shook in six ways, and a great rain of flowers began to fall. The gods, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas began to let out a great roar of "kiliki-li. Immediately upon being spoken, Amoghapāśa—

3. All the wicked yakṣas, rākṣasas, and evil vināyakas—the Śakalparājā-hṛdaya [mantra] causes them to fall face-down, to be scorched, to be pierced, and to be shaken; the vighnas and vināyakas with faces of wrath flee in the ten directions. Crying out and running, they shrink back in agitation. For here the bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, will worship the noble Avalokiteśvara with various divine, variegated ornaments, garments, and fine cloths. Following the concealment of the Dharma—

They shall offer worship with various divine flowers and perform worship with divine fragrant offerings. Then the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, taking various flowers, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, banners, and flags, as well as divine garments, ornaments, and decorations, approached the place where the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara was; having approached, [they paid homage to] the Bodhisattva Āryāvalokiteśvara.

5. They shall perform a great, magnificent worship for this Great Being, the Tathāgata in person. The worship of the Blessed One, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, draws forth [the result]: this Great Pure Being is most difficult to encounter. He is the one who spoke this *Amogharājahṛdaya*, the King of Ritual Manuals for the Liberation Maṇḍala, and the Noble *Amoghapāśa-Avalokiteśvara-hṛdaya*. Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni—

6. He spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara: “Speak, O Pure Being, the very extensive ritual. The noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara then spoke this very extensive *Amoghavikurvitā* Dhāraṇī. If a practitioner of spells (*vidyādhara*) recites this *Amoghavikurvitā* Dhāraṇī one thousand and eight times every day, then by means of the Heart of the King Amogha, through the illusion-like meditative absorption (*māyopama-samādhi*), all that—the manifestation of various forms, the manifestation of illusions, and the miraculous transformations of the meditative absorption—is accomplished. They become graced; they enter everywhere; they attain the state of the pledge (*samaya*) everywhere; they enter everywhere into the rituals of the seals (*mudrā*), mandalas, and mantras; they stand at the pinnacle of the banner of the miraculous transformations of meditative absorption everywhere; they follow and enter the secret of all the Tathāgatas; they become established in the unfailing accomplishment of the complete sciences (*vidyā-siddhi*); and they become endowed with unfailing miraculous power. Unfailing...

69a. He possesses a form, color, marks, and configuration that are not in vain; he is endowed with the proclamation of unfailing qualities; he is endowed with unfailing roots of merit; he is embraced by the unfailing prophecy of the Tathāgata; he has planted roots of merit through the unfailing great mass of merit of the Tathāgata; he is endowed with the unfailing empowerment in the presence of the vision of the Tathāgata; he has entered the unfailing family of the Tathāgata; [he is endowed with the unfailing Vajra family...]

2. He has entered into the [mandala]; he is empowered by the pledge of the Amoghapadma family; he is favored by the pledge of the Amoghamani family; he is favored by the pledge of the Amogharāja family; he is empowered by the empowerment of the miraculous manifestations of the mandalas of all the Tathāgatas; he is empowered by being established under the influence of the Amoghacakravartin family; he is consecrated with the consecration of the Amogha-vidyā; he is consecrated with the consecration of all the Tathāgatas.

3. ...he becomes established in the mantra practice of the chapter on the Unfailing Great Seal (*amoghamahāmudrāpaṭala*). He becomes empowered by the approach to the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*) of all unfailing Tathāgatas. He becomes one who unfailingly turns the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas. He becomes one who unfailingly beats the drum of Dharma; he becomes one who unfailingly fills the conch of Dharma. He becomes one who unfailingly fulfills the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*). [He becomes one who unfailingly [fulfills] all Tathāgatas...]

4. He becomes the womb of the *dharmadhātu*. He becomes endowed with the womb of the profound *dharmadhātu* of unfailing hearing. He becomes endowed with the unfailing supramundane noble eightfold path of all Tathāgatas. He attains the accomplishment of the great ritual manual (*mahākalpa*) for accomplishing worldly dharmas that is unfailing. He experiences the unfailing worldly and divine glory. He shall become one who stands at the head of all sentient beings as their supreme teacher and object of veneration.

5. ...will come to be. Thus, he will be endowed with the qualities of a great accumulation and followed by great benefits. For whomsoever this *Amogharājahṛdayakalpa*—complete with its chapters, mudrās, maṇḍalas, and the ritual procedures for the noose—is finished [and mastered], and who shall hear it, uphold it, recite it, master it, attend to it with systematic mental attention (*yoniso manasikāra*), perform it according to the rules of recitation (*jāpavidhi*), and cultivate the recollection of the Buddha (*buddhānusmṛti*), all that karma in this very life...

6. All conflict and all evil are completely purified and cast out. One becomes liberated from all diseases, from birth, old age, and death. One reaches the further shore of the vast ocean of saṃsāra. How much more so, Blessed One, for anyone who performs even greater service for the sake of sentient beings? And that person, Blessed One, should be known as irreversible; they are said to be established on the ten stages (daśabhūmi). Blessed One, whether it be a son of good family or a daughter of good family, or a monk, a nun, a layman, or a laywoman—anyone [who acts thus].

7. This *Amogharājahṛdaya*, the great king of ritual manuals (*mahākalparāja*), the seal-mandala (*mudrāmaṇḍala*) on a cloth-painting (*duṣyapaṭa*), shall be written with mental attention (*manasikāra*), with faith and reverence, and with serene confidence in the resolute intention (*adhyāśaya*) of all Tathāgatas. It shall be written by a scribe endowed with faith and reverence, with a mind purified by loving-kindness (*maitrī*), and by a scribe who provides no deficiency in materials and offers worship and honor. Having been written, it shall be for the sake of [discerning] the strength and weakness of all sentient beings; and that sentient being [who writes it] shall become irreversible (*avaivartika*).

1. This should be understood; no doubt or hesitation should be raised here. Moreover, this being is to be known as the heart-born son of all the Tathāgatas. Born from their mouth, born of the Dharma, fashioned by the Dharma, he will be sustained by the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhita*) of all the Tathāgatas and has been prophesied (*vyākṛta*) that he shall awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Thus, this King of Rituals (*kalparāja*), possessing such great supernatural power (*maharddhika*), should be understood as equal to the Tathāgata himself. Therefore, these great merits and benefits have been proclaimed. Henceforth, I shall explain the procedure for the ritual service (*upacāravidhi*). Amogha...

2. One should have the supreme *Ghasiddhi* painted on a cloth measuring two cubits, perfectly square on all sides, clearly defined, and well-executed. It must be painted by a painter who is pure, wears clean garments, and has hands that are soft and well-blended. [The painting should be done] with various brilliant colors, using non-sticky pigments kept in new vessels. One must avoid alcohol, meat, onions, garlic, *gṛñjanaka*, refuse, and impure food. An image of the noble Avalokiteśvara should be painted, holding the *Amoghapāśa*, with a gentle face, three eyes, and a crown of matted hair (*jaṭāmakuṭa*).

3. He should be depicted with eleven faces and thirty-two arms, adorned with all ornaments, holding various weapons in his hands, and grasping a noose. His body is the color of a pale lotus. He wears various garments. On the right face is the face of Maheśvara; on the left, the form of Nārāyaṇa. Above Maheśvara is the form of Yama; above Yama is the form of Varuṇa; above Varuṇa is the form of Kubera. Above Kubera is Kumāra with a frowning face; above Kumāra is Varuṇa with a frowning face; and above Varuṇa is the form of Maheśvara.

4. Above [him] is the Youth (Kumāra), fierce with formidable fangs; above him is Īśvara, of fierce form and with formidable fangs. Above Īśvara is Ādityamukha Maheśvara, with the moon as his face. On the matted locks of his head is the noble Amitābha, radiant with light, with his hand extended, consoling [the deity]. Between the hair on his right arm, Vāyu should be depicted. His body is half-formed. On the left side, the deity Agni should be made, with half a body, holding the previously mentioned mudrās and weapons in his hands. To the right...

5. One should depict the Noble Krodharāja, adorned with all ornaments and having a wrathful form. To his left, the Vidyārāja should be depicted, likewise adorned with all ornaments. The Krodharāja should be holding a lotus noose, and the Vidyārāja should be holding a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*) and a flower bud. He should be depicted looking up at the face of Āryāvalokiteśvara, seated upon a lotus throne, his body draped with a garland of lotuses. Below Āryāvalokiteśvara—

6. The goddess Maṇḍaladevī of Padma should be depicted as Raudrī, laughing with a loud, boisterous laugh (aṭṭaṭṭahāsinī), four-armed, adorned with all ornaments, holding a lotus, a noose, an axe, and a sword, seated in the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka); she should be placed behind the Wrathful King (Krodharāja) upon a lotus seat. Āryatārā should be depicted holding a handful of flowers with her hands and her head bowed; she is adorned with all ornaments. Behind the Knowledge-King (Vidyārāja), Mahāśveta should be depicted, adorned with all ornaments, with her hands joined in añjali and her head bowed.

7. Rāḥ. Within that [maṇḍala], the deity Maṇḍaladeva should be depicted on the right side, kneeling with his knees touching the ground and looking toward the face of Āryāvalokiteśvara, holding a flower-basket in his hand. On the four sides, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, should be painted seated in the *paryaṅka* posture. The maṇḍala shape should be divided into thirty-eight [sections]. In the upper part, sages and sons of gods should be depicted. In the four corners, the Four Great Kings [should be placed]. 70a (P. omitted; D. 131b4)

1. The goddesses Śrī, Sarasvatī, and Bhīmā-Rātri should be depicted fully armored and with their breastplates fastened, standing from the waist down on their feet. Having well-executed the work and painted it upon a perfectly prepared cloth, it should then be placed in a secret location. In a clean spot, a cow-dung mandala should be made, square on all sides. Upon that, various fragrant ointments should be applied; it should be strewn with flowers and arranged with full vases and incense burners. As for the incense, [use] sandalwood...

2. Incense made of *kunduru*, *agaru*, *turuṣka*, and *guggulu* should be burned, and water for the guest-offering (*argha*) and water for the feet (*pādya*) should be prepared. Having placed the cloth mandala (*paṭamaṇḍalaka*) facing [the practitioner], the holder of the vidyā must be pure, wearing clean garments, and having bathed well. One should worship it upon a fine cotton cloth and light sixteen lamps. Then, sitting cross-legged facing the cloth, one should perform the mudrās while reciting the *Mahāmogha-hṛdaya-mantra-dhāraṇī-samaya* ten thousand times. [Then recite] the *Amogharāja-hṛdaya* and the *Krodharāja*...

3. And one should recite [the mantra] twenty-one times during the three periods of the day. When ten thousand [recitations] are complete, a crest of light blazes upon the *vidyādhara*. On that cloth-painting (*duṣyapaṭa*), various rays of light blaze forth. By its power, at a certain time of twilight, the noble Avalokiteśvara appears before the cloth-painting in his divine form. He consoles the *vidyādhara* and speaks thus: "Speak, O *vidyādhara*, speak!"

4. "I shall grant whatever is in your mind; I shall grant all of that. The Vidyādhara should request two boons: mundane supreme accomplishment (*laukikī uttamasiddhi*) and supramundane Buddhahood (*lokottaraṃ buddhatvam*). If you request the mundane boon, he grants it all. There will be the supreme accomplishment of the practice (*paramasādhanasiddhi*) from the Great King of Ritual Manuals (*mahākalparāja*) of the Amoghapāśa-vimokṣa-maṇḍala. Just as there is accomplishment through the face-to-face practice (*sādhana*) with the noble Avalokiteśvara, so too is this—

5. One will attain the great accomplishment (*mahāsiddhi*) consisting of the supreme accomplishment of the lower and higher realms; one will possess noble accomplishments (*udārasiddhi*). There will be the accomplishment of the supreme means for all worldly activities. It grants all other desired boons, such as: mantra-accomplishment, magical illusions (*indrajāla*), nets of light (*prabhājāla*), the manifestation of divine forms, invisibility (*antarddhāna*), traveling through the sky, entering fissures, entering forests, entering the abodes of *nāgas*, and the abodes of *kinnarīs*.

6. Entering [the body], entering water, entering space, entering the underworld (pātāla), discourse on the elements, discourse on fields, discourse on archery, marching into battle, summoning, causing rain, sustaining, subjugating, expelling yakṣas, causing [them] to depart, crossing great rivers, discourse on the stars, discourse on mantras, moving substances and medicinal herbs, the accomplishment of alchemy (rasapācana), transferring, expelling, accomplishing crops, covering clothes [with gold], and subjugating kings—all these are mundane accomplishments (laukikasādhana).

7. [The mantra] succeeds thus. Now, one who desires the next world should wish for it and place his right hand upon the crown of his head. As soon as it is placed there, he obtains the purification of the body called "the stainless and utterly pure body. He casts off his body like the slough of a serpent. Immediately, while still alive, he departs for the world-system of Sukhāvatī. In birth after birth, throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of lifetimes, he will remember [his past lives]. Immediately, [he shall go] to Amitāyus.

1. One receives a prophecy from the Tathāgata; immediately one will become non-retrogressive regarding unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, [knowing] "this indeed is my final birth and final arising. One attains the samādhi named *Sarvāvaraṇavigatāmoghavikurvaṇa*; one attains hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of other samādhis. All the Tathāgatas in the ten directions everywhere will take heed of one and bestow their approval (*sādhukāra*). One will be taken into the care of all bodhisattvas.

2. ...will [be accomplished]. He will be protected by all the deities. Upon merely seeing these, they will bestow upon him two excellent accomplishments, both mundane and supramundane. He accomplishes many other various tasks as well: liberation from planetary influences, possession, examination of thread, examination of lifespan, the pacification of diseases, and [the curing of] all swellings, boils, carbuncles, fistulas, hemorrhoids, scabies, leprosy, kiṭibha, scabies, erysipelas, abdominal dropsy, colic, eye pain, headache, and hemicrania.

3. It destroys toothache, throat pain, tongue and palate pain, diseases of the mouth, diseases of the nose, earache, heartache, abdominal pain, side pain, pain in the hands, pain in the feet, pain in the calves, and pain in the nails; it destroys all fevers—those occurring every day, every second day, every third day, every fourth day, constant fever, night fever, daily fever, and that caused by the combination of all three humors—as soon as this mantra is merely remembered. His sins shall be destroyed.

4. All wicked ones, all adversaries, and all enemies shall perish. Thus, this *Mahāhalavatī* dhāraṇī-heart-mantra will become the supreme mundane accomplishment (*laukikī-parama-siddhi*). Now, one who wishes to perform the rite must first be a pure *vidyādhara*, wearing clean garments and having bathed well. Then, by reciting the *Mahāmogha-hṛdaya-mantra-dhāraṇī*, these [powers] are accomplished through the recitation; [specifically] by eighteen thousand [recitations].

5. By means of all sins [being pacified], the worldly accomplishments (*laukikīsiddhi*) of great knowledge (*mahāvidyā*) are attained; they are accomplished everywhere and within all bodies. Now, for one who wishes to accomplish the ritual procedure of the supramundane recitation (*lokottarajāpavidhi*), that Vidyādhara must be pure day by day, well-bathed, and wearing clean garments. Beginning from the full moon (*pūrṇṇapratipad*), ten thousand recitations (*jāpa*) should be performed day by day. On the eleventh lunar day, there are three [sessions] during the fortnight. Within a single day and night—

6. Every day, one should perform two thousand recitations. Worship of the noble Avalokiteśvara must be performed; on the full moon of the fifteenth day, an offering of the three white foods (*triśukla-bali*) should be presented. Water for the guest-offering (*argha*) and water for the feet (*pādya*) should be given. Then, one should eat the meal of the three white foods. On the night of the full moon of the fifteenth day, one thousand and eight recitations should be performed. During the final watch of the night, the noble Avalokiteśvara arrives. He says "Excellent! to the knowledge-holder (*vidyādhara*). "You have accomplished the *Amogharājahṛdaya*, together with its entire and complete ritual manual (*kalpa*) and the maṇḍala of liberation. Extending his right hand, he gives a lotus to the knowledge-holder, who should receive it. As soon as it is received, one travels through the sky by supernatural power (*ṛddhi*); one goes to whichever Buddha-field one desires and brings comfort to all the Tathāgatas. Now, for one who wishes to perform the fire-sacrifice (*homa*), a lotus-heart-shaped pit should be prepared. It should be circular in measurement. One should offer into the fire stalks, stems, and petals of the lotus, smeared with clarified butter (*ghṛta*), eight thousand times. O Sugata...
71a (P. omitted, D. 133b5)

1. Having kindled a fire with *indha* wood, when [the recitation] is completed, eight thousand [times], the Great Goddess Śrī appears in person. One should offer her a respectful oblation (*argha*) with scented water, and she will say, "O Vidyādhara, what shall I do? She should be told, "O Blessed One, grant me inexhaustible gain of wealth and the discovery of treasure. Then, having said "So be it," she comforts him and vanishes. Wherever the Vidyādhara goes, there he sees great treasures, and they never come to exhaustion. They should be given away and enjoyed.

2. One should perform worship of the Three Jewels. One should worship the noble Avalokiteśvara and offer a portion daily to the Great Goddess Śrī. Having kindled a fire with *arka* wood smeared with blue lotuses, sandalwood powder, and fresh butter, one should offer [the oblation] for one fortnight before a cloth painting (*paṭa*) of the noble Avalokiteśvara; one should offer it in immeasurable quantities. When the rite is completed, one obtains all-encompassing enjoyment. Before the painting, [one should offer] *hiṅgu* oil mixed with mustard seeds and lotus petals... [of] *devadāru*...

3. One should offer one hundred and eight fuel-sticks of *rusama* wood at the three junctions of the day for seven nights; one obtains a hundred villages. One should offer one hundred and eight fuel-sticks of *aśoka* wood smeared with ghee at the three junctions of the day for one fortnight; one attains kingship. One should offer one hundred and eight fuel-sticks at the three junctions of the day for seven nights; [the deity] reveals the method for indicating locations. Eight thousand *mallikā* flowers should be offered to an image of the noble Avalokiteśvara; [after] twelve—

4. By means of this rite, one becomes devoted to all the Blessed Buddhas and devoted to the gods and nāgas. One accomplishes all obstacles and all tasks. One who desires to summon Maṇibhadra should place the ring finger upon the heart and recite [the mantra] eight hundred times at the three junctions of the day. When the practice is completed after twelve nights, Maṇibhadra grants a vision. While being rubbed with the heart-mantra, he gives a hundred dināras day by day, and that [wealth] is inexhaustible.

5. One who gives again and again should not make an accumulation, nor should one give no more. Standing facing the noble Avalokiteśvara, or else placing a cloth painting (*paṭa*) before a reliquary (*caitya*) containing relics with its back toward oneself, one should offer oblations at the three junctions of the day—clarified butter, honey, and curd—mixed with *khadirasamidh* wood, eight hundred times each. For seven full days, one obtains ten thousand *rūpaka*s. Thus, and so forth.

6. Prosperity rites (*pauṣṭika*) should be employed in all circumstances. // O // Now, one who wishes to accomplish the eye-salve (*añjana*) must be a pure *vidyādhara* and must perform the practice with purity. He must be well-bathed. He should place realgar (*manaḥśilā*) in a copper vessel. Sitting cross-legged facing a painted cloth (*duṣyapaṭa*), having fasted for a day and night on the eighth or fifteenth day of the lunar fortnight, he should cover it with four leaves of the *aśvattha* tree and recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment occurs: [the vessel] becomes warm, emits smoke, and blazes.

7. {By fumigating with incense} and applying it as eye-salve, he who looks [with such eyes] becomes subject to one's will; whatever he desires, he obtains; he becomes greatly honored by the entire world; he shall become worthy of great honor by all kings, kingdoms, ministers, harems, and retinues; and he stands at the head [of all]. By fumigating with incense and applying it as eye-salve, he touches the earth ten finger-breadths deep with his feet, and having gone a thousand *yojanas*, he returns again. He hears a thousand *yojanas*... [71b] (P. omitted, D.134b5)

4. He sees for a thousand *yojanas* and lives for thirty thousand years. He does not carry out the commands of anyone, nor does he obey the commands of anyone; he is constantly endowed with great happiness and always occupies the position of a teacher. He becomes one who is sustained by the vision of all the Tathāgatas. Blazing, he flies up with himself as his second [companion] and lives for ten thousand years. Beyond this, for one practicing the *manaḥśilā* (realgar) accomplishment, there are mundane and supramundane accomplishments. Then, having taken the *karavīraka* realgar—

2. One should purify it with *dhīrakraya* (mercury); having purified it, one should fast for three nights on the full moon day, perform a grand worship of the Blessed One, the Noble Avalokiteśvara, place realgar (*manaḥśilā*) upon four lotus petals, and cover it with three [petals]. One should recite [the mantra] until the threefold accomplishment occurs: it becomes warm, smokes, and blazes. Having made a forehead mark (*tilaka*) while it is warming, as many beings as he sees and those by whom he is seen—all of them become subject to his will. Even those born as animals [attain] even double their lifespan.

3. It increases. By making a *tilaka* with [the substance] while it is emitting smoke, one becomes the subduer (*vaśya*) of all people of the four castes. The earth is touched by the feet at a distance of a man’s height. One sees three thousand *yojanas*; one hears from three thousand *yojanas*. One lives for twelve thousand years. By making a *tilaka* with [the substance] while it is blazing, one becomes a traveler through the sky; one flies up accompanied by twenty attendants, and becomes the king of all those who have attained mastery through realgar (*manaḥśilā*).

4. One flies up three thousand *yojanas* and lives for eighty thousand years. For one desiring to accomplish the *rocanā* (bezoar) rite, having purified the *rocanā* with the ghee of a tawny cow on either the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight or the eighth, and having fasted for three nights, one should perform a grand worship of the Blessed Lord Avalokiteśvara. Having established [the image], one should grasp it with the right hand and recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment is attained. When it begins to emit heat—

5. Having made a *tilaka* with [the powder], one subdues the yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, bhūtas, and andhasas; whatever one seeks, they provide that. Starting from that very day, one’s lifespan becomes five thousand years. Having made a *tilaka* with [the powder] while it is emitting smoke, one becomes the king of all those who possess the power of invisibility. One travels by means of a peaceful mass of wind; having gone twenty thousand *yojanas*, one returns again. One’s lifespan becomes sixty thousand years. From sixty *yojanas*—

6. [He] sees [them]. Having made a mark (*tilaka*) with blazing [substance], one gains the power of traveling through the sky; one flies up surrounded by a retinue of a hundred [attendants]; one becomes the king of all the *Sarvarocana* adepts (*siddhas*) and lives for ten million years. And when he dies, he becomes a king, a sovereign of the four continents (*caturdvīpādhipati*). Now, by a *vidyādhara* who desires to accomplish himself as golden-colored, that *vidyādhara* must perform the ritual of recitation (*jāpavidhi*) within six fortnights. Then, the *vidyādhara*—pure, wearing clean garments, and having bathed well—should proceed.

7. It should be done as follows: one should prepare these medicinal substances—realgar, yellow orpiment, honey, *saki*, costus, saffron, *gorocana*, *aśoka* flowers, white pigment (*pāṇḍudravya*), the *jāmbūnada* medicinal, gold powder, cow’s milk, *arkka* milk, gold-milk, *snuhā* milk, *bodhivṛkṣa* milk, and *viṣṇukrama* milk. Having combined these in equal parts, one should place them in a copper vessel and stir them. There is no doubt that within a fortnight they will turn into cow’s milk. [One should do this] facing the cloth-painting (*paṭa*).
72a (P. omitted; D. 135b5)

1. Having placed the cloth painting in a forest, a monastery, a walking path, or on a clean spot of ground; having established the painting and recollected the Great Loving-kindness, Compassion, and the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha; being armored with the great armor, possessing firm vigor and prowess, and with supreme devotion and reverence for the noble Avalokiteśvara; desiring enlightenment, one should perform worship daily according to one's ability as previously described and recite [the mantra] for six months. Then, when the six months are complete, the Vidyādhara, having dried the excellent medicinal herbs and having them made into fine powder, should place them in a copper vessel.

2. Having recited the *Amogharājahṛdaya* one thousand and eight times, and having recited the *Krodharāja* one thousand and eight times; then, on the fifteenth day of the full moon, having fasted for three nights and performed a grand worship of the Buddha, the Blessed One, and the Noble Avalokiteśvara, and having offered a most magnificent sacrificial oblation (*bali*) in the four directions; thereafter, the Vidyādhara should meditate upon the supreme medicinal herb together with *pārata*, along with white sugar and honey; then, once again, he should recite the mantra ten thousand times for the Noble Avalokiteśvara.

3. In front [of him], it blazes in a copper vessel; it emits heat; rays of various colors blaze forth; the body of the vidyādhara blazes; and an earthquake occurs. Then, the vidyādhara should become joyful in his mental disposition. When it has blazed, he should stir it with *brahmaputraka* oil and smear his own body with it. As soon as it has been smeared, his own body will become golden-colored in its complexion; his body will become as firm as a diamond (*vajrasāra*).

4. One flies up with a retinue of a hundred thousand, [the body] being neither cuttable nor pierceable. If one anoints the hair, it will become golden hair; if one anoints the nails, they will become golden nails; if one anoints the teeth, they will become golden teeth. Wherever one anoints the human body, right there it will become golden-colored. Apart from the oil, this supreme single elixir transforms a thousand palas of copper into gold. [Copper] treated with the oil—

One should coat [the vessel] with three *pala*s; it produces ten *pala*s of gold. It must be heated by fire. One should boil cow’s milk with this supreme elixir (*rasāyana*) and cook it over a gentle fire until it is combined with a portion of clarified butter (*ghṛta*). When one knows it is perfected, one should then remove it from the heat. Having bathed cleanly and being clad in clean garments, one should first rinse with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). Then, this supreme elixir should be drunk with lukewarm water. By its application for seven nights, the body—

6. [By this] one is purified. It immediately removes all sins, instantly incinerates all afflictions (*kleśa*), and immediately removes all diseases. It wards off all poisons. No poison takes hold of him again, nor does a weapon [strike him]; he is not diminished by water, nor is he burned by fire, nor again by other terrible poisons. By practicing it for two weeks, all diseases are shattered and his complexion becomes pure, free from wrinkles and grey hair. By practicing it for three weeks, he becomes like a ten-year-old child and attains a body with a complexion as fair as a lotus.

7. One who possesses eyes like blue lotuses, divine and as delicate as a lotus petal or a water lily; who is skilled in the voice of a *kiṃnara*; whose hair is curly and coiled, and who has the color of a divine, excellent bee—by practicing for only one month, such a person lives for ten thousand years. Invisible to all enemies, including hosts of *yakṣas* and *rākṣasas*, and even by spirits (*bhūtas*), he is not seen, nor are others who commit evil deeds. Having served the deity for a full year, he sports with her in divine enjoyments and celestial palaces, just like the gods.

1. One who eats it daily lives for ten thousand years, even while sweating profusely, provided he consumes it with honey. He travels through the sky. Take a thousand *palas* of copper; make one *pala* of this excellent elixir (*rasāyana*). Melt ten *palas* of copper and pierce it so that it flows [into the elixir] mixed with tin (*śulba*). A thousand *palas* of silver will thus become an excellent elixir. By means of one *pala*, one transforms a hundred *palas* of copper into the appearance of silver. As it emits rays of various colors, it produces various colors. Melting white gold, it becomes a jewel of various forms and colors.

2. One holds the jewel. One should boil it with oil. By merely anointing the head, the hair becomes inexhaustible and takes on various colors. By anointing the body, rays of light of various colors issue forth. If one applies it as collyrium to the eyes, one travels through the sky. One sees all the doors of palaces opened. Everywhere, one will become a sovereign lord of the palaces. Having made a mark (*tilaka*) on the forehead, one becomes invisible. Holding it in the mouth, whoever one speaks to becomes submissive. [With] oneself, [one gains] wealth—

And not otherwise. Or else, O Kapilagavya, one should boil fresh butter, ghee, milk, and the best elixir together with blazing [fire]. Then, taking the excellent cooked substance—which is like white sugar—one should recite the *Amogharājahṛdaya* eight thousand times. One should then anoint oneself; by the mere act of being anointed, one will become a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) among the *vidyādharas*. One lives for ten great eons (*mahākalpa*). During an intermediate eon (*antarakalpa*), one beholds the Buddha, the Blessed One, at the most excellent and supreme seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).

4. He obtains the prophecy [of his future enlightenment]. Having made a *tilaka* mark, he flies up into the sky. By means of the sound of the syllable *oṃ*, he causes Brahmā to emerge from his abode; with merely a snap of the fingers, he goes as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven and returns again. When his time of death arrives, he proceeds to the world-system of Sukhāvatī. This one will be liberated from all dwellings in his final birth. Therefore, I shall proclaim the Amogha-guṭikā; let the Vidyādhara accomplish it.

5. For the accomplishment of this reality (tattvasādhana), one should wear clean garments. [The ingredients are: lotus, antimony (śrotāñjana), nāgakeśara, gorocanā, the best *araṇī* wood, collyrium (*añjana*), and likewise agallochum (*agaru*). Having prepared these substances in equal portions as a finely ground powder, wrap it in gold or silver, and further wrap it in copper. Saturate it with white sugar-candy, place it in a vessel made of white sandalwood, and press it with the hollow of the palms. Then, having fasted for one night on either the eighth or the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, [one should proceed].

6. In front of a cloth painting (*duṣyapaṭa*) of the noble Avalokiteśvara, one should recite the *Amogharājahṛdaya* one thousand and eight times, and the *Krodharāja* one hundred and eight times. By reciting the mantra eight thousand times, it will then begin to vibrate. Taking it and placing it in one’s mouth, one becomes invisible. One will have a lifespan of a thousand years. Measuring four finger-breadths, one does not touch the ground with one’s feet. One can travel a hundred *yojanas* and return again. One will become a Flower-Vidyādhara Universal Monarch (*cakravartin*). [The name of the deity is] Kumuda—

7. A body with the fragrance of blue lotuses is expelled [from impurities]. One should mix blue lotus (*nīlotpala*), *campaka*, and *ketaki* flowers in equal parts with honey; the wise one should form them into pills and encase them in gold, silver, copper, or other metals. On the eighth day of the waxing moon, the fourteenth, or the fifteenth, having fasted for three nights, being well-bathed, pure, and wearing clean garments, one should perform a grand worship of the Buddha, the Blessed One, and the cloth-painting (*duṣyapaṭa*) of Noble Avalokiteśvara, [placing the pills] in a casket made of *aśvattha* wood.

Having placed the pill and held it with the hollow of one's hands before the cloth painting, one should recite the mantra until it trembles. Then it becomes perfected. Having placed it in the mouth, one travels three thousand *yojanas* and returns again. One’s feet, measuring eight finger-breadths, do not touch the ground. One lives for ten thousand years. One’s eyes become like blue lotuses. One exhales the fragrance of a blue lotus from the mouth. The face becomes like the full orb of the moon, and the complexion becomes like a lotus. The body exudes the fragrance of *campaka*.

He shall become the universal monarch (*cakravartirāja*) of all the space-dwelling vidyādharas. One should have sandalwood powder, agallochum powder, *tagara*, and *abhaya* (myrobalan)—these in equal parts—ground into a fine powder. Having formed pills with Turkish oil (*turuṣkataila*), one should wrap them with three layers of thread, place them in a sandalwood casket, and on the full moon of the bright fortnight, having fasted for three nights and performed a grand worship and a grand offering to the Blessed Buddha and the noble Avalokiteśvara, one should grasp the casket with the hand while holding *darbha* grass.

3. Having sat down on a seat and recited the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* one thousand and eight times, one should then recite the *Krodharāja* one hundred and eight times. Then, the pill (*gulikā*) begins to revolve; at that point, the *vidyādhara* should know that the success has been achieved, for this pill is now perfected. Thereafter, the *vidyādhara* must perform worship to the noble Avalokiteśvara.
