At the time of dawn, when the sun has risen with the radiance of gold and the colors of twilight, it should be consumed as food. [This is the practice] of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

4. Having paid homage, one should cultivate a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*) toward all sentient beings. One should give [the medicine] to one's attendants. One should place a single pill (*gulikā*) in the mouth. As soon as the pill has been placed in the hand, it becomes invisible. One travels through the sky; one travels five thousand *yojanas* and returns again. One becomes a universal monarch (*cakravartin*), sovereign over those who have attained the accomplishment of the *sādhana* of the pill that rests all limbs. One’s lifespan will be five thousand years. With the palm of the hand, the earth—

5. Then one does not touch it. Now, by one who wishes to excavate a treasure, at the place where there is a suspicion of a treasure, one should prepare a circle of cow dung in that spot, scatter flowers over it, offer incense of guggulu, and present the threefold offering: an offering of white substances, an offering of meat and blood, and an offering of roasted barley flour, fruit, and lotuses. One should perform worship to the noble Avalokiteśvara. While reciting the mantra ten thousand times, when the ten thousand are completed, at whichever place the treasure—

6. [The treasure] will open. Thereupon, the guardian of the treasure arises; the treasure vault flies up. An offering of *bali* and *argha* must be presented to the guardian of the treasure. That guardian of the treasure shall become a servant for as long as one lives; wherever you send him or whatever you command, he will perform all those tasks. Having recited the *Amogharājahṛdaya* seven times over mustard-seed ashes, they should be scattered in the four directions; all obstructors, Vināyakas, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas will be bound, and a great boundary-binding (*mahāsīmābandha*) will be established.

7. Regarding the destruction of Vināyakas: one should kindle a fire with *karavīra* wood fuel smeared with honey, and offer one hundred and eight oblations of *kaṭṭuka* oil, mustard seeds, *guggulu*, *caṇḍabījaka*, and salt at the three junctions of the day for three days; all families of Vināyakas will be struck down and destroyed. One who wishes to paralyze an army should kindle a fire facing the army with *nimba* wood, using mustard seeds, *viśarājikā*, and seven types of seeds smeared with honey, and first [offer] one hundred and eight...

1. It does not paralyze an army. On the second [recitation], a great disease falls upon it; on the third, when recited one hundred and eight times, all armies are destroyed and shall never again prevail. Now, for one who wishes to perform the rite of the staff (*daṇḍasādhana*), a staff made of *khadira* wood should be fashioned as the Staff of Yama (*yamadaṇḍa*). It should be two cubits in length. Then, having eaten food that is pure in three ways (*triśuklabhojana*) before the noble Avalokiteśvara, one should recite ten thousand times. Then, on the full moon day of the fifteenth, having fasted for a day and night, one should recite the Amogharājahṛdaya one hundred and eight times. One hundred and eight [times]—kro-...

2. While reciting the *dharāja* mantra, the staff (*daṇḍa*) then blazes. Thereupon, one should know that it is accomplished; the sound "Amoghadaṇḍa" (Infallible Staff) issues forth. Then, worship of the noble Avalokiteśvara must be performed. Then the Vidyādhara, taking the staff, should whirl it around seven times in every direction. Then, with the staff, the earth should be struck. And upon the staff, the earth should be measured out as a square. A great celestial palace (*vimāna*), a square mansion on all sides, complete and perfect in every aspect, a divine palace, manifests.

3. It becomes crowded with women, men, boys, and girls. Then a divine woman arrives; adorned with all ornaments, beautiful, pleasing, and lovely to behold, she stands in the middle of the doorway. She holds a full pitcher in a vessel made of the seven precious gems. Then that divine woman says, "Vidyādhara, enter your own abode. The Vidyādhara should say, "What shall I do with this essenceless house and celestial mansion? She says—

4. "Accept this full vessel; for you, there will be great prosperity. Then, the *vidyādhara*, becoming enraged, should exclaim, "Fie! Fie! Thereupon, that divine woman weeps; as the god rains down large drops, so do tears fall from her eyes. The *vidyādhara* must catch them and smear them upon his own body. As soon as his body is smeared, it becomes like Jāmbūnada gold, and the fragrance of uraga-sandalwood and śāra-gośīrṣa-candana issues from his person. [Having taken it] from her mouth, he should lift it up.

5. One’s mouth is perfumed with the fragrance of a divine blue lotus. By applying divine collyrium to the eyes, one’s vision becomes like that of a divine being. By anointing the hair, one’s hair becomes like that of a divine peacock. If one places [the powder] in the hollows of the ears, one gains divine hearing; one sees for three thousand *yojanas*. It should be drunk; by doing so, one lives for ten thousand *kalpas*. For an interval of a thousand *kalpas*, one remembers one's births, as well as all dramas, comedies, fables, treatises, the *Mahābhārata*, and the *Rāmāyaṇa*.

6. All the systems of the Purāṇas, Vinaya, Jātaka, Kāvya, Vaiśeṣika, all the maṇḍalas of ritual procedures, mudrās, mantras, dhāraṇīs, sūtras, and Abhidharma of the Mahāyāna—all these appear before him. He attains a great state in every respect. Then that woman says: "Enter, O Blessed One, into your own abode. The Vidyādhara should say: "One must enter by stepping upon one's own feet. Then that woman shows her two breasts; the Vidyādhara should grasp them and press them. That milk flows forth. Ta-

7. It should be grasped and consumed by the Vidyādhara. Smearing it on his feet, as soon as they are smeared, he flies up into the sky with a retinue of a thousand and accompanied by that divine woman. He will be followed by the first wind-element. Eighty-four thousand Vidyādharas appear; he becomes a universal monarch (cakravartin), a king of the Vidyādharas. He goes to the world-system of Sukhāvatī and becomes the foremost of the Vidyādharas. This is the procedure for the worldly accomplishment. [He should grasp] a staff in his right hand...

1. Regarding the *Amogharājahṛdaya*: while reciting it twenty-one times, one should brandish a staff. Whatever purpose you contemplate in your mind or whatever you pray for, all that shall be accomplished instantly. Whomever you summon shall be summoned and will stand before you. One who wishes to invoke a *yakṣa* or *yakṣiṇī* should paint their image with red ochre; the *Amogharāja* mantra should be recited seven times over the staff, which should then be brandished above the *yakṣiṇī*, and *guggulu* incense should be offered. [The practitioner should be] pure...

2. One should present the offering vessel. As soon as it is rotated together [with the mantra], the yakṣas and yakṣiṇīs will appear before one. They will become obedient; whatever you command, they will perform that task. They bring about everything without deficiency. They provide wealth, grain, gold, jewels, pearls, silver, bullion, clothing, beds, seats, ornaments, decorations, and so forth. Whatever else you command, they accomplish all of that. By rotating the Śrī [vessel] before oneself, one receives abundant and most excellent riches.

3. It stands before one in its own form. Whatever you pray for, it grants all of that. One should strike the feet of Vaiśravaṇa seven times; the Amogharājahṛdaya should be recited twenty-one times. Running forward, Vaiśravaṇa stands before one and gives abundant, vast wealth. Whatever you pray for, he will accomplish all of that. Without speaking, having recited the mantra over a staff twenty-one times, one should brandish it seven times at the king’s gate.

They will come under his control, along with the king and his retinue of queens, by means of both his own person and his wealth. As he causes it to be recited at the city gates, all the inhabitants of the city—men, women, boys, and girls—will remain under his control. He alone shall become worthy of worship, and all shall become his male and female servants, following his will. Having gone to a temple and reciting the *Amogharājahṛdaya* before the deity while causing it to be recited, that deity will appear in her own form before him.

5. He will do whatever you say; he will grant everything that you pray for. While reciting the *Amogharājahṛdaya*, one should rotate [the image] facing the rising sun, and the Sun will descend; he will grant every boon that one desires. While reciting the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, one should rotate [the image] facing the full moon, and the Moon, together with the hosts of constellations and stars, will descend; he will grant all desired boons. One should circumambulate a reliquary (*caitya*) containing relics...

6. By reciting the *Amogharāja* [mantra] while brandishing a staff, the *caitya* blazes and a sound issues forth; it tells you everything regarding whatever intention you inquire about and grants you everything you desire. Having circumambulated the Tathāgata while reciting the *Amogharāja-hṛdaya*, one should brandish [the staff]; one obtains the vision of all the Tathāgatas, and all the Tathāgatas provide consolation. It will fulfill all one's heart's desires. Then, during the final watch of the night, Noble Avalokiteśvara appears in his own form—

7. One should worship it. It will grant and bestow the most excellent of all desires; it bestows the accomplishment of all tasks. One attains the accomplishment of an Amoghadaṇḍa Vidyādhara Cakravartin. In times of drought, having gone to the abode of the Nāgas, one should recollect the Heart-mantra of Amogharāja and brandish the staff. By the mere act of brandishing it, the Nāgas immediately release great torrents of rain; they rain according to one's wish. In times of excessive rain, [one should go] to the refuge above the Amoghapāśa...

1. Having reminded [the deity] with a loud voice, one should brandish the staff; it will hold back excessive rain. At the time of a thunderstorm, standing facing the clouds, one should angrily remind the King of Wrath with a loud voice and brandish the staff with anger; cold winds and lightning will not fall. There will be a great boundary-binding for a league (yojana) all around. For one seized by any planetary spirit (*graha*), one should remind the King of Wrath seven times and show him the staff; all the planetary spirits will flee, crying out. This applies even to cases such as epilepsy (*apasmāra*) upon mere sight—

2. Three [types of fevers] flee away. In all fevers, by merely sprinkling [the patient] with water consecrated by the *Amogharājahṛdaya* while reciting "Oṃ ārjya," one is liberated from all fevers; even quartan fever flees away wailing. In battles and combats, one who recites the *Amogharājahṛdaya* with wrath must brandish a staff; then all the weapons and missiles of the warriors vanish, and that enemy army flees away crying out "Hā hā! For one who has gone into the midst of a caravan or into the middle of a forest wilderness, [one should recite] the *Amogharāja*.

3. One should recollect [this] and brandish the staff; then all thieves, rogues, robbers, bands of *sigha*, tigers, bears, hyenas, venomous serpents, fierce beasts, elephants, buffaloes, and poisonous creatures will vanish. They will go to their own homes in safety and well-being. All plagues—the death of cattle, the death of livestock, the death of horses, and the death of men, women, boys, and girls—[shall cease]. One should recollect the *Amogharājahṛdaya*, the King of Wrath (*Krodharāja*), with a loud voice and brandish the staff at the four city gates.

It should be whirled around. As soon as it is whirled, all calamities, misfortunes, portents, and afflictions will be pacified; all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes will be stilled, and they will be liberated from all fears. If one desires to summon a woman or a man, standing on a high place, one should chant the *Amogharājahṛdaya* twenty-one times in a loud voice while whirling a staff, and one should utter the name of the person for whose sake this is done.

5. He comes from a hundred *yojanas* away; they remain under one's control, both by one's own person and by one's wealth, and they attend upon one for as long as life lasts. Now, for one desiring to summon Māṇibhadra, having fasted for a day and night on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one should empower a staff by reciting the *Amogharājahṛdaya* twenty-one times and place it within the belly of Māṇibhadra, while reciting the *Krodharāja*. Then, during the final watch of the night, Māṇibhadra will appear in his own form.

He stands before the Vidyādhara and gives ten thousand *dīnāras*. From that, a portion must be given to the Three Jewels; worship of the noble Avalokiteśvara must be performed, and an offering of water for the feet (*arghapādya*) must be presented to Māṇibhadra. Day by day, one should present the offering of water for the feet to Māṇibhadra; day by day he gives ten thousand *dīnāras*. As long as he lives, half of that [income] must be spent by the Vidyādhara; gifts must be given and a store of merit (*puṇyasaṃcaya*) must be made. Together with Māṇibhadra—

7. One should perform a rite of joy (*modanā*). In the middle of a forest where water is lacking, or in a wilderness (*kāntāra*), one should take a staff and recite the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* twenty-one times. At a place where there is green, grassy ground, one should strike the surface of the earth with it, whirl it seven times, and while raising one's voice, recollect the *Amogharājahṛdaya*. Then, one should cry out to the noble Avalokiteśvara. Thereafter, at the very spot where the ground was struck, a lotus pond (*puṣkiriṇī*) shall appear.

A divine water-bearing stream appears; it will be neither too cold nor too hot, but delicious. Then, the Vidyādhara, having recited the mantra of Daṇḍa-Krodharāja seven times, should strike the middle of the lotus pond with water. Thereupon, a tawny man emerges from the middle of the lotus pond and stands before the Vidyādhara with his palms joined in reverence. He says, "Tell me, Vidyādhara, what do you desire? The Vidyādhara should say, "I am seeking food; let it be given."

2. Then, a benediction (*svastivācanā*) should be recited for the Vidyādhara man, and that man enters into the middle of the lotus pond. In an instant, a moment, or a brief hour (*kṣaṇalavamuhūrtena*), he brings various kinds of food and drink of the finest flavors and presents them to the Vidyādhara. There will be food for hundreds of thousands of people; he shall obtain an abundance of all necessary utensils and provisions. This occurs provided the Vidyādhara does not dismiss the lotus pond; and that lotus pond [remains] until the time of departure.

3. It does not remain, nor will it disappear. For all sentient beings and all merchants, every requisite shall appear without deficiency. Then, by that vidyādhara who desires to make the wheel unfailing, one should bathe [the disciple] with scented water over which the mantra has been recited twenty-one times, and the topknot should be bound. Without speaking, one should empower a staff by reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times and then brandish it. Thereupon, the great multitude in the assembly, who had been bewildered and deluded, [shall be restored].

4. They do not come forth. Then, one should brandish the staff. Just as the form of mental attention [is directed], so does it manifest everything; it rains down fruits and flowers and displays various kinds of illusions. Now, if one wishes to perform the rite for raising a *vetāḍa*, that *vidyādhara* must be pure, wearing clean garments, and having bathed well. Having gone to a cremation ground, he should recite the mantra over the staff seven times, and over the *Amogharājahṛdaya* seven times, and over the *Krodharāja*—

5. While reciting [the mantra], one must circumambulate the middle of the cremation ground on all sides; within a boundary of one *yojana*, there will be a binding of the perimeter. All obstacles, all wicked ones, and the *yakṣas* and *rākṣasas* will be bound. Then, the *vidyādhara* should take the corpse, bathe it, and purify it with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). A square maṇḍala made of cow dung should be prepared, well-proportioned. Four stakes of *khadira* wood, twelve finger-breadths in length, [should be placed] at the four corners.

6. One should drive [stakes] into the [corners] and surround the mandala on all sides with a five-fingered thread. The corpse should be wrapped in a white cloth and placed within the central mandala. It should be strewn with flowers, and the three-fold white offering (triśuklabali) should be presented. The water for honor (argha) and water for the feet (pādya) should be set out, and incense of guggulu should be offered. The Vidyādhara, seated facing the east, should hold a staff in his right hand and recite the King of Vidyās. The Wrathful King should be invoked sixty times. To the south—

7. One must not wipe it; rather, the staff should be struck with the right arm. Then the corpse moves, trembles, and rises up. It looks toward the ten directions. The *vidyādhara* should place the staff upon its head. That corpse then utters speech. The *vidyādhara* should cause it to remember the mantra; it should be contemplated with the mind. Then that corpse tells everything—past, future, and present; they speak of the future and the current. Thereafter, the *vidyādhara* [should hold] the staff to the heart. (75b) (P.126b8, D.142b1)

1. Standing, one blows blood; having made a *tilaka* with that blood, the doorkeeper is unimpeded, and in all cases the doors of all palaces become opened. All women, men, boys, and girls remain under one's control. Pressing the staff [against the victim], one causes the heart to vomit; this must be taken by the *vidyādhara*. Having consumed it entirely, as soon as it is consumed, one travels through the sky. One becomes like Maheśvara, the lord of the great elements (*mahābhūta*). One lives for a thousand divine years. With the syllable *oṃ*—da-

One should press the staff and threaten it; then the tongue will protrude, which the Vidyādhara must cut off and seize. As soon as it is seized, he flies up into the sky. He shall become a Sword-Vidyādhara Universal Monarch (cakravartin) and live for ten thousand years. He will have a retinue of eighteen Vidyādharas. Then, O Vidyādhara, the staff should be struck upon the head of the corpse; it becomes released. One should take the corpse, which is now a solid mass of gold, weighing one pala.

3. One thousand *palas* of copper becomes gold. This is the worldly method of accomplishment (*laukikīsādhanavidhi*). Then the Bodhisattva Noble Avalokiteśvara said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, this worldly method of accomplishment of mine is for the sake of compassion toward all sentient beings. The Tathāgata Śākyamuni said: "Speak, O Great Being, out of compassion for all sentient beings, the supramundane method, the supreme secret heart-maṇḍala."

4. One attains steadfastness, intelligence, and fearlessness. For all holders of the sciences (*vidyādharas*), there shall be the supreme accomplishment of the reality of the practice (*paramasādhanatatvasiddhi*). By merely reciting and remembering [this], they shall obtain every great accomplishment. There shall be the accomplishment of fulfilling their great hopes. They shall obtain all excellent great accomplishments. There shall be the accomplishment of fulfilling the hopes of the holders of the sciences regarding the attainment of all desires. Then, the noble Avalokiteśvara...

5. Having heard the consolation and the invitation from the presence of the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva was filled with great joy. He rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and extending his joined palms toward the Blessed One, bowed his head at the Blessed One’s feet. Having performed a grand and magnificent act of worship and service with various and manifold flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, and ointments—

6. Having honored the Blessed One with flower-powder, robes, parasols, banners, and flags, and with various garments, ornaments, and decorations, as well as that great circle of the assembly—the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, those deities dwelling in the mandala, the accomplished Vidyādharas, and the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas who are established in the supreme essence of the Great Amoghapāśa Liberation Mandala and its ritual observances, and all those dwelling at Potalaka—all of them [were honored] with various flowers, incense, and perfumes.

7. Having worshipped [the Blessed One] with various garlands, ointments, diverse garments, ornaments, and decorations, with a joyful mind he circumambulated the Blessed One one hundred thousand times. Having worshipped the assembly circle as well, he bowed with palms joined toward where the Blessed One was, and standing before the Blessed One with unblinking eyes, he addressed the Blessed One in these most sweet words: "Blessed One, I possess a wondrous gaze, an unfailing miraculous transformation belonging to all the Tathāgatas."

1. This is the Heart-Liberation Maṇḍala, the miraculous manifestation of the reality of all Tathāgatas, the Great Samaya Maṇḍala empowered by Vairocana; it is the Heart-mantra of the Noose of Amoghavilokita, the heart that is the essence of the accomplishment of supramundane recitation and practice, the supreme supramundane sādhana, and the prophecy empowered by all the Tathāgatas. Therefore, being in the presence of the Blessed One, I shall proclaim this through the empowerment of the Blessed One for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of all Vidyādharas and for the sake of all sentient beings.

2. For the sake of deliverance, it is the warding off of all hells, animal births, and the world of Yama; the destruction of all former obscurations, sins, and defilements; the prevention of all miserable destinies; the total incineration of all worldly and supramundane sins and obscurations; [it is for those who] have rejected the awakening of a Buddha, who have rejected the perfected ones, who are destined for the Avīci hell, who have committed offenses against the Noble Saṅgha, and who have rejected the assembly of all Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Bodhisattvas. By merely hearing or seeing it, or by merely observing its restraint—

3. By merely suppressing anger and by merely revealing the teaching, they will extinguish everything. By the mere sight of me, everything is completely consumed; it is vomited out. They shall become free from all fevers, all diseases, and all stains of greed, stinginess, and envy. They become liberated from all afflictions and hindrances, and they become free from all worldly and supramundane sufferings—namely, birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, and despair.

4. [It wards off] all fears of strife, quarrels, tumults, riots, beatings, threats, imprisonment, disputes, shackles, fetters, litigation, binding, thieves, rogues, robbers, lions, elephants, buffaloes, tigers, lepers, dropsy, various forms of leprosy, scabies, ringworm, skin eruptions, itching, headaches, hemicrania, bears, hyenas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, epilepsy, snake-poisoning, black cobras, vipers, and various other venomous creatures.

5. Through the mere recitation, study, or even the sight [of this], all fears of fire, water, poison, weapons, precipices, falling from houses, cold, wind, heat, swords, and rats shall perish; they shall dissolve and crumble away. One is immediately liberated. In this matter, no doubt or uncertainty should be conceived; one should not be skeptical. One should produce a mind free from dualistic hesitation. O Blessed One, I must always remember [this] face-to-face and always maintain mental attention toward it.

6. One should set this into motion; and this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, the heart-mantra of the Wrathful King (*Krodharāja*), should be set into motion. This *Adbhutāvalokite*, the *Amoghavikurvaṇa* (Infallible Miraculous Transformation), the *Sarvatathāgatahṛdayavimokṣamaṇḍala* (Maṇḍala of the Liberation of the Hearts of All Tathāgatas), the *Sarvatathāgatādbhutavikurvaṇavairocanādhiṣṭhāna-mahāsamayamaṇḍala* (Great Samaya Maṇḍala of the Empowerment of Vairocana through the Miraculous Transformations of All Tathāgatas), and the *Amoghavilokitapāśahṛdaya* (Heart-mantra of the Infallible Gaze of the Noose) should be set into motion constantly and continuously, always present in the mind and at the tip of the tongue. One should cultivate constant and continuous mindfulness. By the mere cultivation of this mindfulness, by the mere act of recollection, there will be the attainment of the perfection of all mundane and supramundane qualities. It is called "irreversible" (*avaivarttika*); one will be established in the state of irreversibility. One will be empowered by the attention and prophecy of all the Tathāgatas. How much more so, then, [the merit of] seeing, reading, reciting, beholding Noble Avalokiteśvara, bowing to him, making offerings, remembering him, and [practicing] at the three times of day?

1. With very clear mental attention, one performs worship and prostration. It should be understood that such a being is like me; it should be understood as being empowered by the body of Lokeśvara; it should be understood as having been prophesied through the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas. How much more so for those who will perform even greater service? That being should be understood as containing the essence of a Tathāgata (*tathāgatagarbha*). And I shall always and at all times remain closely attached to them; I shall grant them a vision at every hundredth moment.

"I shall fulfill the desires of all; then I, as every sentient being, shall very swiftly cause [all beings] to reach the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍala) and establish them in the turning of the great wheel of Dharma. O Blessed One, I am one who has ascended to the vow of a most firm armor. Thus, through the deliverance of all sentient beings and the fulfillment of all hopes and obscurations, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara: "Excellent, excellent!"

3. O Pure Being, this is extremely difficult to encounter; by the mere grasping of these supramundane rites, those beings are completely liberated. How much more so for one who abides in the vows of the ritual procedures for visualization, recitation, accomplishment, and fasting! And that being shall become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Speak, O Pure Being, whenever you deem it the right time. Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—

4. Looking up at the face of the Blessed One, with a smiling countenance, he spoke the heart-mantra of the no-futile-gaze-pāśa: Homage to all the Tathāgatas who are established in accordance with the three times! Homage to the entire Saṅgha of Pratyekabuddhas and Noble Śrāvakas! Homage to those headed by Maitreya, the excellent and great assembly of Noble Bodhisattvas! Homage to the Noble Vajradhara and the deities of the maṇḍala! Homage to Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and the Ṛṣis...

5. Homage to the foremost of the hosts! Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One! It is thus: Oṃ, [homage] to the heart-knot of the noose of all Tathāgatas! Blaze, blaze, O you who are the womb of the *dharmadhātu*! Move, move, O you who hold the great lotus in your hand! Hold, hold, O you who hold the great noose! Grant, grant, O you whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of excellent rays! Cross over, cross over, O you who bear vast splendor and the burden of the six perfections!

6. Ripūraṇe! Kala kala, you who wear the garb of Mahābrahmā! Mala mala, destroyer of all evil, obscurations, stains, and defilements! Dhuru dhuru, you who are purified as a Bodhisattva! Bhuru bhuru, you who are compassionate toward Great Beings (mahāsattva)! You who are saluted by Yama, Varuṇa, and Kubera! Huru huru, you who are honored and saluted by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Kumāra, Nandikeśvara, Īśvara, Maheśvara, and the sons of the gods of Maheśvara! You who wear various jeweled crowns! You who wear the crown of the Jina Amitābha! Divine...

His body is adorned with divine gems, gold, vajras, lapis lazuli, emeralds, rubies, sapphires, and pearls; he wears a white sacrificial thread (*yajñopavīta*). Adorned with a crown of matted hair and bearing a lotus fashioned from the new moon, he holds a lotus, sits upon a lotus throne, has lotus-like arms, three eyes, and holds a trident and a noose. He is consecrated by all the Tathāgatas. O you who pacify all sins, *sara sara*! O Great Compassionate One! *turu turu*, bestower of all boons! *bodhi bodhi*, beheld by all the Tathāgatas! 77a (P.130a2, D.145b3)

O Beholder of the Seat of Enlightenment! O Great Lord, Sovereign of the World! O Bearer of the Great Wish-Fulfilling Gem! O Great Compassionate One with a face as universally beautiful and exceedingly serene! Awaken, awaken! Enlighten, enlighten, O Blessed One, Womb of Light for all Tathāgatas! O Bearer of Great Merit and Splendor! O Performer of Supreme Accomplishments! O Remover of All Diseases, remover of all diseases! O You who are devoted to compassion for all sentient beings! O Liberator from all suffering! O Great Compassionate One, homage be to you, svāhā! This, O Blessed One, is my marvelous [spell].

The Heart of Avalokiteśvara’s Noose, the Heart of Amoghapāśa, the Maṇḍala of Liberation, the Heart of the Supramundane Dhāraṇī, the Heart of Noble Avalokiteśvara, the Great Multiformity; manifested through the transformations of the illusion-like samādhi, possessing a thousand arms, a thousand heads, and the gaze of a thousand eyes, empowered by a thousand mudrās; it enters into maṇḍalas equal in number to the atoms within hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Ganges rivers; [it is the essence] of all Tathāgatas—

3. It is the secret entrance, the entry into all buddha-fields; the descent upon the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*); the turning of the wheel of Dharma; the kindling of the torch of Dharma; the crushing of all wicked Māras and their hosts; the blowing of the conch of Dharma; the raising of the banner of Dharma; the warding off of all hells; the accomplishment of all ritual procedures (*kalpa*); the supreme means for curing all diseases; the establishment in the great ten stages (*bhūmi*); the entry into the state of non-retrogression; [and the presence of] all Tathāgatas—

Empowered by the empowerment of consecration; bringing about the attainment of unfailing supreme perfection; manifesting unfailing miraculous transformations; gathering in the unfailing ocean of the mind; establishing the unfailing seed of sentient beings; entering into the unfailing miraculous transformations of the bodhisattvas; proclaiming the unfailing miraculous transformations of all the Tathāgatas; setting in motion clouds of unfailing worship and service to all the Tathāgatas. <tha tha tha tha tha>

5. It is the entry into the city of fearlessness for all beings without exception; it is the unfailing fulfillment of the six perfections through the great gift of fearlessness; it is the unfailing rain of various divine flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, garments, ornaments, and the seven precious jewels; it is the unfailing manifestation of all Tathāgatas in various Buddha-fields adorned throughout one’s successive births; it is the unfailing fulfillment of the great mass of merit. The unfailing—

6. It reveals the miraculous display of supernatural powers (*ṛddhiprātihārya*) that manifests all the Tathāgatas; it accomplishes unfailing sovereignty; it reveals the chapters and ritual procedures (*kalpa*) for the vidyā-maṇḍala and mudrās; it reveals unfailing success; it reveals unfailing treasures; it increases unfailing longevity; it displays unfailing fame and renown; it brings about unfailing liberation from doubt; it unfailingly liberates one from birth, old age, and death; it bestows unfailing boons; it [is] unfailing birth—

7. The fulfillment of the ritual procedures; the fulfillment of the roots of virtue through unfailing mindfulness; the manifestation of the attainment of the status of an unfailing Vidyādhara-Cakravartin; the unfailing entry into the celestial palaces of the gods and the abodes of the thirty-three gods; the unfailing entry into the Tuṣita heaven; the unfailing entry into the Akaniṣṭha heaven; the unfailing entry into the abode of Śakra, the king of the gods in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven; and the unfailing shaking of Mount Mahāmeru with a single hand. 77b (P.131a2, D.146b4)

1. The manifestation of the sight of the Unfailing; the manifestation of the sight of unfailing invisibility; the increase of unfailing power; the manifestation of the attainment of the voice of an unfailing universal monarch over the four continents; the raining down of various jewels like an unfailing great wish-fulfilling gem; the raining down of unfailing grain; the raining down of unfailing garments; the manifestation of the raining down of unfailing ornaments and decorations—various gems, pearl necklaces, earrings, golden threads, bracelets, armlets, and bangles; and the [manifestation of] unfailing various flavors, the finest essences, and food of a hundred flavors.

2. It is the showering [of rain]; it is the manifestation of the unfailing liberation of various sentient beings; it is the displayer of the unfailing various methods of treatises, verses, discipline (*vinaya*), discourses (*sūtra*), prophecies (*vyākaraṇa*), stanzas (*gāthā*), inspired utterances (*udāna*), introductory narratives (*nidāna*), historical accounts (*itivṛttaka*), birth stories (*jātaka*), extensive teachings (*vaipulya*), marvelous events (*adbhutadharma*), instructions (*upadeśa*), and the various discourses on the Abhidharma; it is the demonstration of plunging into the unfailing great ocean of the various Mahāyāna [teachings]; it is the great power of the Bodhisattva against all yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, pretas, kumbhāṇḍas, and apasmāras.

3. They covered him [with offerings], for the purpose of hearing and seeing this *dhāraṇī-maṇḍala-mudrā*. And in these three thousand great thousandfold world-systems, which were empowered by the nature of vajra, a great and mighty earthquake occurred. A great rain of divine flowers began to fall; it was rained down for the sake of making offerings to all the Tathāgatas, for the sake of making offerings to all the Bodhisattvas, and for the sake of making the supreme great offering to this *dhāraṇī-maṇḍala*. Then, indeed, Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, with a smiling face—

4. Whirling his staff, he approached the place where the Blessed One was; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and addressed him as follows: "O Blessed One, this ritual procedure for the supramundane *dhāraṇī*-maṇḍala is exceedingly rare, since such a display of supernatural power, transformations, and miracles as these are seen—namely, the appearance of a Tathāgata. The turning of the Wheel of Dharma is seen; it should be regarded as equal to the Tathāgata himself. O Blessed One, its great majesty is supremely difficult to encounter."

5. This will be seen in Jambudvīpa; through the deeds of a Tathāgata, in the final age, in the final time, he shall perform the work of a Buddha. By merely being a śramaṇa, one obtains such qualities and benefits as these. He alone shall be a bringer of light for all sentient beings, and there is no other protector in the world except for the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Lokeśvara. The Blessed One said: "It is so, Vajrapāṇi, it is exactly as you have said. Born of father and mother—"

6. O Vajrapāṇi, all the beings of Jambudvīpa, this maṇḍala of dhāraṇīs, and this noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—[he who is] the hope, protection, refuge, and final resort for all beings, both mundane and supramundane, up to establishing all beings, whether women, men, boys, or girls, in Buddhahood; such is the power, vigor, and prowess of the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, who has set out for the sake of the welfare of previous beings.

7. Then Vajrapāṇi, the great yakṣa general, taking a great maṇi-jewel named Sūryaprabhāgarbhavimala (Stainless Interior of Solar Radiance), approached the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and offered him that great maṇi-jewel canopy. Having scattered various divine flowers for the sake of worship, he departed to his own seat.

1. Having sat down, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, entered the samādhi named Amoghavimalaviśuddhaprabhāśaraśmi (The Light-Ray of Unfailing, Stainless Purity). By means of that samādhi having been entered by the Blessed One, there appeared at the junction of his crown a gabled pavilion shaped like a parasol. From that gabled pavilion issued forth various and manifold rays of light; and by the illumination of those various rays, a great miracle of manifold supernatural transformations occurred in the expanse of the sky.

2. Manifestation of the Noble Ones: From the radiance of each individual ray of light, nine hundred and ninety billion nayutas of kotis of Tathāgata-forms appeared. All those Tathāgata-forms gave their approval to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara, saying: "Excellent, excellent, Mahāsattva! This Dhāraṇī-maṇḍala-seal that has been spoken is most difficult to encounter; it is the entry into the supramundane and preeminent seat of awakening."

3. This is the path of the [noble] eightfold path; this is the path of setting the wheel of Dharma in motion; it is the blazing forth of the Dharma, the manifestation of miraculous powers, the raising of the banner of Dharma, and the blowing of the conch of Dharma. It is the victory over the mandala of the four Māras, the treading upon the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the fulfillment of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the mastery of the four grounds of self-confidence. It is the exertion toward suchness and the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the fulfillment of the ten perfections, and this is the cultivation of the noble eightfold path. This is the path for those who have lost their way...

4. The path for the aged, the walking meditation, the dwelling place for those who have lost their way, purification, the practice for those wandering toward evil rebirths, and the treading upon the path of the Sugatas—this is the demonstration of the seed and fruit of the seat of great enlightenment (*mahābodhimaṇḍa*). Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara: "Speak, O Pure Being, the supramundane and distinguished maṇḍala of liberation, the miraculous manifestation of the Amoghapāśa."

5. The Ritual for the Preparation of the Transcendent Maṇḍala. Having heard the request from the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara spoke before the Blessed One regarding the ritual for the preparation of the maṇḍala and the means of accomplishment for the transcendent rite: "In a divine place, on excellent ground, with pure earth and lush grass, strewn with trees bearing fruit and flowers, and filled with flowering creepers; in a spot where the ground is moist and pure, and where water flows—[and] fire..."

6. One’s own delightful ground is a charming object for the mind’s aspiration, established in a vast expanse, perfectly pure and free from defilement. It is a circular area of ground, clean, pure, and thoroughly cleansed, where the skeletal remains have been removed and the heaps of excrement and filth have been discarded. Having constructed there a well-proportioned, confident, and spacious dwelling of appropriate dimensions—pure, soft, and smooth—one should establish the maṇḍala therein. There, one attains the unsurpassed awakening of a Buddha, which is transcendent and distinguished above all Tathāgatas.

7. Having consecrated it, one should have the ground excavated to a depth of one man’s height. If the soil is red, or the color of saffron, white, fine-grained, smooth, and as soft as fresh butter—this is the most excellent ground, praised by all the Tathāgatas; this is the ground equal to the stage of enlightenment (*bodhisamā*). It should be like a reliquary (*dhātugarbha*) or a shrine (*caitya*). Then the wise man should fill the pit with earth again. If the pit is filled level [with the surface], this is according to the reality of the maṇḍala. There should be no excess or deficiency.

1. Indeed, no success is ordained here for one who lacks praise [or: for whom there is no instruction]. With a cord, the wise one should mark out a mandala measuring thirty-two cubits, or sixteen cubits, or five cubits; it should be level, four-cornered, well-proportioned, and smeared with a mixture of clay and cow dung. It must be made very smooth, well-finished, soft, and supple. Then, one should trace the mandala all around with various color divisions, divided by four doors, and provided with four archways (toraṇas). Having divided the center of the mandala into a square measuring three or four cubits—[the text continues with *ra-*].

2. The divisions of the *Nyagrodha* Sūtra: the measurement of the inner lines, the three-pronged jewel-gem ornamentation, and the demonstration of the warding off, slaying, and destruction of *kumbhāṇḍas*, *apasmāras*, *vighnas*, and *vināyakas*. Thus, O Blessed One, this great *dhāraṇī* bestows great benefits; it pacifies all evils, grants fearlessness everywhere, shows the excellent path of the supramundane way, shows the path to *nirvāṇa*, and bestows the state of non-retrogression and Buddhahood. O Blessed One, this is the great *dhāraṇī* of the Heart-mantra of the Unfailing Gaze and Noose.

3. *Āryāvalokiteśvarahṛdaya*: The Proclamation of the Distinctive Qualities. It is established as the secret heart of all Tathāgatas. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara: "Excellent, excellent, Mahāsattva! This which has been spoken as the Heart-Dhāraṇī is extremely rare; it is a supramundane miraculous manifestation, the miraculous display of the qualities and supernatural powers of all Tathāgatas and all Bodhisattvas."

4. These have been proclaimed as the secret heart-mantras (hṛdaya-guhya) for all sentient beings. This is the most excellent, supreme, and sublime path for all beings—the unsurpassed and peerless proclamation of the secret heart-mantra dhāraṇīs, which are exceedingly difficult to obtain. By means of this, all sentient beings cross over to the further shore of the great flood of the ocean of saṃsāra, [escaping] from the abyss of existence. Whosoever—whether a son of good family or a daughter of good family belonging to the family of Avalokiteśvara, or a monk, nun, layman, or laywoman, or a śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa—[who recites it...]

Whether they be kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, or any other beings, by merely grasping the names of this *Amoghāvilokitahṛdaya*, this *Āścaryāvalokitāmeghahṛdaya*—the maṇḍala of liberation of all Tathāgatas—and this Great Samaya Maṇḍala, the empowerment of Vairocana through the miraculous manifestation of the reality of all Tathāgatas, one plants a great root of merit and becomes endowed with and sustained by a great mass of merit.

There will be ninety-two quadrillion times one hundred thousand nayutas of Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones, equal in number to the atoms in the sands of the river Gaṅgā, whom they shall behold face to face, hear the Dharma face to face, hear their voice face to face, and receive a prophecy face to face. By that, those Great Beings will become exceedingly embraced by a mass of great merit and roots of great virtue. This is the same for any being who now [enters] this Dhāraṇī-maṇḍala.

7. They shall hear it by receiving it according to the ritual; or they shall recite it; or they shall behold it even by mere sight. For that son of good family or daughter of good family, this shall be equal [in merit]: they will be endowed with a great mass of merit and roots of virtue. What is difficult to achieve? It will be as if they have heard and seen the Tathāgata himself. And whoever shall apply themselves to the power, vigor, and prowess of this *dhāraṇī*-maṇḍala—searching for it, writing it, reciting it, and performing the rite of its recitation—[they shall likewise attain such merit].

1. He will practice according to the ritual of the maṇḍala; he will apply himself with resolve; he will have performed great hardships. Why does he say this is difficult? It is equal to the hardships performed by the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, over three incalculable eons, until he turned the wheel of Dharma in his state as a Buddha. And if any son of good family or daughter of good family—whether a monk, a nun, a layman, or a laywoman; whether a śramaṇa, a brāhmaṇa, a kṣatriya, a vaiśya, or a śūdra; or anyone else—[should do so...]

2. There may be some being who, with great strength, vigor, and prowess, shall apply themselves to this ritual of the *dhāraṇī*-maṇḍala; who shall seek out this supramundane ritual—namely, the procedure for writing, reciting, studying, and chanting, as well as the entry into and the observance of the maṇḍala; who shall take it up, hear it, retain it, read it, master it, and attend to it with proper mental focus; and who shall contemplate it three times during the three junctions of the day. [He shall recite] the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*...

3. He shall succeed; the King of Wrath shall consecrate him, and he shall remember the procedure for reciting this dhāraṇī twenty-one times. With a heart abiding in loving-kindness and compassion, he will become one who is beyond all other sentient beings. He will have practiced the great difficult austerities; his practice of the three incalculable eons of difficult austerities will be neither less nor more [than that of others]. In this very life, he will attain a great fruit that is supramundane—namely, the state of Buddhahood.

4. He will become firmly established; he will have planted roots of merit through a great mass of *puṇya*; he will be constantly followed by Lokeśvara; and [Lokeśvara] will always hold the crown of that being’s head with his right hand, always be a granter of boons, and always appear visibly before him. Thus, this revelation of great qualities—the ritual for the *dhāraṇī*-maṇḍala and mudrās—is extremely difficult to obtain. Merely by hearing this ritual for the *dhāraṇī*-maṇḍala, [one attains...]

5. Into his ear-cavity, the sound shall fall seven times. Merely by the act of passing away and through that very state of being, he will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī. He will be born from lotuses at the feet of Amitābha in his presence. Adorned with all ornaments, he will stand before the faces of the maṇḍalas of the sūtras, kalpas, and mudrās spoken by all the Tathāgatas. He will possess the recollection of his past births, and his six sense-faculties will be completely purified. Five...

6. And one who has attained knowledge will give birth to offspring as soon as they are born, purified by divine form, color, marks, and proportions. Therefore, indeed, by means of its power, this [dhāraṇī] should be made heard, recited, and studied by all beings. One should be free from the stain of stinginess and envy; one should be endowed with all beings and devoted to loving-kindness, compassion, and mercy. And this should be made heard, shown, and introduced through the arrangement of the maṇḍala of this dhāraṇī.

7. "One must exert effort in this most extreme of times, in this final age. This method for achieving the supramundane is unsurpassed. Why say more? It should be heard with competitive zeal. Now, as soon as this dhāraṇī was spoken by the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, in a mere instant, a moment, or a brief flash, this Mount Potalaka became composed of the seven precious gems. And those flower-trees and fruit-trees [became] peaks made of the seven precious gems.

1. A gabled pavilion appeared; it manifested as many as the atoms in nine hundred and ninety million billion *koṭīs* of *gaṅgā*-river sands. Various kinds of diverse divine flowers and fruits were produced, and it was adorned with various and manifold ornaments: networks of tinkling bells, golden chimes, and lattices, suspended from canopies. Above each divine lion throne, within every single gabled pavilion, there appeared ninety-nine million lion thrones arranged.

2. On every lion-throne, the Tathāgatas from the ten directions had assembled and were seated together. And all those Tathāgatas, extending their gold-colored arms, placed their hands upon the head of the Bodhisattva Noble Avalokiteśvara and uttered the sound of "Well done!": "Excellent, excellent, Avalokiteśvara! This most distinguished supramundane Great Path has been shown for the sake of all sentient beings crossing to the further shore, by the mere hearing of which—"

3. They follow the path of Buddhahood, which is supramundane and preeminent. How much more so will those beings—who perform many recitations, writings, readings, and who behold and enter the maṇḍala—become followers of the samaya? Their embodiment as a Tathāgata is to be realized in this very life. Now, regarding that mountain, the abode of Potalaka, consisting of grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, and forests—all of these [beings] shall be one fathom in height and the size of a wagon wheel.

4. There appeared lotuses made of the seven precious gems, with petals of various colors, stalks of lapis lazuli, and pericarps the color of Jāmbūnada gold, adorned with circles of red pearls and divine pearl filaments, upon which the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas, were seated. Out of reverence for the Dharma, all those Bodhisattvas prostrated themselves on all eight limbs before the noble Avalokiteśvara, offering necklaces of pearls worth hundreds of thousands, reaching as far as the central line of his [trident-jewel-adorned] body.

5. One should draw a lotus and a vajra; outside the measurement of the lines, one should arrange a vajra-shaped railing (*vedikā*), various jewel-palaces (*vimāna*), and the variegated ornamentation of the railing. One should place the central lotus with its palace in the form of a gabled chamber (*kūṭāgāra*). Within the central maṇḍala-lotus, one should place the Sage Vairocana; likewise, Amitābha to the left, and the Tathāgata Śākyarāja to the right. [One should also place] Amogharājalokeśvara, the Protector, standing facing him with his hands joined in *añjali* and slightly bowed.

One should fashion [the deity] with four arms, or alternatively with two arms, holding various flowers and adorned with all ornaments. Standing in the presence of Amitābha, the King of Wrath (Krodharāja) is depicted with four arms, his hands joined in *añjali* and holding various divine flowers. Adorned with diverse ornaments and beautified by various silk scarves, he graces the central mandala with divine decorations. He is further embellished with the great mudrā of Amoghapāśa and a lotus seat; one should likewise cause the Jvālāgarbha [deities] to be fashioned in the four corners.

7. At the intermediate corners and the four cardinal directions, one should place those skilled in the central position: adorned by the goddess Tārā seated in the eastern position; adorned by Pāṇḍaravāsī seated in the southern position; adorned by the goddess Śvetā seated in the western position; and adorned by the goddess Padmasundarī seated in the northern position. In the outer corners of the maṇḍala, one should establish the four Great Kings; having established them in the central position, [one places] Ekajaṭā in the east. 80a (P.133b1, D.152a2)

1. Raudrī is in the west; the messenger Vikṛtānanī is with the staff (on the right); Vajrasaṅkalī is in the north; Vikarāliṇī is there; Bhṛkuṭamukhī is the rākṣasī. All of them, possessing flaming bellies and being fearless, should be placed within this inner maṇḍala. Furthermore, outside the line, one should arrange a garland of lotuses, surrounded on all sides by a mass of flames of vajras and tridents. Around the entire outer maṇḍala, one should paint the symbols, the mudrās, and the deities: Īśvara, Maheśvara, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Indra, Kumāra, and Vaśavartin, as well as the Tuṣita gods.

2. Having painted the deities from the Tāvatṛṃśa heaven up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, the various emblems of the Trāyastriṃśa deities are likewise [to be depicted]. All are established upon lotus seats. [The emblems are: the Wheel of Dharma, the Vajra, the five-pronged Vajra, the noose, the axe, the Sudarśana discus, the trident, the spear, the mallet, the staff, the hammer, the Vajra-maṇḍalī, the lotus garland, the wheel, the conch, the great mace, the sword, and the javelin; as well as the full vase, the mirror, the chest, the lotus, and the blue lotus; the banner, the parasol, and the jewel-staff.

3. At the four corners [of the mandala], one should draw the four mudrās: a vajra marked with a jewel, a jewel-vajra, and an axe-vajra, as well as a *nandikāvarta*. Also, a water-pot (*kharakuṇḍika*), a ritual pitcher (*bhṛṅgāra*), and a deer-skin sacred thread (*eṇeyayajñopavīta*). Furthermore, a canopy above, together with the moon and sun along with the stars—all these should be depicted with flames within them, distinguished by various colors. The wise one should draw the eastern gate; it should have a fierce appearance and be stepped upon by the skillful Vajrapāṇi, who holds a vajra and has flames within him. At the southern gate...

4. Kelīkīla, who is extremely fierce, is in the west; Vajrapiṅgalā is in the north; and Nisumbha should be depicted with a fierce appearance. Around the entire perimeter of the maṇḍala, one should draw garlands of lotuses and water-lilies, and in the four corners, the four Nāga kings. The gatekeepers should also be drawn: Māṇibhadra, Pūrṇabhadra, Baladeva, and likewise Pāñcika. At the inner gates, one should likewise draw the four great rivers: the Gaṅgā, the Sītā, the... [and the fourth].

5. Kṣā and Candrabhāga; by the goddess Śrī, Vāsantī, Anopamā, the earth-deity, the deity of crops and medicinal herbs, Sarasvatī, and Bhīmā, as well as the fire-deity; Hārītī, Śaṅkhinī, Caṇḍīnī, and Puṣpadantī—one should draw these all around within the garland. One should proceed with purity, using a pure painter, pure vessels, and non-adhesive pigments. [One should feed] those who eat the three white foods.

6. One should avoid that which is not accomplished, as well as bad food; [one seeking excellence] should avoid liquor, meat, onions, garlic, and mixtures containing *gṛñjanaka*. These obstructors strike down those who are emaciated. One should wear clean garments after bathing thoroughly and becoming pure. One should adorn the three types of mandalas—the various-colored mandalas—with ornaments. One should hang various banners, colored cloths, and diverse silk streamers; one should suspend celestial banners and encircle them on all sides with thread of five colors.

7. Encircling it, one should place eight blooming copper lotuses, each measuring four finger-breadths, adorned with petals, in the four corners. Having established four golden [vessels] and likewise four made of silver, one should surround them on all sides with coral threads and likewise with threads of pearls. On all sides, having placed golden threads and various jewels, immediately thereafter, one should establish a maṇḍala containing lines and lines within its womb, and place four golden vessels and four silver vessels.

1. Having placed four silver jars filled with silver, and having arranged creepers adorned with flowers of silver, gold, copper, and pearl; having placed four jars filled with gold, and having arranged creepers adorned with flowers of pearl, coral, ruby, red sapphire, silver, and gold; having filled golden vessels with powdered musk, camphor, saffron, and divine sandalwood; and having placed in silver vessels gold flowers, silver flowers, copper flowers, and ornaments of pearls, entwined with various kinds of diverse jewels—[these] four.

Having set up the crown-banners and having set up the four jewel-banners, and having hung streamers of various colors made of silk; having set up four silver bowls and burning incense of sandalwood, kasturī, camphor, and saffron; one should fill [the vessel] with water scented with various diverse fragrances, provided with the seven jewels, and covered with a golden lid. It should be bound with a clean, pure cloth, adorned with various ornaments, and placed upon a copper lotus. It should be situated upon a lotus in the inner maṇḍala. Then, outside the maṇḍala—

3. On all sides, one should place sixty-four vessels made of silver and copper filled with various kinds of powdered perfumes and ointments, as well as flowers. One should place sixty-four jars filled with iron vessels. One should set out sixty-four ladles filled with various flowering creepers and burn various incenses. At the four gates, one should place water-pots made of copper and iron, filled with scented water and adorned with decorative bands and gold ornaments.

4. Having placed sixty-four hundred banners upon it, variegated with various colors, and having adorned it with hundreds of circular garlands of various kinds of jewel-threads, one should then, outside the maṇḍala, prepare a circular base of clay and cow dung all around. Having sprinkled it above with scented water, one should mark it out with five-colored threads, divided into four gates. One should drive sixty-four stakes of khadira wood, measuring twelve finger-breadths in length, which are five-colored—into the ground.

5. Wrap it all around with a *kasūtra* cord; place sixty-four jars, vases, and pitchers filled with various offerings; having placed sixty-four saucers and bowls filled with various offerings, set out sixty-four separate offerings of various forms; having placed sixty-four complete sets of five-colored food of many kinds consisting of various snacks, and having placed various white offerings, [provide] all the necessary implements.

6. Offerings of various flavors should be fully prepared. Various fruits and various flowers should be scattered; one hundred and twenty-one garlands [should be placed] in the offering mandala, sixty-four in the outer mandala, and thirty-two in the inner (garbha) mandala. Four island-trees should be ignited. Around the entire perimeter of the offering mandala, one hundred and sixty-four lamps should be lit. [The offerings] must be free from human flesh, onions, garlic, leeks, and green roots; other various [substances]—

7. A seat should be established. The *Amoghapāśasūtra* should be recited in the four corners of the area outside the maṇḍala. At each door, the *Bhagavatī Prajñāpāramitā* should be recited by a Dharma-preacher who is well-adorned, seated upon a Dharma-throne draped with divine garments, bathed and pure, perfumed with various fragrances, clad in new, clean robes, seated upon a divine throne, and reciting with sweet, melodious, and gentle speech. [In the] western direction...

1. In the eastern direction, having placed the Amitābha image facing the Maṇḍala on a high, circular cloth-painting (*duṣya*) depicting the array of Sukhāvatī, one should place the images of Āryāvalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta. In the northeastern quarter, on a high, square platform, having placed the Śākyamuni image facing the cloth-Maṇḍala of the Vimokṣa-maṇḍala, one should place the images of Āryavajradhara and Amoghapāśakrodha. In the southern direction, on a high platform shaped like a mountain, [one should place] the Amoghapāśa cloth-painting facing the Maṇḍala...

Having established Khaṃ; having established the Tathāgata Lokendrarāja and Mañjuśrī Sarvanivaraṇaviṣkambhin; and having established the Wrathful King Duṣṭa-maṇḍala facing toward the northern direction, one should establish the Tathāgata Vairocana, Maitreya, and Kṣitigarbha. In this manner, a high place should be prepared, adorned with all [ornaments], provided with seats, and decorated with silk streamers. One should cause it to be attended by full jars adorned with all ornaments, and a fragrant mandala should be made. [There should be] various kinds of excellent, choice, white juices and various types of food.

3. One should place an alms-offering (*piṇḍapāta*) consisting of various fruits, well-prepared and heaped together. Incense mixed with sandalwood, agallochum, *turuṣka*, camphor, musk, and saffron should be offered upon a fine cloth. Here, the Vidyādhara must bathe at the three junctions of the day and change his garments at the three junctions. He must perform the ritual of recitation and fire-oblation (*jāpa-homa*) at the three junctions. Beginning from the eighth day until the full moon on the fifteenth, the Amoghapāśa mantra should be recited twenty-one times. [The mantra of] the twenty-one Wrathful Kings—

4. Having consecrated [the practitioner], one should recite twenty-one times the *Amoghapāśāṅkuśī*, the twenty-onefold *Amoghavilokitapāśahṛdaya*—which possesses supramundane miraculous power—and the *Vimokṣamaṇḍala* consisting of one thousand and eight [recitations], which is honored by all bodhisattvas. One should recite the *Vimokṣamaṇḍalapāśahṛdaya* one thousand and eight times. This should continue until the full fifteenth day, while subsisting on the three white foods; then, on the fifteenth day, throughout the day and night, one should recite the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* an immeasurable number of times.

5. One should recite throughout the entire night, free from fatigue and physical exhaustion; the recitation should be performed with a mind characterized by the resolve of loving-kindness and compassion. Having completed the procedure for the recitation, one should perform the rites of the mandala: the binding of the boundary, the binding of the directions, the protection of oneself and others, and the binding of the mandala itself. Then, one should cause the retinue to enter the mandala. Once the entry into the samaya-mandala and the rites of the mandala are completed, one should then commence the worship; this is the procedure for worship.

6. Having stood there, one should then begin the recitation. Standing facing the Amoghapāśa maṇḍala and reciting the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya one hundred and eight times, one is consecrated by the King of Wrath (Krodharāja). Immediately upon being consecrated with the recitation twenty-one times, [the practitioner] blazes forth on all sides within the entire maṇḍala of all deities; various rays of light issue forth, they utter sounds, and they grant the cry of "Well done! The Vidyādhara rejoices, his body blazes, and Noble Avalokiteśvara emerges from the center of the maṇḍala in his own form.

7. Blazing and radiant, illuminated by rays of light exceeding a hundred thousand suns, he who bears the form and attire of Brahmā with the Amoghapāśa [mantra] surveys the entire mandala-circle throughout the ten directions. They utter cries of "Well done! to the vidyādhara; extending his right arm, he places his hand upon the head [of the practitioner], saying: "Excellent, excellent, O vidyādhara! This mandala is most beautiful, supremely well-adorned and perfectly fashioned. Then follows the Vimokṣamaṇḍala of Amoghapāśa.

1. This is the miraculous manifestation empowered by all Tathāgatas and honored by all Bodhisattvas; the secret of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas; the maṇḍala of all gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and amaras; the maṇḍala that conquers all Māras and crushes all obstacles and impediments; the deliverer from the wilderness of saṃsāra for all beings—women, men, boys, girls, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and even the multitudes of birds born of the animal realm. This is it—

2. It is the liberator from all evil obstructions, the sufferings of hell, disease, birth, old age, and death; it is that which causes entry into the city of fearlessness. This is the Great Maṇḍala of Liberation, together with its heart-mantra (*sahṛdayamantra*). Therefore, O Vidyādhara, it is called the "Maṇḍala of Liberation" which is honored by all Bodhisattvas. By merely remembering it, seeing it, hearing it, or even grasping its name, one crosses to the further shore of saṃsāra. One proceeds through the state of non-retrogression and the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*), becoming irreversible in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

3. [They] attain perfect enlightenment. How much more so, then, for one who, through such a direct vision of the great maṇḍala, performs the recitation, reading, and mindfulness of the liberations, dhāraṇīs, and supramundane mantra-words, or even teaches them; or who observes a single fast, or sees [the maṇḍala] for even a moment, an instant, or a brief flash? I declare that he is equal to me, truly equal, truly equal. I, the Tathāgata, also uphold that being upon my head and protect him from both worldly and supramundane [dangers].

"4. *M*! O Vidyādhara, grant favor! Grant all that is desired as a boon, according to the intent of one's heart's desire; I give it all. Then the Vidyādhara should state his intention with the mind, and [the practitioner] grants all of that. He attains the samādhi named "Stainless Array of Unfailing Knowledge" (*Amoghajñānavyūhavimokṣavimala*). Furthermore, he attains hundreds of thousands of millions of other samādhis, equal in number to the sands of the Ganges River. He travels through the sky by means of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*). Those—

5. And all those who have entered the maṇḍala and entered into the pledge (*samaya*) and the knowledge of the pledge shall become established in the ten stages and attain the state of non-retrogression. That is to say, they shall be empowered by the prophecy of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment from which there is no turning back. This is their final dwelling in a womb; they shall no longer be stained by the impurity of a womb-dwelling. Having passed away, they will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī, born spontaneously from lotuses. From these spontaneously arisen lotuses, beings will be produced...

He shall be born adorned with all ornaments and will remember his births from birth to birth. And this *Amogharājasampada-mahākalparāja*, the *Vimokṣamaṇḍala*, the great assembly for turning the wheel of Dharma at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*) of all Tathāgatas, will abide before his very face. Seated at the seats of awakening in the Buddha-fields of all the Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions, they shall behold him; he shall receive the cry of "Excellent! from all those Tathāgatas: "Excellent, excellent, noble son! You are one whose birth is well-born and abundant; you are established in the non-retrogressive state toward unexcelled, perfect awakening. And those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, the Tathāgatas of the ten directions—golden-hued, adorned with the merit of a hundred thousand times ten million rays of light—will extend their arms and place their hands upon his head. They will comfort him and cause him to hear a discourse on the Dharma in their presence, until the final attainment of awakening. Furthermore, within that great maṇḍala, there shall be outer instrumental music, conchs, cymbals, drums, and so forth.

And those beings who are played upon by the sounds of musical instruments, upon hearing that sound, fall into the mere sound of the ear; they all become non-retrogressive and are established in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Even down to birds and those of the animal realm, upon hearing the sound, they will all become non-retrogressive. Such is the great miraculous display endowed with great transformations, the manifestation of the power of the ritual of the maṇḍala of liberation. And whichever son of good family or daughter of good family, or monk—

2. Whether it be a bhikṣuṇī, an upāsaka, an upāsikā, or any other being—be they śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, or śūdras—who shall recite this ritual of the Maṇḍala of Liberation in the midst of a great assembly; and those beings who, having heard that sound and that resonance of the name "Śramaṇa," let it fall upon their ears—they all become free from the obscurations of evil and defilement. They become liberated from former obscurations and sins. They become non-retrogressive [in their progress toward enlightenment]. They become sons of all the Tathāgatas.

3. It should be known that he is followed by the noble Avalokiteśvara; he is always a source of consolation and a constant protector until the very end at the seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). Furthermore, those beings who approach that entrance to the mandala and see even just the sight of that ground shall all become non-retrogressive (*avaivarttika*); their afflictions will be consumed by fire, and they will be completely liberated from all obscurations. And as for those who carry the dust of that place—the wind...

They shall not cause [the weapon] to fall upon their bodies; even if they are in a state of evil, all of them shall become established in the stage of non-retrogression, liberated from all sins. They shall be endowed with the constant vision of the noble Avalokiteśvara. They shall be attended by all the Tathāgatas and comforted by all the Bodhisattvas. They shall be protected by all the deities and embraced by a great mass of merit.
They will come to possess great roots of merit. Thus, by the mere sound of the word "shramana" and by the mere taking up of the name, there will be the attainment of a great fruit. // O //
Amoghapāśakalparāja – Part VI.

82a (P. 137b8, D. 156b6) 5. Thereafter, I shall proclaim the ritual procedure for the fire offering (*homa*) of the Liberation Maṇḍala. By this, one is completely purified of all sins and obscurations; likewise, one is liberated from all sufferings, from transgressions, and from the terrible oceans of afflictions. The crossing over of *saṃsāra* is accomplished, and one becomes irreversible.

6. This is the unsurpassed state; it brings comfort to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. It is the supreme vision of the supramundane path and the very vision of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. There is no doubt that by the mere offering of this oblation (*āhuti*), the gods will immediately arrive. Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Īśvara, Maheśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and even Kumāra—all will come at once through this mere *homa* offering; of this there is no doubt. So too shall the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and asuras.

7. Garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, and kumbhāṇḍas all arrive at that very moment; they all bow down at the feet of the vidyādhara for a hundred years. Day and night, they protect him on all sides. And the four great kings, together with the high-souled Vajrapāṇi, and the ten great lords of yakṣas, protect the ten directions. They ward off wicked and evil people, and they prevent all sinful and malicious beings from falling into the terrifying hells.

1. Immediately thereafter, the unsurpassed great mountain of merit and the mass of great merit proceed. Twenty palas of *candana*, five palas of *agaru*, seven palas of *turuṣka* at all times, one part each of *karpūra* and *kāstūrikā*, and the fruit of *kuṅkuma*; five palas of *kundruka* and always seven palas of *guggulu*: having ground these together into a powder and mixed them with white sugar and honey, one should form pills the size of an *akṣa*. One should offer as an oblation one thousand and eight mustard seeds mixed with parched grain (*lāja*), mixing the pills with them and anointing them with clarified butter.

2. Having kindled the fire with fuel-sticks of *rabhika*, *arka*, and *samī* wood, whenever one performs the rite of oblation by offering one thousand and eight [offerings], at each such instance they destroy all sinful obscurations and defilements; at each such instance one is completely liberated from all diseases; at each such instance one is completely liberated from all ailments; and at each such instance, for all beings in Jambudvīpa—men, women, boys, girls, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and so forth—they destroy all sinful obscurations. All evil...

3. It pacifies all plagues, all calamities, all misfortunes, all seizing spirits (*graha*), all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes; and all fears regarding one’s own army or the armies of others; all fears regarding adversaries and enemies; and all fears regarding thieves, rogues, robbers, and fierce wild beasts. Furthermore, all those beings who smell that fragrance—whether women, men, boys, or girls; whether *śramaṇas*, *brāhmaṇas*, *kṣatriyas*, *vaiśyas*, or *śūdras*—shall all become irreversible (*avaivarttika*) in their [attainment of] enlightenment.

4. They will set out for unexcelled perfect enlightenment (*anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau*). Throughout their succession of births, they will all follow after the world-system of Sukhāvatī; they will be born from spontaneously produced lotuses (*upapādukapadma*). And all those belonging to the animal realm—whether bipeds or quadrupeds—by the mere scenting of [their] fragrance, will certainly become non-retrogressive (*avaivarttika*). They will awaken to the state of unexcelled perfect enlightenment (*anuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau*) as those who are irreversible. O holders of all vidyās, in whatever manner one performs the fire-oblation (*juhati*), [so shall it be].

5. In such and such a manner, his body will become perfectly stainless and pure. When one thousand and eight [recitations] are completed, the body of the Vidyādhara blazes forth. He beholds the great forms of the Buddhas in the ten directions. And those forms of the Tathāgatas utter words of praise to the Vidyādhara: "Excellent, excellent, O Vidyādhara! This is the supreme mandala of the secret liberation of all Tathāgatas; this is the supramundane ritual for the fire-offering (homa). This is the great ritual for the fire-offering that crushes all Māras. This is..."

6. [And] the unsurpassed path to enlightenment. Then all those forms of the Tathāgatas extend their gold-colored right arms and place their hands upon the head of the vidyādhara. Thereupon, Noble Avalokiteśvara appears before him in his own form, adorned with every ornament, wearing the attire of Brahmā Amoghapāśa, decorated with a crown of matted hair, and holding a lotus, a trident, and a noose. He says to the vidyādhara: "Excellent, excellent, vidyādhara! You have accomplished the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya and the Maṇḍala of Liberation."

7. The Ritual for the Great Homa of Koṭṭara. “I grant you a boon; whatever you pray for, I shall give it all. Then the vidyādhara should state the boons as he desires, and he shall obtain them all. Noble Avalokiteśvara extends his arms and places his hand upon the crown of the vidyādhara’s head. As soon as the hand is placed there, the vidyādhara travels through the sky. He traverses all the buddha-fields in the ten directions and obtains the direct vision of all the Tathāgatas. A—

1. One attains the state of non-retrogression (*avaivarttika-avinivartanīya*). One receives the prophecy (*vyākaraṇa*) from all Tathāgatas in all Buddha-fields. Having attended upon [the Buddhas] in all Buddha-fields, one proceeds to the world-system of Sukhāvatī. There, in the presence of the Tathāgata Amitābha and before the assembly of all Bodhisattvas, one shall hear the teaching of the Dharma until the very end at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*). Therefore, I shall now explain the site for the supramundane fire offering (*lokottara-homa*).

2. Having opened up a lotus [mandala] with a circumference of three cubits, mixed with clay and cow dung, one should dig a pit in the center of the filaments of the lotus measuring one cubit in depth. Then, extending horizontally all around, one should arrange sixteen petals—five in the center—and adorn the lotus with various colorful designs. Outside the lotus, on all sides, construct a square mandala and adorn it with various fragrant substances. Around the perimeter of the mandala, place four full vases filled with silver vessels, and four *argha* bowls.

3. Filling silver vessels with various perfumes, filling four golden vessels with [perfumes], and having set out various strengthening foods (*rasabali*), as well as various kinds of the three white substances (*triśukla*) and various diverse fruits, one should scatter various flowers. Arranging various types of garlands all around the maṇḍala, one should adorn it with arrows and banners of five colors. Having placed four well-adorned jars at the four gate-divisions, filled with scented water—four [jars].

4. At the gate, one should recite the *Prajñāpāramitā* and have the well-adorned Dharma-preacher take his seat. In the four corners, one should recite the *Amoghapāśa-sūtra*. One should worship with gold flowers, silver flowers, copper flowers, and the seven precious gems upon the Dharma-seat of the well-adorned Dharma-preacher. Then, the Vidyādhara—pure, wearing clean garments, having bathed well, and being scented with fragrant perfumes—should [recite] the *Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya* over the pills eight and more times.

5. That should be recited. Having been consecrated by the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*) one hundred and eight times, the Heart-mantra of Amoghavilokita should be recited one hundred and eight times. Then, one should offer oblations (*juhuyāt*) one thousand and eight times into the mandala of the Amoghajvalanavimokṣa with the Pāśahṛdaya mantra, remaining silent. One should maintain a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*) and a heart of compassion. This is the subsequent ritual procedure (*karmānantara*). Oṃ. Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the Noble Avalokiteśvara!

To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One: Tadyathā | Oṃ padmapāṇi dhara dhara padmabhuje | jvala jvala hutāsane bhuru bhuru vimokṣabhuje | daha daha sarvamalām amoghapāṇivarade | hūṃ hūṃ | nirdaha pāpān | śama śamani lokottāraṇi | samantaraśmivarade | turu turu pravaramoghasiddhiḥ | oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ namo ’stu te svāhā || O || This is the Great [Mantra] of the Blazing Liberation Mandala.

7. This is the supreme, unsurpassed ritual for the fire-offering (*homa*) of the *Pāśahṛdayadhāraṇī*. Then, that *vidyādhara* should perform all wondrous deeds with those ashes. And whoever has those ashes fall upon their body becomes completely liberated from all obscurations and sins. Having applied a mark (*tilaka*) on the forehead, one is immediately freed from quartan fever—whether it be every second day, every third day, daily, at midnight, every half-day, yearly, or monthly.
