1. No fever occurring daily, nor continuous fever, nor intermittent fever shall remain; they flee at a distance of a hundred *yojanas*. By making a *tilaka* on the crown of the head, one is liberated from eighty-four hundred thousand planetary spirits (*graha*). And all [spirits] flee for thousands of *yojanas* in the ten directions. Having taken ashes or dust, one should scatter them facing [the threat]; in whatever place or direction they fall, there the king of *yakṣas* shall no longer [dwell].

2. Kṣetrapas, bhūtas, piśācas, pretas, kumbhāṇḍas, apasmāras, vighnas, and vināyakas—all who stand there shall flee; they will no longer be able to invade that place. By making a *tilaka* at the location of the heart, one is freed from all diseases. By making a *tilaka* at the location of the navel, one is immediately liberated from all diseases residing in the abdomen. If one touches someone bitten by poison, they will become free of poison. If one gives [this substance] to one intoxicated by poison, they will become free of poison. One should bathe with ashes [against] all *kākhorda* and *aukiraṇa* spells.

3. One should then rub [the area] with ghee over which the mantra has been recited seven times; immediately one is liberated from all diseases. If one throws [the powder] toward the clouds, no white winds will fall upon all those who eat [them]. If one throws it toward the wind, the binding of the wind is accomplished. If one throws it in the four directions, a great boundary-binding (*mahāsīmābandha*) is established. Immediately—

6. ...until they shall abide in Buddhahood. Or, one should scatter ashes over a cemetery or over a corpse that has been cremated; all those beings who have been reborn in hell will immediately fall away from hell and will be reborn in Abhirati or Sukhāvatī. Or, one should scatter [ashes] in a city, a monastery, a temple, a village, a house, or a forest hermitage in a complete circle; there will be a great boundary-binding and a great pacification. If one scatters it at the gate of a royal palace, the king will be pacified—

7. One becomes well-protected along with one's city and retinue. Even if one were surrounded by all enemies in the midst of a great multitude, at the mere moment of being so surrounded, all those people will become free from the obscurations of evil; they will also become free from disease and defilement. One accomplishes hundreds of thousands of other tasks as well. This should be applied everywhere according to one’s own inclination and intelligence. Thus it is said. Therefore, I shall proclaim the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, the supramundane cloth of the *Vimokṣamaṇḍala*.

1. // O // On a cloth or on fine Chinese silk, well-cleaned and properly prepared, measuring two cubits, three cubits, or four cubits in size—one should draw in its center Lokeśvara Amoghapāśa, wearing the attire of Brahmā, adorned with a crown of matted locks, bearing the image of the Victorious Amitābha upon his diadem, holding a crescent moon in his right hand, four-armed, and decorated with all ornaments, seated in the paryanka posture. One should depict Mount Potalaka strewn with various flowering creepers and various jewel-creepers; above it, a lion throne should be fashioned.

2. A lotus seat should be fashioned upon a lion throne adorned with all ornaments. Upon that, the noble Avalokiteśvara should be depicted seated, holding a lotus and a trident, bearing a noose, and possessing his [proper] form. His hand should be in the gesture of granting reassurance (*āśvāsa*). Above his head, there should be a gabled palace (*kūṭāgāra-vimāna*) inlaid with various divine jewels, having the appearance of a railing (*vedikā*). Upon that railing, seven Tathāgatas should be fashioned, adorned with all ornaments, seated on lotus seats according to their proper proportions. Above that Tathāgata, in the center—

3. And the Noble Avalokiteśvara is to be fashioned surrounded by a circle of thirty-two Tathāgatas. Within that circle of Tathāgatas, various blazing rays of light are to be fashioned. Furthermore, a garland of tridents is to be fashioned for that very circle, consisting of thirty-two [elements].

The deities are to be fashioned. In the center above, Vajradhara is to be made with a distorted face, gaping, and brandishing a vajra. Then [are to be placed] Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Īśvara, Maheśvaradevaputra, Indra, the Tridaśendra, the Akaniṣṭha devaputras, the Tuṣita devaputras, the Nirmita devaputras, the devaputras Candra and Sūrya, the four Mahārājās—Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Kumāra—and the deity Agni, Mahākāla, and so forth.

5. The gods Nandikeśvara, Nanda, Upananda, Baladeva, Pūrṇabhadra, Māṇibhadra, and the Śuddhāvāsa deities, as well as the sons of the gods belonging to the Paranirmitavaśavartin realm, are to be depicted. A circle of deities is to be made, and a lotus garland is to be fashioned all around. Outside the lotus garland, it should be arranged so that a vajra-trident is encircled by hands emerging from all sides. They are to be depicted holding various flowers, various jewels, and various weapons on all sides.

6. A garland of flames (jvālāmāla) should be fashioned. On the right side, Noble Tārā should be depicted seated in the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka), gazing up at the face of Noble Avalokiteśvara; she holds a blue lotus, a jewel, and a gem in her hands and is adorned with all ornaments. Behind her, Bhṛkuṭī should be fashioned, holding various flowers and adorned with all ornaments. On the left, Śvetā should be fashioned seated in the half-lotus posture, holding a white water-lily (kumuda), a jewel, and a gem in her hands, looking toward Avalokiteśvara, and [adorned] with various...

Adorned with various ornaments, behind her, Padmasundarī should be made white. She holds various flowers and is adorned with all ornaments. Below the white Tārā-devī, the ten Pāramitās should be made; they all have their heads bowed, wear white garments, are adorned with all ornaments, and stand upright. On the right side, the Rākṣasī Ekajaṭā should be made fierce (raudrī); she sits in the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka), has four arms, and holds a noose, an axe, a sword, and a vajra in her hands.

1. One should depict Āryāvalokiteśvara looking [at them], with a female messenger (dūtī) on his left whose face is terrifying with bared fangs, adorned with all ornaments. She should have four arms, holding a vajra, an axe, a noose, and a trident, and be seated in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*), gazing at Lokeśvara who is ablaze within. Between the Potalaka mountain and the interior [of the scene], the Naga kings Nanda and Upananda should be depicted together with their palaces and Naga maidens. Above, they should be shown holding various flowers and lifting up the Blessed One Lokeśvara. Below the mountain—

Above the roof of the gabled pavilion (kūṭāgāra), the Caitya of the Eight Great Fears is to be made in a single row, and it is to be decorated with the same ornaments as the decoration of a caitya. The victory [scene] should be depicted. Noble Vajradhara should be depicted with a fly-whisk in his hand. Below him, ṛṣis and sons of gods should be depicted. He should be depicted worshipping the Blessed One with various flowers. On the left side, the Turning of the Wheel of Dharma should be depicted. Ānanda-Vajradhara should be depicted worshipping the Blessed One with a fly-whisk in his hand. Noble Avalokiteśvara and Amoghapāśa should be depicted on the right side facing the Blessed One, worshipping the Blessed One.

On the left side, the Wrathful King (Krodharāja) should be depicted worshipping the Blessed One; beneath him, the hosts of ṛṣis and gods should be depicted worshipping the Blessed One. To the left and right of the cloth, all around the exterior, one hundred and eight images of Tathāgatas should be made, seated in the cross-legged posture (paryaṅka) upon lotus seats according to their proper proportions. They should be adorned with ornaments. A Vidyādhara should be depicted at the base of the lion-throne of the noble Avalokiteśvara.

5. One should prostrate with the knees on the ground, holding in one's hands a flower, incense, and a handful of cow-dung. The face of the noble Avalokiteśvara should be depicted. One must be pure, well-bathed, and wear clean garments; one should have eaten various delicious foods that are white in color. One should paint [the image] using pure, new vessels and non-sticky pigments. Furthermore, one must avoid various kinds of bad food and poor clothing, and abstain from alcohol, meat, onions, garlic, leeks, and mixed impurities.

6. One must be diligent day by day; one must rinse the mouth with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*); one must be free from impurity, stinginess, and envy; one must possess the resolute intention of loving-kindness and compassion and be devoted to faith in the Three Jewels. It should be painted on a cloth of fine silk (*duṣyapaṭa*), painted with various colors perfumed with camphor and musk. One must be undisturbed and avoid socializing; one must avoid sloth and torpor. Thus it should be painted.

7. It must be performed in this way by one who has well-prepared [the site] through ritual action (*karmakṛta*). It should be painted during the bright fortnight (*śuklapakṣa*), and not painted during the dark fortnight (*kṛṣṇapakṣa*). It should be commenced under a highly auspicious lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*) and on a day with a very propitious date (*tithi*). [It should be done] under the auspicious Puṣya lunar mansion, which is praised by all the Tathāgatas, presided over by all the Bodhisattvas, and blessed by all the deities. Any son of good family or daughter of good family, or monk, nun, layman, or laywoman—85a (P143a2, D162a4)—[should do so].

1. Whether they be śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, or śūdras; or women, men, boys, or girls—whoever beholds this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, which is honored by all bodhisattvas, beheld by all tathāgatas, the secret of the great seat of enlightenment (*mahābodhimaṇḍala*), and the secret of the maṇḍala of liberation—the great cloth-painting (*mahāduṣyapaṭa*)—upon the mere sight of that cloth-painting, they shall become completely liberated from all sins and obscurations. This applies even to one who has committed the five deeds of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*), is destined for the Avīci hell, has rejected the true Dharma, or has slandered the noble ones (*ārya*).

2. Who, upon merely seeing [this], shall have all their sins purified and liberated—without exception, including all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas—and shall be embraced by the Great Vow (mahāsaṃvara)? It should be known that they are worthy of being seen at the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) in the presence of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Ganges-river sands of Buddhas, as they approach the seat of awakening, turn the wheel of Dharma, and dwell in the mountain abodes and celestial palaces of Potalaka, within the circles of their assemblies, together with the noble Avalokiteśvara.

3. This vision in the presence of the Lord is equal to seeing a fine cloth of silk; herein no doubt or uncertainty should be produced. By the clarity of mind for a single moment, one will be embraced by a great mass of merit. One will become endowed with the planting of great roots of virtue. One will be granted boons through the empowerment of Avalokiteśvara. And one will be protected by all the Tathāgatas. With body and mind completely purified—

And thus it shall be: he will have all his faculties completely purified; he will be free from the stains of stinginess and envy; he will behold all the pleasant worlds; he will be long-lived; and he will be free from all diseases. Upon passing away from that state, he will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī. He will remember his births in every life and will be born spontaneously within lotuses; he will be irreversible.

5. Upon the mere sight of the Tathāgata Amitābha, whoever shall worship this cloth-painting (duṣya) has thereby worshipped all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions. This is his final dwelling in a womb; he shall no longer fall into the darkness of ignorance. Thus, this ritual procedure for the cloth-painting, which is the unsurpassed method for supramundane accomplishment, is equal to the peerless and the unequalled. O! Therefore, the supramundane accomplishment of the mantra ritual— (Note: The text provided ends with "pra-", indicating the beginning of a new section.)
