Furthermore, no bodily sensations of illness shall arise for them; they shall be eternally endowed with happiness and possess bodies free from ailment. // O // The Knowledge-mantra for Purifying the Ground // O // Homage to the Triple Gem. Homage to the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great...

To the pericarp: *tadyathā oṃ amogha drumalatāvṛkṣaśākhapatrapuṣpaphalaviṭapārohanadītaḍāgapuṣkiriṇyotsahradasundaraprasravaṇavividhavicitra pariśodhaya padmabhuja / sama sama samantena parimaṇḍala pariśodhaya / mala mala vimala nirmala supariśuddhapadmopalipta / jalamalāṃ viśuddha śodhaya śodhaya paramamahāśuddhasatva hūṃ phaṭ svāhā / namo tribhuvane hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* By this [mantra]...

1. Having consecrated sandalwood, red sandalwood, mustard seeds, and white mustard seeds with mantras, one should sprinkle them upon tree trunks, flowering trees, fruit trees, various creepers, grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, rivers, lakes, ponds, pools, and beautiful springs. All of these will become sprinkled with ambrosia (*amṛta*). They will all come to possess divine flowers and fruits; even the grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, and forest trees will become divine. And those who merely touch them, as soon as they are touched, will all become free from stains, devoid of stinginess and envy, and rid of [the imbalances of] bile, phlegm, and wind.

2. The giver [of this water] shall have a foul-smelling body, yet both internally and externally they shall become completely purified. Those whose internal bodies are afflicted by various diseases and ailments shall all be fully liberated; they shall be cleansed, destroyed, and shall become utterly pure and stainless. And those who bathe with that water shall be bathed with the divine waters of the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*). They shall be bathed from all stains, sins, and obscurations. They shall be bathed with the water of the eightfold path (*aṣṭāṅga-jala*). And those who shall consume that tooth-stick...

3. At the end, he will be greatly increased in mindfulness, intelligence, and wisdom; he will be free from all sorrow; he will be liberated from all bonds. And his mouth will constantly emit the fragrance of a blue lotus; he will possess smooth and sweet speech; he will have gentle words; he will be pleasant in conversation; he will be beloved and pleasing to all people; he will become a lord of the *kinnaras*; and [he will master] all treatises, rituals, mantras, and the Mahāyāna.

4. By merely hearing it, one grasps it; it remains upon the tip of the tongue. And those who smell that flower, which is bound as a garland, will become adorned with the flowers of the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*). They will be consecrated by the consecration of the Tathāgatas. Their sense of smell will be purified, and they will be endowed with the touch of divine fragrance. Their tongue will be purified like the petal of a lotus, and their complexion will be like that of divine teeth. Whoever—

5. He shall always be a lord of brothers-in-law; women, men, wives, and daughters shall come under his control. When he passes away, upon the change of birth, he will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī. He will be born from spontaneously appearing lotuses and will possess the recollection of his past lives. This is the mantra for purifying fruits, flowers, water, trees, grasses, shrubs, and medicinal herbs. Om. Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the Noble Avalokiteśvara...

To the Lord Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Greatly Compassionate One: Tadyathā | Oṃ amogha-amale trimale vimale nirmale divyapariśuddhe sarvamalopakarṣite | mahābodhisattvavarade pravarapariśuddhe | mahāmaṇiratnakāyapariśuddhe maṇimaṇi śodhani mahāmoghacintāmaṇiśuddhe | hṛdayaśuddhe kāyanirmalamahāmaṇipariśuddhe | huru huru pravarapāṇi mahābhujava-

7. *Rade turu turu mahāsattvavatsale / pariśodhaya māṃ sarvapāpāt suviśuddhamale svāhā //* By means of this vidyā, the vidyādhara should purify his own body. One should fill a new earthen jar with sandalwood water, saffron water, kastūrikā water, camphor water, and mustard seeds mixed with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). This vidyā should be recited one thousand and eight times over it. [The practitioner] should be bathed with a white cloth. Seven times—[seven palas]—should be drunk. 87b (P.146b4, D.166b7)

1. It must be done. Immediately upon being bathed, one should consecrate oneself with the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*). By merely being bathed and consecrated at once, one’s own self will become perfectly pure and stainless both internally and externally. One will be free from the obscurations and defilements of evil; one will be free from the afflictions and diseases of the *kleśas*; one will be free from old age and the like. One will be completely liberated from all obstacles, obstructors, Māras, and so forth. One will be abandoned by all yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, and piśācas. Furthermore, [one's] knowledge—

2. It is possible to approach the presence of Dhara for the purpose of removing obstacles; one accomplishes the vidyā with ease, sleeps in comfort, awakens in comfort, and dwells in comfort for as long as life lasts. With all impurities abandoned, there shall be a vision of all the Tathāgatas and a vision of the Bodhisattvas. There shall be a direct vision of the noble Avalokiteśvara at the time of death, and together with that existence, one will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī, arising spontaneously from lotuses in the presence of the Tathāgata Amitābha.

3. Whom will she give birth to? [One who] is adorned with all ornaments, whose body is embellished with the primary and secondary marks (*lakṣaṇa-vyañjana*), and who will possess the recollection of former births (*jāti-jātismara*). He will travel from buddha-field to buddha-field until he reaches the culmination of awakening (*bodhi-paryavasāna*). Furthermore, this circle of liberation (*vimokṣamaṇḍala*) and the ritual manual (*kalpa*) of the Heart of Amoghapāśa shall remain present before his mouth in its entirety; as well as other various and diverse [teachings] composed in beautiful verses, and the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgata.

4. They shall abide at the tip of the tongue; they will remember their births within the interval of a hundred thousand eons. Oṃ amoghapadmavimale prasara samantamukhe svāhā. This is the mantra for the division of the instructions on the maṇḍala lines. Oṃ amoghavividharūpavicitragandharasabharapravarabhuje svāhā. This is the mantra for the painting of the colors, the forms, the divisions, the signs, and the weapons. Oṃ amoghasamantaparimaṇḍalapāśabaddhe.

5. HŪṂ. For the binding of the maṇḍala, with mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited seven times: OṂ AMOGHASAMANTADAŚADIGMAHĀSĪMĀBANDHAYA DHURU DHURU HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ. For the binding of the boundary, with water and mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited seven times: OṂ AMOGHARAKṢAṆAPAŚAHASTE BHURU BHURU SVĀHĀ. For self-protection, with scented water and mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited seven times: OṂ AMOGHACŪḌĀMAṆI HURU HURU NAGAPĀŚABADDHE HŪṂ SVĀHĀ. This is the mantra for binding the topknot (śikhā), to be recited twenty-one times.

6. // [220] Oṃ amogharakṣā samantena mahāpāśe bhuru bhuru svāhā // Protection for the disciple and his companions should be performed with mustard seeds and ashes, over which the mantra has been recited twenty-one times. [221] Oṃ amoghajalavimale suru suru svāhā // This is the bathing mantra; it is used with scented water over which the mantra has been recited twenty-one times. [222] Oṃ amoghāmṛtabindu cara cara svāhā // O // This is the mantra for sipping water (upaspṛśana). [223] Oṃ amoghavidyāvastre curu curu svāhā<ḥ> // This is the mantra for the garment. [224] Oṃ amoghabhuga(ja)-

7. *Ja(ga)kavacavarade ciri ciri svāhā* // This is the armor-mantra (*kavaca-mantra*). With white mustard seeds and saffron water: [225] *Oṃ amoghabrahmabhuje paryantena prasara svāhā* // This is the sacred thread mantra (*yajñopavīta-mantra*). [226] *Oṃ amoghacūḍāmaṇipadme abhiṣiñcaya mama sarvatathāgatābhiṣekair maṇi maṇi svāhā* / This is the consecration mantra (*abhiṣeka-mantra*). [227] *Oṃ amoghapadmavasuvandhare dhare dhara dharaṇi maṇḍe hūṃ* // This is the seat mantra (*āsana-mantra*). [228] *Oṃ amoghasamantaparyaṅke bhuvanabhuve svāhā* //

1. The mantra for the seat (*paryaṅka*): *Oṃ amoghasurabhipadme para para hūṃ*. The mantra for flowers (*puṣpa*): *Oṃ amoghavividhagandhaprasaraiḥ puru pūrṇṇabhuje svāhā*. The mantra for incense (*gandha*): *Oṃ amoghavividhalepanapravare piri piri svāhā*. The mantra for unguents (*vilepana*): *Oṃ amoghagaganasphuraṇamayai dhūra dhūra hūṃ*. The mantra for incense smoke (*dhūpa*): *Oṃ amoghaśuklarasarasāgrādhara vidhara hūṃ*. The mantra for the food offering (*bali*): *Oṃ amoghapravarānnavilokite kiri kiri hūṃ*. [This applies to] all types of offerings (*sarvatṛka*). The mantra for food (*āhāra*): [Oṃ amoghapravarānnavilokite kiri kiri hūṃ].

2. The *limantra*: Oṃ vividhāmoghamaghama(pha)la para para hūṃ. This is the *phalamantra*. [236] Oṃ amoghādbhutagandhavare hūṃ. This is the *arghamantra*. [237] Oṃ amoghavividhamaṇibhūṣaṇavaravare jvala jvala hūṃ. This is the *alaṃkārapaṭṭapatākaśarapañcaraṅgikasūtramantra*. [238] Oṃ amoghavividhabhājane jaya jaya svāhā. This is the *bhājanamantra*, common to all three. [239] Oṃ amoghapravarabhavanabhuve thara thara svāhā. This is the *praveśamantra*. [240] Oṃ amoghanamaskaraṇasarvvata-

3. <Ta>tāgatāñjali hūṃ // This is the mantra for the salutation-gesture (namaskārāñjali). [241] Oṃ amoghacakre duru duru praduru svāhā // This is the mantra for circumambulation (pradakṣiṇa). [242] Oṃ amoghasamanta yāntu bhavane bhava bhava svāhā // This is the mantra for invocation (āvāhana). [243] Oṃ amoghacintāmaṇe prakarṣaya dhuru dhuru svāhā // This is the mantra for supplication (āyācana). [244] Oṃ amoghanimantraṇavimokṣamaṇḍale mili mili svāhā // This is the mantra for invitation (nimantraṇa). [245] Oṃ amoghamahāraśmijvālasahasre...

4. *Jvala jvala samante svāhā*. This is the lamp mantra. [246] *Oṃ amoghapāśahaste prasara gacchasva bhavanaṃ visarjito 'si sara sara hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. This is the dismissal mantra. [247] *Oṃ amoghapāśabandhasamantamahāsamayadṛḍhe hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. This is the pledge (samaya) mantra. [248] *Oṃ amoghasamante pravara sara sara prasara mahābhūteśvara dhiri dhiri hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. With this mantra, [one should offer] sweetmeat balls (*laḍḍuka*).

5. One should offer an oblation (*bali*) consisting of sweetmeats (*modaka*), parched grain flour (*saktu*), radish, and tubers, as well as a white oblation, to Mahāgaṇapati. Having caused flowers and incense to be offered, [it is said: "It is no longer possible for obstacles (*vighna*) to arise. Now I shall explain the mudrā of the supramundane maṇḍala. By merely grasping it, all evil deeds are destroyed; the obscurations of afflictions (*kleśa*), karma, and all defilements are utterly shattered. This is the reality (*tattva*) of the liberation-maṇḍala, the family, and the commitment-mudrā (*samayamudrā*). One should place a lotus in the hand and meditate.

6. Placing the thumbs together, with the two hands concentrated in the shape of a hook (aṅkuśa) by means of the middle fingers—this is the Mudrā of the Samaya of Liberation, empowered as the Amoghapāśa. It is the bringer of the fruit and the path, the excellence of the supramundane. OṂ PADMABHUJE PADMAKARE PADMAVIMALE SVĀHĀ. The wise one, the foremost of those who hold the supreme Samaya, should always form the Vajra-lotus; with the middle fingers slightly bent, it is always held in the hand in the shape of a lotus. For whomsoever this Mudrā of Vision is shown in the world...

7. There shall be incomparable sovereignty; through the *vimokṣamudrā*, there shall undoubtedly be incomparable Buddhahood. This seal, the wondrous *vimokṣamaṇḍala*, is honored by all Bodhisattvas. OṂ PADME SUPADME VIMOKṢAMAṆḌALAPADMABHUJE SVĀHĀ. Having established the lotus-binding (*padmabandha*), one should contract the middle fingers into a vajra-lotus. This is the seal of the secret liberation of all Tathāgatas, which demonstrates the reality of liberation. By merely seeing this seal, all misdeeds are destroyed. 88b (P.148a7, D.168b4)

1. Oṃ amoghe vajrapadmabhuje mili mili svāhā. With both hands joined at the wrists, the *vajra*-shaped jewel seal (*mudrā*) is formed; this is the *Cintāmaṇi* seal. It makes one's actions unfailing (*amogha*), raining down the supreme worship of the Unfailing One. It fulfills the six unfailing perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*), brings about the unfailing vision of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and is the secret mandala of the unfailing liberation that purifies the five sins of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*). Oṃ amoghamani mani mahāmani padmamani svāhā. One should form the *vajrapadma* (lotus-vajra) *añjali*; [one should perform] the *padmasphuraṇa*...

2. This mudrā, which is fearless, shaped like a middle-sized hook, and most beautiful, is a mudrā that can be seen by those capable of seeing it; it yields great and wondrous fruit. It is supramundane and distinguished, and it brings about the vision of the Buddhas of the three times. Oṃ amoghavajre mahāpadme ñjali sujali mahājali svāhā. Forming the vajra-heart-lotus and the complete vajra-bind, one should press the threatening finger into the shape of a hook. This mudrā possesses great splendor and great power and prowess; it is the locus that effects all accomplishments and the bestower of all accomplishments.

3. Oṃ! The unsurpassed, great supramundane accomplishment for the sake of Buddhahood; the unsurpassed accomplishment that removes all sins. Oṃ amoghasiddhe sarvatathāgatasiddhe avalokaya siddhe mahāvipulasiddhe kuru kuru svāhā. Having placed the lotus-añjali gesture, standing thus with the body upright, one should extend the little fingers and thumbs and slightly bend the middle fingers. This is the Great Being Padmeśvara, the Guru Lokeśvara, who is the perpetual Maṇḍala of Liberation.

4. "Worshipped by all Bodhisattvas"—thus [is it said]. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa. By the mere sight of this seal, one becomes equal to the sight of Lokeśvara; this supreme seal of sight is equal to the Maṇḍala of Liberation. One attains the state of non-retrogression (*avaivarttikatva*). By the mere sight and application of this seal, for one who knows the ritual commitment (*samaya*), there shall be [realization] everywhere. By the mere grasping of the sight of this seal, one obtains a great fruit: the immediate, unsurpassed awakening of a Buddha.

5. *M* iti // O // [255] Homage to the Triple Gem! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One! *Oṃ*, you who are the great pure being (*mahāśuddhasatva*) beheld by all; you who wear earrings that radiate light in every direction; you who wear a crown of Amitābha; you who are adorned with a crown of matted locks and a fresh vajra-moon; move, move! Gather, gather! To the lotus-handed Lord of the World, *svāhā*! These seven are the great mudrās that reveal the supramundane fruit. Darśa...

6. Who? He who sets in motion the wheel of Dharma on the path to the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*). The abode of the Lord of the World, the eternal teacher of Lokeśvara. There are seven seals (*mudrā*), the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*), accompanied by a retinue of seventy million. Where these seven Great Seals operate, the supreme seals are grasped; the seventy million Great Seals become set in motion and are grasped. All of them become honored and venerated; they are esteemed and their names are taken up [in devotion]. These seven Great Seals are present everywhere.

7. Accomplishing the mantra: it is to be employed in all places and for all rites; the mudrā that accomplishes everything is the unsurpassed path of the supramundane. The practitioner who, having bathed well and being pure, performs this mudrā of the manifestation of movement, shall not go to an evil destiny or hell. Merely by the performance of this mudrā, they will immediately see their former obscurations cleared away and will have planted roots of merit in the presence of seven hundred thousand *niyuta* of *koṭi* (seven hundred trillion) perfectly enlightened Buddhas. They will have accumulated a great mass of merit.

1. He shall become one who has fulfilled the six perfections; he shall be established on the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*); he shall attain the state of non-retrogression. Even one who has committed the five deeds of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*), who has rejected the true Dharma (*saddharma*), or who has slandered the noble ones (*ārya*)—destined for the Avīci hell—if [he receives this] merely by grasping the seal or merely by seeing it, all these evils shall be destroyed instantly. He shall be embraced by all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; he shall be well-guarded by all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, and piśācas. I—

2. O Great King, Śiva and Maheśvara, along with the four—Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Kumāra—will always and continuously provide protection, defense, and guardianship for him. He will be pleasing to behold for all sentient beings. He will possess a body that is a treasury of relics, equal to a caitya-bhūta. His body will be as firm as a diamond. Poison shall not affect him, nor fire, nor weapons, nor water, nor lightning; there shall be no fear of rats, no lions, no fierce beasts, no venomous snakes, no thieves, no robbers, and no [evil spirits] in his home.

3. No longer shall there be falling away, nor shall yakṣas, rākṣasas, or grahas, nor any disease, afflict him. No fear of poison, *kākhorda* spells, or magical incantations shall assail his body, nor shall he ever see evil dreams. He shall constantly behold the Tathāgata; he shall behold the Bodhisattvas; and he shall always behold the noble Avalokiteśvara. He shall always be a granter of boons, and all the deities shall constantly and perpetually desire to see him.

4. They shall exist; and his virtue and merit shall blaze eternally. His body shall be resplendent with glory, and he shall become one whose person shines brilliantly. Everywhere he shall be highly honored. He shall be greatly venerated by kings, ministers, brahmins, and householders, along with their harems and retinues. Even from the thirty-three celestial abodes, Śakra the lord of the gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, and Kubera will desire to honor him.

5. He shall become a youth, a host of sages, and one worthy of great veneration. All sentient beings will always desire to see him, and they will constantly long for his pleasing appearance. The vidyādhara must be well-bathed, pure, and wear clean garments; his body should be anointed with various perfumes and scented with various incenses. He should smear both arms with white sandalwood and saffron, which have been scented with camphor and musk, and he must remain pure on the ground.

6. In a secluded place, one should sit in the cross-legged posture (paryaṅka) before a cloth banner, or before an image of the Buddha, or before the noble Avalokiteśvara; one should perform this mudrā, performing the mudrā at the front of a caitya containing relics (dhātugarbha). This should be done according to the ritual for worshipping the Buddha, with the offering of water for the feet (argha-pādya) and so forth. One must possess a mind of loving-kindness (maitrī) and compassion (karuṇā); one must be intent on pity for all sentient beings, with a heart pervaded by great compassion (mahākaruṇā), regarding all sentient beings as if they were an only son.

7. One must maintain mental attention upon the noble Avalokiteśvara; one must cultivate mindfulness through mental attention upon the Buddha. This sevenfold great seal (*saptamahāmudrā*) should be set in motion; thus, seven crores of seals will have been set in motion. Now, I shall explain the presence (*sāṃnidhya*): presence is the vision of supramundane reality, the miraculous manifestation of Amoghapāśa, and the direct vision of his own natural body (*svābhāvikātmabhāva*), whether in the midst of the royal court or within the inner apartments.

In a great assembly (*mahāsambheda*), in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a multitude of monks, or within a monastic community (*nikāya*); in a circle of the fourfold knowledge; among ascetics (*śramaṇa*) and brahmins (*brāhmaṇa*), and among the multitudes of kṣatriyas, women, men, boys, girls, *viṭas*, *śūdras*, and vaiśyas—in their midst, there is direct perception of the immediate miraculous manifestation of the Amoghapāśa: the transcendent passing away and rebirth of those who are past, those who are future, and those who are present; the reality of birth, action, and the fruit of non-action; and the passing away and rebirth through what is auspicious or inauspicious, and through sovereignty.

Whether it be poverty or the attainment of kingship, the enjoyment of divine pleasures, or the thirty-two celestial abodes; whether it be the state of Śakra, the state of Brahmā, or the status of Viṣṇu and Maheśvara forever; or birth among the *nāgas*, *pretas*, *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, and *guhyakas*; or the vision of the terrible hells arising from calamities, seen as far as the limits of Avīci; or birth in a Brahmin family, a Kṣatriya family, or birth in various other diverse lineages—all this is seen as if before one's eyes through the power of the Lord of the World, as everything achievable by worldly karma is revealed.

3. Victory or defeat, security or famine, pestilence or calamity; whether it be the army of another or one's own, an adversary or an enemy, or even a battle and conflict; long life or short life, illness or health; rain or excessive rain, drought or untimely rain; sovereignty or its loss, prosperity or misfortune, arrival or departure, the acquisition of wealth and grain, increase or decrease, or famine—[all these he knows].

4. Whatever vision there may be—whether the present operations of the karma of *saṃsāra*, deeds well-done or ill-done, wholesome or unwholesome, increase or decline, the obtaining of birth, a good birth, a son, or a daughter; or the obtaining of a good son or a bad son; or whether one is meritorious or lacking merit while situated in the womb—all such visions are undoubtedly the result of the application of well-performed actions. Neither the lunar day (*tithi*), nor the asterism (*nakṣatra*), nor the day and night (*ahorātra*) are prescribed [as requirements]; it depends solely upon the recitation (*jāpa*), the offering (*bali*), and being pure, clean, and well-bathed.

5. Wearing that pure garment, speaking the truth, possessing a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*), serving the teacher (*guruśuśrūṣā*), O bearer [of the vow], consuming pure food and drink, and avoiding mixed food; avoiding liquor, meat, onions, garlic, *gṛñjanaka*, and food made from refuse; and avoiding the leavings of others—one who desires the specific goal should perform this rite. This is to be accomplished, for its manifestation is directly perceived everywhere. One practicing the vow (*vratacārī*) should not despise [others] nor show disrespect; one must never act behind the back [of the teacher], according to the instruction.

6. This is the supreme [instruction]. This Lord of the World, the Protector, spoke thus: Having fashioned a mirror made of silver, perfectly circular, sixteen finger-breadths in width, with a seat of a copper lotus and a handle for the mirror measuring one cubit in height—one should fashion the Noble Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa [therein]. Alternatively, he may be made of silver or gold; the lotus seat should measure four finger-breadths, and he should be depicted with four arms, holding a trident, a noose, a lotus, and a jewel-gem, well-purified, beautifully crafted, and radiant.

7. It must be purified. Then the Vidyādhara should place the relics within the body of the mirror-image of Lokeśvara; the body should be filled with camphor and musk. A garland inlaid with various jewels and flowers of silver and gold should be fastened all around the mirror. Then the Vidyādhara, having recited the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya one hundred and eight times over that mirror at each of the three junctions of the day, should consecrate it with the King of Wrath (Krodharāja). When the full eight thousand recitations are completed, the mirror blazes forth.

1. Various colors become a single flame. Divine water flows from that image of Lokeśvara, and various rays of light issue forth. Thereupon, the body of the vidyādhara blazes and rejoices. He attains the accomplishment of the ritual manual (*kalpa*) of the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa, named "The Immaculate Joy of Unfailing Bliss" (*Amoghaprītivimalā*), and his body will become perfectly stainless and pure. Then, the vidyādhara must manifest before the eyes of all the world the miraculous power (*vikurvaṇa*) of the accomplishment of Amoghapāśa. Then, by the vidyādhara, a square [mandala]...

2. Having prepared a mandala base mixed with clay and cow dung, four cubits in width and two cubits in height, it should be made very smooth and well-finished. Dividing it with the cord-line, one should arrange the various color sections; divided by four gates, one should delineate the central womb. One should paint one hundred and eight lotus petals for the mandala-lotus, skillfully using various colors, with a circular arrangement of filaments and a pericarp. The circumference of the lotus should be square, decorated with a railing (*vedikā*), adorned with various jewels. And at the four corners of the railing—

3. One should draw the four Great Kings, armored, girt with mail, fierce in form, and terrifying. In the locations of the central altars, one should draw the deities in the intermediate spaces between the altars: Īśvara, Maheśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Kuvera, Kumāra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Indra, Vajrapāṇi, Ekajaṭā, Tārā, Śvetā, Bhṛkuṭī, and Vajradūtī. They should be depicted with various colorful hues, adorned with all ornaments, and with all manner of diverse flowers.

4. These [deities] are to be fashioned. Outside the altar, a garland of tridents (triśūla-mālā) and a garland of vajras are to be made, as well as a lotus garland all around. Within the space between the garlands and in the four corners, the eight goddesses are to be fashioned: Bhīmā, Anopamyā, Vāsantī, Śrī, Sarasvatī, Pṛthivī-devatā, Saṃkhinī, and Puṣpadantī. They are to be depicted adorned with all ornaments, holding various flowers and jeweled vessels. Around the interior and exterior of the garlands, the mandala is to be [filled] with various perfumes.

5. One should smear white sandalwood paste mixed with saffron and perform worship in various ways. One should worship with camphor and musk and decorate the entire mandala on all sides with five-colored silk banners, as well as autumnal archways (*toraṇa*). Four silver vessels filled to the brim with *pūrṇapūra* should be placed. Four silver vessels should be filled with the three white offerings (*triśuklabali*). Four silver vessels for the water of honor (*argha*) and the water for washing the feet (*pādya*) should be set out. [Four silver vessels for the water of honor and the water for washing the feet should be set out.]

6. One should fill eight vessels with offerings of various flavors. One should arrange various kinds of fruits. One should set out an offering of food consisting of various types of edibles. One should set out the base of various scents, ointments, and silver vessels. Eight silver ladles should be filled. While burning various incenses—sandalwood, agallochum, turuṣka, camphor, kasturikā, saffron, resin, and kunduruka—one should scatter silver, copper, and golden flowers upon the inner maṇḍala, and [scatter them] outside the maṇḍala as well.

7. Having scattered flowers as they were obtained outside the maṇḍala, one should arrange garlands all around it. Then, having well-adorned that mirror, the Vidyādhara—being pure, having bathed well, and wearing clean garments—should place it facing east upon the filaments and pericarp of the lotus in the central maṇḍala. Having performed all the ritual duties for the maṇḍala, he should sit cross-legged facing the mirror and recite the Heart Mantra of the Noble Amoghapāśa.
90b (omitted in P; D.172b2)

1. By reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times over the water for the bath with the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*), as soon as he is consecrated, he is seen by all the world in the midst of the great assembly in the form of the noble Avalokiteśvara within that mirror. And within that mirror, he gives his approval to the knowledge-holder (*vidyādhara*), saying: "Excellent, excellent, O Great Knowledge-Holder! This true and unfailing mirror-entry of mine is real; everything is seen therein. It is the unsurpassed fruit of mundane and supramundane actions. Thus is its purity.

"O Vidyādhara, you have attained the incomparable supramundane path; a great fruit has been achieved by you. You have mastered the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, including the mundane and supramundane methods of accomplishment (*sādhana*), the ritual manuals (*kalpa*), mandalas, and mudrās. Choose a boon, O Vidyādhara; I shall grant it all—both mundane and supramundane. Then, whatever excellent object the Vidyādhara might request, he grants it all immediately. And those men, women, boys, girls, śramaṇas, and brahmins who had gathered in that assembly circle...

3. Whether they be Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, Vaiśyas, kings, ministers, courtiers, priests, or those gathered in the inner apartments—whether meritorious or demeritorious, whether pure in intention or holding wrong views; and whatever other beings there may be in the various hells, fallen into the darkness of delusion, destined for Avīci, or who have committed the five deeds of immediate retribution, or who have slandered the noble ones and rejected the true Dharma—they too all see that very form of the Noble Avalokiteśvara. All—

4. He converses with them and comforts them; he reveals to all of them the ripening of their own karmic fruits, whether auspicious or inauspicious—with the exception of those who are thieves of knowledge (*vidyā-caura*), outcastes (*caṇḍāla*), those who destroy the deposit of knowledge, those who corrupt knowledge, and those who lack faith in or desire for knowledge, for whom there is no vision [of him]. He sees other various things produced as the painful fruits of their own karma. Then those beings, whatever purpose they had in mind—

5. Whatever worldly or supramundane [phenomenon] occurs, all of it manifests its respective fruits within that great circle of the assembly. They behold the fruits of merit and demerit; they behold all the buddha-fields of the Tathāgatas; they behold the great forms of the Tathāgatas together with their celestial palaces (vimānas) and towers. They behold the palaces on Mount Potalaka and the miraculous manifestations of the Blessed One. They behold the noble Avalokiteśvara together with his retinue and his palace, surrounded by gods and nāgas.

6. Whatever else occurs, whether auspicious or inauspicious, such as abundance or famine; illness, death, short life or long life; the threat of war from one's own army or an enemy army, battle, or conflict, or victory or defeat; loss or destruction; pestilence, excessive rain, untimely rain, or drought; wind, cold, or heat—all that is seen, as well as the arrival of wealth, decline or increase, the growth of crops, flowers, and fruits—all that is seen, or the fear of thieves, robbers, poison, or weapons, or the king—

7. Whether it be fear, or fear of yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, ḍākinīs, or apasmāras—all that shall be seen. Or whether it be a great treasure—all that shall be seen. And the passing away and rebirth shall be seen. Or the obtaining of a son, the obtaining of a village, city, district, or country, or the obtaining of a woman—all that shall be seen. One should not give rise to doubt, indecision, or uncertainty in this regard. This rite must be accomplished with great diligence, supreme faith, and reverence. Thus ends the Amoghapāśa [Sūtra]. 91a (P. omitted; D.173b4).
1. The procedure for the supramundane accomplishment within the maṇḍala of liberation is completed.

Amoghapāśakalparāja – Part VII. 91a (P. omitted; D. 173b4) Oṃ! Then indeed, Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Behold, Blessed One, how the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara has spoken this Amoghapāśahṛdaya, together with its ritual manual, mandala, mudrās, and chapter on cloth-paintings (*duṣya*). It is exceedingly profound, exceedingly difficult to fathom, exceedingly vast, and exceedingly difficult to accomplish; it contains many mandalas, many mudrās, and many mantras."

2. These have been proclaimed as the dust-particles of the earth. O Blessed One, they are like the great ocean, deep as the sea; they are like Mount Sumeru; they are like a mirage; they are like atoms; they are equal to the wisdom of the Tathāgata. They transcend calculation; they are incomparable, immeasurable, infinite, and their number exceeds that of incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*). Their measure is that of an eon; their measure is that of an inconceivable eon; their measure is that of the domain of the gods; their measure is that of the domain of the *nāgas*...

3. [The measures are: the measure of pride; the measure of the realm of sentient beings; the inconceivable measure of the Tathāgata; the measure of the appearance of the Tathāgata’s eye; the measure of the illumination of the Tathāgata’s gnosis; the measure of the Bodhisattva’s gnosis; and the measure of the realm of Māra. O Blessed One, no beginning is perceived, no middle is perceived, and no end is perceived. Therefore, O Blessed One, how may I understand this? By what method of accomplishment should I accomplish it? Which...

4. What is the mantra? What is the mudrā? What is the maṇḍala? What is the painted mudrā? What is the hand mudrā? What is the application of incense? What is the collyrium? What is the pill? What is the incense? What is the cloth painting (duṣyapaṭa)? What is the root mantra? What is the heart [mantra]? What is the secondary heart [mantra]? What is the wrathful mantra? What is the fierce one? What is the gentle one? What is the single-syllable [mantra]? What is the two-syllable? What is the three-syllable? What is the four-syllable? What is the five-syllable...

5. What is the *kṣara*? What is the six-syllable [mantra]? What is the seven-syllable? What is the eight-syllable? What is the nine-syllable? What is the ten-syllable? How is the fast (*upavāsa*) performed? How is the day-and-night (*ahorātra*) [observance]? What is the ritual for bathing (*snānavidhi*)? How is the upper garment (*vastraprāvaraṇa*) put on? How is the binding of the directions (*diśābandha*)? How is the binding of the mandala (*maṇḍalabandha*)? How is the binding of the topknot (*śikhābandha*)? How is self-protection (*ātmarakṣā*)? How is the protection of others (*pararakṣā*)? How is the protection of companions (*sahāyarakṣā*)? How is the protection of disciples (*śiṣyarakṣā*)? How is the entrance (*praveśa*)? How is the salutation (*namaskāra*)? How is the circumambulation (*pradakṣiṇa*)?

5. How is the offering of water for the feet (*arghapādya*) performed? How is the offering of betel (*vīta*) performed? How is the offering of flowers performed? How is incense (*dhūpa*) offered? How are perfumes (*gandha*) offered? How is the lamp (*dīpa*) offered? How is the ritual rinsing (*upaspṛśana*) performed? How is the offering made in all cases? How is the invocation (*āvāhana*) performed? How is the invitation (*nimantraṇa*) performed? How is the awakening by means of a dream (*svapnasaṃcodana*) performed? What is the procedure for the fire-oblation (*homavidhi*)? Which is the rite for pacification (*śāntika*)? Which is the rite for enrichment (*pauṣṭika*)? Which is the rite of sorcery (*abhicāruka*)? What is the noose (*pāśa*)? What is the vajra? What is the lotus (*padma*)? What is the dismissal (*visarjana*)? To whom should one approach? O Blessed One, I do not know what these are like.

7. Of what kind is the movement characterized by signs? O Blessed One, which ritual procedure for accomplishing karma shall I follow? How, O Blessed One, shall I act for the sake of sentient beings in the future time, in the final age? Which accomplishment shall I bestow? How shall I deliver sentient beings? Regarding this, O Blessed One, I am bewildered. O Blessed One, I lack eloquence; it is not possible for me to know [this]. Therefore, O Blessed One, tell me that.

1. Regarding the characteristics according to the rule: "O Blessed One, I have a doubt; may the Blessed One sever my doubt. Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, having heard the true inquiry being asked, spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi, the great yakṣa general: "Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi! This question you have asked is extremely difficult to obtain. O Vajrapāṇi, eloquence has arisen in you for the sake of asking. You are compassionate, Vajrapāṇi, in that you ask for the benefit of all sentient beings and for the sake of all vidyādharas."

2. For the sake of the supreme accomplishment of those who inquire, O Vajrapāṇi, this most wonderful [teaching]—whether asked or unasked—is equal to the illusion-like samādhi. O Vajrapāṇi, this procedure for the Great King of Rituals, the Amoghapāśahṛdaya, is equal to the great ocean in its depth; it is difficult to fathom. O Vajrapāṇi, it is not possible to count the drops of the great ocean, nor, O Vajrapāṇi, is it possible to grasp the measure of the Amoghapāśahṛdaya. And this, O Vajrapāṇi, is like Sumeru, the king of mountains...

3. Even if one were to count the dust motes scattered by the horses of Māra, it might be possible to determine their limit and even to re-establish Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, in its own place; yet it is not possible to grasp the measure of the *Amoghapāśahṛdayakalpa*. It is so vast, so difficult to fathom, and so profound that, O Vajrapāṇi, it is impossible to penetrate the knowledge of the minds of all the Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present. But [this] Amogha...

4. Vajrapāṇi, it is impossible to grasp the measure of this *Hṛdaya* of the *Pāśa-kalpa*. That which is like an illusion (*māyopama*) is the *Hṛdaya*; that which is meditative absorption (*samādhi*) is the *Pāśa*. This is the miraculous manifestation of the *Māyopama-samādhi*. The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara displays various forms, colors, marks, signs, and diverse appearances for the sake of delivering all sentient beings. O Vajrapāṇi, he is the supreme achiever of success for all holders of spells (*vidyādharas*).

5. The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara flows equally everywhere; wherever milk and water meet, he becomes equal. He pervades all places with equal great loving-kindness and compassion. With the unfailing lasso (*amoghapāśa*), he draws them forth and delivers them, establishing them upon the deathless ground (*amṛtasthala*) in the vajra-maṇḍala. Whether they be inferior, superior, or middling; whether from low or high families; or those in the realms of hell, animals, the world of Yama, and so forth—he [acts] equally everywhere through the mere act of remembering him, uttering his name, or grasping it.

6. He does not run about; he delivers all sentient beings, and he is free from weariness, fatigue, or regret, nor does pride arise within him. With a single production of thought, he traverses the realms of the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, apasmāras, pretas, and in the forests, through the abodes of Yama, down to the depths of Pātāla, from the peak of existence (bhavāgra) to the Avīci hell, and up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven. He delivers everyone—including gods and nāgas, and even those in the animal realm, men, women, boys, and girls.

7. Just as the rays of the sun dispel all darkness and illuminate Jambudvīpa equally everywhere, even so the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara illuminates everywhere with great compassion; he abides equally in all places and liberates [beings] from all painful sensations, fears, terrible diseases, sorrows, sufferings, and bonds. He liberates them from the sufferings of birth, old age, and death, and [establishes them] in all the higher realms.

He establishes them on the path in all directions. Thus, Great Compassion and Great Loving-kindness pursue all equally; they deliver all equally; they establish all equally on the path to enlightenment; and they become a refuge and final resort for all equally. In this way, O Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, possessing the resolve and vigor of a most firm armor, has set out for the sake of all vidyādharas and all sentient beings. He, O Vajrapāṇi, is the great caravan leader of all—

He leads sentient beings along the path of great fear and establishes them on the secure and auspicious path; he does not engage in conceptualization, discursive thought, or changeability, nor does his mind become remorseful. Then, indeed, Vajrapāṇi, the Great General of the Yakṣas, having heard this praise of the great virtues of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara in the presence of the Blessed One, was satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and serenity.

Those born from the nose uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*): "O, how wonderful is the Lord of the World! O, how wonderful is the Guru, the Lord of the World! By the manifestation of the qualities of your name, all are liberated from the miserable realms. Vajrapāṇi said to the Bodhisattva: "This is the Teacher and Protector of the world; this is the Grandfather of the world. This is the Savior of the world, O Protector, this Sun among Munis. The Blessed One said: "It is even so, Vajrapāṇi, as you have spoken. The Blessed One said: [Thus it was.]

4. "Go, Vajrapāṇi! Pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and inquire of him; he will show you his true speech according to the ritual procedure, revealing the essential nature (*svabhāva*) of the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-tattva*). He will demonstrate the accomplishment (*siddhi*) of the ritual manual (*kalpa*) for the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* and will instruct you. Then Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, who moves with a most profound gait and walks with the stride of a lion, brandishing his vajra like the moon—

5. Holding celestial flowers, he approached the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara; having approached, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara bowed his head at [the other’s] feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and offered the stainless Candraroca flower. Then, placing his right knee upon the ground, he addressed the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara as follows:

6. "O Blessed One, I have not fallen into delusion, nor is my mindfulness lost, nor is my intellect impaired. Yet this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* is exceedingly vast, with its many mantras, mudrās, and procedures for the cloth-painting (*paṭa*). Therefore, I do not know which is the beginning, which is the middle, and which is the end; which is the root-mantra, which is the heart-mantra, which is the subsidiary-heart-mantra, and so on, up to the ten-syllable mantra; and what is the ritual manual (*kalpa*) for the mandala and the cloth-painting? O Blessed One, please grant me the opportunity."

7. Thus it was said. Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, out of compassion for Vajrapāṇi, took a flower as pure as moonlight and cast it into the expanse of the sky as an offering to the Blessed One. As soon as it was cast, it remained above the crown of the Blessed One’s head in the form of a wheel, five hundred *yojanas* in width and rising far above the earth, reaching as high as the Akaniṣṭha heaven, with a great blue beryl shaft and hanging bells of Jāmbūnada gold.

1. That radiant, blazing head-band was well-finished, perfectly circular, and shaped like a wheel; it shone with a brilliance exceeding that of hundreds of thousands of millions of suns. It was utterly pure, cleansed, stainless, firmly set upon a golden base, and resplendent. Inlaid with various great maṇi-jewels, it was delightful, heart-captivating, gladdening, and lovely to behold. It was worthy of being venerated and worshipped by gods and asuras, praised by the ṛṣis, and prophesied by the Blessed Buddhas. And everywhere—

2. There was a gabled pavilion made of the seven precious gems, adorned with Indra-roca-vimala flowers and the seated forms of Tathāgatas; it was surrounded by circles of assemblies seated beneath a parasol that was perfectly circular on all sides. It was filled with divine palaces belonging to gods, nāgas, apsarases, and celestial maidens, as well as nāga maidens, kinnara maidens, and [other] divine beings. Hundreds of thousands of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, kinnaras, mahoragas, and vidyādharas, along with vidyādharīs, were present, adorned with various divine flower-palaces and divine ornaments, garments, and decorations.

3. They bore [offerings] consisting of silk cloths, banners, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, standards, and flags. They honored the Blessed One and the circle of the assembly by raining down clouds of various divine offerings. For the sake of worship, they offered celestial gandharva songs, music, instrumental ensembles, and percussion. On Mount Potalaka, within the assembly circle and its celestial palaces, they raised a great sound of joyful acclaim. And those gods who dwell on Mount Potalaka...

The nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas were filled with joy; they were struck with wonder. And those deities of the Tathāgata family maṇḍala, those deities of the Padma family maṇḍala, those deities of the Vajra family maṇḍala, those deities of the Maṇi family maṇḍala, those deities of the Gaja family maṇḍala, and those deities of the Great Maṇḍala—all of them attained supreme amazement. They were struck with wonder and filled with joy. Ā-

5. Struck with wonder, they remained gazing up at the Blessed One. And those deities of the moon, sun, constellations, and clusters of stars; the night deities; Śakra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Kumāra, Nandikeśvara, Gaṇeśvara, Mahākāla, Īśvara, Maheśvara, the divine son Brahmā, and the four Great Kings; the deities Māṇibhadra, Pūrṇabhadra, Baladeva, Yama, Varuṇa, and Kuvera; and the deity Kumāra—all held the parasol and staff surrounding the Blessed One.

He honored him with great celestial palaces; through divine transformations, clouds of offerings rained down from all sides in the shape of parasols. Within, the Tuṣita gods and the Akaniṣṭha gods—surrounded by hosts of sons of gods in all the celestial abodes—proceeded in the sky with great clouds of offerings to perform worship for the Blessed One Śākyamuni and Avalokiteśvara within the circle of the assembly. And those earth-deities, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, and earth-deities [nāga-yakṣa... [continued].

7. The rākṣasas, gandharvas, earth deities, water deities, forest deities, crop deities, and medicinal herb deities—all of them purified the celestial palaces upon the surface of the earth. They adorned the circles of the earth by sprinkling them with various scented waters, anointing them with various fragrant powders, scattering various flowers, and perfuming them with various incenses. Such was the vast display of miraculous power and the bull-like majesty of the Tathāgata. 93a (omitted in P; D.177b5)

1. The Empowerment of the Departed Time. Then, the great yakṣa general Vajrapāṇi, having seen such a vast and extensive display of great miraculous transformations, was struck with extreme wonder and amazement. He thought: "This has been manifested by the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara; it is truly marvelous! Then, the great yakṣa general Vajrapāṇi once again entreated the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara: "O Blessed One, please act—"

2. [An] opportunity. Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara said this to Vajrapāṇi, the great yakṣa general: "Vajrapāṇi, favor us by dispelling our longing and cutting through our doubt. Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, bowed with palms joined toward the Blessed One, circumambulated him three times, and stood before the Blessed One with unblinking eyes and a smiling face, [emitting] rays of light—

3. Jvālaśarīra addressed the Blessed One as follows: “Blessed One, I possess within the Amoghapāśa maṇḍala, the Padmodāravikurvaṇa [Padmodāravikurvaṇa], the Padmoṣṇīṣamaṇi maṇḍala, the secret of Amoghapāśa, the Māyopama-hṛdaya-mudrā, and the chapter on the great maṇḍala of Samantāvalokita. Therefore, Blessed One, I shall proclaim it before the Blessed One. It is the easy-to-accomplish recitation—”

4. ...the secret seals (mudrās) that are the true essence of the samaya; I shall reveal the heart-mantra (hṛdaya). Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, extended his arm—adorned with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of various rays of light—and placed his hand upon the head of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying: "Excellent, excellent, O Great Pure Being! Speak, Avalokiteśvara, for you consider this now to be the right time."

5. Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, having understood the Blessed One’s request, looked toward the ten directions, paid homage to all the Tathāgatas, and, looking upon all the Tathāgatas, spoke the root mantra—the Amoghapāśa Padmoṣṇīṣa Maṇi, the Amoghapāśa Heart Sūtra. [Oṃ] Amoghapāśahṛdayamaṇḍale padmoṣṇīṣaguhyo vikurvvaṇaprasnavidhi-maḥ.

Chapter One. Oṃ. Homage to all the Tathāgatas who abide throughout the three times, to the Unfailing Secret Maṇḍalas of the Uṣṇīṣas of all the Tathāgatas, and to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Homage to the assemblies of all the Pratyekabuddhas and Noble Śrāvakas of the past, future, and present. Homage to the heart-samayas of the secret family of all the Tathāgatas. Homage to those who have gone rightly; homage to those who have practiced rightly. Homage to the Greatly Wise Śāradvatīputra. Homage.

Homage to the noble assembly of the foremost Great Bodhisattvas, headed by the noble Maitreya. Homage to the noble Amitābha, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha. Homage to the Three Jewels. Homage to the noble Padmoṣṇīṣa, the bearer of the maṇḍala, to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, Mahāsattva, and Great Compassionate One—to those noble and preeminent assemblies of great ṛṣis. Having paid homage to them, [I shall explain] this Liberation Maṇḍala.
(Folio 93b, Peking edition omitted; Derge 178b4)

1. This *Amogharāja-padmoṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya*, which issued from the mouth of Avalokiteśvara and was spoken by the Tathāgata in the presence of a great assembly—I shall now recite it. May they be effective for the monk Śīlākaragupta in all his undertakings; may there be protection from all fears. It is as follows: Oṃ padmoṣṇīṣa-varada hūṃ! Cara cara ciri ciri curu curu, O Great Compassionate One! Ciri ciri piri piri ciri ciri, O Supreme Compassionate One! Siri siri ciri ciri piri...

2. *Piri viri viri*, O you who hold the great lotus in your hand! *Kala kala*! *Kili kili kulu kulu*, O Great Pure Being (*mahāśuddhasatva*), come, come! Awaken, awaken! Run, run! *Kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu*, O Supreme Pure Being (*paramaśuddhasatva*)! *Kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru*, O you who have attained great power (*mahāsthāmaprāpta*)! *Cala cala sañcala vicala*, move, move, shake, tremble! *Eṭaṭ eṭaṭa bhara bhara bhiri bhiri bhuru bhuru*, O you whose crown is the great stainless lotus, O dustless one (*viraja*), accomplish it! *Hūṃ hūṃ*, come, come, O Great Compassionate One (*mahākāruṇika*), O you who wear the guise of the Great Lord of Beasts (*mahāpaśupati*)!

Dhara! Dhara! O bearer of the great lotus crown; sara sara! O remover of all obscurations; cara cara! O you who are honored by all the vidyādharas; hara hara! O remover of all sins! Hāhā hāhā! Hīhī hīhī! Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! O wearer of the garb of Brahmā, the syllable Oṃ! Dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhara dhuru! O bearer of the blazing light of the great lotus! Tara tara sara sara para para! O bearer of the lotus noose! Cara cara! Vara vara! O you whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of excellent rays of light!

4. *Ya* / *jvala jvala*, burn, burn! *tapa tapa*, heat, heat! O you whose feet are worshipped by the Blessed One, Soma, Āditya, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Brahmā, Indra, the hosts of ṛṣis, and the hosts of gods; *sura sura*, *curu curu*, *puru puru*, *muru muru*; *sanatkumāra-rudra-vāsava-viṣṇu-dhanada-deva-ṛṣi-nāyaka-bahu-vividha-veṣadharaḥ* (you who assume many various guises as the leaders of the gods, ṛṣis, Vasus, Viṣṇu, and the Giver of Wealth); *mahāpadma-daṇḍadharaḥ* (bearer of the great lotus-staff), *pāśadharaḥ* (bearer of the noose); *dhara dhara*, *dhiri dhiri*, *dhuru dhuru*, *thara thara*, *ghara ghara*, *yara yara*, *lara lara*; *hara hara*, *para para*, *para para*; *ca*.

5. *Ra cara vara vara mahāvaradāyaka / Samantamaṇḍalāvalokita lokeśvara maheśvara / Muhu muhu / Muru muru muya muya muñca muñca bhagavann āryāvalokiteśvara rakṣa rakṣa mama Śilākaraguptena sarvabhayebhyaḥ sarvopadravebhyaḥ sarvagrahebhyaḥ sarvajvarebhyaḥ sarvavyādhibhyaḥ vadhbandhanatādanatarjanarājacorata-skarāgnir-udakaviṣaśastraparimocanaṃ kuru.*

6. cakaḥ kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi / kuṇu kuṇu / cara cara, you who illuminate the faculties, the powers, the factors of awakening, and the four noble truths / tama tama dama dama sama sama / sama sama, you who dispel the great darkness and gloom / ṣaṭpāramitāparipūraka, you who fulfill the six perfections mili mili / ṭaṭa ṭaṭa / ṭhaṭha ṭhaṭha ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭhiṭhi ṭhiṭhi / ṭaṭa ṭuṭu ṭhuṭhu ṭhuṭhu / you who have made a girdle of eneya-deer skin / ehy ehi, come, come, O Īśvara, Maheśvara, Padmeśvara, you who shatter the hosts of great spirits!

7. <ḥ> / O Lord of Great Siddhis, act! Act! Go forth! Go forth! Kaṭa kaṭa! Maṭa maṭa! O you who dwell in the pure realm, O Great Compassionate One, wearer of a white sacrificial thread and a crest-garland of jewels, whose crown is placed upon the head of the Omniscient One, O Great Wonder, whose palms are marked with lotuses, unshakable through meditation, concentration, and liberation, ripener of the continuums of many sentient beings, Great Compassionate One, purifier of all karmic obscurations, liberator from all diseases, fulfiller of all hopes.
94a (omitted in P, D.179a7)

1. *Kaḥ* sarvasattvasamāśvāsaka! Oṃ padmoṣṇīṣapāśahṛdayamaṇḍala, namo ’stu te svāhā! // O // As soon as this noble Padmoṣṇīṣa-Guhyahṛdayamaṇḍala of the Amoghapāda of Āryāvalokiteśvara was spoken, this trichiliocosm, the great world-system, experienced a great earthquake; together with its mountains, forests, and groves, it began to tremble in six ways. And upon the entire surface of the earth, there appeared everywhere lotus-thrones made of the seven precious gems.

2. Having crossed over, from the navel-center of the Blessed One Padmapāṇi, a great lotus emerged, possessing a thousand petals, composed of the seven precious gems, with a stalk of great emerald and lapis lazuli, a pericarp of Jambūnada gold, a filaments of red pearls and divine great pearls, all of which became a single blaze, emitting various rays that shone, gleamed, and blazed forth in all ten directions.

3. It illuminates all Buddha-fields in every direction. It illuminates all the abodes of the devas, the abodes of the nāgas, the abodes of the yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas; it gladdens them, inspires them, and comforts them. Having illuminated the sixteen great hells, by its touch those great hells became manifest as vast lotus ponds. And those sentient beings in the hells, by that illumination—

4. By the mere touch [of his light], they were all completely liberated and reborn through spontaneous birth (*upapāduka*) in lotuses within the world-system of Sukhāvatī. Possessing divine bodies, adorned with ornaments, garments, and finery, they became those who remember their births in every successive life. Having thus illuminated those belonging to the animal realm—the beasts and birds—all those in the animal realm were completely liberated and reborn in the heavens, possessing earrings as pure as crystal.

1. Thus, the radiance touched all sentient beings throughout the ten directions. They all became established upon the eight great stages (*mahābhūmi*). And by that, the great hosts of bodhisattvas assembled in the vast assembly were all established in the state of non-retrogression regarding unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. And those in the assembly of the knowledge-holders (*vidyādhara*), they all attained the secret accomplishment of the *amoghapāśa* of the heart-mantra of the Great Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa.

2. They attained [these states]: all those in the assembly of the Naga kings were inspired by the Cintamani-dhvaja; all those in the assembly of the gods attained the Jvalanolkā-samādhi; all those in the assembly of Yakshas, Rakshasas, and serpents came to dwell in jeweled palaces; all those in the assembly of spirits (bhūtas) attained the Vimalatejas-samādhi; and all those in the assembly of Asuras were armored in the Vajra-kavaca and Vajra-dhvaja armor.

3. Those who were in the assembly of Garuḍas became possessed of great peaks with diamond beaks and attained powerful speed. Those who were in the assembly of Kinnaras and Mahoragas all became pure in body, speech, and mind. And those who were laymen, laywomen, men, women, boys, and girls—all of them became completely liberated from the suffering of birth, old age, and death. And from the body of the Blessed One, a great ray of light named Sūryaketu was emitted toward the noble Avalokiteśvara.

1. Having entered into the heart of the Great Being Dhiṣatva, immediately upon entering, [the Blessed One] spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi, the great yakṣa general, regarding the heart of Avalokiteśvara: "Behold, Vajrapāṇi, the miraculous manifestation of the secret heart and the lotus-uṣṇīṣa of Amoghapāśa! Vajrapāṇi replied: "I have seen it, Blessed One; I have seen it, Pure Being! This is the inconceivable miraculous manifestation of the Great Pure Being, the Lord of the Lotus, the secret heart and the lotus-uṣṇīṣa of the Heart of Amoghapāśa."

2. "O Blessed One, please speak in full detail regarding this most profound and vast Maṇḍala, the supreme means for achieving great and wondrous accomplishments. O Tathāgata, in our very presence, speak of the Maṇḍala of Knowledge (Vidyāmaṇḍala) from the chapter on the Entrails (Mantrapatala), along with the ritual procedures for the wondrous offerings, for the sake of destroying the sins of all sentient beings and for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of the Vidyādharas. Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the Yakṣas: "Vajrapāṇi, show favor..."

3. This is the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, the supreme secret; the mandala of all *uṣṇīṣas*. It is for the benefit of all sentient beings, the destroyer of all evil, the purifier of all obscurations, the remover of all stains and turbidity, the pacifier of all diseases, and the warder-off of all misfortune. It is the pacifier of the fear of all wicked beings, enemies, and adversaries; the subduer of all obstacles and obstructors; the crusher of all Māras and other malevolent forces; [and the protector against] all poisons, weapons, and fire.

4. It wards off the fear of water, venomous serpents, lions, kings, yakṣas, and rākṣasas; it destroys all poisons, sorcery, sprinkled spells, and the application of powders. This is the Heart of Amoghapāśa, the wondrous essence of reality (*tattvasāra*). It is the unsurpassed accomplishment through recitation, the essence of the reality of practice. Then Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣa army—his face smiling, his brow free from frowns, brandishing his vajra—spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara:

5. "O Blessed One, what is that true secret-heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa, the maṇḍala of the lotus-uṣṇīṣa? O Blessed One, please speak it! Then, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, perceiving the request of Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, touched his right hand to the lotus at his navel in the form of a mudrā. Immediately upon touching it, a lotus appeared in his right hand, and he sat in his own form upon that heart-mantra-lotus within a celestial palace.

6. He is seen wearing the garb of Brahmā, possessing unfailing form, three eyes, and four arms, adorned with all ornaments, with a water-pot made of jewels and gold, and adorned with a crown bearing Amitābha. His matted hair is decorated with a lotus-ushṇīṣa and a crown; he is resplendent with a half-moon. He holds a noose, a lotus-ushṇīṣa, a jewel-staff, and a vajra-staff, and is seated in the paryanka posture. He is beautifully adorned with masses of radiating rays, and with various variegated garments that outshine the sun and moon in their brilliance, he shines upon a lotus.

7. Blazing brightly, it is that which delights the hearts of all Tathāgatas; it is to be venerated by all Bodhisattvas, worshipped by all deities, favored by all Nāgas, gratified by all Yakṣas, followed by all Asuras, Garuḍas, Kinnaras, and Mahoragas, and by which all sentient beings are delivered. Thus, in this vast expanse, the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, has revealed the Heart that is the essence of reality. Then Vajrapāṇi— [95a (omitted, D.181a6)]

1. O Great Yakṣa General, as soon as they beheld him within that great circle of the assembly, they all attained the secret heart-mantra, the *Amoghapadmavimaloṣṇīṣaraśmijvāla-samādhi*. By means of this attainment—the *Māyopama-samādhi* (Illusion-like Samādhi)—they all entered into it; with hearts full of joy, they prostrated at his feet and paid homage. Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya-mantra*.

2. // O // Oṃ! O Padmoṣṇīṣa of the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya, you who wear the garb of a youth, Lord of the Lotus (Padmeśvara)! Cause [them] to enter! O heart of the samaya of the entire Amogha family, grant all unfailing accomplishments (siddhi)! Padma padma! Hūṃ hūṃ! Homage to you, svāhā! This is the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya, the practice for accomplishment through recitation. // O // Oṃ! O Lord of the Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa, Lord of the Lotus! Summon all the Tathāgatas! Draw forth the samaya of the Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa; cause [them] to enter all activities.

3. Grant me success! Śilākaragupta, O Avalokiteśvara, hūṃ hūṃ, O you whose arm is the Great Lotus Uṣṇīṣa, svāhā! This is the mantra of the Family King. Oṃ, O Mahācaṇḍapadmeśvara, you whose various forms are formidable, whose lotus fangs are terrifyingly fierce, O you with a face that strikes fear into all evil hearts, devour the obstacles, O Lotus-Bearer! Ciṭi dhṛṭi hūṃ svāhā! This is the Wrathful King of the Family Heart-mantra. These are the secret rites for the inner maṇḍala. Oṃ, Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa...

4. O Great Padma-pāśa-Krodha, enter into the activity! You who wear the disguises of Mahāpaśupati, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Brahmā; [enter] into the lotus of the unerring family vow (*samaya*) of the Great Fierce Impetus, *hūṃ hūṃ*! This is the heart-mantra of the Unerring Lasso-Lotus Uṣṇīṣa King of Wrath. // O // Now, the activities of the Unerring Heart-mantra come to pass by the mere act of recollection: one shall become equal and identical to all the Tathāgatas of the three times, and one’s own body shall become equal to that of Amitāyus.

5. In all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, it proceeds as entirely equal to all Tathāgatas; it is seen as entirely equal, indeed as incomparable to all Tathāgatas. By holding a lotus in the hand and placing the Padmoṣṇīṣa upon the head with the hand, one becomes equal to Lokeśvara. Having bound the Padmoṣṇīṣa, one is indeed consecrated upon the body of the head; for all Tathāgatas of the three times are consecrated by the Padmoṣṇīṣas. Whoever [recites] the Padmoṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya, the unfailing consecration of the Padmoṣṇīṣas, [is empowered] by its heat...

6. He obtains hundreds of thousands of samādhis; he obtains unsurpassed glory. O Noble One, having mastered the mantra of the King of Families, Padmoṣṇīṣa indeed exists within the maṇḍala. There arises the excellent accomplishment of the King of Families, and in all the excellent accomplishments of the King of Families, the Kings of Mantras, the Kings of Knowledge (vidyārāja), and the most supreme ones will surely come. They follow [the practitioner] just as they do for Padmapāṇi; the Amogha family is accomplished. Accomplished through mere recitation—of this there is no doubt. Accomplishment in the Padmoṣṇīṣa family—pa-

7. In the *Dmodāra* maṇḍala, or in the *Amoghapāśa* maṇḍala, having accomplished [the practice] or merely recited the mantra, one becomes a King of Vidyādharas of the family; he becomes a sovereign lord over all maṇḍalas through the ritual manual and mudrās of the Bodhisattvas’ common family. By means of this family vidyā, he shall perform royal duties everywhere throughout thousands and hundreds of Buddha-fields—fields as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā. He becomes a lord of the gods among the gods, and a lord of the hosts.

1. He shall eternally be among the yakṣas and rākṣasas; likewise, among the gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, he will always be a sovereign king everywhere—of this there is no doubt. Among the garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, he will be the family king everywhere until he abides in enlightenment. Now, by the mere recollection of the King of Wrath, even with a fierce mind, one could instantly cause Sumeru to fall and shatter the Cakravāḍa mountains; through the agitation of the great ocean, the sea itself would arise [in turmoil], and all things would be set ablaze.

2. All the abodes of the *nāgas* and all the *nāga* dwellings blaze forth entirely; they are scorched for a mere moment by all the *vighnas* and *vināyakas*. Yakṣas, *rākṣasas*, *bhūtas*, and the terrible *grahas* and *apasmāras*—all of them go to destruction merely by recollecting the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*). All the *guhyakas* who abide by the family commitments (*kulasaṃmaya*), those established in the mudrās within the maṇḍala, and whatever other mantra-deities there may be—all of them take refuge in the *vidyādhara* merely by recollecting the King of Wrath. They will all become his followers; stay!

Whether walking or standing anywhere, Śakra and the thirty-three gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Sāgara the Naga king, Nanda and Upananda, as well as Kumāra the commander-in-chief, and the four Great Kings, will always follow the Vidyādhara; of this there is no doubt. Whether all his actions are cruel or even fierce, success is seen therein by merely uttering the syllable *HŪṂ*. Enemies, adversaries, and the wicked—

4. All beings who are extremely cruel, those belonging to hostile armies, those who are terrible, hateful, or sinful toward people—all these go to destruction and are reduced to ashes merely by the pressure of the syllable *hūṃ*. All wicked beings, those who are difficult to understand, the ungrateful, and those who have become enemies—by the mere utterance of the fierce *hūṃ*, they are all instantly consumed, like moths in a fire. Other thousands of rites, even hundreds of thousands of rites, are accomplished merely by recitation; indeed, by the mere remembrance [of this], all rites are accomplished immediately.

5. ...are accomplished. // O // Now, by the mere recollection of Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa, all undertakings will be accomplished twice over, exactly as one intends. Whatever rite one may perform—whether in a maṇḍala, at a sacred site, or elsewhere—in every case, one accomplishes the task exactly as it dwells in the mind. // O // Furthermore, as the mantras are set in motion, all undertakings are accomplished individually. [261] Oṃkāra, [this is for] the entire maṇḍala of Amoghapāśa Padmoṣṇīṣa.

6. By recollecting the single-syllable mantra of the Lord of the World in his presence, one will become established in the first stage (*bhūmi*). Whatever evil has been accumulated—all those terrible hells—will all be destroyed, just as dust is by the wind. One attains all accomplishments (*siddhi*); all purposes are fulfilled; and the Tathāgatas, as well as the other deities of the mandala, remain silent [in approval]. Noble Avalokiteśvara is always the granter of boons. Through the recollection of the *oṃ*-syllable mantra, there is rebirth in Sukhāvatī.

7. The single-syllable mantra goes to the world-system: *Oṃ bhūḥ*. By reciting it two hundred thousand times, one will attain the second stage (*bhūmi*). One stands before the Tathāgata Amitābha; he will grant every boon and purify all sins. One is also completely liberated from previous illnesses. One stands in the presence of Maṇibhadra, the lord of wealth, who acts according to one's will. No non-human being shall ever again be able to create obstacles. Upon passing away, one will be reborn on Mount Potalaka.

He utters the word "Kāra": "Excellent, excellent, Vidyādhara! A great mass of merit has been produced by you. You, Vidyādhara, have planted great roots of virtue; you, Vidyādhara, have transcended [birth]. Having cultivated roots of virtue in the presence of ninety-two hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of Tathāgatas, you shall be born spontaneously in my Buddha-fields. You, Vidyādhara, are a protector who has abandoned all evil. The Amoghapāśa has been accomplished by you."

5. Perform all activities as you desire within the secret mandala of the heart of the Padmoṣṇīṣa according to this chapter on the Great Seal (mahāmudrā). Whatever resides in the mind, all that shall be well-accomplished; it is the means for accomplishing everything. Oṃ padmāvalokite. Oṃ. By reciting the six dhāraṇīs one hundred thousand times, one attains the empowerment of the six stages (ṣadbhūmi). One brings light to all the Tathāgatas. One becomes equal to the Tathāgatas, who are as numerous as the atoms in a great trichiliocosm world system.

The Arhats, the Perfectly Awakened Ones, look upon him; they grant him a face-to-face vision and offer him consolation. Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Awakened One Padmāvalokitadhvaja consoles that Vidyādhara: "Come, Vidyādhara! In my Buddha-field, until the very end at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍala*), your deeds shall be perfectly accomplished. The gates of hell have been closed by you, and the gates to all the Buddha-fields have been opened for you. You have attained the common lineage of the seed-family of all the Tathāgatas."

7. "O Siddha, by you the secret maṇḍala of the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāda-padmoṣṇīṣa has been mastered. The doors to all your abodes—both mundane and supramundane rites for the accomplishment of activities—have been opened. Perform all activities according to your heart's desire. [267] OṂ PADMAJVĀLA HŪṂ DHṚK. Immediately upon the recitation of one hundred thousand repetitions of these seven syllables, one attains the samādhi named *Padmavimalavigatāvaraṇaśuddhi* (The Pure State Free from Obstructions, Stainless as a Lotus). By means of that attained samādhi, one becomes intensely radiant... 96b (P.153a7, D.184b1)

1. His developing body will possess rays of light of various colors; he will be established in the seventh stage (*bhūmi*). And by the illumination of the rays from his body, he will illuminate the entire great trichiliocosm (*trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu*) and all the abodes of the Buddha-fields. Wherever those rays fall, there will appear rains of various flowers, radiant with diverse jewels and various precious gems. Offerings to all the Tathāgatas will proceed. Then, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vimalapadmājvalaraśmi—Suva...

2. Extending his arms of golden hue, he places his right hand upon the head of the *vidyādhara* and grants him approval (*sādhukāra*). He consoles him, saying: "Excellent, excellent, *vidyādhara*! This is the supreme rite of worship and recitation, the secret heart of the Blessed Buddhas. This is the true secret heart of the noble Avalokiteśvara, the essence-maṇḍala. O *vidyādhara*, you have accomplished the *Amoghapāśa-padmoṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya*; the ritual manual (*kalpa*) of the *Padmoṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya* for the entire maṇḍala is now complete. [The *Amoghapāśa*-..."

"Go, Vidyādhara, and perform the work of a Buddha in my Buddha-field. Oṃ amoghamaṇipadme. By reciting this Heart Dhāraṇī of the Eighth [Stage] one hundred thousand times, one becomes pure of body and stainless through mere recitation. Just as a great crystal maṇi-jewel is perfectly pure both inside and out, so shall the body of the Vidyādhara become purified. He will be established in the eighth stage (bhūmi). [To] Āryāvalokiteśvara—
