You who have entered into the supreme resolve, O vidyādhara, come, O vidyādhara, to the buddha-field called *Samanubaddhalokavilokitā*. There, by you, [the Buddha...]"

5. "The task shall be accomplished. You have mastered the secret heart-mantra and maṇḍala of Amoghapāśapadmoṣṇīṣa; perform all rites, the supreme accomplishment of both worldly and transcendent matters. Oṃ padmalocane huru hūṃ. By reciting this ninth heart-dhāraṇī one hundred thousand times, one will be established on the ninth stage (bhūmi). One will become the eldest son of the noble Avalokiteśvara. [One will see] ninety-nine koṭī-niyuta Tathāgatas...

6. One hundred thousand Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas appear before the sight of the vidyādhara, manifesting the miraculous transformations of the various domains of the Buddhas. They place all their hands upon the head of the vidyādhara and grant him their approval, saying: "Excellent, excellent, O great vidyādhara! You have accomplished all these things that were taught by the Leader of the World through the ritual procedures of the Amoghapāśa Maṇḍala Kalpa, the Sūtra-instructions, and the ritual methods for achieving both mundane and supramundane Buddhahood."

7. // Oṃ padmoṣṇīṣavimale hūṃ phaṭ // O // For one who performs one hundred thousand recitations of the ten-syllable heart mantra, having established irreversibility (*avaivarttikatā*) and being stationed on the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*), he is to be called a Tathāgata. Among the populations of gods and humans, he becomes irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment (*anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi*). There is no doubt that the turning of the wheel of the Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa will occur. This is indeed the accomplishment of the ten mantras; it is the unsurpassed attainment of reality (*tattvasiddhi*). Merely by recitation, they are accomplished as the Amogha.

I have previously explained all the transformations of the Heart of the Noose (*pāśahṛdayavikurvitam*), which pertains to resolute application (*adhyavasānikam*). [One should be] pure, practicing purity, wearing clean garments, possessing a mind of loving-kindness and compassion, speaking the truth, affectionate toward the Guru, intent upon faith in the Three Jewels, and constantly honoring the Guru and the Teacher. This is declared to be the procedure for recitation (*jāpavidhi*); it is the unsurpassed awakening of the Buddha. Thus [it is said]. Then indeed, Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, [addressed] the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...

The Great Being, his face beaming with a smile and brandishing a vajra, spoke thus to those with bowed heads: "This Great Being is exceedingly rare! These ten mantra-words of the *dhāraṇī*, the *Amoghapāśa-padmoṣṇīṣa-maṇḍala-hṛdaya-mahāvipula-guhya*, perform the work of a Buddha. Each single heart-mantra and *dhāraṇī*-heart will accomplish their purpose by mere recitation (*jāpa*). How much more so for those, O Avalokiteśvara, who undergo even greater fatigue and exertion to accomplish the extensive ritual procedures of recitation and sadhana throughout day and night?"

"Having consumed food consisting of fasts, alms, fruits, tubers, and roots, this person will accomplish the vidyā. O Avalokiteśvara, tell me, does accomplishment arise for him? Avalokiteśvara said: "Listen, Vajrapāṇi! Merely by fasting and reciting for a day and night—that is, in just a single day—accomplishment regarding the fruit arises. Vajrapāṇi, whether it be a son of good family or a daughter of good family, a monk, a nun, a layman, a laywoman, or anyone else who is shaven-headed—"

4. O Vajrapāṇi, whether it be a Śramaṇa, a member of a noble family, a Brāhmaṇa, a Kṣatriya, a woman, a man, a boy, a girl, a Vaiśya, or a Śūdra—whoever, for even a single moment, a fraction of a moment, or a muhūrta; or for a single twilight, or for the full three twilights—without speaking [of other things], shall remember this chapter on the mantras of the Wrathful Family, the Heart of the Amoghapāśa Padmoṣṇīṣa, which is the heart among the ten great dhāraṇīs; or shall recite it, or even merely remember its name—for such a person, during that single twilight—

5. Even one who has committed the five acts of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*) and is destined for the Avīci hell and remains there for an eon—by mere recollection [of this], all of that will be purified. All accumulated obscurations and sinful hindrances will be exhausted; they will possess a completely pure and stainless body, and their sins and obscurations will be removed. Upon the transition of death and rebirth, they will be born spontaneously within lotuses in the world-system of Sukhāvatī. They will remember their past lives, and furthermore...

Furthermore, at some point there will be a descent into the miserable realms; however, for eighty hundred thousand kalpas he will become a supreme universal monarch (cakravartin), and thereafter there will never again be a descent into the miserable realms. For eighty hundred thousand kalpas he will experience happiness in the world-system Sukhāvatī; for sixty-two hundred thousand kalpas he will experience happiness in the world-system Abhirati; and for seventy-two hundred thousand kalpas he will be reborn in the world-system Lokavilokitā. Birth after birth—

7. He will possess perfect recollection (*jatismara*). For twelve hundred thousand eons (*kalpa*), he will be a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) named Maṇindhara. For eighteen thousand eons, he will experience happiness in the abode of the noble Avalokiteśvara on Mount Potalaka. For ninety-nine hundred thousand eons, he will be reborn among the Akaniṣṭha gods. For eighty hundred thousand eons, he will experience happiness among the Tuṣita gods. For a hundred thousand eons, he will hold the position of Śakra among the Trāyastriṃśa gods.

1. He shall act as follows: for fifty-two hundred thousand kalpas, he will traverse all the buddha-fields in the ten directions; for twenty thousand kalpas, he will enjoy the sovereignty of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*). Furthermore, he shall never again be born within the womb of a mother; wherever he is born, he will always be born by spontaneous transformation (*upapāduka*). In every birth, he will possess the recollection of his former lives (*jātismara*). Thus, O Vajrapāṇi, by the mere recollection of this single vidyā, one will become endowed with a great mass of merit consisting of roots of virtue.

2. ...will [attain it], Vajrapāṇi. If anyone, Vajrapāṇi, shall dwell for one night or perform one fast and recitation, then in this very birth, in this human body, he shall obtain the samādhi named *Nādhigatāvaraṇamahāmoghavimala* (The Great Unobstructed Stainless One Who Has Not Attained [Otherwise]). He shall obtain the *Amoghavyūhasamādhi* (The Samādhi of the Unfailing Array). He shall obtain the *Padmojvalavikurvaṇasamādhi* (The Samādhi of the Lotus’s Blazing Transformation). He shall obtain the samādhi named *Amoghavimalanirbhāsa* (The Unfailing Stainless Radiance). He shall obtain the samādhi named *Amoghavilokitadhvaja* (The Unfailing Banner of Observation)...

He attains the *dhī*; he attains the samādhi named Padmoṣṇīṣaviratadhvaja; he attains the accomplishment of the secret heart-mantra of the Amoghajvalanoṣṇīṣa. He will have planted roots of merit in the presence of ninety-two hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of Tathāgatas, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā. He will be endowed with a great mass of merit, and in his next rebirth, [he will be born] in the world-system Sukhāvatī.

4. You shall be born from spontaneously arisen lotuses; and this *Amoghapāśahṛdayakalpa*, the *Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣamaṇḍala*, the *Vimokṣamaṇḍalakalpa* in its entirety, and the *Mudrākalpa* in its entirety, shall abide before your very eyes. You shall become an Amogha Vidyādhara Cakravartin. // O // This is the procedure for the accomplishment of the Heart Mantra within the *Amoghapāśahṛdayapadmoṣṇīṣamaṇḍala*. This is the second procedure for accomplishment.
